The factory runs its init calls with elevated rights, and those calls act only on the storage of the token being created, whose address must hold no code. transfer returns success only after the debit, except for a zero amount and for a transfer to self. Every successful transfer returns a 32 byte true and never empty data. balanceOf reads the token ledger and returns 0 for an address that holds only BNB. No CAS20 file reads or writes a native balance or calls a contract, and every entry point reverts when value is attached. The millisecond timestamp precompile 0x70 ignores its input and returns one 32 byte word that is constant within a block. After the fork the singleton addresses, 0x2007 and uncreated token addresses of variant 0 and 1 revert on every shape, so take and sync both revert. 0x70 answers balanceOf and transfer with the millisecond timestamp: sync succeeds, settle credits zero because the word is constant within a block (src/PoolManager.sol:358-360), and take reverts because the word is not 1. As a hook address 0x70 has the flags afterSwap, beforeDonate and afterDonate, and its answer fails the selector test at src/libraries/Hooks.sol:152-154 before and after the fork. The fork therefore changes no balance and no claim of the deployed PoolManager. On success it writes exactly two balance slots, the source and the named recipient. There is no escrow, no pending credit and no recovery account. Chapel confirmed the revert for a token with a sender policy and the exact credit for 12 tokens. No CAS20 code touches a BNB balance. Evidence: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/bnb-chain/bsc/master/core/vm/cas20_token.go lines 239 to 269; rpc https://bsc-testnet-dataseed.bnbchain.org (Chapel, chain id 97, Geth v1.8.1, Jenner active since 2026-10-29), eth_call with state override, blocks 144360009 to 144364040 on 2026-11-23
- Polygon, cycle 5. Faces on Polygon: walk of sync, settle, take, mint, burn and protocol fee collection across the two EURe addresses and across address(0) and 0x1010, in every order, for an ordinary caller. Result: No order credits one payment twice or pays out more than was credited. sync holds one currency and one reserve figure at a time (src/libraries/CurrencyReserves.sol:27-32). settle credits only the rise of the synced currency's balance since that sync (src/PoolManager.sol:358-360), and a native settle is refused while a token is synced (src/PoolManager.sol:356). take debits the id it names before it transfers (src/PoolManager.sol:294-295). A take or a fee collection of the other face between sync and settle lowers the measured rise and costs the settling caller. mint and burn act on separate claim ids (src/PoolManager.sol:322-336). A standing surplus cannot be claimed, because sync always starts from the current balance. The hazards that remain are the issuer hazard recorded for EURe and the dead credit recorded for 0x1010. Evidence: src/PoolManager.sol:279-365; rpc https://polygon-bor-rpc.publicnode.com (bor v2.11.1), eth_call with state override, 2026-11-23, blocks 97808115 to 97808450
- Polygon, cycle 5. Can an ordinary account move the PoolManager's EURe through the forwarding functions of the two EURe addresses?. Result: No. transfer_withCaller, transferFrom_withCaller and approve_withCaller revert at the V2 address when an ordinary account calls them. At the V1 address the same calls fall into a fallback that returns success with no data and changes no balance and no allowance. transferFrom reverts at both addresses for a spender without allowance, and the PoolManager never grants an allowance. setController reverts at both addresses for an ordinary caller. Evidence: rpc https://polygon-bor-rpc.publicnode.com (bor v2.11.1), eth_call with state override, 2026-11-23, block 97808450
- Polygon, Avalanche, cycle 5. Is any other balance of the PoolManager reachable under two currency ids? Full list of pooled currencies from all Initialize logs (7,456 on Polygon, 2,242 on Avalanche), balanceOf(PoolManager) for each, grouping by identical non-zero balance, a simulated transfer of one base unit for every member of every group, and a bit partition group test that moves half of the balance of 170 most pooled tokens per chain and reads all 170 balances. Result: Polygon: the EURe pair is the only shared balance, and 0x1010 is the only currency that equals the native balance. Avalanche: none. Two addresses that share a ledger one to one show equal balances for every holder, so the grouping covers all such pairs among currencies with a non-zero PoolManager balance. Faces in different units are covered only for the 170 most pooled tokens per chain, because the endpoints cap return data at 100,000 bytes. Evidence: rpc https://polygon.gateway.tenderly.co eth_getLogs; https://api.routescan.io/v2/network/mainnet/evm/43114/etherscan/api; rpc https://polygon-bor-rpc.publicnode.com (bor v2.11.1), eth_call with state override, 2026-11-23, blocks 97808010 to 97808355; rpc https://avalanche-c-chain-rpc.publicnode.com (avalanchego 1.15.3), eth_call with state override, 2026-11-23, blocks 101142789 to 101143228
- BNB Smart Chain, cycle 5. Faces on BNB Smart Chain: sample of 1,364 currencies from the 2,985 pools initialized in blocks 134,978,682 to 135,228,681, with the same balance grouping, one unit transfers for 172 members of 41 groups, and the group test on the 170 most pooled tokens. Result: No shared balance and no address that reports the native BNB balance. One token balance rose when another token was moved, which is a reward style inflow and is recorded as a lead. The sample covers about 31 hours of pool creation. Older pools were not listed, because public endpoints do not serve older logs. Evidence: rpc https://bsc-rpc.publicnode.com eth_getLogs and eth_call with Multicall3 code at the PoolManager address, blocks 135228681 to 135229095 on 2026-11-23
- Avalanche, cycle 5. Lead L-159: do the PositionManager, Permit2, the Universal Routers or any hook on Avalanche hold two constant storage slots that differ only in bit 248?. Result: No. All PUSH32 constants were extracted from the runtime code of 11 periphery contracts (652 constants) and of 282 hooks with code plus one ERC-1967 implementation (4,766 constants), the hooks being every hook address named in the 5,779 Initialize logs. No contract holds two constants that are equal after the lowest bit of the first byte is cleared. Slots that a contract computes at run time by arithmetic on a constant are not covered by this test. Evidence: https://api.routescan.io/v2/network/mainnet/evm/43114/etherscan/api (Initialize logs); rpc https://avalanche-c-chain-rpc.publicnode.com (avalanchego 1.15.3), eth_call with state override, 2026-11-23, eth_getCode and eth_getStorageAt at the latest block
- Polygon, cycle 5. Upcoming fork on Polygon: does the dormant Hampi fork or any scheduled Bor fork change what the PoolManager bytecode computes?. Result: No. Hampi has no activation block and its single gate changes only whether SSTORE reads committed state before an out of gas exit. Gas charged, results and state roots stay the same according to the pull request and its tests. Bor master and develop define no fork after Uburu. A fork distributed privately, as Uburu was, could not be reviewed in advance. Evidence: https://github.com/0xPolygon/bor/pull/2361; https://raw.githubusercontent.com/0xPolygon/bor/develop/params/config.go
- Avalanche, cycle 5. Upcoming fork on Avalanche: does Igloo or ACP-209 change what an ordinary account can make the PoolManager do in the next six months?. Result: Nothing is scheduled. IglooTime is unscheduled on Mainnet and Fuji, and its public scope is the move of L1 chains to the Continuous Execution engine. ACP-209 is Proposed without an implementation. If it ships as written, delegated accounts become possible as hooks (the case of finding F-004), and any account could deposit AVAX into the reserved balance of the PoolManager, which contract code cannot see or spend. Neither changes settle, which credits msg.value (src/PoolManager.sol:352-354). Evidence: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ava-labs/avalanchego/master/upgrade/upgrade.go; https://github.com/avalanche-foundation/ACPs/blob/main/ACPs/209-eip7702-style-account-abstraction/README.md
- BNB Smart Chain, cycle 5. Upcoming fork: does the BEP-703 payment lane move balances, pay fees in tokens or change how PoolManager transactions are priced?. Result: No. The lane is one inequality on gas totals per block. It reserves 5 percent of the block gas limit by default, at most 10 percent, for bare BNB transfers to accounts without code and for transactions to contracts that governance lists. A PoolManager transaction is a general transaction and competes for the remaining 90 to 95 percent of an 80,000,000 gas block. The transaction cap of 16,777,216 gas is unchanged, and the largest Quoter simulation of this cycle used 11,518,424 gas. Evidence: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/bnb-chain/BEPs/master/BEPs/BEP-703.md; https://raw.githubusercontent.com/bnb-chain/bsc/master/core/paymentlane/paymentlane.go
- BNB Smart Chain, cycle 5. Can a CAS20 balanceOf call that runs short of gas return zero, so that sync records a false zero reserve and settle credits the whole balance?. Result: No. A storage read that cannot be paid returns a zero word inside the native code and sets a sticky out of gas flag. finishCAS20Metered checks that flag before it returns data and ends the call with ErrOutOfGas, which the EVM reports as a failed call. The high level balanceOf call at src/types/Currency.sol:94 then reverts. Evidence: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/bnb-chain/bsc/master/core/vm/cas20_storage.go lines 124 to 146 and cas20_errors.go lines 55 to 63
- Polygon, cycle 5. Pools on Polygon whose currency has no code: can anything be deposited or credited under 0x455e53cbb86018ac2b8092fdcd39d8444affc3f6 (two pools) or 0x000000000000000000000000000000000000dead (one pool)?. Result: No. sync reverts for both addresses on the deployed PoolManager because balanceOf returns no data, so settle can never credit these ids, liquidity cannot be paid for, and no claim can be minted against a positive delta. A take of a non-zero amount would leave a debt that cannot be settled and the unlock reverts (src/PoolManager.sol:112). Evidence: rpc https://polygon-bor-rpc.publicnode.com eth_call sync(address) on 0x67366782805870060151383f4bbff9dab53e5cd6 and eth_getCode, block 97808450
- Polygon, BNB Smart Chain, Avalanche, cycle 8. Exits: can an ordinary account make another user's liquidity removal or claim redemption impossible to include on these networks through gas caps, storage prices or the cost of tick crossings. Result: No. Removal runs Pool.modifyLiquidity, which has no loop and touches two ticks, at most two bitmap words, one position and the pool liquidity (src/libraries/Pool.sol:146-236). Its gas does not grow with the number of initialized ticks or positions. Under the Polygon storage prices of PIP-88 (cold read 5460, cold write surcharge 2940) the dozen cold slots of a removal add an estimated 40,000 gas to the 85,099 to 130,613 gas that the repository snapshots record for a removal (snapshots/PoolManagerTest.json:10-15). The caps are 16,777,216 gas on BNB Smart Chain, 33,554,432 on Polygon and the block limit of 80,000,000 on Avalanche. burn and take have no loop either (src/PoolManager.sol:291-297 and 331-336). The swap loop is the only part of core whose gas an outsider can raise, and that is filed as a finding of this cycle with effect degrade. Evidence: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/0xPolygon/bor/v2.11.1/params/protocol_params.go ; https://raw.githubusercontent.com/bnb-chain/bsc/v1.8.2/params/protocol_params.go ; https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ava-labs/avalanchego/v1.15.3/vms/saevm/worstcase/state.go ; src/libraries/Pool.sol:146-236
- Polygon, BNB Smart Chain, Avalanche, cycle 8. Exits: special recipients. Can an outsider make the native payout of another user's take revert, or does any of the three chains refuse value transfers from the PoolManager to particular recipients. Result: No. The recipient of a take is chosen by the caller, and the native payout forwards all gas (src/types/Currency.sol:48). The earlier sweeps list the addresses that refuse value (system contracts that revert on empty calldata, the Polygon token contract 0x1010, the deprecated C-Chain precompiles), and a user reaches them only by naming them. The BNB Smart Chain client skips the value transfer only when the caller of the frame is the system address (core/vm/evm.go lines 291 to 347 at tag v1.8.2), which the PoolManager never is. The hard coded address filter of BNB Smart Chain applies to the sender and recipient of the top level transaction only, as cycle 1 recorded. Evidence: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/bnb-chain/bsc/v1.8.2/core/vm/evm.go ; src/types/Currency.sol:44-52
- Polygon, cycle 8. Known weakness and by design behaviour: the StateReceiver installed by Uburu lets any account replay a failed state sync. Can an ordinary account use the replay paths to make 0x1001 or FxChild call the PoolManager or its owner contract with data of its choice. Result: No. A replay must match the stored hash of receiver and data, or a leaf under the historic Merkle root, so the caller chooses only the time (StateReceiver.sol lines 85 to 133). The call is onStateReceive(uint256,bytes), which the PoolManager does not implement: an eth_call from 0x1001 to the PoolManager with that selector reverts with empty data. FxChild forwards to processMessageFromRoot on a receiver named in the record, and the PoolManager owner 0x8a1b966ac46f42275860f905dbc75efbfdc12374 reverts unless the caller is FxChild and the sender is the Ethereum timelock 0x1a9c8182c09f50c8318d769245bea52c32be35bc. Any Ethereum account can send a record through FxRoot, and FxRoot writes that account as the sender. Of the 25 failed records pending since Uburu, 23 are for FxChild, and none has the timelock as sender or the owner contract as receiver. The 67 historic leaves that have not been replayed were not enumerated and are a lead. Evidence: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/0xPolygon/genesis-contracts/master/contracts/StateReceiver.sol ; rpc https://polygon-bor-rpc.publicnode.com eth_call, rpc https://mainnet.gateway.tenderly.co eth_getLogs, 2026-11-23; research/network-risk/cycles/008/established-l1.work/raw/polygon_statesync_since_uburu.json ; research/network-risk/cycles/008/established-l1.work/raw/polygon_owner_proxy_auth.json
- Polygon, cycle 8. Known weaknesses of Bor disclosed in 2026 that earlier cycles did not judge: the four issues of v2.5.9 (handshake panic, header panic, state sync pagination, truncated block number checks) and the BlockSTM items of v2.10.3. Result: None gives an ordinary account a lever on PoolManager funds. The two panics and the two BlockSTM items stop or slow nodes. The pagination gap made nodes reject each other's blocks. The block number issue let an authorised producer present a block number far above the parent's, which matters to contracts that read block.number. The PoolManager bytecode has no NUMBER, TIMESTAMP or BLOCKHASH opcode (assumption A10) and its accounting closes inside one transaction (src/PoolManager.sol:104-114). The v2.10.3 post states that execution results are unchanged by its fixes, and the serial and parallel processors must agree on every block. Evidence: https://forum.polygon.technology/t/bor-security-bug-fix-v2-5-9-review-post/21765 ; https://forum.polygon.technology/t/bor-security-bug-fix-review-v2-10-3/22379
- Polygon, cycle 8. Known weakness: the 2021 fault in transferWithSig of the native token contract 0x1010, which moved POL without a balance check. Is the function live, and could it move the PoolManager's native balance. Result: The function is disabled. A call reverts with the string Disabled feature. A signature transfer debits the recovered signer, and no signature recovers to a contract address, so the PoolManager balance could not be the source even if the function were live. The mirror of the native balance at 0x1010 stays as finding F-008 describes. Evidence: rpc https://polygon-bor-rpc.publicnode.com eth_call to 0x0000000000000000000000000000000000001010 with selector 0x19d27d9c, 2026-11-23; research/network-risk/cycles/008/established-l1.work/raw/special_probe.json
- BNB Smart Chain, cycle 8. Known weakness: the superinstruction interpreter of BNB Smart Chain v1.7.x let SSTORE run inside a STATICCALL frame (pull request 3582). Does any accounting step of the PoolManager rely on the write protection of STATICCALL. Result: No. The PoolManager makes one kind of static call, balanceOf on a currency, in sync and in _settle (src/types/Currency.sol:94, src/PoolManager.sol:285 and 359). A token that could write or re-enter during that call would gain nothing over calling the PoolManager before or after it: sync stores the currency and the returned balance after the call (src/PoolManager.sol:285-286), and _settle reads the stored reserves before the call, credits only the currency it read at line 350 and then clears the slot (lines 358-364). In both places the returned number is already chosen by the token. A token that is not written by the attacker does not re-enter. The pull request describes the outcome as wrong gas use and a bad block on nodes that ran the optimized interpreter, which was an opt-in flag. The changelog records that v1.8.0-alpha removed the interpreter, and v1.8.2 is mandatory before 2026-12-08. Evidence: https://github.com/bnb-chain/bsc/pull/3582 ; https://raw.githubusercontent.com/bnb-chain/bsc/master/CHANGELOG.md ; src/PoolManager.sol:279-288 and 349-365
- BNB Smart Chain, cycle 8. The fork boundary of Jenner on 2026-12-08. Until then a transfer call to 0x70 or to a CAS20 address succeeds with empty data. Can an account create a debt, a credit, a claim or pool liquidity in such a currency before the fork that becomes a claim on real tokens after it. Result: No. Before the fork take of such a currency succeeds and only debits the caller (src/PoolManager.sol:294-295, src/types/Currency.sol:64-74). A positive delta in it can come only from settle, which needs sync, and sync reverts because balanceOf returns no data (src/types/Currency.sol:94). mint adds a debt of the same size as the claim (src/PoolManager.sol:322-329). Pool operations move deltas between the caller, the hook and the pool and add to zero, so no unlock can close while any party owes the currency (src/PoolManager.sol:112). Nothing denominated in the currency can therefore exist in storage when the fork arrives, except pools with zero liquidity. After the fork an uncreated CAS20 address reverts on every call, as cycle 5 saw on Chapel, and a created token is an issuer matter (F-007, F-076). Evidence: rpc https://bsc-dataseed1.bnbchain.org eth_getCode and eth_call at block 135,334,992; research/network-risk/cycles/008/established-l1.work/raw/special_probe.json ; https://www.bnbchain.org/en/blog/jenner-hardfork-changes-upgrade-guide
- BNB Smart Chain, cycle 8. Lead L-331: do PIT, ASS, CATE and GFH charge the PoolManager more than the amount when it transfers them. Result: No. Eight simulated transfers per token set (one thousandth and one third of the balance, to a fresh address and to 0xdead) at block 135,335,118 all returned a 32 byte true. For ASS, PIT and CATE the PoolManager balance fell by slightly less than the amount, because the fee is taken from what the recipient receives and part of it is reflected to holders, the PoolManager among them. For GFH it fell by exactly the amount. take debits the caller the requested amount (src/PoolManager.sol:294), so a payout leaves the PoolManager whole or a few thousand base units ahead. Evidence: rpc https://bsc-dataseed1.bnbchain.org (Geth v1.8.2) eth_call with Multicall3 code at the PoolManager address, 2026-11-23; research/network-risk/cycles/008/established-l1.work/raw/l331_fee_tokens.json
- BNB Smart Chain, cycle 8. Lead L-160, reflection tokens: can a caller profit by putting its own transfer of a reflection token between sync and settle, so that the reflected fee on the PoolManager balance is credited to it. Result: No. settle credits the rise of the PoolManager balance since sync (src/PoolManager.sol:358-360). A transfer of one third of the PoolManager's PIT balance (168,336,790 PIT) paid a fee of about 6,733,000 PIT and raised the PoolManager balance by 0.0113 PIT. For ASS the same test paid about 1,604,000 ASS and raised it by 0.0026 ASS. The caller pays the whole fee and can be credited only the PoolManager's share of it, which is about two parts in a billion. Reflection that accrued before the sync is already inside the stored reserves and is credited to nobody. Evidence: rpc https://bsc-dataseed1.bnbchain.org (Geth v1.8.2) eth_call with Multicall3 code at the PoolManager address, 2026-11-23; research/network-risk/cycles/008/established-l1.work/raw/l331_fee_tokens.json

Result: No. Every one of the 7,428 logs of the plugin 0xf58fed40fba1ab7aa7ffc160b863bedd998386a7 on Polygon names VCNT in an indexed topic, so the contract serves that one token. The plugin address and the VCNT address hold no code on BNB Smart Chain and Avalanche. Another issuer of the same framework would deploy its own plugin, which this check cannot see. - Avalanche, cycle 8. Open question of the cycle 6 and cycle 7 critics: does the C-Chain accept set code transactions, so that an account can carry a delegation and act as a hook or as a caller with code. Result: No. The code that decides block validity under Continuous Execution validates each transaction with an accept mask of legacy, access list and dynamic fee types (worstcase/state.go lines 181 to 193) and rejects a sender that holds code (lines 202 to 209). The CLZ opcode of Osaka is undefined on the public endpoint, which matches a rule set without the later Ethereum forks. Code at a hook address on the C-Chain can therefore change only through a contract's own upgrade path, as on Ethereum before EIP-7702 (assumption A7, src/libraries/Hooks.sol:337-339). Evidence: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ava-labs/avalanchego/v1.15.3/vms/saevm/worstcase/state.go ; rpc https://api.avax.network/ext/bc/C/rpc eth_call with data 0x60011e5f5260205ff3, 2026-11-23
- Avalanche, cycle 8. By design behaviour of Continuous Execution: consensus accepts a block before it is executed, includes a transaction when the sender can pay its worst case cost, and treats an execution error as fatal. Does any of this break the atomic settlement that unlock relies on, or let state reach the PoolManager outside a transaction. Result: No. Execution still applies transactions one by one with core.ApplyTransaction, in block order, each on the state left by the one before (saexec/execution.go lines 346 to 364), and cycle 2 showed that each call resets transient storage. A transaction that reverts is still included and charged, and all PoolManager state it wrote is rolled back with it. The fatal branch concerns a transaction that is invalid at execution time, which the worst case check exists to exclude. It would stop the chain for everyone and gives no account PoolManager funds. Whether an ordinary account can reach that branch is filed as a low lead. Evidence: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ava-labs/avalanchego/v1.15.3/vms/saevm/saexec/execution.go ; https://docs.avax.network/docs/nodes/architecture/execution/continuous-execution
- Avalanche, cycle 8. Can a cross-chain import write into the storage of the PoolManager account. The C-Chain keeps balances of other X-Chain assets inside the storage trie of the holder. Result: No. At tip an import whose inputs or outputs carry an asset other than AVAX is rejected (cchain/tx/import.go lines 112 to 129). Asset balances live under slot indexes with the lowest bit of the first byte set, and contract code can only reach slot indexes with that bit cleared (cchain/libevm/extstate/statedb.go lines 45 to 62 and 124 to 171). An AVAX import raises the native balance, which cycle 2 cleared. Evidence: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ava-labs/avalanchego/v1.15.3/vms/saevm/cchain/tx/import.go ; https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ava-labs/avalanchego/v1.15.3/vms/saevm/cchain/libevm/extstate/statedb.go
- BNB Smart Chain, cycle 8. Known weaknesses of the BNB Smart Chain clients in the Jenner release line that earlier cycles did not judge: the reth-bsc state root fault fixed in v0.1.4-hotfix, the per byte pricing of precompile 0x68, and the BEP-706 sample code that accepts an empty answer from 0x70. Result: None reaches PoolManager funds through an ordinary account. The state root fault decides which blocks a reth-bsc node accepts. The pricing change concerns a precompile that the PoolManager never calls and that reverts on its call shapes, as the earlier sweeps showed. The empty answer of 0x70 before activation affects contracts that read the timestamp from it. The PoolManager reaches 0x70 only when a caller names it as currency or hook: sync reverts on the empty answer before the fork and stores a timestamp that is constant inside a block after it, so settle credits zero (src/PoolManager.sol:358-360). Evidence: https://github.com/bnb-chain/reth-bsc/releases ; https://raw.githubusercontent.com/bnb-chain/bsc/master/CHANGELOG.md ; https://thedefiant.io/news/blockchains/bnb-chain-sets-jenner-date-post-flags-timestamp-risk

Result: saexec calls core.ApplyTransaction once per transaction (vms/saevm/saexec/execution.go lines 346 to 364), and libevm's state transition calls StateDB.Prepare, which installs a new transient storage map (core/state_transition.go line 436, core/state/statedb.go line 1335). No delta, lock flag or synced currency can survive into the next transaction. - Polygon, cycle 9. Whether the optional switch dispatch interpreter of Bor v2.11.x, which a validator can enable with evm-switch-dispatch, computes a different result for any opcode the PoolManager uses. Result: No. The file was read in full. Every inlined opcode takes its operands in the jump table order and calls the same uint256 method, the stack checks are the same, JUMP and JUMPI check the jump destination before moving the program counter, and JUMPI tests the whole condition word. SAR with a shift of exactly 256 reaches SRsh, which returns zero for a non-negative value and all ones for a negative value, as specified. Constant gas of the inlined opcodes is charged before the next opcode that can have an effect, so the GAS opcode and every call see the same remaining gas. The setting is off by default. Evidence: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/0xPolygon/bor/v2.11.2/core/vm/interpreter_dispatch.go and https://raw.githubusercontent.com/0xPolygon/bor/v2.11.2/internal/cli/server/config.go
- Polygon, cycle 9. Whether Bor v2.11.2, released 2026-11-19 and served by OnFinality, changes execution relative to v2.11.1. Result: No. core/vm, the state code, the chain config, the protocol parameters and the parallel state processor are byte identical at the two tags. The release changes peering, fork ID handling and a sequence store producer path, and moves to Go 1.26.11. Evidence: https://github.com/0xPolygon/bor/releases/tag/v2.11.2 and https://raw.githubusercontent.com/0xPolygon/bor/v2.11.2/core/vm/instructions.go
- Polygon, cycle 9. Lead L-580: rerun the battery against a bor endpoint and check whether any public Polygon RPC still runs Erigon. Result: Both bor endpoints (publicnode and QuickNode, v2.11.1-private) passed the 185,529 vectors and the 550 scripts with the same results as the drpc run of OPCODES.md. Polygon Labs ended Erigon support on 1 August 2026, and none of the 14 endpoints probed reported Erigon. - BNB Smart Chain, cycle 9. Whether reth-bsc, which serves https://bsc-rpc.publicnode.com, replaces any instruction. Result: No. It uses the stock revm-interpreter 35.0.1 instruction table for the configured spec (src/evm/api/mod.rs line 90). The battery, the targeted set and both pmdiff sets gave the specified results there. Evidence: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/bnb-chain/reth-bsc/v0.1.4-hotfix/src/evm/api/mod.rs
- BNB Smart Chain, cycle 9. Transient storage and system transaction detection in reth-bsc. Result: commit_tx and discard_tx of revm-context 16.0.1 clear the transient map at the end of every transaction, and a transaction is a system transaction only when its caller is the block beneficiary with a zero gas price and a system contract as target. An ordinary account cannot be the beneficiary. Evidence: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/bnb-chain/reth-bsc/v0.1.4-hotfix/src/evm/handler.rs and https://static.crates.io/crates/revm-context/revm-context-16.0.1.crate
- BNB Smart Chain, cycle 9. The BNB Smart Chain rule that code cannot run at the block coinbase address (geth v1.8.2 core/vm/interpreter.go lines 96 to 98, reth-bsc src/evm/api/mod.rs lines 235 to 270): can an ordinary account use it against the PoolManager. Result: No. The coinbase is the signing address of the validator that produced the block, so only a validator can choose it, and it has code only if the validator delegated its own key through EIP-7702. A hook or token at that address would fail in that validator's blocks, which hurts only pools that chose such a contract. A native take to an address without code is not affected, because the rule applies only when code runs. Recorded with actor operator. Evidence: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/bnb-chain/bsc/v1.8.2/core/vm/interpreter.go
- BNB Smart Chain, cycle 9. Whether an ordinary account can place a contract at an address that becomes a CAS20 precompile at Jenner, so that the code of a hook or currency changes after pools are created (A7). Result: Not feasible. The prefix rule fixes 0xca52 and eight zero bytes and limits byte 10 to two values, about 81 fixed bits, so a CREATE2 search for such an address needs about 2^80 hashes. Before Jenner these addresses hold no code, so sync and settle of such a currency revert in balanceOf and no account can be credited in it. Evidence: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/bnb-chain/reth-bsc/v0.1.4-hotfix/src/evm/precompiles/cas20/mod.rs and rpc https://bsc-dataseed1.bnbchain.org eth_getCode, 2026-11-24
- Avalanche, cycle 9. What the PoolManager does when an ordinary caller names an Avalanche precompile address after Helicon (P1 and P2). Result: The three native asset addresses run DeprecatedContract and revert, warp rejects a call without a valid selector, and P256 at 0x100 returns empty data and moves nothing. A take to the native asset addresses therefore reverts, and a take naming 0x100 as currency succeeds with empty data and debits the caller the full amount, as for any address without code. No call moves value that the caller does not owe. Evidence: https://proxy.golang.org/github.com/ava-labs/avalanchego/graft/coreth/@v/v1.15.3.zip and rpc https://api.avax.network/ext/bc/C/rpc eth_call from the PoolManager address, 2026-11-24

- Polygon, cycle 12. Does the MULMOD memo of bor v2.12.0-beta give the stock result for every input, including FullMath's modulus 2^256-1, destination equal to modulus, and state carried between calls, frames and transactions of one EVM. Result: Yes as read. The memo compares all four limbs of the modulus before reuse and recomputes Reciprocal(z) on a miss (core/vm/mulmod_memo.go lines 55-66). MulModWithReciprocal and MulMod in uint256 v1.3.2 run the same umul and the same reduce4 call (uint256.go lines 688-748), reduce4 only reads the reciprocal (mod.go lines 334-381), and opMulmod aliases destination and modulus in the same way in both versions (instructions.go line 202 at v2.11.1 and v2.12.0-beta). Moduli with a zero top limb and a zero modulus take the stock call. Each parallel incarnation constructs its own EVM (core/parallel_state_processor.go lines 132 and 628), so the unsynchronised memo is not shared between goroutines. The ruint 1.21.0 fault class (OPCODES.md) does not apply: bor uses holiman/uint256. Evidence: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/0xPolygon/bor/v2.12.0-beta/core/vm/mulmod_memo.go and https://raw.githubusercontent.com/holiman/uint256/v1.3.2/uint256.go
- Polygon, cycle 12. Can the widened keccak result cache of bor v2.12.0-beta (--precompile-cache) return a hash for another input, for example across lengths or after EVM memory changes. Result: No as read. Keys are string(data) over the whole input, so inputs of different length or content never share an entry; Load builds a non-retained string view, Store copies the input and stores the hash by value with LoadOrStore, and a full cache stops inserting rather than evicting (core/vm/shared_cache.go lines 162-241). The 64 byte legacy path is unchanged from v2.11.1, which cycle 11 cleared. Evidence: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/0xPolygon/bor/v2.12.0-beta/core/vm/shared_cache.go
- Polygon, cycle 12. Can the ecrecover result cache of bor v2.11.1 be poisoned through an eth_call or eth_simulateV1 that overrides the precompile at 0x01, a hole that v2.12.0-beta closes with precompilesOverridden. Result: Not on the import path of v2.11.1: the shared ecrecover, keccak and jump destination caches are created per block in newSharedBlockCaches and applied only to the import prefetcher and the parallel workers (core/blockchain.go lines 1268-1289); the RPC path creates no shared cache. The PoolManager makes no ecrecover call in any case. Evidence: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/0xPolygon/bor/v2.11.1/core/blockchain.go
- BNB Smart Chain, cycle 12. Lead L-646 for BSC geth v1.8.2: is any code-derived cache shared across transactions or workers and keyed by a code hash read apart from the code. Result: BSC adds a process-wide LRU of jump destination bitmaps keyed by code hash (core/vm/contract.go lines 27-30, used in isCode lines 99-112), which every EVM of the process shares, including the prefetch workers. Each EVM runs on one StateDB copy in one goroutine (core/state_prefetcher.go lines 71-121), and Call takes the code and its hash from that StateDB with no execution in between (evm.go lines 355-363 and resolveCode / resolveCodeHash at lines 700-724). The account's code hash is the hash of the stored code, so every bitmap is stored under the hash of the bytes it was computed from. Init code is analysed under the zero hash and never stored (evm.go line 631). Pooled Contract objects clear the cached analysis on reuse (contract_pool.go line 36). Evidence: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/bnb-chain/bsc/v1.8.2/core/vm/contract.go
- BNB Smart Chain, cycle 12. Lead L-646 for reth-bsc v0.1.4-hotfix: where is the jump table of a contract computed and can it belong to other bytes. Result: revm-bytecode 10.0.0 computes the jump table inside Bytecode::new_legacy from the raw bytes and stores it in the same Bytecode value (bytecode/mod.rs lines 128-134, legacy/analysis.rs lines 10-36). There is no separate code hash key for the analysis, so a jump table always belongs to the bytes it travels with. Evidence: https://static.crates.io/crates/revm-bytecode/revm-bytecode-10.0.0.crate
- Avalanche, cycle 12. Lead L-646 for avalanchego 1.15.3 (libevm d398bc4dbe41). Result: The jump destination map is created fresh for a top-level call and passed to child frames only (core/vm/contract.go lines 64-72), so it lives for one transaction's call tree on one StateDB and is never shared between transactions or goroutines. Evidence: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ava-labs/libevm/d398bc4dbe41/core/vm/contract.go

The cycle 11 critic's concern for bor v2.11.1: under BlockSTM, can resolveCode and resolveCodeHash of one Call read two versions of a delegating account's code, so that a bitmap is stored in the block-shared jump destination cache under another contract's code hash. Result: Not as read. ParallelStateDB.readCodeKey stores the first MVHashMap read of each address's code for the rest of the transaction (core/state/parallel_statedb.go lines 365-377), and the field comment names this exact case (lines 170-177). For code written earlier in the block, GetCodeHash hashes the bytes returned by that same cached read (lines 899-907, cachedCodeHash lines 871-887); for pre-block code both reads come from the same base state. The per-transaction hash memo is dropped on SetCode (line 949) and on revert of a create (parallel_statedb_journal.go lines 93-104). The deeper questions of the code theme (prefetcher views, entries written by incarnations that later fail validation) are left to that unit; given the pinning, an entry is computed from the bytes it is keyed by whichever incarnation wrote it. - Polygon, cycle 15. Lead L-750: the cache that --precompile-cache adds in bor v2.12.0-beta. What is its key, and can a STATICCALL from sync(X) get a cached result for a different input or a different precompile?. Result: The flag adds the extended keccak store, keyed by string(data) (shared_cache.go lines 160-245), and gives the builder and the serial importer the ecrecover cache. The ecrecover cache serves only address 0x01 with input of at most 128 bytes. Its key is the input right-padded to 128 bytes, which is the padding ecrecover applies anyway. It is skipped when the precompile set is overridden. Gas is charged from RequiredGas on a hit, and the stored and returned slices are clones (evm.go lines 53-116). No other precompile is cached. A sync(0x01) gets the same bytes as an uncached call, and balanceOfSelf (src/types/Currency.sol:90-95) parses them the same way. Result: No. The targets hold no ERC-6909 claims in the six largest currency ids and no PositionManager NFT. A pool that names one of them as hook or currency already fails on every flagged call while the address has no code, and afterwards it reverts. The same holds for a native take to such an address, which only fails the caller's own action (src/types/Currency.sol:44-52). The sweeper moves only the native balance of its own address. Evidence: https://heimdall-api.polygon.technology/clerk/event-records/3212586 and rpc: eth_call failedStateSyncHashes(3212586) on https://rpc-mainnet.matic.quiknode.pro, file research/network-risk/cycles/021/established-l1.work/l791.log
- Avalanche, cycle 21. L-947: which earlier Avalanche results seeded PoolManager or token storage with a full state override instead of stateDiff?. Result: None found. No Python, JavaScript or shell script in tools/ or in any cycle work directory has a state key in an override. pmdiff.py and pmdiff2.py inject code only (pmdiff.py:181), and pmdiff3.py:104 and pmdiff6.py:145 use stateDiff, which libevm applies with the bit 248 transform. The reruns of sets 1 and 2 on Avalanche in this cycle use the same overrides and match Ethereum. - BNB Smart Chain, cycle 21. Forks in the next six months on BNB Chain: Jenner and anything after it. Result: Jenner (2026-12-08 02:30 UTC) is the only scheduled fork. Its EVM effects (CAS20 precompiles, 0x70 millisecond time, 0x68 repricing) were covered by F-007, F-076, F-139 and the cycle 19 Jenner-rule reruns; the payment lane only limits general gas per block. AmsterdamTime is nil. Evidence: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/bnb-chain/bsc/master/params/config.go and https://docs.chainstack.com/docs/bnb-jenner-hardfork
- Avalanche, cycle 21. Forks in the next six months on Avalanche. Result: Igloo has no activation time on Mainnet or Fuji, so nothing changes for the PoolManager until a release schedules it. Evidence: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ava-labs/avalanchego/master/upgrade/upgrade.go

## Ethereum mainnet reference and cross-chain deployment parity

- Ethereum, cycle 1. Whether ERC-4337 bundles or EIP-7702 batches, which run several users' operations in one transaction, can leak an unlock flag, a delta or a stale sync from one operation into another and move funds. Result: unlock clears the flag before returning and reverts unless every delta is zero, so the flag and the deltas never outlive the unlock that created them. Only the synced currency and reserves can survive. A later operation's own sync overwrites them and any ERC-20 settle resets the currency, and a credit is only ever the balance increase since the most recent sync, so a stale sync cannot capture another user's payment. The remaining effects are reverts, recorded in the info finding. Evidence: src/PoolManager.sol:104-114, 279-288, 349-364; https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ethereum/ERCs/master/ERCS/erc-4337.md
- Ethereum, cycle 1. Whether the native asset has a second, ERC-20 face on mainnet, and whether an attacker-deployed token that mirrors ETH or another token's balance can be credited for funds it did not pay. Result: ETH has no enshrined ERC-20 form; the PoolManager's ETH balance (54,377.2) and WETH balance (576.35) are independent. A mirror token only earns a delta in its own currency id, because _settle credits the synced currency. msg.value is rejected while an ERC-20 is synced, so an ETH payment cannot be read as a balance increase of a mirror token. Evidence: src/PoolManager.sol:349-364; on-chain query via https://ethereum-rpc.publicnode.com at block 26470360 (2026-11-22)
- Ethereum, cycle 1. Whether ETH forced into the PoolManager by SELFDESTRUCT, a beacon withdrawal or a fee recipient setting can be claimed or can break accounting. Result: Native credit is msg.value only and the contract balance is never read for native settlement. Forced ETH becomes an unclaimable surplus. No receive or fallback function appears in the contracts read under src; settle and settleFor are the only payable functions. Evidence: src/PoolManager.sol:279-283, 353-354; https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ethereum/EIPs/master/EIPS/eip-4895.md; https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ethereum/EIPs/master/EIPS/eip-6780.md
- Ethereum, cycle 1. Whether a token reachable at two addresses, such as USDT after deprecate() forwards the old address to a new contract, lets one payment be credited twice or lets one currency id drain the other's backing. Result: There is one sync slot. Each credit equals a real balance increase observed between one sync and the next settle with no other sync in between, and each take or fee collection sends at most the amount it debits. Summed over both currency ids, credits minus debits equals the real balance change, so the shared balance always covers both sets of claims. Collection of the alias while the other address is synced can only lower the settler's credit or revert. Evidence: src/PoolManager.sol:279-297, 349-364; src/libraries/CurrencyReserves.sol:21-32; https://sourcify.dev/server/v2/contract/1/0xdAC17F958D2ee523a2206206994597C13D831ec7?fields=sources,compilation
- Ethereum, cycle 1. Whether the USDT transfer fee switch, if turned on, makes the PoolManager pay out more than it debits or credit more than it receives. Result: take debits the full amount and USDT removes exactly that amount from the sender, with the fee taken from what the recipient gets. settle credits the measured balance increase. The PoolManager stays whole; payers must send more to cover the fee. Evidence: src/PoolManager.sol:291-297, 358-360; https://sourcify.dev/server/v2/contract/1/0xdAC17F958D2ee523a2206206994597C13D831ec7?fields=sources,compilation (lines 122 to 135, 425 to 434)
- Ethereum, cycle 1. Whether the 16,777,216 gas cap per transaction (EIP-7825) or the 60,000,000 block gas limit can make liquidity removal or a necessary swap impossible to include. Result: modifyLiquidity touches two ticks, one position and the bitmap, so its cost is constant. Pool.swap stops at sqrtPriceLimitX96, so any swap can be split across transactions. By my estimate from EIP-2929 costs and the repository gas snapshots, one transaction still crosses several hundred initialized ticks or about 3,000 empty bitmap words. Crossing the full empty range of a pool with tick spacing 1 (6,932 words) no longer fits in one transaction but can be done in steps by anyone. I did not measure these numbers on chain. Evidence: src/libraries/Pool.sol:146-238, 344-437; snapshots/TickBitmapTest.json; https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ethereum/EIPs/master/EIPS/eip-7825.md
- Ethereum, cycle 1. Whether a precompile or system contract address used as a pool currency can produce a settle credit or a silent transfer. Result: I sent the balanceOf and transfer calldata that the PoolManager would send, from the PoolManager address, to all 18 precompiles and the five system contracts with eth_call at block 26470418. SHA256, RIPEMD160 and identity return the same constant for balanceOf on every call, so paid is zero, and their transfer return value is not 1, so take reverts. ECRECOVER and P256VERIFY return empty data: balanceOf fails decoding and transfer succeeds while moving nothing, which costs only the caller. The other precompiles fail and the system contracts revert on both calls. No delta can be created without paying. Evidence: src/types/Currency.sol:60-75, 90-96; src/PoolManager.sol:358-360; on-chain eth_call via https://ethereum-rpc.publicnode.com at block 26470418
- Ethereum, cycle 1. Whether any mainnet system contract or protocol operation can move ETH or tokens out of the PoolManager or change its code. Result: The five system contracts only record roots, hashes and validator requests, and withdrawals only add ETH. Nothing at protocol level debits an arbitrary account or rewrites contract code. Evidence: on-chain query via https://ethereum-rpc.publicnode.com at block 26470360 (2026-11-22) (eth_config, eth_getCode); https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ethereum/EIPs/master/EIPS/eip-4895.md
- Ethereum, cycle 1. Whether every opcode the cancun build needs exists on mainnet at the expected cost, and whether core depends on block or transaction globals that later forks changed. Result: Mainnet is past Dencun (CLZ from Osaka executes), so PUSH0, MCOPY, TLOAD and TSTORE are available. The Pectra and Fusaka EIP lists contain no repricing of an opcode that core uses. A search of src outside src/test finds no use of tx.origin, block fields, blockhash, selfdestruct, create or delegatecall. Evidence: on-chain query via https://ethereum-rpc.publicnode.com at block 26470360 (2026-11-22) (eth_call running CLZ); https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ethereum/EIPs/master/EIPS/eip-7569.md; https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ethereum/EIPs/master/EIPS/eip-7600.md; https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ethereum/EIPs/master/EIPS/eip-7607.md; src/ (search)
- Ethereum, cycle 1. Whether an EOA that delegates to the PoolManager's code through EIP-7702 can reach the real PoolManager's funds or pass as it. Result: Delegated code runs with the EOA's own storage and balance. initialize, modifyLiquidity, swap and donate revert there because address(this) differs from the immutable original. The other functions act only on the EOA's own state and tokens. The real contract's storage and balances are untouched. Evidence: src/NoDelegateCall.sol:14-26; https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ethereum/EIPs/master/EIPS/eip-7702.md
- Ethereum, cycle 1. Whether a currency or hook contract can lose its code on mainnet, and what take, sync and hook calls do at an address with no code. Result: After EIP-6780 a contract keeps its code unless it self-destructs in its creation transaction, so only EIP-7702 accounts can lose code later. A take of a codeless currency debits the caller and moves nothing, which harms only the caller. balanceOf on a codeless address returns no data and the Solidity decoder is expected to revert, so sync fails and no credit arises; I did not execute this. A codeless hook makes hook calls revert, covered in the EIP-7702 finding. Evidence: src/types/Currency.sol:60-75, 94; src/libraries/Hooks.sol:152-154; https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ethereum/EIPs/master/EIPS/eip-6780.md
- Ethereum, cycle 1. Whether the math and bit libraries are numerically self-consistent as written: TickMath constants and both directions, BitMath lookup tables, FullMath.mulDiv, LiquidityMath.addDelta, SwapMath.getSqrtPriceTarget, BalanceDelta packing, tickSpacingToMaxLiquidityPerTick, and the four transient slot constants. Result: A Python model of the code as written matched exact integer arithmetic on 300,000 random mulDiv cases, all bit positions and 200,000 random words for BitMath, about 70,000 ticks and 60,000 prices for TickMath including both ends of the range, and 100,000 cases each for the helpers. The TickMath multipliers equal 2^128 divided by sqrt(1.0001)^(2^i) to within one unit. The slot constants equal keccak256 of their names minus one. This is a self-consistency check and uses no other copy of the code. Evidence: src/libraries/TickMath.sol:57-237; src/libraries/BitMath.sol:12-48; src/libraries/FullMath.sol:14-116; src/libraries/Lock.sol:8; src/libraries/CurrencyReserves.sol:11-13; src/libraries/NonzeroDeltaCount.sol:9-10
- Ethereum, cycle 1. Whether the permissionless collect and triggerFeeUpdate functions of the mainnet fee controller let an outsider take pool funds or raise fees beyond the cap. Result: collectProtocolFees subtracts from protocolFeesAccrued with checked arithmetic, so it cannot pay more than accrued fees, and accrual only happens in _swap from amounts the swapper owes. The adapter fixes the recipient to the TokenJar. setProtocolFee rejects any direction above 1,000 pips, and the fee value comes from the adapter's override or policy, not from the caller. Pool.swap makes no external call between reading and writing slot0, so a fee update cannot interleave with a swap. Evidence: src/ProtocolFees.sol:35-57, 66-70; src/libraries/ProtocolFeeLibrary.sol:25-32; src/PoolManager.sol:230-253; src/libraries/Pool.sol:283-439; https://sourcify.dev/server/v2/contract/1/0x89a5d5bf00a27d55c02951e49078a5c5771051db?fields=sources,abi,compilation
- Ethereum, cycle 1. Whether free borrowing of every pooled token inside one transaction (A5) gives an attacker something of value on mainnet that existing free flash loans do not. Result: Mainnet has no protocol feature that reads a token balance for gas payment, staking or voting within a transaction; gas is paid in ETH only. take creates a negative delta that must be zero before unlock returns, so the tokens come back in the same transaction. Evidence: src/PoolManager.sol:104-114, 291-297
- Ethereum, cycle 1. Whether msg.value can be counted twice in native settlement through batching inside the PoolManager. Result: The PoolManager has no multicall and performs no delegatecall, so each settle call sees its own msg.value once. settle and settleFor are the only payable functions. Evidence: src/PoolManager.sol:300-307, 349-364
- Ethereum, cycle 1. Whether the Glamsterdam changes scheduled so far alter how the existing bytecode executes: new opcodes, code size, ETH transfer logs and the state gas reservoir. Result: EIP-8024 keeps jump destination analysis unchanged and states that contracts which never execute the new opcode bytes are unaffected. EIP-7954 only raises size limits. EIP-7708 adds a log to value transfers. EIP-8037 forwards the state gas reservoir to child calls in full and leaves the 63/64 rule on ordinary gas; core forwards all gas to hooks and to native recipients and reverts as a whole if a callee burns it. EIP-8038 raises costs only, which is tracked as a lead. Evidence: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ethereum/EIPs/master/EIPS/eip-8024.md; https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ethereum/EIPs/master/EIPS/eip-7954.md; https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ethereum/EIPs/master/EIPS/eip-7708.md; https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ethereum/EIPs/master/EIPS/eip-8037.md; src/libraries/Hooks.sol:134; src/types/Currency.sol:48
- Ethereum, cycle 1. Whether block ordering power, reorgs or finality delay on mainnet can split a settlement or let funds leave before payment is final. Result: Every delta must net to zero before unlock returns, inside one transaction, and a transaction is included or dropped as a whole. Core holds no cross-chain or delayed obligations. I did not fetch a source on finality time or reorg depth; the conclusion rests on the code alone. Evidence: src/PoolManager.sol:104-114
- Ethereum, cycle 2. Sweep of all 18 precompiles with the PoolManager as sender: empty calldata with zero value and with 1 ETH (P1), transfer(address,uint256) with zero and 1e18 (P2), balanceOf(PoolManager) (P3) and all ten IHooks selectors with well-formed arguments (P5). Follow-up on each target that did not revert. Result: No precompile yields a credit or an unpaid outflow. ECRECOVER and P256VERIFY return empty data: take succeeds and moves nothing while the caller is debited, and sync reverts because the Solidity decoder needs 32 bytes, so no credit can arise. SHA256, RIPEMD160 and IDENTITY return 32 bytes or more that depend only on the input, so the value read at sync equals the value read at settle and paid is zero; their answer to transfer is a digest or the echoed calldata, never the word 1, so take reverts. The other precompiles fail on the input lengths the PoolManager can produce. ETH sent to a precompile address with a native take stays there and the caller owes it. The sync results on the existing mainnet deployment (reverts for 0x01, 0x100 and an empty address, succeeds for 0x02, 0x03, 0x04) agree with this reading of the source; I used them as a behavioural reference and did not compare code. Evidence: src/types/Currency.sol:44-52, 60-75, 90-96; src/PoolManager.sol:279-297, 349-364; on-chain eth_call via https://ethereum-rpc.publicnode.com at block 26471525 (2026-11-22)
- Ethereum, cycle 2. Same 15 call shapes against the beacon roots, history storage, deposit, withdrawal request and consolidation request contracts, and whether the PoolManager can be made to file a withdrawal or consolidation request. Result: Three contracts revert on every shape. The two request contracts answer only the empty call without value, with the fee. A request needs a call of exactly 56 or 96 bytes that carries the fee. The PoolManager sends to a caller-chosen address only empty calldata (native take), 36 bytes by STATICCALL (sync), 68 bytes without value (token take) or at least 228 bytes without value (hook calls), so it cannot file a request. A request with the PoolManager as source would in any case only act on a validator whose withdrawal credentials already point at the PoolManager. Evidence: src/types/Currency.sol:48, 73, 94; src/libraries/Hooks.sol:134, 180; https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ethereum/EIPs/master/EIPS/eip-7002.md; on-chain eth_call via https://ethereum-rpc.publicnode.com at block 26471525 (2026-11-22)
- Ethereum, cycle 2. Whether any special address on mainnet can serve as a hook that the PoolManager accepts, so that a hook call has a lasting side effect made with the PoolManager as sender. Result: A hook call is kept only if the return data is at least 32 bytes and starts with the called selector. Of all swept targets only the identity precompile does that, and 0x04 fails the address check because it sets the after-swap returns-delta bit without the after-swap bit. An EIP-7702 delegation to a precompile runs empty code, so it cannot proxy the identity precompile. The valid special addresses (0x10, 0x100, beacon roots, deposit contract, WETH9, system address, the PoolManager itself) return empty data or revert, which makes the PoolManager revert. A pool whose hook is 0x100 or any empty address with bit 8 or 9 set accepts deposits and reverts every removal; that is the hook finding of cycle 1 with actor pool-creator and needs no new entry. Evidence: src/libraries/Hooks.sol:109-127, 131-155, 232-243; https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ethereum/EIPs/master/EIPS/eip-7702.md; on-chain eth_call via https://ethereum-rpc.publicnode.com at block 26471525 (2026-11-22)
- Ethereum, cycle 2. Native payout (P1) to contracts that book incoming ETH to the sender: WETH9, Lido stETH, frxETHMinter, EntryPoint v0.6, v0.7 and v0.8, the OptimismPortal of OP Mainnet and Base, and the TokenJar. The call was made by the PoolManager address with an unrelated transaction origin. Does the caller end up owing less than what left, with or without a sync and settle around the payout?. Result: take debits the caller the full amount of currency address(0) before the transfer. With sync(WETH9) before and settle after, the caller is credited exactly the 1e18 WETH that the PoolManager received for 1 ETH, so the PoolManager converts 1:1 and both legs are booked. For stETH the credit is 1 wei less than the debit. EntryPoint credits its deposit ledger, which sync can read, but EntryPoint has no transfer function, so that credit can only become an ERC-6909 claim nobody can redeem. A portal deposit is sent from the aliased PoolManager address to the PoolManager's own address on the L2, where no one can sign for either. The OP Mainnet L1StandardBridge refuses a contract caller. In every case the value is booked to the PoolManager and the caller owes the full native amount. Without the sync bracket the received tokens are an unbooked surplus. This is a loss for a caller who names such a recipient and gives an attacker nothing. The op-stack units recorded the same behaviour for L2 predeploys. Evidence: src/PoolManager.sol:291-297, 349-364; on-chain eth_simulateV1 with traceTransfers and a code override at the PoolManager address via https://ethereum-rpc.publicnode.com at block 26471525 (2026-11-22)
- Ethereum, cycle 2. Whether a zero amount call made by the PoolManager, either take(address(0), X, 0) with empty calldata or take(X, to, 0) as X.transfer(to, 0), changes a balance the PoolManager holds on the targets swept. Result: Nothing is owed for a zero amount, so these calls are free pokes with the PoolManager as sender. On the swept targets they do nothing: WETH9 deposits zero, Lido reverts on a zero value submit, the EntryPoint ledger is unchanged, stETH.transfer(to, 0) from the PoolManager leaves its balance unchanged in simulation, and precompiles and system contracts return data or revert. The PoolManager has no fallback or receive function and none of its own functions matches the transfer(address,uint256) selector or an IHooks selector, so it cannot be made to call itself successfully. A token that pays or rebases its holder on such a poke would fall under the finding in this file. Evidence: src/PoolManager.sol:291-297, 368-369; src/types/Currency.sol:44-75; on-chain eth_simulateV1 via https://ethereum-rpc.publicnode.com at blocks 26471525 and 26471590
- Ethereum, cycle 2. Faces on mainnet: can one balance be reached under two currency ids so that a payment is credited twice or one id drains the other. Checked ETH against WETH9, tokens with two entry points (the PoolManager holds 258.6 TUSD and 4,089 SNX), and a ledger credited by a value transfer (EntryPoint). Result: ETH and WETH9 are separate balances. There is one sync slot, each sync overwrites both transient values, and a credit is the measured rise since the latest sync, so one transfer in is credited once under one id. Each take sends at most what it debits under the id named. Over all ids that share a balance, credits minus debits equal the real change. A native payment cannot be counted under an ERC-20 id because settle rejects msg.value while an ERC-20 is synced, settle and settleFor are the only payable functions, and sync(address(0)) followed by a later sync re-reads the balance. I did not call the second entry point of TUSD or SNX on chain. Evidence: src/PoolManager.sol:279-307, 349-364; src/libraries/CurrencyReserves.sol:21-32; on-chain eth_call via https://ethereum-rpc.publicnode.com at block 26471525 (2026-11-22)
- Ethereum, cycle 2. Opcode and call semantics the PoolManager relies on, read in the Osaka execution specification: transient storage lifetime and rollback, value transfer order, static context, return data after failed calls, gas forwarding and precompile dispatch. Result: Transient storage is created per transaction and rolled back with the frame, value moves before callee code runs and is undone on failure, a failed or underfunded call returns 0 with empty return data, and the callee receives at most 63/64 of the gas. The source handles each case by reverting: a failed native or token transfer reverts with a wrapped error, a failed hook call reverts, and a failed balanceOf reverts through the decoder. No path continues after a failed external call, so the gas rule can make an operation fail and cannot make it half succeed. Evidence: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ethereum/execution-specs/mainnet/src/ethereum/forks/osaka/vm/interpreter.py (lines 263 to 303); https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ethereum/execution-specs/mainnet/src/ethereum/forks/osaka/fork.py (lines 622, 932); src/types/Currency.sol:48-53, 64-86; src/libraries/Hooks.sol:134-137
- Ethereum, cycle 2. Known weaknesses of mainnet execution clients, precompiles and system contracts from the last two years: could an ordinary account use any of them against funds in the PoolManager. Result: The incidents I found are liveness and consensus faults: the Reth state root stall of 2025-09-02, Nethermind nodes rejecting a canonical block at the Fusaka fork, and client fixes for MODEXP in Geth and P256VERIFY in Besu that the Fusaka retrospective lists. A node that stalls or rejects a block does not execute a different result for an included transaction, and settlement in core is atomic inside one transaction. The PoolManager calls a precompile only when a caller names one as currency, hook or recipient, and the sweep shows those calls give the caller nothing. I did not search vendor advisory databases one by one, and I did not find a published mainnet bug in TSTORE, TLOAD or CALL handling. Evidence: https://github.com/paradigmxyz/reth/issues/18205; https://research.lido.fi/t/post-mortem-develp-fleet-fusaka-fork-downtime-2025-12-03/10967; https://notes.ethereum.org/@parithosh/fusaka-retro; src/PoolManager.sol:104-114

Result: At block 26471590 claimComp(PoolManager) paid 0 COMP, the Comet claim reverted, the Olympus rebase changed nothing, and the Origin vault calls are restricted. aToken balances grow with time and with flash loan premiums; a caller who pays a premium to move the index receives only the PoolManager's small share of it back, which is less than the premium. Lead L-209 for Ethereum: the eighteen call shapes (P1 empty calldata with value 0, 1 wei and 1 ETH; P2 transfer of 0, 1 and 1e18; P3 balanceOf under STATICCALL; the ten IHooks selectors; unlockCallback) sent to the 18 precompiles, the five system contracts, the system address and the zero address through a forwarding stub at the PoolManager address, with an unrelated account as transaction origin. Bridge contracts of the other networks on Ethereum as recipient of a native take or as currency or hook: the OptimismPortal of OP Mainnet, Base, Unichain, Zora, World Chain, Ink, Soneium, Celo and MegaETH, seven L1StandardBridge proxies and the OP L1CrossDomainMessenger, the Arbitrum Inbox, Bridge and gateway router, the Polygon RootChainManager, DepositManager and EtherPredicate, the Polygon zkEVM bridge, and the zkSync Era, Linea, Starknet and Scroll entry contracts. Can an ordinary account use the PoolManager to send a cross domain message that some L2 contract trusts, or to move value without the full debit?. Result: No. The only calldata the PoolManager sends with value is empty (src/types/Currency.sol:48). A portal turns that into a deposit from the alias 0x111100000004444c5dc75cb358380d2e3de09ba1 to the PoolManager address on the L2 with empty data and 100,000 gas, and the caller is debited the full value on L1. With amount 0 the call is free and the deposit carries nothing. The alias of the PoolManager is no owner or controller of any deployed PoolManager, and the portals reject the transfer and hook shapes, so the PoolManager cannot be made to send calldata to an L2. The Polygon RootChainManager records an ether deposit for the PoolManager address, again paid in full by the caller. The Polygon DepositManager accepts every shape through its fallback and moves nothing for the token shapes, and its balanceOf call reverts under STATICCALL, so no credit can arise in that currency id. Every L1StandardBridge rejects a caller with code. The Arbitrum, zkSync, Linea, Starknet, Scroll and Polygon zkEVM contracts revert on all shapes. Evidence: on-chain query via https://ethereum-rpc.publicnode.com at block 26,480,192; research/network-risk/cycles/008/ethereum-reference.work/raw_sweep.json and raw_followup.json; src/types/Currency.sol:44-52
- Ethereum, cycle 8. Account abstraction and infrastructure contracts under the same shapes: EntryPoint 0.6, 0.7 and 0.8, Permit2, Multicall3, the two CREATE2 factories with the 69 byte code, CreateX, the ERC-1820 registry, the V4FeeAdapter, the TokenJar, the timelock, the PositionManager and the Universal Router. Result: The three EntryPoints credit their deposit ledger for a value call and answer balanceOf, and they have no transfer(address,uint256), so a credit in that currency id can only become a claim that nobody can redeem, as cycle 2 found. The timelock has a payable fallback that accepts every shape and returns nothing: a take of the timelock address as currency succeeds, moves nothing and costs the caller. The TokenJar, the PositionManager and the Universal Router accept the value call and credit nothing. Permit2, Multicall3, CreateX, the registry and the fee adapter revert on all shapes. The two CREATE2 factories revert on the take, sync and hook shapes. They would create a contract from the unlockCallback calldata, but the PoolManager sends that selector only to its own caller (src/PoolManager.sol:110). Evidence: on-chain query via https://ethereum-rpc.publicnode.com at block 26,480,192; research/network-risk/cycles/008/ethereum-reference.work/raw_sweep.json and raw_followup.json
- Ethereum, cycle 8. Which of the 95 swept addresses pass the hook address check, and does any of them answer a hook call so that a pool with that hook works or traps liquidity in a way an ordinary account can use against others?. Result: 27 addresses pass the check and none returns the selector. A pool whose hook is such an address reverts on every operation whose flag is set, because the call returns empty data or reverts (src/libraries/Hooks.sol:137 and 152-154). For example 0x100 carries only the after remove liquidity flag: a pool with that hook accepts deposits and rejects every removal. That is the known case of a pool whose hook blocks removals (F-004), and it needs victims who deposit into a pool with a hook address that has no hook code, so the actor is the pool creator. Evidence: src/libraries/Hooks.sol:109-155; on-chain query via https://ethereum-rpc.publicnode.com at block 26,480,192; research/network-risk/cycles/008/ethereum-reference.work/raw_sweep.json
- Ethereum, cycle 8. Transaction types and execution contexts of Ethereum against unlock, sync, settle and take: types 0x0, 0x1, 0x2, 0x3 and 0x4, the system calls at block boundaries, withdrawals, and bundles inside one transaction. Who is msg.sender, what is msg.value and what does transient storage hold in each?. Result: Types 0x0, 0x1 and 0x2 differ in fee fields and access list only. Type 0x3 adds blob hashes that the PoolManager never reads and must name a recipient. Type 0x4 sets delegation designators before execution and then runs one ordinary top level call. In all five the sender is the signer, value is debited from the signer before the first frame, and the transaction has one transient map that is empty at the start. A delegated account can be the sender of unlock itself, and the walk with a designator placed by state override passed all four steps with tx.origin equal to msg.sender. A delegation that was set by a transaction which later reverted stays set, which changes code at an account and nothing inside the PoolManager. System calls use the system address as caller, a fixed target and their own transient map, and withdrawals credit balances without execution, as cycles 2 and 3 read in the specification. The census of 120 blocks found no sixth type. The remaining cross user effect is a sync left by an earlier call of the same transaction (F-071). Evidence: on-chain query via https://ethereum-rpc.publicnode.com (eth_getBlockByNumber for 120 blocks from 26,430,231 to 26,480,211; eth_call with state override); research/network-risk/cycles/008/ethereum-reference.work/raw_txtypes.json and walk7702.py; src/PoolManager.sol:104-114
- Ethereum, cycle 8. Critic gap of cycle 7: which Ethereum fork is scheduled, and does it add a transaction type with more than one frame? If the frame transaction of EIP-8141 were live, what would unlock, sync, settle and take see?. Result: Glamsterdam is next and has no mainnet date; its scheduled EIPs add no transaction type. EIP-8141 is scheduled for the fork after it and has no activation date on any network. Read against the draft text: frames are top level calls that run one after another, and transient storage is discarded between frames, so each frame meets a locked PoolManager with no synced currency, and the stale sync of F-071 cannot cross a frame. unlock opens and closes inside one frame (src/PoolManager.sol:104-114). Value enters only in SENDER frames, where it is debited from tx.sender as in a CALL. In DEFAULT frames msg.sender is 0xaa for every author, value is zero, and the only functions that act for 0xaa without an unlock are sync, initialize and the ERC-6909 transfer and approval functions. 0xaa is not a valid hook address, because it sets the after add liquidity returns delta bit without the after add liquidity bit (src/libraries/Hooks.sol:113-116), so updateDynamicLPFee cannot be reached with it. The draft may change before it ships, and I did not read a client implementation. Evidence: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ethereum/EIPs/master/EIPS/eip-8141.md (lines 101 to 131 and 432 to 481); https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ethereum/EIPs/master/EIPS/eip-8081.md; https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ethereum/EIPs/master/EIPS/eip-7773.md
- Ethereum, cycle 8. The Hoodi activation of Glamsterdam was withdrawn because EIP-8037 breaks assumptions of deployed contracts. Does the source hold such an assumption: a fixed gas amount for a call, a gas check, or a path that must fit a gas figure?. Result: No. The three external call sites forward gas() (src/types/Currency.sol:48 and 73, src/libraries/Hooks.sol:134), the unlock callback and balanceOf are plain high level calls, and a search of src outside src/test finds no gasleft and no numeric gas argument. Under the current text a new slot costs 97,920 state gas and a changed slot 10,000 gas, so opening a position at two fresh ticks, which writes between 5 and 11 new slots, costs between about 0.4 and 1.0 million gas more than today, and a tick crossing, which changes two fee growth slots, about 14,000 more. A swap can still be split by its price limit and a removal touches a fixed number of slots. A native take to an address that does not exist would cost 183,600 state gas more. These are costs for the caller and no path becomes unreachable. I did not measure the deployed contract under the new rules. Evidence: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ethereum/EIPs/master/EIPS/eip-8037.md (lines 35 to 53 and 113 to 116); https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ethereum/EIPs/master/EIPS/eip-8038.md (lines 45 to 51); https://blog.ethereum.org/2026/10/22/glamsterdam-hoodi-delay; src/types/Currency.sol:48

Result: Yes, as read at v1.17.9. Each transaction runs on its own state object built from the parent root and the access list overlay of all earlier indices (core/state_processor_parallel.go lines 433-438), whose transient storage starts empty (core/state/statedb.go line 199). Receipts and gas are gathered in block order (lines 239-266). The access list rebuilt from execution must hash to the header's (core/block_validator.go lines 181-190), so a transaction that reads a PoolManager slot an earlier one wrote reads the value the earlier one produced, or the block is rejected. The path is off until Amsterdam has a mainnet time. Evidence: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ethereum/go-ethereum/v1.17.9/core/state_processor_parallel.go

- Ethereum, cycle 21. Lead L-820: reth's parallel executor for blocks with an access list. Does each transaction start with empty transient storage, and is the rebuilt access list checked against the header?. Result: Yes to both. A worker executes each transaction with execute_transaction_without_commit, which detaches the overlay through take_pending_state and calls clear_transaction_state, which clears transient_storage together with the journal, logs and warm sets (evm2 evm/tx.rs lines 240-249, evm/state/mod.rs lines 563-579); a nested transaction gets committed_copy with an empty transient map (lines 135-150). The canonical executor commits worker results in block order and builds the access list from that commit (reth bal/execute.rs lines 157-196), and validation.rs lines 113-131 reject the block when the rebuilt hash differs from the header's. So the unlock flag, deltas and synced currency in src/libraries/Lock.sol:10-26 and src/PoolManager.sol:104-114 cannot cross from one transaction to the next on this path. A builder that ships a false access list only gets its block rejected, which is an operator matter. Evidence: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/paradigmxyz/reth/main/crates/engine/tree/src/tree/payload_processor/bal/execute.rs
- Ethereum, cycle 21. Upcoming forks within six months, assumed shipped the day after: Glamsterdam's 20 scheduled EIPs and Hegota's two scheduled ones. Result: The scheduled list matches what cycles 14 and 17 cleared: new opcodes that the PoolManager bytecode never decodes (EIP-7843, EIP-8024), gas repricing (EIP-2780, 7778, 7976, 7981, 8037, 8038), ETH credited outside a call or a burn removed (EIP-7732, 8246, 8282), logs (EIP-7708), code size (EIP-7954), the existing CREATE2 factory (EIP-7997) and access lists (EIP-7928, read above for reth and in cycle 17 for geth). Native settlement credits msg.value only (src/PoolManager.sol:349-364), so ETH arriving without a call books to no one. Hegota schedules FOCIL, which changes inclusion only, and EIP-8141 frames, which cycle 8 read. Neither fork has a mainnet date. Evidence: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ethereum/EIPs/master/EIPS/eip-7773.md
- Ethereum, cycle 21. Lead L-885: who created the Ethereum copy of the PoolManager at 0x8366a39c..., what it holds, and whether it gives anyone a path to the Robinhood Chain or Arc PoolManager funds at the same address. Result: EOA 0x629f191e... created it at block 25,466,547 through the deterministic CREATE2 factory 0x4e59b448... with a zero salt, so the address follows from the factory, the salt and the creation code with the owner 0x9701fb0a... as constructor argument. Anyone can repeat that creation on a chain that has the factory and get the same address only with the same owner, so a replica on another chain is owned by 0x9701fb0a... and not by its deployer. It holds 0 ETH, 10 initialized pools, no ModifyLiquidity, Swap or ERC-6909 Transfer event since creation, and nonce 1. Nothing on Ethereum moves value at the other chains' addresses. Whether a bridge or interface treats the three as one principal is an integration question outside src/. Evidence: cycles/021/ethereum-reference.work/l885.json, l885logs.json

Cycle 17's census stored the initializing transaction hash in its poolId field (pool 0x462175db... is listed as 0x1559b4e1..., the hash of its creation transaction), so its reading of zero in-range liquidity for all 21 was taken at slots no pool uses. Read at the right slots, four pools hold liquidity: 0x08834f72... (delegated hook, about 0.0059 ETH and 1.03 USDC), 0x992c0ab6... (delegated hook with after remove and after remove returns delta, about 0.0038 ETH), 0x462175db... (empty hook with before remove, frozen, see finding) and 0xf6aaf9bd... (empty hook with only after swap, about 1,000 units of 0x0e90b620... and 2.33 USDT, removable). F-013's measured Ethereum exposure is therefore a few dollars, not nil. Evidence: cycles/021/ethereum-reference.work/l821.json, l821logs.json, l821sim.json
