- HyperEVM, cycle 4. Which system transactions can an ordinary HyperCore account cause, which need a validator vote, and can any of them reach the PoolManager or carry it as sender (assumptions A2 and A8, the question the cycle 2 critic left with F-020 and F-044)?. Result: An ordinary account can cause three kinds: a HYPE credit from the bridge address to an EVM account, a transfer call on a linked contract from that token's system address, and a coreReceiveWithData call on a linked contract. The targets are the recipient account or the token's linked contract and the sender is a system address. The PoolManager is no linked contract and cannot become one without its owner, and a plain HYPE credit to it reverts. The fourth kind, transfers sent in the name of the AQAv2 linked contract and treasury address, follows user flows in size and names only the two addresses fixed at activation, which needs a validator vote. In 1,927 system transactions none targeted the PoolManager, none had it as sender and none came from the zero address, which is the protocol fee controller here (src/ProtocolFees.sol:48). Evidence: https://rpc.purroofgroup.com eth_getBlockByNumber census of 4,725 blocks; https://hyperliquid.gitbook.io/hyperliquid-docs/for-developers/hyperevm/hypercore-less-than-greater-than-hyperevm-transfers.md
- HyperEVM, cycle 4. The protocol fee controller is the zero address. If some transaction ever ran with msg.sender zero, could collectProtocolFees pay out pool funds?. Result: No. collectProtocolFees subtracts the amount from protocolFeesAccrued with a checked subtraction before the transfer (src/ProtocolFees.sol:54-56). That counter grows only by the protocol share of swap fees (src/ProtocolFees.sol:66-70, src/PoolManager.sol:238), and no protocol fee can be set while the controller is zero (src/ProtocolFees.sol:35-41). On chain the counter is 0 for native HYPE, WHYPE, USDC and Wrapped USDC. A call with amount zero transfers nothing. Evidence: src/ProtocolFees.sol:44-57; https://rpc.hyperliquid.xyz/evm eth_call protocolFeesAccrued(address) and eth_getStorageAt slot 2
- HyperEVM, cycle 4. Work item 1, exits: can an ordinary account make another user's liquidity removal or claim redemption impossible to include or always revert on HyperEVM through gas caps, storage pricing, mempool rules or the big block flag?. Result: No. Removal has no loop (src/libraries/Pool.sol:146-238) and two mined removals used about 60,500 gas each in the modifyLiquidity frame against a 3,000,000 gas small block. burn and take have no loop either (src/PoolManager.sol:291-297 and 332-336). The mempool rule of 8 pending nonces and the one day pruning apply to the sender's own account. The big block flag is set by a HyperCore action of the account itself. System transactions do not use block gas. Filling small blocks costs base fee that is burned and rises with each full block. What an attacker can make expensive is a swap, which is recorded in the finding that extends F-039. A pool's own hook can still block removal, which is F-004. Evidence: https://rpc.purroofgroup.com debug_traceTransaction; https://hyperliquid.gitbook.io/hyperliquid-docs/for-developers/hyperevm/dual-block-architecture.md
- HyperEVM, Elysium, cycle 4. Lead L-219: an Elysium account sends a child chain message whose target on HyperEVM is the HYPE bridge address, a token system address or CoreWriter. Is a HyperCore balance credited to the Elysium Bridge contract, can a later message spend it, and can this move the HYPE that backs Elysium?. Result: The credit goes to the Bridge contract's own HyperCore account and any later message can spend it, and neither step reaches the backing. In a simulated executeCall from the allowed outbox the Bridge sent 1 HYPE to the bridge address, which emitted Received with the Bridge as user, and a call to CoreWriter logged an action with the Bridge as user. The Bridge sends only the value of the message it executes, and that value was burned on Elysium when the message was created, so its 297,189 HYPE cannot leave without an equal burn. HYPE routed this way lands in a HyperCore account that every Elysium account can command through CoreWriter, so the sender of such a message can lose it to whoever sends the next message. No Received log and no CoreWriter log names the Bridge since its deployment, and the Bridge has no HyperCore account. Token escrow sits in the gateway 0xd97B30dE0bA0C2eAeE942afce77530e06c5F122c, which a Bridge call cannot command without the counterpart gateway as child chain sender. I did not read the gateway code in this cycle and take that from the standard Arbitrum design. Evidence: https://rpc.purroofgroup.com debug_traceCall executeCall(address,uint256,bytes) on 0x503D572157113fAaaD4DbeD2647Bb10b949216B6 with from 0xec6b106dfa14428fe5eec2a4065a7be599f02728; eth_getLogs from block 48,956,737; https://api.hyperliquid.xyz/info preTransferCheck
- HyperEVM, cycle 4. Can an ordinary account link a HyperCore spot token to the PoolManager, so that HyperCore sends system transactions to it or reads its logs as token movements?. Result: No. HyperCore accepts a link when the finalizer deployed the contract with CREATE at a stated nonce, or is stored in the contract's slot 0, or in the slot keccak256("HyperCore deployer"). The PoolManager was created with CREATE2 by the deterministic deployer, a contract that cannot send actions. Slot 0 holds the owner. The custom slot is zero and no function writes a caller chosen slot: persistent writes go to mappings and pool state (src/ERC6909.sol:25-88, src/ProtocolFees.sol:29-70, src/libraries/Pool.sol). Only the owner contract could finalize a link, which is a governance act. A linked PoolManager would still revert on transfer(address,uint256) and coreReceiveWithData, which it does not implement, and it emits no ERC-20 Transfer log. Evidence: https://rpc.purroofgroup.com debug_traceTransaction 0x886b45bc662d93a4b74935513eb8dc8c1179c4a6c70056f4b4ba5b251c58e4c5; https://rpc.hyperliquid.xyz/evm eth_getStorageAt; https://hyperliquid.gitbook.io/hyperliquid-docs/for-developers/hyperevm/hypercore-less-than-greater-than-hyperevm-transfers.md

The archive client executes every transaction, system or signed, through one transact call (executor.rs lines 192 to 213) and compares gas used, receipts root and logs bloom with the header for the signed transactions. Receipts of system transactions are filtered out of that comparison (reth_copy.rs lines 41 to 47). The official replay client asserts equality of all signed receipts and of system receipts when the block data includes them (run.rs lines 217 to 264). A stale synced currency left by one transaction would change the outcome of a later native settle in the same block (src/PoolManager.sol:349-356), and such a difference in a signed transaction would break the replay. Both clients reproduce the chain to its head, which the archive endpoints I used show. The validator node itself remains unread. Evidence: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/hl-archive-node/nanoreth/master/src/node/evm/executor.rs, https://raw.githubusercontent.com/hl-archive-node/nanoreth/master/src/node/consensus/reth_copy.rs, https://raw.githubusercontent.com/hyperliquid-dex/hyper-evm-sync/main/src/run.rs
- HyperEVM, cycle 4. Lead L-148, second half: which price limit do the deployed routers pass to swap?. Result: The extreme one. Universal Router 2.1.2 passed 4295128740 or 1461446703485210103287273052203988822378723970341 in 5 of 5 traced swaps, seven other callers did so in 29 traced swaps and the Quoter does so in every quote. One caller passes its own limit. The loop stops at the limit and stores the reached price (src/libraries/Pool.sol:344 and 439), so the limit only decides how far a swap that outruns liquidity keeps walking. Opcode differential on the node that produces blocks: do TSTORE and TLOAD roll back on REVERT, INVALID and out of gas, including a successful inner write under a reverted parent, does TSTORE fail under STATICCALL, and do CALL with value, the stipend, calls to addresses without code, the 63/64 rule, RETURNDATASIZE, MCOPY and PUSH0 behave as on Ethereum?. - HyperEVM, cycle 7. Upcoming forks: assume the upgrades scheduled or proposed for the next six months ship. What changes for the PoolManager and for funds inside it?. Result: Nothing that an ordinary account can use. The fork of 2026-11-11 is live and only reprices seven precompiles that core never calls (F-045). The cap of 200,000 gas on sendToEvmWithData narrows what a linked contract can do at the top of a block. The change of HyperEVM error responses concerns the RPC. HIP-3* and the write priority changes concern HyperCore. The AQAv2 requirement for more quote assets widens F-020, which needs a privileged record. No EVM fork past Cancun is announced and the testnet runs the same EVM as mainnet. If EIP-7702 were adopted later, an account with a mined address could serve as a hook whose code its owner can change, which is the pool-creator hazard already recorded for other chains under assumption A7. All are application or key faults outside the PoolManager, and none involves a precompile or system contract acting for it. No client advisory was found. Evidence: https://finance.yahoo.com/news/zachxbt-flags-400k-exploit-hypurr-093215277.html; https://www.cryptopolitan.com/pt/hyperdrive-pauses-markets-after-exploit/; https://cointelegraph.com/news/hyperliquid-hyperevm-bug-bounty-launch-layer1

Result: All 185,529 vectors equal the specification with no errors, the same as cycles 10 and 14. The paths of TickMath (src/libraries/TickMath.sol:61-63, 80, 111, 142-145), FullMath (src/libraries/FullMath.sol:24-25, 48, 52-53, 62, 67, 73, 112), UnsafeMath (src/libraries/UnsafeMath.sol:14) and TickBitmap (src/libraries/TickBitmap.sol:24-26, 57, 64) therefore get the specified operands and results at the edges. - HyperEVM, cycle 17. Rerun of pmdiff.py (250 scripts) and pmdiff2.py (300 scripts) for chain 999. Result: pmdiff: 248 of 248 compared scripts identical to Ethereum; two scripts were not compared because the Ethereum reference endpoint failed on them this run (referenceErrors 2), not because HyperEVM differed. pmdiff2: 299 of 300, the exception again script 189, the open price limit swap that needs more than the 30,000,000 gas the endpoint grants. - HyperEVM, cycle 17. Vectors for the arithmetic paths that ruint 1.21 rewrote (power of two divisors, divisors of one and two limbs, numerators one limb longer than the divisor, single limb quotients, add_mod below twice the modulus, mul_mod with modulus 2^256-1 and with high words that share the modulus's top limbs, pow of power of two bases, limb wise comparisons) and for FullMath's constant moduli 2^96 and 2^128 with prod1 equal to 1, in case the closed validator links a newer ruint than the public clients. Result: 74,646 of 74,646 equal to Python integers on the official node, the archive client and the testnet node, no errors. These are the operands that src/libraries/FullMath.sol:24 (mulmod by not(0)), :48 and :112 (remainder by the denominator, including the constant Q96 and Q128 callers), :62, :67 and :73 (division by the power of two twos) and src/libraries/UnsafeMath.sol:14 hand to the interpreter. The answering hl-node build therefore does not carry the 1.21.0 mul_mod fault or a fault in the rewritten division paths at these shapes. Evidence: research/network-risk/cycles/017/hyperevm.work/ruint121.py, out/ruint121.json
- HyperEVM, cycle 17. RUSTSEC-2025-0137 (unsound reciprocal_mg10 in ruint before 1.17.0), which affects both public replay clients (hyper-evm-sync ruint 1.15.0, nanoreth f0cad31 ruint 1.16.0): can any EVM division reach reciprocal_mg10 with a divisor whose top bit is clear?. Result: No. In ruint 1.15.0 and 1.16.0 every division goes through div_inlined (src/algorithms/div/mod.rs lines 47-104 of 1.16.0), which trims zero limbs and sends one and two limb divisors to div_nx1 and div_nx2. Both shift the divisor by its leading zeros before calling reciprocal or reciprocal_2 (src/algorithms/div/small.rs lines 69-75 and 138-144), and the normalized variants are only called when the shift is zero (lines 33-39, 109-114). The precondition d >= 2^63 that the advisory says is only debug-checked therefore always holds. DIV, MOD, SDIV, SMOD, ADDMOD and MULMOD of the PoolManager (22, 3, 4, 3, 1 and 13 instances in the build) cannot reach the unsound input. Evidence: https://rustsec.org/advisories/RUSTSEC-2025-0137; https://raw.githubusercontent.com/recmo/uint/v1.16.0/src/algorithms/div/small.rs and mod.rs (saved research/network-risk/cycles/017/hyperevm.work/src/)
- HyperEVM, cycle 17. RUSTSEC-2026-0220 (ruint before 1.20.0 truncates wrapping_shl and wrapping_shr amounts modulo 2^32 and reports wrong overflow flags), which affects both public replay clients: can SHL, SHR, SAR, BYTE or SIGNEXTEND give a wrong word?. Result: No. revm-interpreter 15.2.0 (hyper-evm-sync) converts the shift with as_usize_saturated and shifts only when the amount is below 256 (src/instructions/bitwise.rs lines 87-92, 100-105, 114-121), BYTE only indexes below 32 (lines 73-79), and SIGNEXTEND only acts below 31 (arithmetic.rs lines 93-99), so a shift of 2^32 or more never reaches ruint. The overflow flag is not used by these handlers. The battery and the cycle 14 high limb set pass on both endpoints. TickMath (src/libraries/TickMath.sol:63, 111, 142-145) and BalanceDelta's SAR therefore keep their results. Evidence: https://rustsec.org/advisories/RUSTSEC-2026-0220; https://static.crates.io/crates/revm-interpreter/revm-interpreter-15.2.0.crate (research/network-risk/cycles/017/hyperevm.work/dl/)
- HyperEVM, cycle 17. The memory size wrap that the new nanoreth Cargo.toml comment names (memory can grow until the size computation in a nested frame wraps unless memory_limit is set), and the revm 43.0.0 fix that returns MemoryOOG when a resize fails. Result: No effect on blocks or on the PoolManager. resize_memory in revm-interpreter 43.0.2 charges the quadratic memory cost before resizing (src/interpreter/shared_memory.rs lines 565-605), and on HyperEVM a transaction holds at most 30,000,000 gas, which pays for about 123,000 words (about 4 MB) across all frames, far from a usize wrap. The comment itself says no block can pay for 4 GiB. The PoolManager's own memory use is bounded by its calldata and return data. The official node returned out of gas during memory expansion for MSTORE at 2^32 and 2^64-1 and invalid operand for 2^64, as specified. Evidence: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/hl-archive-node/nanoreth/master/Cargo.toml; https://static.crates.io/crates/revm-interpreter/revm-interpreter-43.0.2.crate; research/network-risk/cycles/017/hyperevm.work/out/probe_err.json
- HyperEVM, cycle 17. Halt behaviour at the edges on the three endpoints: 0xFE, an undefined opcode, jumps to a non JUMPDEST, into push data and onto a 0x5b inside push data, stack underflow and overflow, huge memory offsets for MSTORE, MLOAD and KECCAK256, zero length CALLDATACOPY and MCOPY at offset 2^256-1, RETURNDATACOPY past the end, and an endless loop. Result: All three return the same halt for each program and the result Ethereum specifies: invalid jumps fail, zero length copies at huge offsets succeed without expansion, RETURNDATACOPY out of range fails with OutOfOffset. Jump destination analysis therefore treats push data as Ethereum does, which is what every Solidity dispatch and internal jump of the PoolManager relies on. Evidence: research/network-risk/cycles/017/hyperevm.work/probe_err.py, out/probe_err.json
- HyperEVM, cycle 17. Does the answering node reuse jump destination analysis keyed by the code hash of an address after the code there changes (L-669 by the only route open to an ordinary caller, state override on eth_call)?. Result: No. After the real PoolManager ran (owner() answered 0x2d09...21f9), the PoolManager address was given code where a real PoolManager JUMPDEST lies inside PUSH32 data, and the jump failed with InvalidJump; code with a JUMPDEST at offset 4, which is not one in the real code, jumped and returned 1. Fresh addresses gave the same answers. Same on the archive client and the testnet node. In blocks, code at an address changes only by creation on Cancun, where the hash is computed from the code. Evidence: research/network-risk/cycles/017/hyperevm.work/jdcache.py, out/jdcache.json
- HyperEVM, cycle 17. L-587: do the state lookups of HyperEVM fold storage keys, transient keys or account addresses by a rule that needs several changed bits?. Result: No fold on any endpoint: 489 storage and 489 transient keys written and read back in one call, 300 storage keys read from overridden backing state and 180 multi byte variant addresses read by BALANCE each returned their own value. Pool state slots (src/libraries/Pool.sol tick and position mappings) and the transient delta slots of src/libraries/CurrencyDelta.sol:21-39 cannot alias by such a rule on the answering node. Evidence: research/network-risk/cycles/017/hyperevm.work/out/foldprobe.json, out/foldprobe2.json
- HyperEVM, cycle 17. L-185: is there a block in which one transaction leaves sync(ERC-20) without a settle and a later transaction makes a native settle with value?. Result: No such pair exists in the history: of 2,782 PoolManager transactions traced, none that succeeded ends with an ERC-20 synced, so the mined test of A1 between transactions cannot be built from HyperEVM blocks. 97 transactions made native settles without their own sync and all succeeded. The A1 boundary was tested directly on the three endpoints in earlier cycles (TSTORE rollback and per transaction reset). - HyperEVM, cycle 17. L-548 on HyperEVM: an EIP-7702 designator pointing at each read precompile 0x0800 to 0x0814, called from the PoolManager address with the transfer, balanceOf, empty calldata with value and hook shapes. Result: The node never runs the precompile logic for the delegated account: all 84 calls return empty success, the behaviour of an account whose code is empty. Such an account cannot exist on chain, because the network rejects type 4 transactions (transaction type not supported) and EIP-3541 forbids deploying code that starts with 0xEF. A take of such a currency would move nothing and still debit the caller (src/libraries/CurrencyDelta.sol:21-39, src/PoolManager.sol:291-297). Evidence: research/network-risk/cycles/017/hyperevm.work/out/probe7702.json, out/probe7702_tx.txt

- HyperEVM, cycle 20. L-896: can mined swaps reach the overflow fallback of getNextSqrtPriceFromAmount0RoundingUp (src/libraries/SqrtPriceMath.sol:40-52)? The fallback runs only on the exact input token0 path (src/libraries/SqrtPriceMath.sol:147, src/libraries/SwapMath.sol:78) and needs amount times sqrtPX96 of at least 2^256 - 2^224; with sqrtPX96 below 2^160 that needs an amount of at least 2^95, and the amount passed is never above the token0 the swap paid. Result: Screen of all Swap events of the v3, Algebra and PoolManager layouts in blocks 52,031,000 to 52,231,000: 389,589 Swap events (389,257 of the v3 and Algebra 1.0/1.1 layout, 331 of the Algebra 1.2 layout, 1 of the PoolManager), 0 with |amount0| at or above 2^95, and the largest |amount0| times logged sqrtPrice is below 2^175. No mined swap comes within reach of the fallback, so the closed validator's result on that branch cannot be checked from mined data; the branch is covered by the opcode vectors and the reference interpreter. - HyperEVM, cycle 20. sendToEvmWithData and its 200,000 gas cap: can an ordinary account make HyperCore move PoolManager funds or bracket its own sync and settle with the delivery?. Result: The action calls coreReceiveWithData on the linked token contract as a system transaction ahead of the signed transactions of the block, so it cannot run between a user's sync and settle (transient state is per transaction, src/PoolManager.sol:279-288). It moves tokens out of the system address, not out of the PoolManager. A smaller gas cap only makes the delivery fail sooner. A delivery addressed to the PoolManager credits nobody and is the stranded payment pattern of F-021. Evidence: https://hyperliquid.gitbook.io/hyperliquid-docs/for-developers/api/exchange-endpoint ; https://tg.me/hyperliquid_api/401
- HyperEVM, cycle 20. The 1 USDC minimum for HyperEVM to HyperCore transfers. Result: A take of USDC to the USDC system address below 1 USDC is lost to the caller who chose that recipient (src/PoolManager.sol:291-297); it debits that caller and no one else. Token and recipient hazard, recorded in one line. Evidence: https://telemetr.io/en/channels/1745127781-hyperliquid_api/posts
- HyperEVM, cycle 20. Upcoming forks: every HyperEVM change announced for the next six months. Result: The announced items are HyperEVM error responses that include HyperCore errors (RPC only), the 200,000 gas cap of sendToEvmWithData, and HyperCore trading changes. No EVM fork past Cancun is announced, and testnet still refuses CLZ and has no Prague precompiles. None of these changes an opcode result, transient storage, the call semantics the PoolManager uses or who can move its balances. ## OP Stack chains with a non-ETH gas token

- Celo, cycle 1. Whether the ERC-20 face of native CELO lets a caller be credited twice for one payment: once as msg.value under currency address(0) and once as a balance increase under the CELO token currency (A3). Result: No path found. A native credit needs settle with msg.value while the synced currency slot is zero. A token credit needs the slot to hold the CELO token from sync until settle. The slot is a single transient value (src/libraries/CurrencyReserves.sol:15-32), sync(address(0)) clears it and sync(token) snapshots the balance at that moment (src/PoolManager.sol:279-288). settle with value reverts with NonzeroNativeValue while a token is synced (src/PoolManager.sol:356). The two windows cannot overlap, so each wei that enters is credited once. Evidence: src/PoolManager.sol:349-364
- Celo, cycle 1. Whether take under one CELO face followed by repayment under the other face nets to a gain, and whether a balance drop between sync and settle can be turned into credit. Result: No. take debits the caller under the currency it names (src/PoolManager.sol:291-297). Repaying under the other face creates a positive delta in a different currency, and unlock requires every delta to be zero (src/PoolManager.sol:112). A balance drop between sync and settle makes reservesNow minus reservesBefore underflow under checked arithmetic and the settle reverts (src/PoolManager.sol:360). Evidence: src/PoolManager.sol:291-297
- Celo, cycle 1. Whether the fee currency functions debitGasFees and creditGasFees, which the client calls with msg.sender address(0), can lower the PoolManager's token balances outside a take (A2). Result: Not reachable. Both clients pass the transaction sender as the debited account, and the PoolManager cannot be a transaction sender because it has code. Deposit transactions do not use a fee currency. Any other caller is rejected: eth_call of debitGasFees(PoolManager, 1) reverts with 'Only VM can call' on USDm, USDT, WETH and COPm, 'caller is not VM' on the USDC adapter and 'caller is not the fee caller' on USDC itself. Fee credits go to the sender, the fee vault and the FeeHandler. Evidence: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/celo-org/op-geth/HEAD/core/celo_state_transition.go
- Celo, X Layer, cycle 1. Whether a call can reach the PoolManager with msg.sender equal to address(0), which is the current protocolFeeController on both chains (A12, A8). Result: No path found. On Celo the state changing calls that the client makes with caller address(0) are debitGasFees and creditGasFees on a fee currency registered by Governance in FeeCurrencyDirectory. The PoolManager is not in getCurrencies(), and any call a fee currency makes onward carries the fee currency as msg.sender. A deposit sender equal to address(0) would need an L1 contract at 0xeeeeffffffffffffffffffffffffffffffffeeef. eth_call from address(0) succeeds in simulation only. On X Layer the gasless check is a system call to a fixed whitelist contract. Its caller address was not confirmed and is listed as a lead. Evidence: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/celo-org/op-geth/HEAD/core/vm/celo_evm.go
- Celo, cycle 1. Whether PoolManager transient storage (unlock flag, deltas, synced currency) can leak across the fee debit and credit calls that surround a CIP-64 transaction (A1). Result: No. celo-revm clears transient storage after the debit and at transaction teardown, and op-geth reset it before the debit. The credit call does see the main transaction's transient storage. By then unlock has returned, the lock is set and all deltas are zero (src/PoolManager.sol:112-113). Only a stale synced currency can remain, and the registered fee currencies are Governance approved tokens and adapters. Whether any of them calls untrusted code during credit is listed as a lead. Evidence: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/celo-org/celo-kona/HEAD/crates/celo-revm/src/contracts/core_contracts.rs
- Celo, cycle 1. Whether CELO borrowed for free inside one transaction through take can be used for Celo governance or validator voting, or to pay gas (A5). Result: No. Voting power comes from CELO locked in LockedGold, and unlocked CELO can be withdrawn only after a 3 day unlocking period, so a lock cannot be undone inside the transaction that must repay the PoolManager. Gas in a fee currency is debited from the sender before execution starts, so tokens taken during execution cannot fund it. Evidence: https://docs.celo.org/learn/protocol/staking/locked-celo.md
- Celo, X Layer, cycle 1. Whether the opcodes the PoolManager bytecode uses exist on both chains (A10). Result: Yes. eth_call with init code returned the expected values for TSTORE and TLOAD, MCOPY and PUSH0 on both chains. SELFBALANCE, RETURNDATACOPY, STATICCALL and CALL with value are pre-Cancun opcodes. Both deployments already serve calls: owner(), protocolFeeController() and protocolFeesAccrued() return. Evidence: https://forno.celo.org and https://rpc.xlayer.tech eth_call with init code 0x602a5f5d5f5c5f5260205ff3, 0x602a5f5260205f60205e60206020f3, 0x5f5f5260205ff3
- Celo, X Layer, cycle 1. Whether block or transaction gas caps can make a large swap or a liquidity removal impossible to include (A9). Result: No. Celo has a 30,000,000 gas block limit and X Layer 210,000,000, and neither enforces the 16,777,216 per transaction cap because Karst is not active. When Karst arrives the cap equals the one Ethereum already has. A swap can be bounded by its price limit, and ASSUMPTIONS.md A9 records that modifyLiquidity touches two ticks and the bitmap. Pool.modifyLiquidity was not read line by line in this unit. Evidence: https://forno.celo.org and https://rpc.xlayer.tech eth_getBlockByNumber latest (gasLimit 0x1c9c380 and 0xc845880)
- Celo, X Layer, cycle 1. Whether L1 to L2 address aliasing lets a deposit arrive with the PoolManager or the owner contract as sender (A8). Result: No. A deposit sender is the L1 EOA itself or an L1 contract address plus 0x1111000000000000000000000000000000001111. Producing the PoolManager address or the owner address needs control of a specific L1 address. The owner contract additionally requires msg.sender to be the messenger predeploy. Evidence: https://specs.optimism.io/protocol/deposits.html
- X Layer, cycle 1. Whether native OKB has an ERC-20 face or another alias that shares the PoolManager's native balance (A3). Result: No. The custom gas token design keeps OKB as a plain native asset. The two Wrapped OKB contracts hold their own native balance: the predeploy has zero supply and 0xe538905cf8410324e03A5A23C1c177a474D59b2b holds 241,385 OKB against its own supply. A token balanceOf(PoolManager) on either returns the wrapped amount and not the native balance (73.3 and 0 against 321.7 OKB native). Evidence: https://rpc.xlayer.tech eth_call balanceOf, totalSupply; eth_getBalance
- X Layer, cycle 1. Whether the custom gas token predeploys LiquidityController and NativeAssetLiquidity can debit native OKB from the PoolManager or inflate supply (A2, A3). Result: No. mint releases native asset that NativeAssetLiquidity already holds to an authorised minter, and burn accepts value from the caller. Neither takes an account to debit. NativeAssetLiquidity holds zero OKB, so no mint can happen now. Evidence: https://docs.optimism.io/op-stack/features/custom-gas-token
- X Layer, cycle 1. Whether the gasless transaction rule changes any balance at the PoolManager or weakens the per transaction lifetime of transient storage (A1, A2). Result: No effect found. The rule waives the fee for whitelisted zero priced transactions and leaves execution unchanged. The whitelist lookup runs as an uncommitted system call before the transaction. A per block gas budget limits gasless transactions in the builder. Evidence: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/okx/xlayer-reth/main/crates/builder/src/flashblocks/context.rs
- Celo, X Layer, cycle 1. Whether CREATE2 address derivation and hook permission bits behave as on Ethereum (A7). Result: No difference found. The deterministic deployment proxy 0x4e59b44847b379578588920cA78FbF26c0B4956C (69 bytes) and Permit2 0x000000000022D473030F116dDEE9F6B43aC78BA3 (9,152 bytes) sit at their usual addresses on both chains, which is consistent with standard CREATE2 derivation. The Celo specification index and the X Layer docs list no change to CREATE2. Celo's larger code size limit lets hooks be bigger and does not change how the 14 permission bits are read (src/libraries/Hooks.sol:27). Evidence: https://forno.celo.org and https://rpc.xlayer.tech eth_getCode 0x4e59b44847b379578588920cA78FbF26c0B4956C and 0x000000000022D473030F116dDEE9F6B43aC78BA3
- Celo, X Layer, cycle 2. P1, native take to a special address: does any precompile, predeploy, registry contract, bridge, wrapper, fee contract or preinstalled contract accept value with empty calldata from the PoolManager and give the caller more than the amount the caller is debited. Result: No. 365 addresses on Celo and 302 on X Layer were called with msg.sender set to the PoolManager, empty calldata and values 0, 1 wei and 10^18 wei. The targets that accept value keep it (fee vaults, FeeHandler contracts, Reserve, Governance, L1BlockNumber), book it to the PoolManager address (EntryPoints, wrapped native contracts) or start a withdrawal for the PoolManager address (Celo L2ToL1MessagePasser). take debits the caller the full amount before the call (src/PoolManager.sol:294), so none of these gives the caller value. The low finding in this file records the loss to the caller. Evidence: https://forno.celo.org and https://rpc.xlayer.tech eth_call sweep, 2026-11-22; src/PoolManager.sol:291-297
- Celo, X Layer, cycle 2. P2 and P3, a special address used as a currency: can transfer(address,uint256) from the PoolManager succeed while it moves something the caller is not debited for, and can balanceOf(PoolManager) rise between sync and settle without a payment. Result: No. transfer returns true only on real tokens (CELO, the Mento stable tokens, bridged WETH, USDC, USDT, USDT0, the wrapped native contracts), where the caller is debited the same amount under the same currency id. FeeHandler, MentoFeeHandlerSeller, UniswapFeeHandlerSeller and Reserve on Celo, a Safe on X Layer, ecrecover and 0x0100 return success with no data, which core accepts (src/types/Currency.sol:68), and they move nothing. Their balanceOf returns no data, so sync reverts and no credit can be created for them. sha256, ripemd160, identity, L1BlockNumber and the deterministic deployment proxy return data that the transfer check rejects. balanceOf on L1BlockNumber returns the L1 block number, which is constant inside one transaction, so a sync and settle pair credits zero. Evidence: https://forno.celo.org and https://rpc.xlayer.tech eth_call transfer and balanceOf with from set to the PoolManager; eth_call sync(address) on the Celo PoolManager for 0xfd, FeeHandler, L1BlockNumber and an EntryPoint; src/types/Currency.sol:60-96
- Celo, X Layer, cycle 2. P5, a special address used as a hook: does any swept address pass isValidHookAddress and answer a hook call with its selector. Result: No. No swept address returns data that starts with the called selector and has the required length, except the identity precompile, whose address 0x04 sets a return delta flag without its action flag and is rejected (src/libraries/Hooks.sol:112). The wrapped native contracts, the Celo fee contracts and the Reserve accept hook calldata and return no data, which fails the 32 byte minimum (src/libraries/Hooks.sol:152). EntryPoint v0.6 has a valid flag pattern (low bits 0x2789) and reverts on every hook selector. The CELO token (0x2438), its implementation (0x37b1 with reverting calls), the gasless whitelist (0x1b27), the blacklist (0x1727) and 0xfd fail the flag rules or revert. Evidence: https://forno.celo.org and https://rpc.xlayer.tech eth_call with each IHooks selector and from set to the PoolManager; src/libraries/Hooks.sol:109-155
- Celo, cycle 2. Whether a contract that the PoolManager calls (a hook, an unlock callback, a payout recipient or a currency) can reach the Celo transfer precompile with the PoolManager's balance as source, including through DELEGATECALL or CALLCODE. Result: No. The precompile requires input.caller to be the CELO token address. A CALL or CALLCODE from any other contract carries that contract as caller. A DELEGATECALL carries the caller of the delegating frame, which is the PoolManager when the PoolManager made the call, and the PoolManager is not the token. The inherited caller would be the token only for a contract that the token address itself calls. The deployed implementation calls the precompile, the registry and the unreleased treasury view and nothing else, and it does not call transfer recipients. An eth_call to 0xfd from the PoolManager fails for every call shape. Evidence: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/celo-org/celo-kona/HEAD/crates/celo-revm/src/precompiles/transfer.rs with https://raw.githubusercontent.com/bluealloy/revm/main/crates/interpreter/src/instructions/contract.rs and https://raw.githubusercontent.com/alloy-rs/evm/main/crates/evm/src/precompiles.rs
- Celo, cycle 2. Cycle 1 lead: does the deployed CELO token implementation (version 1.2.0.0) contain a function that passes an account other than msg.sender or an allowance checked account to the transfer precompile. Result: No. The 24 selectors in the deployed bytecode equal the function list of GoldToken.sol at tag core-contracts.v15, which returns version (1, 2, 0, 0). transfer, transferWithComment and burn pass msg.sender. transferFrom requires value to be within allowed[from][msg.sender]. The version has no mint, no fee debit and no other balance moving function. transferFrom with the PoolManager as source reverts on chain, and the PoolManager never calls approve on a currency (src/types/Currency.sol:60-96 holds the only token calls). Evidence: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/celo-org/celo-monorepo/core-contracts.v15/packages/protocol/contracts/common/GoldToken.sol and https://forno.celo.org eth_getCode of 0xFeA1B35f1D5f2A58532a70e7A32e6F2D3Bc4F7B1
- Celo, cycle 2. Faces on Celo: every way the PoolManager's native balance or a token balance can be read under a second currency id (the CELO token proxy, its implementation address, the four fee currency adapters, the wrapped native predeploy, any contract whose balanceOf returns a native balance), walked through sync, settle, take, mint and burn in each order. Result: No gain in any order. Credits arise only in _settle: msg.value when no currency is synced, or the balance rise of the one synced currency (src/PoolManager.sol:349-364). One transient slot holds the synced currency (src/libraries/CurrencyReserves.sol:27-32), and a settle with value reverts while it is set (src/PoolManager.sol:356), so one inflow is credited under one id. I walked these orders. Sync the token, take native, return it by token transfer, settle: the credit is zero. Take native, sync the token, return by token transfer, settle: the caller holds a token credit equal to the native debt and must still pay the debt. Take the token, sync address(0), settle with value: the same with the faces swapped. Sync the implementation address or an adapter, pay the real token, settle: the caller is credited under an id whose transfer reverts, so the credit cannot be taken, and the adapter scales the credit by 10^12 without any way to withdraw it. The PoolManager has no receive or fallback function, and a plain value call to the deployed contract reverts. The wrapped native predeploy keeps its own balance and is a separate asset. Evidence: src/PoolManager.sol:279-297, 349-364; https://forno.celo.org eth_call on the PoolManager (plain value call, settle with value while locked, sync for the CELO token, its implementation and an adapter)
- Celo, cycle 2. A2 on Celo: can an ordinary account raise the PoolManager's native balance inside another party's sync and settle window, or with funds that are not its own. Result: No path found. Native CELO reaches the PoolManager through settle with value, a CELO token transfer, a self destruct beneficiary or a block reward. Each of these spends the sender's own funds. Deposit mints go to the deposit sender. Fee refunds and fee credits of CIP-64 transactions go to the transaction sender, the fee recipient and the FeeHandler. Withdrawals from the wrapped native predeploy pay msg.sender only, and the PoolManager never calls withdraw. A party that syncs the CELO token and then funds the PoolManager is credited what it paid. Evidence: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/celo-org/celo-kona/HEAD/crates/celo-revm/src/handler.rs (credit_gas_fees arguments caller, fee_recipient, fee_handler); src/PoolManager.sol:349-364
- Celo, cycle 2. Opcode differential on Celo: does the client change any opcode or call pattern the PoolManager relies on (TSTORE and TLOAD, CALL with value, CALLVALUE, SELFBALANCE, STATICCALL, RETURNDATASIZE and RETURNDATACOPY, MCOPY, PUSH0, gas forwarding, calls to addresses without code, precompile dispatch). Result: No change found. CeloEvm uses the revm mainnet instruction table for the chain spec, and the precompile map is the OP Stack set plus the transfer precompile. The transfer precompile refuses static contexts, so a balanceOf call made by sync cannot move native value. A probe CALL to an address without code returns success with empty return data, as core assumes for the A4 case. The one address where a plain CALL fails on Celo and succeeds on Ethereum is 0xfd, which makes a take that names it revert. Evidence: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/celo-org/celo-kona/HEAD/crates/celo-revm/src/evm.rs and https://raw.githubusercontent.com/celo-org/celo-kona/HEAD/crates/celo-revm/src/precompiles.rs; https://forno.celo.org eth_call creation probes
- X Layer, cycle 2. Opcode differential on X Layer: does the OKX client change any opcode, the precompile set or call semantics. Result: No change found. revm 40.0.3 comes from crates.io without a patch. The OKX op-revm builds the EVM with the mainnet instruction table and the OP Stack precompile set, and its precompile file has no X Layer entry. The X Layer changes sit in the handler (fee handling of gasless transactions) and in the block executor (the two system calls). Probe calls to 0xfd, 0x0100, the identity precompile and an address without code return what they return on Ethereum. Evidence: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/okx/xlayer-reth/main/Cargo.toml and https://raw.githubusercontent.com/okx/optimism/main/rust/op-revm/src/evm.rs; https://rpc.xlayer.tech eth_call creation probes
- X Layer, cycle 2. Cycle 1 critic gap and lead: where does the X Layer client discard transient storage between two transactions of one block, including the gasless whitelist call, the blacklist call, blacklisted deposits and the flashblocks builder (A1). Result: Transient storage is cleared on every path. The executor and the builder run each transaction with Evm::transact, which ends in the journal's finalize, and finalize, commit_tx and discard_tx each clear transient storage. The whitelist and blacklist lookups are system calls whose result state is dropped. On success they end in finalize and on error the OKX code calls discard_tx. A blacklisted or failed deposit goes through checkpoint_revert and commit_tx. One path does not discard the journal: catch_error for a rejected non-deposit transaction. Such a rejection is raised during validation, before any contract code has run, so no TSTORE can precede it. I did not trace every error variant to confirm that last statement. Evidence: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/bluealloy/revm/main/crates/context/src/journal/inner.rs with https://raw.githubusercontent.com/okx/optimism/refs/tags/xlayer/v0.1.7/rust/alloy-op-evm/src/lib.rs and https://raw.githubusercontent.com/okx/xlayer-reth/main/crates/builder/src/flashblocks/context.rs
- X Layer, cycle 2. Cycle 1 lead: which caller address does the gasless whitelist system call use, and can it reach the PoolManager as address(0), the current protocol fee controller (A12, A8). Result: No. The caller is 0xfffffffffffffffffffffffffffffffffffffffe, the call goes to the whitelist proxy only, and its state changes are never committed. The blacklist lookup uses the same caller. A call made onward by either contract would carry that contract as msg.sender and would be discarded with the rest of the call. collectProtocolFees and setProtocolFee compare msg.sender with the stored controller (src/ProtocolFees.sol:36, 48). Evidence: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/okx/optimism/refs/tags/xlayer/v0.1.7/rust/alloy-op-evm/src/block/xlayer_gasless_contract.rs
- X Layer, cycle 2. Whether a gasless transaction can create native OKB or move value that the sender does not hold (A2, A3). Result: No. The handler rejects a gasless transaction whose sender balance is below its value. It then leaves the balance unchanged, and the call frame moves the value from the sender as for any transaction. Fee deduction, refund and vault payments are skipped, so no account is credited. The earlier bug in this feature left the base fee check relaxed for later transactions of a block and concerned fees only. Evidence: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/okx/optimism/refs/tags/xlayer/v0.1.7/rust/op-revm/src/handler.rs

LiquidityController and NativeAssetLiquidity revert on balanceOf and transfer. The bridge wrapped tokens and USDT0 answer under one address each in the sweep. Tokens with a second entry point among the smaller holdings were not searched for and are listed as a lead. Evidence: https://rpc.xlayer.tech eth_call sweep with from set to the PoolManager
- Celo, X Layer, cycle 2. Known weakness: the reth trie iterator bug fixed upstream on 3 November 2026 (pull request 28264), which can drop a leaf from an incremental state root. Result: No path to PoolManager funds. The bug makes a node compute a wrong state root, stall or serve a wrong proof. It does not change what a transaction executes. xlayer-reth v0.0.7.3-rc.1 integrates the fix as a mandatory patch. For Celo two secondary reports state that celo-kona shipped a backport, and I did not confirm which build the sequencer runs. A stall delays every PoolManager transaction and loses nothing, because core has no time dependence. Evidence: https://github.com/paradigmxyz/reth/pull/28264 with https://github.com/okx/xlayer-reth/releases and https://www.0xcert.com/advisory/0xCERT-2026-0317
- Celo, cycle 2. Known weaknesses of the Celo client and precompile from the last two years: the missing STATICCALL guard in the transfer precompile (Nethermind review, fixed October 2025), the warm slot leak of the fee currency context (fixed May 2026), the June 2026 security review, the node divergence on CIP-64 blocks after a storage migration (issue 192) and the open issues on CIP-64 refunds. Result: None gives an ordinary account a way to move PoolManager funds. With the guard missing, a static call into the CELO token still reverted at the Transfer event, and the guard is present in the current source. The warm slot leak and the refund issue change gas charges. Issue 192 was a history index lost in a node migration and made single nodes reject valid blocks. The June 2026 review reports no critical or high issue. Evidence: https://www.nethermind.io/audits/celo-hokulea-integration with https://github.com/celo-org/celo-kona/pull/79, https://github.com/celo-org/celo-kona/pull/214 and https://github.com/celo-org/celo-kona/issues/192

Known weaknesses of the X Layer client: the public issue that lists 13 alleged vulnerabilities (issue 276), the tracing failure after gasless transactions (issue 277) and the gasless base fee bypass fix. Result: None reaches PoolManager funds. Issue 277 is an RPC tracing defect. The base fee bypass let zero priced transactions pass validation and moved no balance. Pooled assets on Celo: do transfer and balanceOf of the tokens the PoolManager holds behave in a way a holder can use (fee on transfer, rebase on transfer, callbacks, special recipients, zero amounts). - Celo, cycle 3. Leads L-153 and L-202 for Celo: does the fee currency debit or credit, or any other client feature, run code inside a call in progress under a transient storage map separate from the caller's while keeping its transfers and storage writes. Result: No. The debit and the credit are steps of the transaction handler and run before the first frame of the main call and after its last frame has returned. A contract cannot start them. The debit starts from the empty map of a new transaction and the handler clears its transient writes before the main call (handler.rs lines 695 to 698). The credit runs on the same journal as the main call and clears transient storage when it ends (core_contracts.rs lines 241 to 248). The fee currency must be registered in FeeCurrencyDirectory, which Governance owns, so the code that runs is not chosen by the caller. The other system calls of the client read exchange rates through call_read_only, which reverts everything it did. unlock is one call frame (src/PoolManager.sol:104-114), so neither step can separate a take from its debit. Evidence: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/celo-org/celo-kona/HEAD/crates/celo-revm/src/handler.rs; https://raw.githubusercontent.com/celo-org/celo-kona/HEAD/crates/celo-revm/src/contracts/core_contracts.rs; https://raw.githubusercontent.com/celo-org/celo-kona/HEAD/crates/celo-revm/src/contracts/erc20.rs

Lead L-203 on both chains: can a call frame carry value that the caller's balance did not lose in the same journal (fee currency transactions and deposits with mint on Celo, gasless transactions and deposits on X Layer, the transfer precompile). Result: No. On Celo a fee currency transaction is rejected when its value exceeds the sender's native balance, a deposit's mint is added to the sender before execution, and the value then moves in the call frame (handler.rs lines 773 and 805 to 815). The transfer precompile uses the journal transfer and halts on an error, and it accepts only the CELO token as caller (transfer.rs lines 52 to 57 and 91 to 125). On X Layer a gasless transaction is rejected when the sender balance is below the value and the balance is otherwise left as it is, and a deposit adds its mint first (handler.rs lines 113 to 143 and 178 to 188). The one branch that raises a balance to the value runs only with the balance check disabled, which block production does not use. A native credit in core is msg.value (src/PoolManager.sol:352-354), and on both chains that value has left the caller's balance. Evidence: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/celo-org/celo-kona/HEAD/crates/celo-revm/src/handler.rs; https://raw.githubusercontent.com/celo-org/celo-kona/HEAD/crates/celo-revm/src/precompiles/transfer.rs; https://raw.githubusercontent.com/okx/optimism/refs/tags/xlayer/v0.1.7/rust/op-revm/src/handler.rs

- Celo, cycle 6. Opcode differential on Celo at the production tag: does the client that produces blocks change TSTORE and TLOAD (rollback on revert, clearing at the end of a transaction), CALL with value, CALLVALUE, SELFBALANCE, STATICCALL, RETURNDATASIZE and RETURNDATACOPY, MCOPY, PUSH0, gas forwarding, calls to accounts without code, or precompile dispatch. Result: No. Tag celo/reth-v1.0.10 takes revm from a fork whose instruction files, journal, call frame and handler are byte identical to upstream tag v107, and CeloEvm::new uses the upstream instruction table for the block spec. The one addition is the transfer precompile at 0xfd, which the PoolManager can reach only as the recipient of a take or as a currency address. Both calls fail there, because the caller is not the CELO token, so the take reverts (src/types/Currency.sol:44-52 and 60-86). The sweep of this cycle shows 0xfd failing on all sixteen shapes. The repository's settlement path relies on transient storage being cleared per transaction (src/libraries/CurrencyReserves.sol:15-38, src/libraries/Lock.sol:10-27, src/libraries/CurrencyDelta.sol:18-41), which commit_tx, discard_tx and finalize of that journal do. Evidence: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/celo-org/celo-kona/refs/tags/celo/reth-v1.0.10/Cargo.toml

Opcode differential on X Layer at the mainnet release tag: the same list of opcodes and call patterns, read in the revm version and the OKX execution crates that tag v0.0.7.3-rc.1 builds. Result: No difference found. revm 40.0.3 comes from crates.io and equals upstream tag v112, where the transient map is cleared in commit_tx, discard_tx and finalize, TSTORE fails in a static frame, value moves before precompile dispatch and a call to an account without code returns success with no data. The OKX fork leaves op-revm evm.rs and precompiles.rs without an X Layer branch and its six consensus files are identical between tag xlayer/v0.1.7 and the newest xlayer-dep tag. X Layer changes sit in the handler (fee handling for gasless transactions) and in transact_raw (the blacklist lookup before deposits), which do not touch a call that an ordinary transaction makes to the PoolManager. Evidence: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/okx/xlayer-reth/refs/tags/v0.0.7.3-rc.1/Cargo.toml
- Celo, cycle 6. A1 on Celo at the production tag: can a value in the PoolManager's transient slots (unlock flag, deltas, synced currency and reserves) cross from the fee debit into the main call, or from one transaction into the next, for a transaction that pays gas in a fee currency. Result: No. The debit runs inside a checkpoint and the handler clears the transient map after committing it, before the main call (handler.rs lines 616 to 690). The credit uses the committing system call path and call_inner clears the transient map after it (erc20.rs lines 103 to 137, core_contracts.rs lines 211 to 250). The debit and the credit execute the code of a registered fee currency and never the PoolManager, so they cannot write its transient slots. A sync left open by the main call (src/PoolManager.sol:279-288) is still set while the credit runs, and the credit pays the sender, the block beneficiary and the fee handler, none of which is the PoolManager. Evidence: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/celo-org/celo-kona/refs/tags/celo/reth-v1.0.10/crates/celo-revm/src/handler.rs
- Celo, cycle 6. Can an ordinary account make the Celo node call the PoolManager, or a contract of its own, with msg.sender equal to address(0), by naming that address as the fee currency of a transaction. The protocol fee controller is address(0), and collectProtocolFees checks the sender only (src/ProtocolFees.sol:44-57). Result: No. The handler rejects a transaction whose fee currency is missing from the fee currency context before it makes any call to that address (handler.rs lines 509 to 588 at tag celo/reth-v1.0.10), and the context is loaded from FeeCurrencyDirectory, which Governance owns. The calls the node makes with caller address(0) carry the selectors of balanceOf(address), debitGasFees and creditGasFees. The PoolManager has none of the three, since its balanceOf takes an owner and an id (src/ERC6909.sol:17). Evidence: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/celo-org/celo-kona/refs/tags/celo/reth-v1.0.10/crates/celo-revm/src/handler.rs
- Celo, X Layer, cycle 6. Critic gap of cycles 2 and 5: repeat the special address sweep with a forwarding stub at the PoolManager address, so that tx.origin differs from msg.sender as in a real take, sync or hook call. Sixteen shapes (empty calldata with and without value, transfer with 0 and 1, balanceOf, ten hook selectors, unlockCallback) against the predeploy range, the precompiles, the Celo core contracts, the X Layer system contracts, the EntryPoints and the usual preinstalls, with the stub's native balance read before and after every call. Result: No target gives the caller more than it is debited. On both chains 248 of 256 predeploys revert on every shape. The targets that accept value keep it or wrap it one to one, as F-047 records, and the caller still owes the full amount (src/PoolManager.sol:291-297). No target answers transfer with success while moving a third party's balance: the successes are real tokens that need a balance of the PoolManager, accounts without code, the ecrecover and P256 precompiles and two Celo contracts with a catch all fallback (FeeHandler and Reserve), where nothing moves and the caller is debited (src/types/Currency.sol:64-74). No balanceOf answer rises inside the call sequence except where the stub paid. No target returns a hook selector except the identity precompile 0x04, whose address fails isValidHookAddress (src/libraries/Hooks.sol:109-127). The classes equal those of the cycle 2 sweep with the PoolManager as origin, so no swept contract treats the two caller shapes differently. Evidence: https://forno.celo.org and https://rpc.xlayer.tech eth_call aggregate3Value with the Multicall3 runtime code placed at the PoolManager address, blocks 83536386 and 76668110; results in the work directory files raw/sweep/celo.json and raw/sweep/xlayer.json
- Celo, cycle 6. Lead L-218, Celo half: do the deployed Universal Routers and the PositionManager sync before every native settle, do they treat the CELO token as wrapped native, and what happens to a route that names both address(0) and the CELO token. Result: No loss path. All three verified sources call sync before every settle. The PositionManager and the first Universal Router name the CELO token as WETH9, and the two later routers name a contract that always reverts. Wrap and unwrap revert, because the CELO token has neither deposit nor withdraw. Nothing needs them: both ids are backed by the native balance, a debt under the CELO token id can be paid from native value held by the periphery contract through an ordinary token transfer, and a debt under address(0) is paid with msg.value after sync(address(0)). A route that names both ids is handled as two currencies. Paying the wrong id leaves the other delta open and unlock reverts with CurrencyNotSettled (src/PoolManager.sol:112). The guard at src/PoolManager.sol:356 is not reached, because the periphery sends value only after it synced address(0). Evidence: https://celo.blockscout.com/api/v2/smart-contracts/0xcb695bc5d3aa22cad1e6df07801b061a05a0233a
- Celo, cycle 6. Lead L-246: which pools and positions hold the G$ that the issuer froze in the Celo PoolManager, and is a second currency frozen with it because the periphery offers no exit that leaves the G$ side behind. Result: One position holds 550,000,000 of the 550,022,104 G$: token id 523 in the hookless G$/USDC pool, out of range and single sided, with zero USDC. The other four open positions in G$ pools hold 21,143 G$ and less than one unit of USDm and CELO together. The periphery can close a position and give up one side through CLEAR_OR_TAKE, which calls clear for the G$ credit (src/PoolManager.sol:310-319) and takes the other currency, as F-083 describes. No material second currency is locked behind the G$ freeze. - Celo, X Layer, cycle 6. Upcoming fork, Karst on Celo and X Layer (planned for Celo in the fourth quarter of 2026 without a date, not present in the X Layer chain spec): what changes for the PoolManager and for funds inside it when a transaction is capped at 16,777,216 gas, CLZ becomes an opcode, MODEXP and P256VERIFY are repriced and predeploys are replaced by the L2 Contract Manager. Result: No loss or freeze path for an ordinary account. Liquidity removal has no loop: Pool.modifyLiquidity updates two ticks, flips at most two bitmap bits and clears at most two ticks (src/libraries/Pool.sol:146-204), so its gas does not depend on what other accounts did. A swap loops over initialized ticks (src/libraries/Pool.sol:344-437) and stops at the caller's price limit, so a swap that would exceed the cap can be sent in parts. A stranger who fills ticks with dust raises the cost of crossing them and cannot stop an exit. The PoolManager makes no fixed gas call: take, the token transfer and the hook call forward all gas (src/types/Currency.sol:48 and 73, src/libraries/Hooks.sol:134). CLZ occupies an opcode that the build for Cancun does not emit. The replaced predeploys can change which special addresses accept value or answer token calls, which is left as a lead. Evidence: https://docs.optimism.io/notices/archive/upgrade-19
- Celo, X Layer, cycle 6. Upcoming fork, Lagoon (in development, no date, announced for OP Mainnet and Unichain first): can the post execution transaction or the settlement of sequencer defined metering raise or lower a balance of the PoolManager outside a transfer (A2). Result: No. The settlement credits the sender of each refunded transaction and debits the block beneficiary, the base fee vault and the operator fee vault. The PoolManager cannot be the sender of a transaction, because it has no private signer and EIP-7702 delegation applies to accounts with a signer, and it is none of the three debited accounts. The post execution transaction itself charges no fee and moves no balance. Both chains' clients contain the plumbing, and neither chain has announced Lagoon. Evidence: https://specs.optimism.io/protocol/lagoon/post-exec.html
- Celo, X Layer, cycle 6. Upcoming fork on Ethereum, Glamsterdam (not scheduled for mainnet, earliest mid January 2027 according to the 19 November core developer call, held up by EIP-8037 and EIP-8038): does the L1 fork change execution on Celo or X Layer for the PoolManager. Result: No. The fork changes Ethereum execution and headers. The X Layer op-node release xlayer/v0.1.7 supports the new L1 header fields, and Celo moved to celo-reth because op-geth will not support the L1 fork. L2 gas rules stay at the OP Stack fork of each chain. A third party survey of 11 October 2026 found a tracking issue for Amsterdam on the OP Stack without a schedule (https://nonceworks.com/notes/glamsterdam-gas-changes-operators.html). Two side effects are operational. Nodes on op-geth cannot follow after the L1 fork, and forno still answers part of its requests from an op-geth build. The cost of an L1 deposit used as forced exit changes with L1 gas rules. The mid January estimate comes from a press report of 21 November 2026 (https://cryptoslate.com/ethereums-glamsterdam-delay-reveals-a-troubling-pattern-behind-its-biggest-network-upgrades/). Evidence: https://blog.ethereum.org/2026/11/06/glamsterdam-8037-8038
- Celo, cycle 6. Proposed change on Celo, migration to the second custom gas token design of the OP Stack: would the new predeploys NativeAssetLiquidity and LiquidityController, or the changed value rules of the other predeploys, give an ordinary account a way to move the PoolManager's native balance or to be credited for value it did not pay. Result: Not from the published specification. NativeAssetLiquidity accepts calls from LiquidityController only. LiquidityController.mint is limited to minters that the owner of the L1 ProxyAdmin authorises, and burn needs a caller that sends its own value. A mint to the PoolManager address by an authorised minter would raise the native balance without a settle, which is a governance action. The value sink at L2ToL1MessagePasser that F-047 lists for Celo would close, as it is closed on X Layer. Celo has not published its migration, so the fate of the CELO token proxy and of the transfer precompile under that design is an open lead. Evidence: https://specs.optimism.io/protocol/custom-gas-token/predeploys.html

A listed hash or an appointed operator would each add a leaf. The finding F-046 describes a capability that has not left a trace in state. Result: No. revm-interpreter 37.0.3 (crates.io, the version X Layer pins) converts the amount with as_usize_saturated and calls the ruint shift only when it is below 256, returning zero or the sign fill otherwise; BYTE calls byte() only for an index below 32 (instructions/bitwise.rs lines 107-158). The advisory states the shifted values were correct and only the flags were wrong apart from the truncation above 2^32, which the guard excludes. ruint 1.18.0 byte() indexes the little endian limb slice directly (bits.rs lines 71-82). 3,045 new vectors with amounts k*2^32 + r, 2^64 + r, 2^128 + r and 2^255 + r for SHL, SHR, SAR, BYTE and SIGNEXTEND on seven values, each sent three times, gave 0 mismatches on both networks. Evidence: https://static.crates.io/crates/revm-interpreter/revm-interpreter-37.0.3.crate; https://static.crates.io/crates/ruint/ruint-1.18.0.crate; https://raw.githubusercontent.com/rustsec/advisory-db/main/crates/ruint/RUSTSEC-2026-0220.md; research/network-risk/cycles/011/op-stack-custom-gas.work/out/shift32.json; research/network-risk/cycles/011/op-stack-custom-gas.work/scripts/shift32.py
- X Layer, cycle 11. ruint fixes between 1.18.0 and 1.21.1 that could change an EVM result on X Layer: the div_3x2_ref fix of 1.21.0, the shift flag fix of 1.20.0 and the mul_mod fix of the unreleased branch. Result: div_3x2_ref is a reference function used only in tests; production division in knuth.rs and small.rs calls div_3x2, which is div_3x2_mg10 (src/algorithms/div/small.rs line 18). The mul_mod fix concerns the rewritten 1.21.0 path that 1.18.0 does not have. The shift fix is covered by the item above. Evidence: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/recmo/uint/main/CHANGELOG.md; https://static.crates.io/crates/ruint/ruint-1.18.0.crate
- Celo, X Layer, cycle 11. The alloy-primitives keccak cache in front of KECCAK256 on the two clients, for the 58 byte position key (src/libraries/Position.sol:60), the 64 byte delta and mapping slots (src/libraries/CurrencyDelta.sol:14) and the 160 byte pool id (src/types/PoolId.sol:14). Result: Celo's production tag does not link the cache (no fixed-cache dependency of alloy-primitives 1.6.0 in its lockfile). X Layer links it. In alloy-primitives 1.6.0 the cache key stores the length and all bytes and compares both, inputs of 0 bytes and above 87 bytes bypass it, and keccak256 uses it only with keccak-cache-global (src/utils/mod.rs lines 144-163, src/utils/keccak_cache.rs). The same 766 cache vectors as cycle 10, sent three times, gave 0 mismatches on both endpoints, so later rounds that would meet cache hits still return the specified hash. Evidence: https://static.crates.io/crates/alloy-primitives/alloy-primitives-1.6.0.crate; https://raw.githubusercontent.com/okx/xlayer-reth/refs/tags/v0.0.7.3-rc.1/Cargo.lock; https://raw.githubusercontent.com/celo-org/celo-kona/refs/tags/celo/reth-v1.0.10/Cargo.lock; research/network-risk/cycles/011/op-stack-custom-gas.work/out/keccak_cache.json

- Celo, cycle 11. Can the CIP-64 fee debit or credit on celo-kona main leave transient storage that a later frame of the user's transaction reads at the PoolManager (src/libraries/Lock.sol:13-25, src/libraries/CurrencyReserves.sol:17-36). Result: No. The debit's transient storage is cleared after the debit commits and before the main call (handler.rs around line 698). Transient storage is per contract, and the debit and credit system calls run in the registered fee currency, never in the PoolManager. Fee currencies are registered by governance. Evidence: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/celo-org/celo-kona/main/crates/celo-revm/src/handler.rs
- X Layer, cycle 11. Can an ordinary account use the X Layer gasless rule against PoolManager users. Result: No. A transaction is gasless only if the whitelist contract allows its target and calldata, and none of the PoolManager, PositionManager or Universal Router targets is allowed. The rule skips fees only; the PoolManager bytecode reads neither GASPRICE nor BASEFEE (OPCODES.md, bytecode level), and BASEFEE keeps the header value. Evidence: https://rpc.xlayer.tech eth_call getGaslessAllowance at block 0x4933197; https://raw.githubusercontent.com/okx/optimism/xlayer/v0.1.7/rust/alloy-op-evm/src/block/mod.rs

Result: The trie bug affects state roots and eth_getProof, not execution results; both clients shipped the fix (celo-reth v1.0.9, xlayer-reth v0.0.7.3-rc.1). - X Layer, cycle 20. ruint 1.18.0 (X Layer) shift and SAR code against RUSTSEC-2026-0220, read from the crate. Result: 1.18.0 has no primitive fast path: wrapping_shl and wrapping_shr call the generic overflowing loop, which returns zero once rhs / 64 reaches 4 (src/bits.rs lines 329-346 and 412-429), and arithmetic_shr fills with MAX.wrapping_shl(256 - rhs) (lines 467-478). The advisory's truncation modulo 2^32 is in the 1.19 fast paths, and its wrong flags are never read by revm-interpreter 37.0.3, which shifts only when the amount is below 256 (bitwise.rs lines 120-158). RUSTSEC-2025-0137 affects releases before 1.17.1 only. Evidence: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/rustsec/advisory-db/main/crates/ruint/RUSTSEC-2026-0220.md
