- Arbitrum One, Robinhood Chain, Elysium, cycle 3. Arbitrum family: retryable tickets, ETH deposits, unsigned parent chain messages and the native token mint precompile as sources of value without a debit. Result: No path for an ordinary account. An ETH deposit mints to the sender and moves the amount with core.Transfer without running the EVM, so no contract sees CALLVALUE. A retry transaction first moves the call value from the ticket escrow to the sender, and the EVM then debits the sender as for any message. On failure the value goes back to escrow. The escrow was funded by the submission, whose deposit comes from the parent chain. Unsigned and contract messages pay from the aliased sender's own balance. The Nitro fork of go-ethereum checks CanTransfer and calls Transfer for every caller (no system caller rule), and all three endpoints rejected an unfunded value call from the system address. ArbOwnerPublic returns getNativeTokenManagementFrom 0 and an empty native token owner list on Arbitrum One, Robinhood Chain and Elysium, all at ArbOS version word 0x74, so nobody can mint the native asset today. For Elysium this describes the RPC node, a locally built binary. The sequencer was not probed. Evidence: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/OffchainLabs/nitro/master/arbos/tx_processor.go lines 237 to 268, 538 to 565 and 838 to 846; https://raw.githubusercontent.com/OffchainLabs/go-ethereum/master/core/vm/evm.go lines 264 and 294; eth_call to 0x000000000000000000000000000000000000006b and 0x64 on https://arb1.arbitrum.io/rpc, https://rpc.mainnet.chain.robinhood.com and https://rpc.elysium.kinetiq.xyz
- Polygon, cycle 3. Polygon: system caller rule in Bor, value in state sync messages, and the 0x1010 token as a source of native value. Result: Bor checks the balance and transfers for every caller. State sync and span messages are built with From BorSystemAddress and Value 0. The 0x1010 source pays deposits and transfers out of its own native balance with a 2300 gas value call, and transfer returns false unless msg.value equals the amount, so each payout is matched by value received or by a deposit recorded on Ethereum. A deposit addressed to the PoolManager would call it with value and empty calldata and revert, since the PoolManager has no receive function. The system address holds 0.01 POL and a probe call from it moved value normally. I read the MRC20 source in the contracts repository and did not compare it with the bytecode deployed at 0x1010. Evidence: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/0xPolygon/bor/master/core/vm/evm.go lines 326 and 357; https://raw.githubusercontent.com/0xPolygon/bor/master/consensus/bor/statefull/processor.go lines 70 to 80; https://raw.githubusercontent.com/0xPolygon/bor/master/core/evm.go lines 247 to 275; https://raw.githubusercontent.com/maticnetwork/contracts/master/contracts/child/MRC20.sol; eth_call and eth_getBalance via https://polygon.drpc.org
- BNB Smart Chain, cycle 3. BNB Smart Chain: Parlia system transactions, the fee balance kept at the system address, and the stateful precompiles of the Jenner fork as sources or sinks of value. Result: Parlia system transactions are sent from the block's coinbase and pay value from its balance after the client has moved the collected fees there. Native value sent to 0xfffffffffffffffffffffffffffffffffffffffe is swept into the validator reward when the block is finalized, so a payout that names it is lost to the caller who chose it, as with any burn address. The stateful precompile entry for CAS20 tokens rejects CALLCODE and DELEGATECALL and reverts with NonPayable when the frame carries value, so the Jenner tokens add no value path. The system caller rule itself is recorded as a finding of this unit. Evidence: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/bnb-chain/bsc/master/consensus/parlia/parlia.go lines 2022 to 2052 and 2137; https://raw.githubusercontent.com/bnb-chain/bsc/master/core/vm/cas20.go lines 89 to 95; https://raw.githubusercontent.com/bnb-chain/bsc/master/core/vm/contracts_stateful.go lines 37 to 42 and 161 to 186; eth_getBalance of the system address via https://bsc-dataseed1.bnbchain.org returned 0
- Avalanche, cycle 3. Avalanche: value handling in the EVM library, the nativeAssetCall precompile (which calls a target with the precompile's caller as msg.sender) and atomic transactions. Result: libevm checks CanTransfer and calls Transfer for every caller. nativeAssetCall passes value zero to its inner call and needs at least 84 bytes of input, while the PoolManager's token call sends 68 bytes (src/types/Currency.sol:60-73). Its address ends in 0x0002, which sets the add-liquidity return flag without the after-add-liquidity flag and fails isValidHookAddress (src/libraries/Hooks.sol:109-124), so it cannot be a hook. On mainnet the precompile reverted for a well-formed call from the PoolManager address and from a second address, and nativeAssetBalance reverted too. Imports add balance without running code and exports need a signature of the debited address, as earlier cycles recorded. Evidence: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ava-labs/libevm/main/core/vm/evm.go lines 196 and 219; https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ava-labs/avalanchego/v1.15.3/graft/coreth/nativeasset/contract.go lines 101 to 172; eth_call to 0x0100000000000000000000000000000000000001 and 0x0100000000000000000000000000000000000002 via https://api.avax.network/ext/bc/C/rpc
- Monad, cycle 3. Monad: value transfer in the client, the reserve balance design at depth zero, and system transactions. Result: pre_call requires the sender balance for every call kind except DELEGATECALL and then subtracts from the sender and adds to the recipient. Because Monad admits transactions against a reserve balance, a top-level call can lack the value at execution time. The client then fails the call with InsufficientBalance, so no frame runs with unpaid value. System transactions run the staking syscall on their own state and call no other contract. The endpoint rejected an unfunded value call from the system address. Evidence: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/category-labs/monad/main/category/execution/ethereum/execute_message.cpp lines 48 to 71, 115 to 131 and 201 to 215; https://raw.githubusercontent.com/category-labs/monad/main/category/execution/monad/execute_system_transaction.cpp lines 179 to 234; eth_call via https://rpc.monad.xyz
- MegaETH, cycle 3. MegaETH: does the KeylessDeploy sandbox give the inner signer or the created contract value that nobody paid. Result: No. The outer call must carry no value. The inner creation transaction keeps the value signed in the keyless transaction, runs as a deposit-like transaction with gas price 0 and mint None, and is rejected before execution when the signer's balance is below the value. The create frame moves the value from the signer, and the merge copies every changed balance, the signer's lower balance included, into the parent journal. I read the main branch. The endpoint reports mega-reth v2.2.3 and I did not match that build to a commit. Evidence: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/megaeth-labs/mega-evm/main/crates/mega-evm/src/sandbox/execution.rs lines 215 to 217, 512 to 540 and 599 to 613; https://raw.githubusercontent.com/megaeth-labs/mega-evm/main/crates/mega-evm/src/sandbox/state_merge.rs lines 117 to 134
- Tempo, cycle 3. Tempo: can any transaction form (plain, batched 0x76, sponsored, fee token) carry value, and what does the native branch of settle and take do. Result: The handler rejects a batch when any call has nonzero value, in the gas calculation and again in validation, and the endpoint rejects a plain call with value ('value transfer not allowed'), including one from the system address. The fee payer pays in a TIP-20 token and adds no native value. With a balance placed by state override the interpreter moved value as on Ethereum, so the native branch is inert because accounts hold no native balance, which I confirmed for the probe accounts and did not confirm for every account in genesis. eth_getBalance returns the placeholder 4242...42 for every address including the system address. A native credit could in any case only be spent against address(0) pool liquidity, which nobody can fund with value. Evidence: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/tempoxyz/tempo/697ea97/crates/evm/src/handler.rs lines 366 to 374 and 1438 to 1441; eth_call and eth_getBalance via https://rpc.mainnet.tempo.xyz
- Arc, cycle 3. Arc: value in CallFrom subcalls (sender substitution), the Native Coin Authority precompile, blocklist checks on value frames and the 18 versus 6 decimal split as ways to carry or move value without an equal debit. Result: None found. The subcall path rejects a call to CallFrom that carries value, and the child call is built with CallValue::Transfer(0), so a substituted sender never sends value. The substituted sender must be the calling contract or the transaction signer. Before a CALL or CREATE frame with value starts, the client rejects the zero address, a blocklisted sender or recipient and a recipient destroyed in the same transaction, and then revm moves the value. A rejected frame moves nothing and a native payout to such a recipient reverts (src/types/Currency.sol:48-53). CALLCODE and DELEGATECALL are outside that check and move nothing. Native Coin Authority changes balances directly, only for caller 0x3600000000000000000000000000000000000000, and rejects DELEGATECALL. A value CALL moves the stated amount in 18 decimal units. Only the ERC-20 view truncates, which an earlier cycle bounded. The system address holds 0.0001 USDC and a probe call from it moved value normally. I read the main branch and the endpoint reports arc/v1. Evidence: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/circlefin/arc-node/main/crates/evm/src/evm.rs lines 250 to 261, 499 to 611 and 884 to 956; https://raw.githubusercontent.com/circlefin/arc-node/main/crates/precompiles/src/call_from.rs lines 122 to 139; https://raw.githubusercontent.com/circlefin/arc-node/main/crates/precompiles/src/native_coin_authority.rs lines 44, 120, 212 and 300; eth_call via https://rpc.mainnet.arc.io
- HyperEVM, cycle 3. HyperEVM: do system transactions from 0x2222222222222222222222222222222222222222 carry value that no EVM account pays, and can one credit the PoolManager. Result: In both public clients a system transaction runs through the ordinary transact path with base fee 0. The replay client sets only disable_eip3607 for it and the archive client only zeroes the base fee, so the value is debited from the sender's EVM balance. The bridge address holds 944,868,333 HYPE on the EVM side. A HyperCore transfer of HYPE to a contract therefore calls it with value paid by the bridge address and debited from the user on HyperCore. Sent to the PoolManager it reverts, because the call has empty calldata and the PoolManager has no receive function. Sent to another contract it is real value. The validator node is closed source, so the HyperCore debit and the node's own execution path are inferred from these clients. Evidence: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/hyperliquid-dex/hyper-evm-sync/main/src/run.rs lines 123 to 146 and 216 to 232; https://raw.githubusercontent.com/hl-archive-node/nanoreth/master/src/node/evm/mod.rs lines 101 to 117; eth_getBalance and eth_call via https://rpc.hyperliquid.xyz/evm
- all 21 networks, cycle 3. EIP-7702 delegated senders and sponsored, batched or fee-token transactions: can value appear in a frame at the PoolManager without the sender paying it. Result: No. A delegated account that calls itself sees CALLVALUE with no net debit, as any self-transfer does, and any onward call with value to the PoolManager debits that account (probe result above). Every sponsor or fee-token design read here pays gas only: Celo fee currencies, X Layer gasless transactions, Tempo fee payers (value forbidden), MegaETH keyless deploys and the planned Base type 0x79. ERC-4337 accounts pay value from their own balance through an ordinary CALL. Evidence: sources of the per-network items of this unit; eth_call with state overrides on the 21 RPC endpoints of state/networks.json, block latest, 2026-11-22

## Reading of the source (theme-mirrored-ledgers)

- all 21 networks, cycle 3. Lead L-166, method for all 21 networks. For each candidate address X the stub at the PoolManager address reads X.balanceOf(PoolManager), makes one call to X and reads the balance again, in one eth_call. Four shapes per X: a value call of 10^12 wei with empty calldata, a zero value call with empty calldata, transfer(recipient, 0) and transfer(recipient, 1). Candidates: the ERC-4337 EntryPoints v0.6, v0.7 and v0.8 on every chain, the wrapped native token, every address with code from 0x4200000000000000000000000000000000000000 to 00ff on the ten OP Stack chains, the system contracts of BNB Smart Chain and Polygon, the Avalanche and HyperEVM precompile ranges, liquid staking tokens, and the 248 largest pooled tokens. Result: The addresses whose balanceOf(PoolManager) rose on the value call are the wrapped native token of each chain (exactly 10^12 for 10^12 wei on all 20 chains that have native value), the three EntryPoints (exactly 10^12; on Tempo they have code and the value call fails, because the chain has no native value), stETH on Ethereum (999,999,999,999), wstETH on Ethereum (800,071,968,325), sAVAX on Avalanche (771,425,961,435) and qiAVAX on Avalanche (4,276 units of 8 decimals). No address raised the ledger on a zero value call or on a zero amount transfer. The EntryPoints reject transfer(address,uint256), so a credit under their id can only become a claim. For the others the full cycle with A = 10^12 wei is: sync(X) stores B (src/PoolManager.sol:279-288); take(address(0), X, A) sets the caller's delta under address(0) to minus A and sends A to X (src/PoolManager.sol:294-295, src/types/Currency.sol:48); X books r times A to the PoolManager; settle credits the caller r times A under id X (src/PoolManager.sol:358-364); take(X, caller, r times A) pays that out; the caller then pays A with msg.value to clear the native debt, because unlock needs every delta at zero (src/PoolManager.sol:112). The PoolManager's native balance and its X balance end where they started. The caller paid A and holds what a direct deposit of A into X mints, less 1 wei of rounding for stETH. No part of the cycle uses value that belonged to pools. Evidence: rpc eth_call with state override on the 21 endpoints of networks.json, 2026-11-22, blocks 26,474,032 (Ethereum), 159,896,174 (OP Mainnet), 61,003,752 (Base), 64,642,766 (Unichain), 54,348,643 (Zora), 38,027,743 (World Chain), 61,892,714 (Ink), 31,128,186 (Soneium), 83,490,366 (Celo), 76,622,089 (X Layer), 526,647,112 (Arbitrum One), 120,983,007 (Robinhood Chain), 9,697,845 (Elysium), 97,790,438 (Polygon), 135,169,352 (BNB Smart Chain), 101,112,531 (Avalanche), 124,568,074 (Monad), 32,594,114 (MegaETH), 50,343,895 (Tempo), 32,644,012 (Arc), 51,986,345 (HyperEVM); src/PoolManager.sol:279-297, 349-364

L1BlockNumber at 0x4200000000000000000000000000000000000013 answers balanceOf with the L1 block number (26,474,026 on OP Mainnet) and returns that number to transfer, which fails the success test at src/types/Currency.sol:68, so take reverts. The number is fixed within one L2 block, so a sync and settle pair inside one transaction measures zero. - Arc, cycle 3. L-166 on Arc, where the face of the native asset uses another unit: the full cycle across address(0) (18 decimals) and 0x3600000000000000000000000000000000000000 (6 decimals), and the link earlier cycles left open, namely whether native value can be forced into the PoolManager. Result: The face rejects a value call from the PoolManager, so the PoolManager cannot be made to deposit into it. transfer(recipient, 1) from the PoolManager lowers the face balance by 1 and the native balance by exactly 10^12, and transfer(recipient, 0), a transfer to itself and a transfer of one thousandth of the balance are exact. A take under the face id is therefore debited one unit per 10^12 wei paid out, and a native take is debited in wei. A read only creation probe showed that a contract created with value that self destructs to the PoolManager raises its native balance by that value, for 1 wei and for 999,999,999,999 wei, and that the face balance rises by one unit when the sum crosses a multiple of 10^12. The rounding gain per sync and settle pair is the remainder already in the balance, at most 10^12 minus 1 wei, which is under 0.000001 USDC. The remainder was 486,011,262,919 wei at block 32,645,513. The gas price was 25 gwei, so 100,000 gas for one round costs 2.5 * 10^15 wei, more than 2,500 times the largest gain. The implementation address 0xc6ad664ac6679f4ce74e10e91449c93ec1ae3ca6 still reports the same balance and rejects transfer, as recorded. - all 21 networks, cycle 3. Zero amount and dust transfers with the PoolManager as sender, for the largest pooled tokens of each network. Token lists: explorer balances of the PoolManager ranked by value on OP Mainnet, Unichain, World Chain, Ink, Soneium, Celo and MegaETH (Blockscout), on Ethereum and Avalanche (Routescan), the largest currencies of Uniswap v4 pools by tracked reserve on Base, Arbitrum One, BNB Smart Chain, Polygon, Monad, X Layer, Zora, Tempo, Arc, Robinhood Chain and Elysium (GeckoTerminal), and a hand list on HyperEVM. 248 tokens, 9 to 16 per chain. For each token: transfer(recipient, 0), transfer(recipient, 1), transfer(PoolManager, 0), a transfer of one thousandth of the balance to a plain recipient, to the PoolManager itself, to the token address and to the zero address, with the sender balance read before and after and the gas of the inner call measured. On 13 endpoints the logs of the zero amount transfer were read with eth_simulateV1. Result: In every successful call the sender balance changed by exactly the amount sent: zero for a zero amount, zero for a transfer to itself, minus the amount otherwise. On the 8 endpoints without eth_simulateV1 (World Chain, Celo, X Layer, Avalanche, Monad, MegaETH, Arc, HyperEVM) the statement about second tokens rests on the gas figures and on the balance of the token itself. ## Reading of the source (theme-nested-transient)

- all 21 networks, cycle 3. What the two dangerous shapes would do to this code, so that each network can be judged against them. Shape A: an inner run that starts with an empty transient map and whose storage writes and token transfers are kept. Shape B: an inner run, or a rollback, that drops transient writes while keeping storage writes and token transfers. Walked through unlock, sync, settle, settleFor, take, mint and burn. Result: The code has no defence of its own against either shape, so the answer rests on the chain. Shape A: sync needs no lock and stores the currency and the balance in two transient slots (src/PoolManager.sol:279-288, src/libraries/CurrencyReserves.sol:27-32). An inner run that sees no unlock flag (src/libraries/Lock.sol:23-27) can call unlock itself (src/PoolManager.sol:105-107), sync, pay, settle and mint a claim (src/PoolManager.sol:322-329), and end with its own counter at zero (src/PoolManager.sol:112). The outer run still holds the older reserves value, so its settle measures the same balance rise again (src/PoolManager.sol:358-360) and credits it a second time. Shape B: take writes the debit to a transient slot and then transfers (src/PoolManager.sol:294-295, src/libraries/CurrencyDelta.sol:32-40). If the debit and the counter increment (src/libraries/NonzeroDeltaCount.sol:18-24) are dropped while the transfer is kept, unlock passes its check at src/PoolManager.sol:112 with the tokens gone. The reverse of shape B, where transient writes survive a rollback that undoes a token transfer, lets a settle credit (src/PoolManager.sol:364) outlive the payment. burn and settleFor follow the same pattern (src/PoolManager.sol:305-307, 332-336). Calls that follow one another at the top level of one transaction (a Tempo type 0x76 batch, the phases of a Base type 0x79 transaction, user operations of one bundle) do not produce either shape: unlock opens and closes inside one call frame (src/PoolManager.sol:104-114), so between two top-level calls the flag is false and every delta is zero, and only the synced currency and reserves can carry over, which earlier cycles cleared. The remaining items of this file answer, network by network, whether shape A or B exists. No network has one that an ordinary contract can start from inside a call. Evidence: src/PoolManager.sol:104-114, 279-297, 300-307, 322-336, 349-364; src/libraries/Lock.sol:10-27; src/libraries/CurrencyDelta.sol:28-41; src/libraries/CurrencyReserves.sol:15-38; src/libraries/NonzeroDeltaCount.sol:12-34
- all 21 networks, cycle 3. On-chain test on all 21 RPC endpoints: does a call from an inner frame to any precompile, predeploy or system address change the caller's transient storage. One 3,640 byte creation payload, sent with eth_call and no to address, stores 0xaa55 in transient slot 1, then calls each of 173 addresses three ways with 20,000 gas (3,000 on HyperEVM): CALL with empty calldata, CALL with transfer(address,uint256), STATICCALL with balanceOf(address). It returns the slot and the loop counter. Result: All 21 endpoints returned 0xaa55 and a count of 173. The address list holds the standard precompiles 0x01 to 0x11 and 0x100, the OP Stack predeploys 0x4200..00 to 0x4200..2f, the ArbOS precompiles 0x64 to 0x74 with 0xc8, 0xff and 0xa4b05, the Celo transfer precompile 0xfd and the CELO token, sixteen Tempo precompile and TIP-20 addresses, the Arc range 0x1800..00 to 0x1800..09 and 0x3600..00, the HyperEVM range 0x0800 to 0x0813 with 0x2222..22, 0x3333..33 and 0x5555..55, the BNB Smart Chain and Polygon system contracts 0x1000 to 0x1008, 0x2000 to 0x2006, 0x3000 and 0x1010, the MegaETH system contracts 0x6342..00 to 0x6342..05, the Avalanche ranges 0x0100..00 to 02 and 0x0200..00 to 05, and the two Base precompiles 0x8130..aa01 and aa02. The test uses zeroed arguments, so it shows that no special address resets or replaces the transient map on a plain call. It does not exercise the function of each precompile. The items below cover the features that take specific input. Evidence: eth_call on the rpc URL of each entry in research/network-risk/state/networks.json at the latest block on 2026-11-22 (for example Ethereum near block 26473884, Tempo near 50340613, HyperEVM near 51984554); payload sha256 prefix 519864eafc678a1d
- all 21 networks, cycle 3. On-chain test on all 21 RPC endpoints: is transient storage restored on every way a frame can fail, and is it restored to the earlier nonzero value. The earlier critic probe covered REVERT. This probe creates a child contract and calls it so that the child writes transient slot 1 and then ends with REVERT, with INVALID, by running out of gas in a loop, and with REVERT after a nested call that itself succeeded and wrote slot 2. It then lets a write succeed, repeats the reverting call, and runs the same writes through DELEGATECALL against the parent's own slot. Result: All 21 endpoints returned the same 15 words: slot 1 and slot 2 read zero after each of the four failures, slot 1 reads 0x55 after the successful write and still 0x55 after a later reverted write of 0x11, and the parent's slot reads 0xaa after a reverted and after an INVALID delegatecall and 0x55 after a successful one. A settle credit or a take debit written in a frame that fails is therefore undone together with the token transfer of that frame on every network, including the clients that do not use revm or go-ethereum (Tempo with evm2, Monad, HyperEVM). The result describes the RPC node of each network. Evidence: eth_call with no to address on the rpc URL of each entry in research/network-risk/state/networks.json, latest block on 2026-11-22, data 
- Tempo, cycle 3. Tempo. Type 0x76 batches, precompiles that might call out to contracts, the storage credit settlement that removes transient slots, T14 configurable accounts and the zone contracts. For each: can a contract start it from inside a call, which transient map does it use, and are transient writes journaled like storage writes. Result: No feature gives a second transient map. The mainnet node reports tempo/v1.19.0-697ea97, and the manifest at that commit pins evm2 at revision 66687c18 (the main branch pins e25a95fb today, which is the revision an earlier cleared item quoted). A type 0x76 batch runs every call as a top-level frame with the signer as caller under one checkpoint (handler.rs lines 1277 to 1372, checkpoint at 1289, rollback at 1339), and the calls share one transient map that is not cleared between them. An ordinary contract cannot start a batch. evm2 keeps one transient map per transaction (state/mod.rs line 59), journals each TSTORE (lines 806 to 836), restores it in rollback (lines 891 to 898) and clears it in clear_transaction_state (lines 523 to 539). Every call frame and every precompile call takes a checkpoint from that journal and rolls back on failure (evm/mod.rs lines 1691 to 1795). Tempo precompiles run native code through a storage provider that offers sload, sstore, tload, tstore, events and checkpoints and has no function that calls a contract (precompiles/src/storage/mod.rs lines 92 to 280, dispatch at precompiles/src/lib.rs lines 309 to 342), so no precompile runs caller-chosen code. take_transient_storage removes slots part way through settlement, and its only caller passes the storage credits address 0x1060..00 (state/mod.rs lines 842 to 859, handler/config.rs lines 444 to 455), so PoolManager slots are untouched. T14 is not active on mainnet: eth_getCode at 0xAACC000000000000000000000000000000000000 returned 0x near block 50341036 while the T7 and T8 precompiles return 0xef. The specification of TIP-1107 registers a configurable account before any call runs and outside the rollback checkpoint, and the code does the same (handler.rs line 1693), so it is a top-level step that touches no PoolManager state. Zone contracts are ordinary EVM bytecode on the main chain (ZonePortal implementation 23,994 bytes at 0x5AD1..00, ZoneMessenger 1,858 bytes at 0x5A4D..00, and nextZoneId() on the factory returned 4), so a callback from them is an ordinary call on the same journal, and the zone itself is a separate chain where this PoolManager does not exist. Not confirmed: whether validators run the evm2 JIT backend, and whether its TSTORE path matches the interpreter. Both probes above passed on the public RPC node. Evidence: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/tempoxyz/tempo/697ea97/crates/evm/src/handler.rs; https://raw.githubusercontent.com/tempoxyz/tempo/697ea97/crates/evm/src/handler/config.rs; https://raw.githubusercontent.com/tempoxyz/tempo/697ea97/crates/precompiles/src/lib.rs; https://raw.githubusercontent.com/tempoxyz/tempo/697ea97/crates/precompiles/src/storage/mod.rs; https://raw.githubusercontent.com/alloy-rs/evm2/66687c18b34d3bdbb899f5eb7605070615c03475/crates/evm2/src/evm/state/mod.rs; https://raw.githubusercontent.com/alloy-rs/evm2/66687c18b34d3bdbb899f5eb7605070615c03475/crates/evm2/src/evm/mod.rs; https://tips.sh/1107; eth_getCode and eth_call on https://rpc.mainnet.tempo.xyz
- Base, cycle 3. Base. Type 0x79 Base Transactions, the B20, policy, nonce and transaction context precompiles, and validity transactions. Can any of them run caller-chosen code under another transient map, or drop transient writes while keeping storage writes. Result: No. The node reports base/v1.5.6 on reth v2.5.2 and that release builds on revm 42. Type 0x79 belongs to the Everest upgrade, which the Base upgrade page lists with no date for Sepolia or mainnet, and the latest mainnet block held only types 0x7e, 0x2 and 0x0. In the v1.5.6 source each phase takes one journal checkpoint, a failed phase is reverted through it and a completed phase is committed (eip8130.rs lines 1260 to 1344). revm restores transient storage in checkpoint_revert, so a reverted phase loses its transient writes together with its storage writes and transfers. The specification states that every call is dispatched from the sender, so phases are top-level calls and no contract can start one. Phases of one transaction share the transient map, which gives the sender nothing beyond what a contract with several calls has. The Base precompiles reach state through a provider with sload, sstore, tload, tstore, events and checkpoints and no function that calls a contract (precompile-storage/src/provider.rs lines 34 to 140). Validity transactions add inclusion conditions and no execution context. Evidence: https://docs.base.org/specifications/base-transactions; https://docs.base.org/upgrades/overview; https://raw.githubusercontent.com/base/base/v1.5.6/crates/common/evm/src/eip8130.rs; https://raw.githubusercontent.com/base/base/v1.5.6/crates/common/precompile-storage/src/provider.rs; web3_clientVersion and eth_getBlockByNumber on https://mainnet.base.org/
- Arbitrum One, Robinhood Chain, Elysium, cycle 3. Arbitrum One, Robinhood Chain and Elysium. Stylus host calls, retryable redeems started with ArbRetryableTx.redeem from inside a call, and the group rollback of the sequencer. Does any of them execute code under a transient map other than the one of the running transaction, or undo transient writes apart from storage writes. Result: No. A Stylus program reaches other contracts through closures that call evm.Call, evm.DelegateCall and evm.StaticCall on the EVM that is already running (arbos/programs/api.go lines 186 to 190), and its transient host calls read and write the same StateDB under the acting address (lines 119 to 127). A contract called by a Stylus program therefore sees the PoolManager's lock flag and deltas as any other callee does. redeem only emits RedeemScheduled. The node builds the retry transaction from that log after the scheduling transaction has finished and appends it to the queue as its own transaction (tx_processor.go lines 924 to 950, block_processor.go line 719), and an earlier cleared item showed that every transaction starts with StateDB.Prepare. The group rollback saves a checkpoint for a user transaction and the redeems it scheduled and restores whole transactions (block_processor.go lines 125 to 134 and 583 to 594), so storage, balances and transient state go back together. Not confirmed: Arbitrum One and Robinhood Chain report nitro v3.13.0-rc.9 at commit b72783f, and neither that tag nor that commit is served by raw.githubusercontent.com. I read master and v3.12.0, whose api.go has the same call sites. Elysium reports a locally built binary. Both probes above passed on all three RPC nodes. Evidence: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/OffchainLabs/nitro/master/arbos/programs/api.go; https://raw.githubusercontent.com/OffchainLabs/nitro/v3.12.0/arbos/programs/api.go; https://raw.githubusercontent.com/OffchainLabs/nitro/master/arbos/tx_processor.go; https://raw.githubusercontent.com/OffchainLabs/nitro/master/arbos/block_processor.go; web3_clientVersion on https://arb1.arbitrum.io/rpc, https://rpc.mainnet.chain.robinhood.com and https://rpc.elysium.kinetiq.xyz
- MegaETH, cycle 3. MegaETH. The KeylessDeploy sandbox is the one feature on the 21 networks with shape A: it runs caller-chosen init code in a second EVM with a new journal over live state and merges the resulting state into the parent. Can an ordinary contract start it from inside a call, and is transient state merged back. Result: It cannot be started from inside a call, and transient state is not merged. The interceptor returns without acting when the call is inside a sandbox or its depth is not zero (system/intercept.rs lines 295 to 303). The sandbox builds a new context over a database wrapper and runs one transaction in it (sandbox/execution.rs lines 583 to 650), and the sandbox sources never copy transient storage in either direction, so the inner run starts empty and its transient values are dropped. On the public RPC node near block 32592160, eth_call straight to 0x6342000000000000000000000000000000000003 with keylessDeploy(bytes,uint256) and a one byte payload reverted with 0xae1270d3, which is MalformedEncoding() and shows interception at depth zero. The same calldata sent from a creation frame, one level down, failed with return data 0x1894f076, which is NotIntercepted(), the revert of the Solidity stub. A sandbox is therefore the first frame of a transaction whose target is the KeylessDeploy address. The parent has run no contract code before it and runs none after it, so the PoolManager has no transient state in the parent that the sandbox could bypass, and inside the sandbox unlock, sync, settle and take share one map. The latest block held transaction types 0x7e, 0x0 and 0x2, each of which has one top-level call. I did not enumerate the transaction types the node accepts, and the lead below asks for that. Not confirmed: which mega-evm revision mega-reth v2.2.3 pins. I read the main branch, version 1.7.3, and the on-chain result agrees with it. Evidence: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/megaeth-labs/mega-evm/main/crates/mega-evm/src/system/intercept.rs; https://raw.githubusercontent.com/megaeth-labs/mega-evm/main/crates/mega-evm/src/sandbox/mod.rs; https://raw.githubusercontent.com/megaeth-labs/mega-evm/main/crates/mega-evm/src/sandbox/execution.rs; https://raw.githubusercontent.com/megaeth-labs/mega-evm/main/crates/system-contracts/contracts/KeylessDeploy.sol; eth_call on https://mainnet.megaeth.com/rpc with and without a to address
- Arc, cycle 3. Arc. On-chain test of the CallFrom precompile at 0x1800000000000000000000000000000000000003: does the child call it starts see the transient storage of the surrounding transaction, and are the child's transient writes kept. Earlier cycles answered from the main branch source only. Result: The child runs on the same map. With state overrides I placed a probe at the Multicall3From address 0x522fAf9A91c41c443c66765030741e4AaCe147D0, which is one of the two callers the precompile accepts, and a counter contract at a second address. The counter returns its transient slot 2 and adds 0x22 to it. The probe called the counter directly, then through callFrom, then directly again. The three readings were 0, 0x22 and 0x44 near block 32640276, both with the helper and with tx.origin as the substituted sender. An empty map for the child would give 0 as the second reading, and dropped child writes would give 0x22 as the third. The same probe at an address outside the allowlist failed at the precompile call. The source agrees: init_subcall rejects callers outside the allowlist, static context, value and a sender that is neither the caller nor the transaction signer, and pushes the child onto the same frame stack with a checkpoint from the same journal (evm.rs lines 884 to 952 and 1031 to 1040), and a failed child is rolled back through that checkpoint (lines 1228 to 1231). Evidence: eth_call with state overrides on https://rpc.mainnet.arc.io; https://raw.githubusercontent.com/circlefin/arc-node/main/crates/evm/src/evm.rs; https://raw.githubusercontent.com/circlefin/arc-node/main/crates/precompiles/src/call_from.rs; https://raw.githubusercontent.com/circlefin/arc-node/main/crates/execution-config/src/call_from.rs
- Celo, cycle 3. Celo. The fee currency calls debitGasFees and creditGasFees that the node makes around a CIP-64 transaction. Can a contract start them, which transient map do they use, and is anything discarded between them and the main call. Result: They are node calls at the top level and use the map of the transaction. The sequencer RPC reports the op-geth fork at commit c7ed55b8. In that source innerExecute calls StateDB.Prepare, which replaces the transient map, at state_transition.go line 602, and the debit runs after it inside preCheck at line 605. The credit runs after the main call has returned (line 824). Both go through evm.CallWithABI on the same EVM and StateDB (contracts/fee_currencies.go lines 88 and 154). Nothing clears transient storage between the debit, the main call and the credit, and no opcode or precompile lets a contract trigger either call. By the time the credit runs, unlock has returned or the main call has reverted, so the flag is false and all deltas are zero (src/PoolManager.sol:112-113). The fee currency is chosen from the governance list, so no caller-chosen code runs in these calls. Whether a listed token calls out to untrusted code during credit stays with the open lead of the Celo unit. Evidence: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/celo-org/op-geth/c7ed55b8/core/state_transition.go; https://raw.githubusercontent.com/celo-org/op-geth/c7ed55b8/contracts/fee_currencies.go; web3_clientVersion on https://forno.celo.org
- HyperEVM, cycle 3. HyperEVM. The sendToEvmWithData action that makes the node call coreReceiveWithData on a linked contract, and CoreWriter. Can an ordinary contract start either from inside a call so that code runs under another transient map. Result: No, on the documentation and the public clients. sendToEvmWithData is an action signed on HyperCore and posted to the exchange endpoint. The documentation describes Core to EVM transfers as credited by a system transaction that calls the linked contract as the system address. A system transaction is a transaction of its own, and earlier cycles read in the archive client that each one runs through a single transact call with transient storage cleared at its end. The inner run therefore starts with an empty map because it is a different transaction, and no PoolManager unlock can be open around it. A contract on HyperEVM cannot start one within its own call: transfers back to HyperCore are picked up from Transfer logs after execution, as the documentation states, and CoreWriter at 0x3333333333333333333333333333333333333333 emits a log that HyperCore processes as an action after execution, with a delay of a few seconds for some actions. Both probes above passed on the RPC node, including the calls to 0x3333333333333333333333333333333333333333 and 0x2222222222222222222222222222222222222222. Not confirmed: the validator binary is closed, so the statement that no in-call path exists rests on documentation, on the archive client and on these probes. Evidence: https://hyperliquid.gitbook.io/hyperliquid-docs/for-developers/hyperevm/hypercore-less-than-greater-than-hyperevm-transfers; https://hyperliquid.gitbook.io/hyperliquid-docs/for-developers/api/exchange-endpoint; https://hyperliquid.gitbook.io/hyperliquid-docs/for-developers/hyperevm/interacting-with-hypercore; eth_call on https://rpc.hyperliquid.xyz/evm
- Monad, cycle 3. Monad. Whether optimistic parallel execution, the call frame model of the client or the staking precompile gives a call a transient map of its own, and whether a failed frame restores transient storage together with storage. Result: No. Transient storage is a field of the per-account state object next to storage (account_state.hpp line 70, accessors at lines 126 to 154). The state keeps a version stack per account: entering a frame pushes a version, a write copies the account state into the new version, pop_accept folds it into the parent and pop_reject drops it (state.cpp lines 129 to 183, version_stack.hpp). Storage and transient storage of an account are therefore kept or dropped by the same operation. An earlier cleared item showed that each execution attempt of a transaction builds a new State. The staking contract source contains no call into the EVM host, and precompiles.cpp dispatches only the standard precompiles, so no precompile runs caller-chosen code. Both probes above passed on the RPC node. I did not read the JIT compiler's TSTORE path. Evidence: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/category-labs/monad/main/category/execution/ethereum/state3/state.cpp; https://raw.githubusercontent.com/category-labs/monad/main/category/execution/ethereum/state3/account_state.hpp; https://raw.githubusercontent.com/category-labs/monad/main/category/execution/ethereum/state3/version_stack.hpp; https://raw.githubusercontent.com/category-labs/monad/main/category/execution/monad/staking/staking_contract.cpp; https://raw.githubusercontent.com/category-labs/monad/main/category/execution/ethereum/precompiles.cpp
- Avalanche, cycle 3. Avalanche. The nativeAssetCall precompile at 0x0100000000000000000000000000000000000002 transfers an Avalanche native asset and then calls an address chosen by the caller, keeping the original caller as msg.sender. Is it active, and which state does its inner call use. Result: It is switched off, and it used the same state when it was active. From the Banff rules on, all three native asset addresses map to DeprecatedContract, whose Run returns ErrExecutionReverted (params/hooks_libevm.go lines 113 to 122, nativeasset/contract.go line 178). eth_call to the address with 84 zero bytes on the public endpoint returned execution reverted. The earlier implementation took a StateDB snapshot and called env.Call on the running EVM (nativeasset/contract.go lines 146 to 171), so its callee shared the transient map of the transaction. The endpoint reports avalanchego 1.15.3, the release I read. No other C-Chain precompile takes a call target. Evidence: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ava-labs/avalanchego/v1.15.3/graft/coreth/params/hooks_libevm.go; https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ava-labs/avalanchego/v1.15.3/graft/coreth/nativeasset/contract.go; eth_call on https://api.avax.network/ext/bc/C/rpc
- Polygon, BNB Smart Chain, cycle 3. Polygon and BNB Smart Chain. Can a precompile or a system contract path run caller-chosen code with a separate transient map, and does the parallel executor of Bor give a task a map that outlives the task. Result: No. In Bor v2.11.0 and in BSC v1.8.2 (the version the BSC endpoint reports) a precompile implements RequiredGas, Run(input) and Name, and Run receives only the input bytes (core/vm/contracts.go lines 51 to 55 and 56 to 60), so a precompile has no handle on the EVM and cannot start a call. Both clients replace the transient map in StateDB.Prepare (Bor statedb.go line 3051, BSC statedb.go line 1532). Bor's parallel tasks run ApplyMessage, which calls Prepare, on a state object of their own (parallel_state_processor.go lines 101 to 150 and 451). State sync records and Parlia system transactions run at the top level between user transactions, as earlier cycles recorded. A public Polygon endpoint reports bor v2.11.1-private, one patch above the source I read. Both probes above passed on both networks. Evidence: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/0xPolygon/bor/v2.11.0/core/vm/contracts.go; https://raw.githubusercontent.com/0xPolygon/bor/v2.11.0/core/state/statedb.go; https://raw.githubusercontent.com/0xPolygon/bor/v2.11.0/core/parallel_state_processor.go; https://raw.githubusercontent.com/bnb-chain/bsc/v1.8.2/core/vm/contracts.go; https://raw.githubusercontent.com/bnb-chain/bsc/v1.8.2/core/state/statedb.go
- Worldchain, X Layer, cycle 3. World Chain and X Layer. PBH bundles, and the node additions of both chains that I could locate (the World Chain EVM crate and the X Layer bridge intercept crate). Does any of them run user code in a context of its own inside a transaction. Result: No. A PBH transaction is a standard OP transaction that targets the PBHEntryPoint contract, and a PBH bundle is a standard ERC-4337 bundle, so every user operation runs as a nested call of one transaction on one journal. The builder checks proofs and orders transactions. The World Chain manifest at tag v2.8.2, the version the endpoint reports, pins revm 43.0.2, and the EVM crate on the main branch holds configuration, an EVM factory, execution wiring and caches, and its lib.rs and factory.rs name no precompile. The X Layer intercept crate inspects the logs of a finished transaction in the payload builder and drops the whole transaction when a bridge event matches, which is a decision about inclusion. The gasless rule of X Layer was covered by an earlier cleared item and I did not read it again. Both nodes keep the revm journal, where transient storage is cleared in commit_tx, discard_tx and finalize and restored in checkpoint_revert (journal/inner.rs lines 141 to 250 and 622 to 638). Both probes above passed on both networks. I did not read every crate of either node. Evidence: https://worldcoin.github.io/world-chain/pbh/txs.html; https://raw.githubusercontent.com/worldcoin/world-chain/v2.8.2/Cargo.toml; https://raw.githubusercontent.com/worldcoin/world-chain/main/crates/evm/src/factory.rs; https://raw.githubusercontent.com/worldcoin/world-chain/main/crates/evm/src/lib.rs; https://raw.githubusercontent.com/okx/xlayer-reth/main/crates/intercept/src/lib.rs; https://raw.githubusercontent.com/bluealloy/revm/main/crates/context/src/journal/inner.rs
- Ethereum, Optimism, Unichain, Zora, Ink, Soneium, cycle 3. Ethereum and the OP Stack chains without node additions (OP Mainnet, Unichain, Zora, Ink, Soneium). EIP-7702 delegated accounts, ERC-4337 bundles, deposit transactions, and any frame style transaction type. Is there an execution context with its own transient map inside a transaction. Result: No. EIP-1153 defines transient storage as discarded after every transaction and shared by all frames of the transaction. Delegated code under EIP-7702 runs in an ordinary frame at the account's address, and an ERC-4337 bundle is one transaction that calls the EntryPoint contract, so both use the one map. No frame transaction type is live: the latest Ethereum block (26473884) held types 0x0, 0x2, 0x3 and 0x4 and its header has no field beyond the Osaka set, and the latest blocks of the five OP Stack chains held types 0x7e, 0x2 and 0x0. The endpoints report reth or op-reth builds, which keep the revm journal (transient storage at journal/inner.rs line 68, cleared at lines 141 to 250, restored at lines 622 to 638, written at lines 1080 to 1105). Both probes above passed on all six networks. The Unichain PoolManager is a predeploy with other bytecode, and this item speaks about the chain, as the other Unichain items do. Evidence: https://eips.ethereum.org/EIPS/eip-1153; https://raw.githubusercontent.com/bluealloy/revm/main/crates/context/src/journal/inner.rs; eth_getBlockByNumber and web3_clientVersion on the rpc URL of each of the six networks

## Reading of the source (theme-balance-reconcile)

- Ethereum, Optimism, Base, Unichain, Ink, Monad, BNB Smart Chain, cycle 4. Wrapped native tokens showed the largest unexplained rise: 298.98 WETH on Ethereum, 18,572.57 WMON on Monad, 13.85 WBNB, 5.77 WETH on Base, 1.05 on Unichain, 0.47 on Optimism and 0.02 on Ink in one day. Does the PoolManager gain wrapped native without paying?. Result: No. On each chain the difference equals the sum of Deposit(dst, wad) logs with the PoolManager as dst, to the base unit (359 such logs on Ethereum). A native take to the wrapper address makes the PoolManager call the wrapper with value and empty calldata (src/types/Currency.sol:48), the wrapper credits msg.sender, and the caller is debited the native amount (src/PoolManager.sol:294). A sync and settle around it credit the same amount in the wrapped currency. Value is conserved one to one. Evidence: research/network-risk/cycles/004/theme-balance-reconcile.work/raw/verify_1.log and verify_10, 130, 143, 56, 8453, 57073: column afterWrap is 0 for every wrapped native row
- Arc, cycle 4. Arc: USDC at 0x3600000000000000000000000000000000000000 rose 415.53 beyond its Transfer logs in one day, and 0xfffffffffffffffffffffffffffffffffffffffe emitted 86,069 Transfer logs naming the PoolManager. Is any of this an unpaid gain or a shortfall?. Result: No. The native balance change of the PoolManager, 4,952.463804115787157019 in 18 decimals, equals the net of the logs from 0xff..fe exactly, and the ERC-20 balance equals the native balance divided by 1e12 and rounded down at both blocks. The difference at the ERC-20 address is value that moved as msg.value or by native take. This is the two faces of one balance already recorded in F-032 and F-050. All other 261,428 currencies on Arc reconcile. Evidence: https://rpc.mainnet.arc.io eth_getBalance at blocks 32,501,227 and 32,671,826; research/network-risk/cycles/004/theme-balance-reconcile.work/raw/reconcile_5042.json.gz
- Ethereum, Polygon, cycle 4. Monerium EURe has two token addresses over one ledger: 0x3231cb76718cdef2155fc47b5286d82e6eda273f and 0x39b8b6385416f4ca36a20319f70d28621895279d on Ethereum, 0x18ec0a6e18e5bc3784fdd3a3634b31245ab704f6 and 0xe0aea583266584dafbb3f9c3211d5588c73fea8d on Polygon. Both are pool currencies (30 and 36 Initialize logs on Ethereum, 21 and 27 on Polygon) and balanceOf(PoolManager) is identical at both. Can one deposit be credited in both currency ids, or one face be paid from the other's pools?. Result: No path found. Only one currency can be synced at a time (src/libraries/CurrencyReserves.sol:27-32), settle resets it (src/PoolManager.sol:361), and a credit always equals a real rise of the shared balance, while every take debits the id it names. The sum of what both ids are owed therefore stays equal to the shared balance. The older address logs only its own transfers, so it fails the reconcile (minus 433.38 and minus 5,812.69 in the window) while the newer one passes. The PoolManager holds 4,188.47 EURe on Ethereum and 67,861.00 on Polygon. Evidence: research/network-risk/cycles/004/theme-balance-reconcile.work/raw/reconcile_1.json.gz and raw/reconcile_137.json.gz, rows for the four addresses; src/libraries/CurrencyReserves.sol:27-32
- Ethereum, cycle 4. Currency 0x4f95c5ba0c7c69fb2f9340e190ccee890b3bd87c on Ethereum reports a PoolManager balance that fell 3.4 percent with no Transfer log. What is it?. Result: It is the Frax custodian contract FrxUSDCustodianUsdc, named as a currency in a pool by mistake or on purpose. Its balanceOf returns the frxUSD balance of the account: both calls return 75,016,586,273,325,944,925,532 for the PoolManager. frxUSD itself reconciles. A credit in this currency id needs a real frxUSD payment that is then stranded, so the mirror gives nothing to its user. Same class as F-050. Evidence: https://eth.drpc.org eth_call balanceOf(PoolManager) on the custodian and on frxUSD 0xcacd6fd266af91b8aed52accc382b4e165586e29; https://sourcify.dev/server/v2/contract/1/0x0a2d27a86a2ea07bcc34e457c65aeca7631c0f10?fields=sources,abi,compilation
- Ethereum, Polygon, Base, BNB Smart Chain, cycle 4. Reflection and fee tokens: KISHU on Ethereum, #GMM and HKU on Polygon, Share and BRTM on Base, PIT, ASS, DRP, CATE and GFH on BNB Smart Chain, and RISE on Ethereum. Any transfer by anyone raises the PoolManager balance of a reflection token. Can a caller profit by bracketing its own transfer with sync and settle, and does a payout cost the PoolManager more than the debited amount?. Result: No profit path. The caller pays the whole fee and is credited only the PoolManager's share of the reflected part, which is its share of supply: 0.00007 percent for KISHU, 4.6 percent for BRTM, 5.2 percent for Share. The BRTM source takes the fee only on transfers to or from a listed pair and its burn is limited to the bonding curve. RISE: the PoolManager balance fell by 1,231,670.27 while the log shows 1,170,086.75 to the recipient, a ratio of 0.95, and the next hop shows the same ratio, so the fee comes out of the amount sent and the PoolManager loses what was debited. I could not fetch the trace for the RISE payout and did not read the five BNB Smart Chain tokens. Evidence: https://sourcify.dev/server/v2/contract/8453/0x74f84a0add717a6c405b2c8c0b82d94b514e113e?fields=sources,abi,compilation lines 187-201 and 258-300; research/network-risk/cycles/004/theme-balance-reconcile.work/raw/classified.json

Tokens whose Transfer logs name the PoolManager while no balance moves: a look-alike USDC at 0x20204018a5a97149168faa73477bd5db9756a141 on Polygon and 130 contracts on BNB Smart Chain. Result: Harmless for core. The Polygon token logged a transfer of 377.85 from the PoolManager while its reported balance went from 0 to 377.85. The 130 BNB Smart Chain contracts had no code at the first block, log transfers from the PoolManager, and revert on balanceOf. The PoolManager never called them; core does not read logs. They matter only to explorers and indexers. Evidence: research/network-risk/cycles/004/theme-balance-reconcile.work/raw/unreadable_56.json and raw/mismatch_137.json

On HyperEVM the PoolManager received one Transfer in a day and holds no stHYPE (balance 0 at three blocks), so the rebasing face in F-043 is not pooled today. The 231 mismatches of the first pass were an artefact: old-block multicalls sent to https://mainnet.base.org came back with the same value for both blocks, while single calls to four endpoints agreed with the logs for the three tokens I rechecked. - all 21 networks, cycle 4. Do calls that one contract makes one after another inside one transaction meet the same transient map of the PoolManager, and does sync leave its two values behind when the call ends. One eth_call per network to Multicall3.aggregate3 with the calls exttload(currency slot), sync(token), exttload(currency slot), exttload(reserves slot), token.balanceOf(PoolManager), sync(address(0)), exttload(currency slot), exttload(reserves slot). Result: Yes on all 21 networks. Before the first sync the currency slot read zero. After sync(token) the next call read the token address in the currency slot and a reserves value equal to balanceOf(PoolManager). After sync(address(0)) the currency slot read zero and the reserves slot kept the old number, which is harmless because the native branch of _settle never reads it (src/PoolManager.sol:353-354). This is the shape of every contract level carrier: sibling calls of one caller in one transaction. I recomputed the four slot constants from their comments and they match (src/libraries/Lock.sol:8, NonzeroDeltaCount.sol:9-10, CurrencyReserves.sol:11-13). The Multicall3 code on Zora differs from the Ethereum code in bytes and has the same length; the probe passed there as well. Evidence: research/network-risk/cycles/004/theme-shared-transaction.work/probe_chain.json (eth_call on the rpc URL of each network in state/networks.json); https://eips.ethereum.org/EIPS/eip-1153

- all 21 networks, cycle 4. Every state an ordinary account can leave in the PoolManager for the next party in the same transaction, and who is credited what when a later party pays. Walked in the source for the order: attacker calls sync(X) while the PoolManager holds R, then either sends d of X by plain transfer (balance R+d) or removes d inside an unlock of its own by burning claims and taking X (balance R-d); then the victim pays X or pays native. Result: The lock flag is false and all deltas are zero after any unlock (src/PoolManager.sol:105-113), and take, settle, settleFor, clear, mint, burn, swap, modifyLiquidity and donate all require the unlocked state (lines 147, 189, 258, 291, 300, 305, 310, 322, 332). The only leftover is the pair (synced currency X, reserves R). Inside its own later unlock the attacker cannot call settle without consuming the leftover (line 361), so a lower balance needs claims burned and taken, and a higher balance needs a plain transfer. Victim pays X and calls sync(X) first: the sync stores the current balance (line 286), the victim is credited exactly its own transfer (line 360), and a donated d stays in the PoolManager without an owner. Victim pays native and calls sync(address(0)) first: the currency slot is zero (line 283) and the victim is credited msg.value (line 354). Victim pays native without sync: revert at line 356, which is the finding of this unit. Victim calls settle with zero value and no sync: with balance R+d it is credited d of X, the attacker's own gift, and with balance R-d the checked subtraction at line 360 reverts. A settle never credits one currency for a payment made in another, because the credited currency and the measured balance come from the same slot (lines 350, 358-359, 364). settleFor changes the recipient only (lines 305-307). Evidence: src/PoolManager.sol:104-114, 279-289, 291-336, 349-365; src/libraries/CurrencyReserves.sol:15-38
- all 21 networks, cycle 4. How the Universal Router and the v4 PositionManager at the addresses in state/networks.json pay the PoolManager, from their verified source: sync before a token settle, sync(address(0)) before a native settle, settle without a sync of their own, exttload of the reserves or currency slot, settleFor. 77 deployments on 21 networks. Result: All 77 pay through one function, DeltaResolver._settle, whose text is the same in every verified build: return when the amount is zero, then poolManager.sync(currency), then settle with value for the native currency, or _pay followed by settle for a token (DeltaResolver.sol lines 38 to 48). _pay is a token transfer by the router or a Permit2 transferFrom to the PoolManager (PositionManager.sol lines 522 to 529, Permit2Payments.sol lines 42 to 45), so no other external call sits between sync and settle. No source line calls settle outside this function, none calls settleFor, and exttload is used for deltas, the delta count and the lock flag only. 54 deployments are verified on Sourcify. The other 23 were matched by runtime code after zeroing PUSH20 to PUSH32 operands: 20 equal a verified deployment on another network, and the three first routers on X Layer, MegaETH and Tempo equal each other, with the MegaETH one verified on Blockscout as a partial match with the same _settle. The HyperEVM and Elysium builds use 500 optimizer runs and hold the sync and settle selectors as shifted constants (0x29610465 shifted left by 226 bits equals the sync selector). None of these contracts holds the reserves or currency slot constant in its code. A stale sync therefore cannot change what these routers are credited, and a native payment through them does not revert. Evidence: research/network-risk/cycles/004/theme-shared-transaction.work/routers_fetched.json, code_groups.json, slot_reads.json; https://sourcify.dev/server/v2/contract/1/0x66a9893cc07d91d95644aedd05d03f95e1dba8af?fields=sources,compilation; https://sourcify.dev/server/v2/contract/1/0xbd216513d74c8cf14cf4747e6aaa6420ff64ee9e?fields=sources,compilation; https://sourcify.dev/server/v2/contract/999/0x0d7Ab5B3db668128Aff6F70C4eBC71D7d4DA9bf9?fields=sources,compilation; https://megaeth.blockscout.com/api/v2/smart-contracts/0x47837eb80db5908eabba9105626d9b348bea7b02

- all 21 networks, cycle 4. Can an attacker that runs later in the same transaction settle to itself a surplus that a victim's token payment left behind. Result: No surplus exists to take. A payer that follows sync, transfer, settle is credited the whole balance rise and the settle resets the currency slot (src/PoolManager.sol:358-361), so the next party starts from a zero slot and its own sync records the full balance. The canonical routers, the 0x Settler and every replayed router that pays tokens do follow that order, and none of the 251 scanned contracts reads the leftover slots to size a payment. A victim that sent tokens and then failed to settle them would itself revert on a nonzero delta when its unlock ends (src/PoolManager.sol:112), which undoes the transfer. Tokens sent to the PoolManager outside any unlock and never settled can be claimed by the next caller of sync and settle only if that caller synced before the transfer, which the sender controls by never sending first. Evidence: src/PoolManager.sol:104-114, 349-365; research/network-risk/cycles/004/theme-shared-transaction.work/slot_reads.json
- all 21 networks, cycle 4. Do the canonical routers keep transient state of their own that one user's operation could leave for the next user in the same transaction. Result: No. The Universal Router stores the caller in a transient locker slot when execute begins and writes zero when it ends (Lock.sol modifier isNotLocked, Locker.sol), and the PositionManager does the same (ReentrancyLock.sol). A revert undoes the write. The maximum input amount slot of the Universal Router is the only other transient slot in its source. These slots belong to the router's address and say nothing about PoolManager funds. Evidence: https://sourcify.dev/server/v2/contract/1/0x23617e59A5925b2A4Bf75d73ff6711cD0b29De85?fields=sources,compilation; https://sourcify.dev/server/v2/contract/1/0xbd216513d74c8cf14cf4747e6aaa6420ff64ee9e?fields=sources,compilation

## Reading of the source (theme-transfer-quota)

- Ethereum, Optimism, Base, Unichain, X Layer, Arbitrum One, Robinhood Chain, Elysium, Polygon, BNB Smart Chain, Avalanche, Monad, MegaETH, Tempo, HyperEVM, Ink, cycle 4. L-259 on the sixteen networks with a trace endpoint: does a take of the whole PoolManager balance that is repaid in the same transaction leave any storage changed, in the token or in any contract it calls. Method: Multicall3 runtime code placed by state override at the PoolManager address and at a second address, transfer of the full balance out and back, state diff of the round trip, the same round trip three times with balances read after every step, and for every token with a clean round trip a one way transfer of half the balance with its state diff. Token lists: the most active currencies of each PoolManager by Transfer logs of the last day and all priced holdings from the balance reconcile sweep of this cycle, the lists of cycle 3, GeckoTerminal Uniswap v4 pools, and every pooled token with a balance on HyperEVM, Tempo, MegaETH and X Layer. Result: No token keeps a count or a volume of transfers per sender, a cooldown or a last transfer block for the PoolManager that a repaid take can use up. Coverage: Ethereum 304 tokens (304 traced, blocks 26475322 to 26475361); Optimism 108 tokens (108 traced, blocks 159903969 to 159904258); Base 253 tokens (248 traced, blocks 61081750 to 61081750); Unichain 34 tokens (34 traced, blocks 64658362 to 64658362); X Layer 107 tokens (107 traced, blocks 76637685 to 76638664); Arbitrum One 195 tokens (195 traced, blocks 526700807 to 526701162); Robinhood Chain 201 tokens (201 traced, blocks 121133905 to 121139717); Elysium 300 tokens (300 traced, blocks 9752024 to 9752024); Polygon 262 tokens (262 traced, blocks 97800833 to 97801219); BNB Smart Chain 39 tokens (39 traced, blocks 135204514 to 135208099); Avalanche 75 tokens (75 traced, blocks 101130625 to 101130625); Monad 111 tokens (111 traced, blocks 124619495 to 124619495); MegaETH 67 tokens (67 traced, blocks 32609710 to 32610811); Tempo 73 tokens (73 traced, blocks 50372931 to 50374937); HyperEVM 262 tokens (262 traced, blocks 52002201 to 52003492); Ink 94 tokens (94 traced, blocks 61908538 to 61909282). The round trip left no storage change for 2,302 of 2,480 traced tokens. For the rest the changes are of these kinds, none of which can make a later take or payment fail: balance checkpoints that add one entry per block (FXS, LDO, RHUB, PACDAO, PEAK); Aave style tokens, where a full transfer clears the collateral flag of the PoolManager in the Aave pool and updates incentive indexes, with no effect for an account without debt; Compound v3, Pendle, Radiant, Neverland, Benqi and DeltaPrime reward or index updates; rebasing tokens with rounding of one base unit; the deposit timestamp of the PoolManager in the Hop swap contract; the USDG timestamp on X Layer (see finding); holder lists and reward trackers that change for the recipient only. I retested 40 tokens of these kinds with 25 consecutive round trips in one call. 39 succeeded with the final balance equal to the starting balance. The call for uPEG on Ethereum, an ERC-404 style token, ran out of a 45 million gas allowance and gave no result. The one way diff differed from the plain pattern of two balance slots for 111 of 2,281 tokens: storage credit slots on Tempo, holder counts, dividend corrections, reward trackers and tokens that refused the transfer. The only one that enforces a limit is ViciCoin on Polygon (see finding). Tokens that refuse a transfer from the PoolManager are listed in a separate item. Evidence: eth_call with state override on the rpc endpoints of networks.json and debug_traceCall (prestateTracer, diffMode) on https://eth.drpc.org, https://optimism.drpc.org, https://base.drpc.org, https://unichain.drpc.org, https://xlayer.drpc.org, https://arbitrum.drpc.org, https://robinhood.drpc.org, https://elysium.drpc.org, https://polygon.drpc.org, https://bsc.drpc.org, https://avalanche.drpc.org, https://megaeth.drpc.org, https://rpc.monad.xyz, https://rpc.mainnet.tempo.xyz, https://rpc.purroofgroup.com and https://rpc-qnd.inkonchain.com, 2026-11-23
- Zora, Worldchain, Soneium, Celo, Arc, cycle 4. L-259 on Zora, World Chain, Soneium, Celo and Arc, where no public endpoint served debug_traceCall: three and then 25 consecutive round trips of the full PoolManager balance in one eth_call with state override, with balances read after each step. Result: No failure in a later round and no balance change. Coverage: Zora 41 tokens (0 traced, blocks 54356439 to 54356974); Worldchain 851 tokens (0 traced, blocks 38035539 to 38036199); Soneium 70 tokens (0 traced, blocks 31136518 to 31136530); Celo 92 tokens (0 traced, blocks 83507056 to 83507096); Arc 299 tokens (0 traced, blocks 32674810 to 32674810). The 25 round test ran on 41 tokens on Zora, 67 on Soneium, 87 on Celo, the 200 first tokens on World Chain and 299 on Arc, all without a failed step. This rules out a cooldown, a rule of one transfer per block, a count limit below 50 transfers and a gross volume cap below 25 times the PoolManager balance, and a net cap below the balance. A counter with a higher cap would not show, because the state diff could not be read on these five networks. For wBRL and wARS the source closes that gap (separate item). Evidence: eth_call with state override on https://rpc.zora.energy/, https://worldchain-mainnet.g.alchemy.com/public, https://rpc.soneium.org, https://forno.celo.org and https://rpc.mainnet.arc.io, 2026-11-23; debug_traceCall refused by these and by zora.drpc.org, worldchain.drpc.org, soneium.drpc.org, celo.drpc.org, arc.drpc.org and the thirdweb endpoints of the five chain ids
- Robinhood Chain, Ink, Arbitrum One, Ethereum, X Layer, cycle 4. USDG (Paxos) on Robinhood Chain, Ink, Arbitrum One, Ethereum and X Layer: does the reward accounting count transfers or volume of the PoolManager, and can a repaid take make a later transfer revert. Result: No. On Robinhood Chain, Ink, Arbitrum One and Ethereum payoutGroupIdOf(PoolManager) is 0 and _transfer takes the path that writes two balance words. The traced round trips on Robinhood Chain (17.03 million USDG) and Ink left no storage change. On X Layer the PoolManager is in payout group 2 and only its timestamp field changed (see finding). _applyDelta saturates at zero and the 64 bit conversions bound balances at 18 trillion USDG, so no counter can be driven to a revert by transfers. Evidence: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/paxosglobal/paxos-token-contracts/master/contracts/ClaimableRewardsBase.sol lines 206 to 233 and 473 to 619; rpc eth_call payoutGroupIdOf(PoolManager) on the endpoints of chain ids 4663, 57073, 42161, 1 and 196 at blocks 121,136,395, 61,908,924, 526,702,099, 26,475,378 and 76,638,290; debug_traceCall on https://robinhood.drpc.org and https://rpc-qnd.inkonchain.com
- Robinhood Chain, Monad, Ink, BNB Smart Chain, Base, Tempo, cycle 4. The tokens that L-259 names: stock tokens on Robinhood Chain (SPY, NVDA, GOOGL), wrapped stock tokens on Monad (wSPYx, wSPCXx, wTSLAx, wEWYx) and Ink (WSPYX, WQQQX), SPCXB on BNB Smart Chain, B20 tokens on Base (AMDc, OUSD, CIGARETTE) and all 73 pooled TIP-20 and ERC-20 tokens on Tempo: state diff of a full round trip and of a one way transfer from the PoolManager address. Result: The round trip left no storage change for any of them, and three consecutive round trips succeeded. A one way transfer of a B20 token changes the two balance slots of the token address and nothing else. A one way TIP-20 transfer changes two balance slots and the storage credit counter of the token at 0x1060000000000000000000000000000000000000, which is gas accounting (separate item). - Celo, Worldchain, cycle 4. wBRL (0xD76f5Faf6888e24D9F04Bf92a0c8B921FE4390e0) and wARS (0x0DC4F92879B7670e5f4e4e6e3c801D229129D90D) on Celo and World Chain: transfer limits, cooldowns or counters in the implementation. Result: None. The Celo implementation LatamStable overrides _update only to check a pause flag and, when enforcement is switched on, a block list for sender and recipient. It has no per address amounts, counts or timestamps. On Celo enforceBlocklist() returns false and isBlocked(PoolManager) returns false for both tokens. On World Chain the proxies point at the same implementation addresses with a shorter code (8,746 bytes against 9,856) that does not answer enforceBlocklist. I did not read that older code. On both networks 25 consecutive round trips of the full PoolManager balance succeeded.
