- Arc, cycle 6. Arc: group the 194,252 hook addresses by code and examine the ten largest groups. Result: Grouping by code hash gives 193,626 different hashes, because nearly every hook is deployed once per pool with its own constants. Grouping by code size and flag bits gives 605 groups. The ten largest: 5175 bytes, flags 0x2044, 180653 hooks, 0 with holdings, about 0 USD; 10423 bytes, flags 0x20cc, 11999 hooks, 0 with holdings, about 0 USD; 12193 bytes, flags 0x840, 298 hooks, 0 with holdings, about 0 USD; 5205 bytes, flags 0x2044, 94 hooks, 0 with holdings, about 0 USD; 16139 bytes, flags 0x840, 77 hooks, 7 with holdings, about 1 USD; 4102 bytes, flags 0xcc, 52 hooks, 0 with holdings, about 0 USD; 8951 bytes, flags 0x80, 45 hooks, 0 with holdings, about 0 USD; 19222 bytes, flags 0xc4, 21 hooks, 6 with holdings, about 36 USD; 1478 bytes, flags 0x2080, 19 hooks, 0 with holdings, about 0 USD; 19351 bytes, flags 0x5c7, 18 hooks, 8 with holdings, about 113 USD. The two largest groups (180,653 hooks of 5,175 bytes and 11,999 hooks of 10,423 bytes) hold no claims, none of the 14 most used currencies and no native balance, reject initialize from an ordinary account with 0x3f94bdf3 and answer the swap callbacks with 0xe524afd1 and the pool id for a pool they did not create. The groups that accept any initialize return a zero delta or revert for a foreign pool. The ten groups hold about 150 USD together. None has verified source on Sourcify or the Arc explorer. One sample per group was probed. Evidence: https://rpc.mainnet.arc.io
- Ethereum, Base, BNB Smart Chain, Avalanche, Robinhood Chain, cycle 6. Single token bonding curve hooks with flags beforeInitialize, beforeAddLiquidity, beforeSwap, beforeSwapReturnDelta that hold native ETH, BNB or AVAX (SatoHook 0x0000f07d2b5f1ddf3244b8780f972f306efd2888 with 981.27 ETH, SurtHook, Sat1Hook, VitaHook, SatopegHook on Ethereum, BloomHook, HookTemplate, J3sseHook on Base, three SatoHook copies and AizoHook on BNB Smart Chain, one on Avalanche, NakamotoHook with 25.89 ETH on Robinhood Chain): they accept a second pool. Can it reach the reserve?. Result: No. SatoHook source lines 224 to 231: beforeInitialize requires currency0 native, currency1 the hook's own token, fee 3000 and this hook, so a second pool can differ in tick spacing only. beforeSwap (253 to 272) checks the two currencies again and trades against one curve state (ethCum, totalMintedFair), so every pool of the hook is the same market for the same token. beforeAddLiquidity always reverts. The probe confirms it for the family: foreign pairs revert with InvalidPool and only the own pair with another tick spacing is accepted. For the hooks other than SatoHook I relied on the probe and on the matching error selectors, without reading each source. Evidence: https://sourcify.dev/server/v2/contract/1/0x0000f07d2b5f1ddf3244b8780f972f306efd2888
- Ethereum, Arc, cycle 6. RobinVistaHook 0xc2988a37d611779ad34b561231ee33603d15a0cc on Ethereum (160 pools, claims of 9.24 ETH plus PEPE, UNI, ONDO and others, about 18,100 USD) keeps accrued and banked fees per launch token, and poolIdOf[launchToken] is overwritten on every registerPool. Can an account register a second pool of a token with another base currency and withdraw in it? LongHook 0xfb6369c30573f9af1b88314c732fca944a34e0cc on Arc has the same mappings. Result: Not through the deployed factory. The ledger has the Klik shape: fees are added to accrued[launchToken] in the base token of the swapping pool and withdrawn in the base token of the pool that poolIdOf[launchToken] points at (hook lines 178 to 199, 296 to 366). registerPool and beforeInitialize accept allowed factories only, and one FactorySet log exists, for RobinVistaFactory 0x5407f136d0ddd6e6edcf5d2720ee7e26eeb9ac9a. Its launchToken (lines 309 to 419) deploys a new clone token for every launch and takes the base token from an owner curated registry, so each launch token has one pool and one base token. The fault would open if the owner allowed a factory that registers a pool for an existing token. For LongHook I read the mappings and the factory gate only, and did not read its factory. Evidence: https://sourcify.dev/server/v2/contract/1/0x5407f136d0ddd6e6edcf5d2720ee7e26eeb9ac9a
- Ethereum, cycle 6. OndexHook 0xf6ce7756e6813f259a2b2bcb746f8cf0042fe0cc (179 pools, claims of 1.68 ETH, ONDO, SPCXon, TSLAon, about 5,400 USD), LaunchHook 0x322dcec4958c14e021a9f1cd49df11b9457968cc (6,691 pools, about 10,000 USD of claims), LaunchpadHook 0x51768f5da32ba2008304cc81674da51acb802888 (211 pools) and EthCreatorFeeHookV3 0x35fe236ea82f7cf525c9719d7df8f49f94d720cc (346 pools): under what is the fee ledger stored and who may initialize?. Result: OndexHook stores treasury, creator, holder and liquidity amounts in ledger[PoolId] (lines 100 to 108) and accepts initialize from its factory only (258 to 263). LaunchHook stores launches per pool id, its FeeEscrow is claimable[recipient][currency], and beforeInitialize requires the hook itself as sender. LaunchpadHook stores curves per pool id and creatorEthOwed per coin, all 211 pools pair with native ETH, and beforeInitialize requires a curve already registered for the pool id. EthCreatorFeeHookV3 stores its configuration per pool id and accepts the registrar of that configuration only. None of them pays from a ledger that omits both the pool id and the currency. Evidence: https://sourcify.dev/server/v2/contract/1/0xf6ce7756e6813f259a2b2bcb746f8cf0042fe0cc
- Ethereum, cycle 6. TurbineHook 0x1be2e33d8f468c09c1aa9e53d54e400470b2a088 (three pools, claims of 14,720 USDC and 0.4 WETH): beforeInitialize registers any currency pair with tick spacing 1 from any caller, and beforeSwap mints input claims and burns output claims. Can a pool opened by a stranger burn the claims of the real pools?. Result: No. beforeSwap, mint and burn carry the routerOnly modifier (lines 222 to 280 and 370 to 424), so only swaps sent by the Turbine router reach the claim moves, with the output amount supplied by that router. The hook keeps reserve0 and reserve1 per pool id and updates them with checked arithmetic, and a source comment at line 246 states that the ERC-6909 balance cannot be used because it aggregates all pools of the hook. A new pool starts with zero reserves, so a swap out of it reverts on the subtraction. The router itself was not read. Evidence: https://sourcify.dev/server/v2/contract/1/0x1be2e33d8f468c09c1aa9e53d54e400470b2a088
- Robinhood Chain, Arc, X Layer, Base, cycle 6. Launch pad hooks named in L-395 that have verified source: CashCatHook and CashCatHookV2, PonsV2MemeHook, the proxy 0x4eb1976978756bd56802d8162f2271844924e0cc and FablesRamp on Robinhood Chain, MinaraFeeHook, WonkHook and LaunchHook on Arc, TaxLaunchHook on X Layer and Base. Is the ledger that decides a payout stored under the pool id, a token or a currency, and who may initialize?. Result: All are stored under the pool id or under the currency that is paid. CashCatHookV2: pending and tab per pool id, platformTab per currency, initialize from the factory only and currency0 must equal the configured quote (line 273). CashCatHook: per pool id, native quote only. PonsV2MemeHook: pendingFees, pendingCreatorTax and pendingBuyback per pool id and currency, factory only. 0x4eb19769 is an ERC-1967 proxy of LunchTaxHookPair: accruedQuote per pool id, owed per recipient and quote token, launcher only. FablesRamp: range ledgers per pool, distributorOwed and claimFeeOwed per currency, initialize needs a fee cap configured for the pool id. MinaraFeeHook: creatorAccrued per pool id, platformAccrued per currency, launcher only with an allowed quote. WonkHook: per pool id and currency, initialize needs a registered launch. TaxLaunchHook: configuration and fee slots per pool id, escrow per recipient and currency, factory only. The factories were not read, so whether a launcher may choose the quote currency is answered only where the hook checks it (CashCatHookV2, MinaraFeeHook). ZoraV4CoinHook 0x0469a4bd3724dc86c9542f4694c976da13c450c0 on Base holds nothing in the currencies checked and rejects initialize. Evidence: https://sourcify.dev/server/v2/contract/4663/0x75a54357d9c78a2db19004a5fdc76c50f9242aec
- Ethereum, Base, Robinhood Chain, cycle 6. The unverified hook 0xc81fd894c0ace037d133af4886550ac8133568e8 (6,024 bytes, same address on three networks) holds 550.25 WETH on Ethereum, 2.70 cbBTC and 1.65 WETH on Base and stock tokens on Robinhood Chain, about 1.1 million USD. Can an ordinary account open a pool on it?. Result: Not by the probe. initialize reverts in beforeInitialize with 0x55e83950 for all seven PoolKey variants, including its own currency pair with another tick spacing. Called from the PoolManager address with a foreign PoolKey, beforeAddLiquidity reverts with 0x880bb123, beforeSwap with 0x19cfd260 and beforeDonate with 0xc4bfabc3, and afterSwap returns a zero delta. The code was not decompiled, so the owner and any registration path are unread. This is the largest unread balance in the ranking and is listed as a lead. Evidence: https://ethereum-rpc.publicnode.com
- Robinhood Chain, Ethereum, cycle 6. Other large single market hooks: UniwallHook 0xbef9c77ec3c1a0d92c4cb6264f8923b37a63eae0 (126.84 ETH of claims, one pool), the Sazare hooks 0x02973ca0c6f13cec5dfd9262f1cef08c4082a888 (92.73 WETH) and 0xbbe4baf7d38b7465beddffeaf29f96fc50c8a888 (10.63 WETH) on Robinhood Chain, and Angstrom 0x0000000aa232009084bd71a5797d089aa4edfad4 on Ethereum (268,605 USDC, 144,472 USDT, 108.26 WETH). Result: Each rejects initialize from an ordinary account in all seven variants (InvalidPool, 0x0dc149f0, empty revert) and each swap callback reverts for a foreign PoolKey. UniwallHook source: every callback carries a modifier that checks the PoolKey and beforeInitialize reverts with Unauthorized. The Sazare proxies and Angstrom were judged from the probe. Angstrom balances are deposits of its own users under its own ledger, which I did not review. Evidence: https://rpc.mainnet.chain.robinhood.com
- Ethereum, Arbitrum One, BNB Smart Chain, Monad, cycle 6. UniswapV4KEMHook 0x4440854b2d02c57a0dc5c58b7a884562d875c0c4 (107 pools on Ethereum, claims of about 4,700 USD in many currencies, also on Arbitrum One and BNB Smart Chain, same code on Monad at 0x4445520306c9c70952bdfec28f3989f53d9f80c4) and the unverified 0x83863f772f93e2a209dab0af924ca3d6764a40c4 (about 2,000 USD of claims on BNB Smart Chain, 618 USD on Arbitrum One) have no initialize flag and no ledger at all. Can a foreign pool spend the claims?. Result: No path found. The hooks have no state mapping, and the claims are surplus kept for the hook operator, so there is no balance owed to a particular pool. For a foreign pool beforeSwap reverts with 0x3b99b53d (0x87fa6e44 on the unverified one) because the swap carries no signed quote, and afterSwap alone reverts with Panic(0x12). The claim withdrawal function was not read. Evidence: https://sourcify.dev/server/v2/contract/1/0x4440854b2d02c57a0dc5c58b7a884562d875c0c4
- Polygon, cycle 6. PolHook 0xa33c9bcd5cada0636f19350d7461003c38814088 and 0xb721b4f9771ed66f85c0ffbf9504f1eaab154088 on Polygon have the same shape as the Arbitrum route hooks: beforeSwap takes the PoolKey input currency and trades hardcoded DAI and USDT on a Curve pool from the hook balance (source lines 53 to 115). They hold 3.0 DAI each and 2.24 USDT. Can a foreign pool empty them?. Result: Not today. In the Quoter test inside an unlock the hook takes the foreign currency and Curve pulls 2.9994 DAI from the hook, and then exchange_underlying reverts because the Aave V2 lending pool 0x8dff5e27ea6b7ac08ebfdf9eb090f32ee9a30fcf rejects the deposit with error string "3". The same revert hits the hooks' own DAI and USDT pool, so the hooks are out of service. The balances are about 3 USD each. beforeSwap in this source has no caller check either. If the Aave reserve accepts deposits again the path opens. Evidence: https://sourcify.dev/server/v2/contract/137/0xa33c9bcd5cada0636f19350d7461003c38814088
- Unichain, Arbitrum One, cycle 6. Hooks that call PoolManager.take or PoolManager.swap with hardcoded currencies inside beforeSwap for any pool, and hold nothing: Unichain proxy 0xad78e0a3b5a552813feb5eb8ecbe842f7b5e9088 (takes native ETH and swaps on a real pool for a foreign PoolKey) and the exact output branch of CamelotHook on Arbitrum One. Can this move PoolManager funds to the swapper?. Result: No. take debits the hook in the currency it names (src/PoolManager.sol:291-297) and the delta it returns is credited in the currencies of the foreign PoolKey (src/libraries/Hooks.sol:299-311), so the hook is left with a debt in the real currency that nobody settles and unlock reverts with CurrencyNotSettled (src/PoolManager.sol:104-114). The Quoter shows a result only because it reverts before that check. A loss needs a hook that owns claims or balances, as in the two findings. Evidence: src/PoolManager.sol:104
- Arbitrum One, cycle 6. Unverified hook 0x6bc99d37114ae54b782c7694368ed5430e9c0ac8 on Arbitrum One (1001 USDC and 1001 USDT on the hook, two pools, no initialize flag): afterSwap does not look at the PoolKey. For any pool it reads prices from 0x451d7e6f and calls PositionManager.modifyLiquiditiesWithoutUnlock on its own position 0x2afe. Result: No loss shown. In the Quoter test for five foreign PoolKeys the third modifyLiquiditiesWithoutUnlock call reverts and afterSwap fails with a wrapped error, so a foreign pool cannot be swapped at all. The rebalance uses the oracle price and the hook's own position, and anyone can trigger the same code by swapping in the real pool. Whether a foreign swap can succeed in another state and move the position at a price the attacker sets was not established and is listed as a lead. Evidence: https://arbitrum.drpc.org

## Reading of the source (theme-token-triggers)

- all 21 networks, cycle 6. Step 1. Which pooled tokens with a market price are worth more than 1,000 USD at each PoolManager today. Method: currency lists of cycle 4, live balanceOf(PoolManager), prices from coins.llama.fi (cycle 5 price files for 18 networks; this cycle priced every currency with a balance on Robinhood Chain, Elysium and Arc, 738,773, 129,491 and 261,204 addresses). Result: 2151 tokens on 19 networks, 1080 of them above 10,000 USD: Ethereum 845 (427 above 10,000 USD); Optimism 29 (9 above 10,000 USD); Base 323 (200 above 10,000 USD); Unichain 18 (12 above 10,000 USD); Zora 0 (0 above 10,000 USD); Worldchain 12 (9 above 10,000 USD); Ink 19 (15 above 10,000 USD); Soneium 6 (2 above 10,000 USD); Celo 5 (3 above 10,000 USD); X Layer 14 (7 above 10,000 USD); Arbitrum One 85 (48 above 10,000 USD); Robinhood Chain 353 (183 above 10,000 USD); Elysium 18 (12 above 10,000 USD); Polygon 70 (36 above 10,000 USD); BNB Smart Chain 250 (67 above 10,000 USD); Avalanche 22 (8 above 10,000 USD); Monad 34 (22 above 10,000 USD); MegaETH 2 (1 above 10,000 USD); Tempo 5 (4 above 10,000 USD); Arc 41 (15 above 10,000 USD); HyperEVM 0 (0 above 10,000 USD). Zora and HyperEVM have no priced token above the threshold (2 and 11 priced currencies, all below 1,000 USD). The lists are complete where cycle 4 read every Initialize log (Ethereum, Robinhood Chain, Elysium, Arc and the other networks with an init census). They are incomplete on Base, BNB Smart Chain and X Layer, where the cycle 4 list holds only currencies that moved in its window, and on World Chain, where it comes from an explorer page. A census of Base Initialize logs started in this cycle counted 2,418,681 currencies in the first 10,000,000 blocks after deployment against 9,116 on the list, and was stopped for size. Two values are price artefacts and were kept as targets: PORT3 on Ethereum and vUSDT on BNB Smart Chain, whose balanceOf returns more than one word. Token lists with values are in the discover files. Evidence: research/network-risk/cycles/006/theme-token-triggers.work/raw/stats.json
- Ethereum, Optimism, Base, Unichain, Worldchain, Ink, Soneium, Celo, X Layer, Arbitrum One, Robinhood Chain, Elysium, Polygon, BNB Smart Chain, Avalanche, Monad, MegaETH, Tempo, Arc, cycle 6. Step 2. For each of the 2151 tokens: every selector of the token, of its implementation and of the contracts that balanceOf(PoolManager) touches (eth_createAccessList, 1442 related contracts) was called from an ordinary account with the PoolManager as address argument. Named functions got arguments by type; the 14775 selectors without a known name got eight fixed calldata shapes. Each trial ran in eth_call with a measuring stub at the PoolManager address and was repeated with the block time moved by 8 hours, 91 days and 400 days. Mode A: the stub hands one third of the balance to the account first. Mode B: the PoolManager sends nothing and the account holds a balance written by state override into the token's balance slot. Mode C: as B without a balance, for tokens whose slot was not found. Measured: balanceOf(PoolManager) before and after, the account's balance, and whether a transfer of the full balance leaves the PoolManager. Result: Mode A 2318914 trials, 140312 calls accepted by the token. Mode B 2279949 trials on 2019 tokens, 133089 accepted. Mode C 38965 trials on 132 tokens. Batches that failed for lack of gas were rerun with eight trials per call and none is left open. One priced token ended a trial with a higher reported balance and a refused full transfer: QANX 0xaaa7a10a8ee237ea61e8ac46c50a8db8bcc1baaa on Ethereum through transferLocked, at every block time. That is finding F-078 and nothing new (21,210,277.64 units at the PoolManager, 205,708 USD at the coins.llama.fi figure that F-078 already calls unreliable). No trial lowered balanceOf(PoolManager) of a priced token, at any of the four times. Every other accepted call that raised the balance took the same amount from the caller and left the full balance transferable (transfer, transferAndCall, multiTransfer, batchTransfer, transferShares and equals), or differed by one or two base units of share rounding. The full list of functions through which a caller's tokens reached the PoolManager is transfer, transferFrom, transferAndCall, transferWithMemo, multiTransfer, batchTransfer, push, move, transferShares, bridgeTransfer, bridgeTransferFrom, transferMultiple, transferForMultiAddresses, transferWithReference, transferFromWithReference, multisend and bulkTransfer. None is a grant, a lock or a deposit for another account, so no priced token offers the grant and revoke sequence of F-079, and no selector without a name raised the balance. One mode B result is an artefact: claimRewardsAndStake on stkAAVE paid the account's own rewards, which exist only because of the overridden balance, to the PoolManager. Control: DeadToken on Base (F-085) is not detected in mode A, because the hand-out by the PoolManager resets its idle timer, and is detected in mode B at 91 and 400 days (claimIdleTokens lowers the balance to 0 and the account gains half). Limits: the trials measure the token's own balance only, so a public call that pays a second asset to the PoolManager is not seen; arguments such as Merkle proofs and signatures are not satisfied; on Monad no endpoint accepted a block override, so Monad was tested at the current time only. Evidence: research/network-risk/cycles/006/theme-token-triggers.work/sweep.py, raw/sweep_<chain>.json.gz, raw/sweepB_<chain>.json.gz, raw/sweepC_<chain>.json.gz
- Ethereum, Optimism, Base, Unichain, Worldchain, Ink, Soneium, Celo, X Layer, Arbitrum One, Robinhood Chain, Elysium, Polygon, BNB Smart Chain, Avalanche, MegaETH, Tempo, Arc, cycle 6. Does the passage of time alone change the PoolManager balance of a target token or stop it from sending the full balance (expiry, demurrage, cooldown, scheduled rebase)? One block was pinned per network and the trial without any call was run at 0, 8 hours, 91 days and 400 days, with and without a hand-out. Result: Six tokens change, all Aave receipt tokens whose balance grows with interest: aEthLINK, aEthWETH, aEthUSDC and aEthUSDT on Ethereum, aArbUSDT on Arbitrum One and aBasWETH on Base (each between 1,500 and 5,800 USD). No token lost balance with time and no full balance transfer turned from accepted to refused at any of the shifted times. Monad could not be tested for lack of a block override. Evidence: research/network-risk/cycles/006/theme-token-triggers.work/timeonly.py, raw/timeonly_<chain>.json.gz
- Base, Tempo, cycle 6. Precompile tokens have no selector table in code: 35 B20 tokens on Base (OUSD with 5.3 million USD, the tokenized stocks with suffix c, cbZEC, cbHYPE) and the 5 TIP-20 tokens on Tempo. The function lists were taken from the published interfaces and run through the same trials. Result: Base B20: 30 state changing functions of IB20, IB20Asset and IERC8056; 3,920 trials per mode; an ordinary account gets transfer, transferWithMemo and approve accepted and nothing else. mint, burnBlocked, seizeWithMemo, pause, updatePolicy and the multiplier setters need roles, and the interface states that balanceOf stays in raw units while the multiplier scales the UI view only. Tempo TIP-20: 29 functions, 620 trials per mode, the accepted calls are transfers, approve and calls that act on the caller. burnBlocked and burnAt need roles, and rewards are claimed by the holder for itself. Issuer powers over these tokens are in F-027 and the Tempo findings of earlier cycles. Evidence: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/base/base-std/main/src/interfaces/IB20.sol ; https://rustdocs.tempo.xyz/tempo_precompiles/tip20/ITIP20/index.html ; research/network-risk/cycles/006/theme-token-triggers.work/b20.py, tempo.py
- Ethereum, cycle 6. Lead L-399, FOLD 0xe172e9b6cfbeeb5593bdce3f077356fdb33af904 (24,275,769 FOLD at the PoolManager, about 742,000 USD). A transfer from CLAIM_SOURCE locks the amount at the recipient until NO_MORE_LOCKS. Can any account still cause such a transfer to the PoolManager, and can the owner name a later claim source?. Result: No. setClaimSource reverts once a source is set (InterfoldToken.sol lines 416 to 422) and CLAIM_SOURCE() returns the auction 0x687cc38d8279df3352b64cf3ec1fe8e033933595. The auction pays tokens to the bid owner only (claimTokens and claimTokensBatch) and accepts bids only while it is active. All 310 bids were read at Ethereum block 26,478,229: none has the PoolManager as owner, 10 are not exited and 1 is exited with 8.33 FOLD unclaimed, all owned by other addresses. lockCount(PoolManager), queuedLockCount(PoolManager) and lockedBalanceOf(PoolManager) are 0 and transferableBalanceOf equals balanceOf. The remaining ways to place a lock (linkClaim, mintAllocations) need LOCK_MANAGER_ROLE or MINTER_ROLE, and minting is closed since tge. Locks end for everyone at NO_MORE_LOCKS = 1915884000 (17 September 2030). Evidence: https://sourcify.dev/server/v2/contract/1/0xe172e9b6cfbeeb5593bdce3f077356fdb33af904?fields=sources,compilation,proxyResolution ; https://sourcify.dev/server/v2/contract/1/0x687cc38d8279df3352b64cf3ec1fe8e033933595?fields=sources,compilation,proxyResolution ; research/network-risk/cycles/006/theme-token-triggers.work/raw/fold_bids.json
- Ethereum, Arbitrum One, cycle 6. Step 3, tokens where balanceOf counts units that transfer cannot move (apart from QANX): who can create such units at another address? Sources read: ondo, skl, SPA, WLFI, SIERRA, fxSAVE and its base pool. Result: Only role holders or the holder itself. ondo: transfers are limited to the freed balance when investorBalances is set; the trial call of the setter by an ordinary account reverted. skl: SkaleToken refuses a transfer that would leave less than the locked amount, and the three lockers add to it through TokenLaunchManager (role), through the holder's own delegation and through a slash of the holder's delegation. SPA: transferWithLock is onlyOwner. WLFI: the transfer hook blocks legacy users that are not activated, a registry state set by the owner; staking locks sit in a separate contract. SIERRA (LYTPool) and the fxUSD base pool lock shares of an open redeem request, and a request is made by msg.sender for its own shares. The PoolManager has made none of these calls and cannot make them (its calls to a currency are transfer and balanceOf, src/types/Currency.sol:60-95). Evidence: https://sourcify.dev/server/v2/contract/1/0x00c83aecc790e8a4453e5dd3b0b4b3680501a7a7?fields=sources,compilation,proxyResolution ; https://sourcify.dev/server/v2/contract/42161/0x5575552988a3a80504bbaeb1311674fcfd40ad4b?fields=sources,compilation,proxyResolution ; https://sourcify.dev/server/v2/contract/1/0xfd10892c8a1cac5b279ee22877dcc735db7b7833?fields=sources,compilation,proxyResolution
- Ethereum, Avalanche, Base, cycle 6. Step 3, staking and vault tokens with cooldown, vesting or escrow words: sUSDe, sENA, sPENDLE, apyUSD, aptUSD, syrupUSDC, syrupUSDT, syrupUSDG, yUSD, yETH, svZCHF, SiloVault shares (USDC on Arbitrum One, mevUSDC on Avalanche by selector match), Yearn vaults on Base. Result: balanceOf is the plain share balance in the sources read. cooldownAssets and cooldownShares burn the caller's own shares into a silo. The vesting in sUSDe, sENA, yUSD, yETH, apyUSD and aptUSD is the release schedule of vault yield and touches no holder balance. redistributeLockedAmount needs the admin role and a restricted source address. Maple pool shares are a plain mapping and every transfer passes a permission check of the pool's manager contract. The remaining risk is the issuer side (deny lists, pause), which earlier findings hold. Evidence: https://sourcify.dev/server/v2/contract/1/0x9d39a5de30e57443bff2a8307a4256c8797a3497?fields=sources,compilation,proxyResolution ; https://sourcify.dev/server/v2/contract/1/0x7fd57b46ae1a7b14f6940508381877ee03e1018b?fields=sources,compilation,proxyResolution ; https://sourcify.dev/server/v2/contract/1/0xfd616567ecc1607f61073951a1e822f7315bb112?fields=sources,compilation,proxyResolution
- Ethereum, cycle 6. Step 3, tokens with lock or escrow functions that act on the caller, and one that locks for a named recipient: AST, BNB, RNDR, TITANX, HEX, DPR. Result: AST lockBalance, BNB freeze, RNDR holdInEscrow and the TITANX and HEX claim, stake and mint functions act on msg.sender. The TITANX burn functions for another user spend that user's allowance. DPR transferWithLock(to, reason, amount, time) moves the caller's tokens into the token contract and records a lock for the recipient. The locked amount is outside balanceOf(recipient). unlock(of) can be called by anyone after expiry and pays the amount to the recipient, so it is a public call that raises the PoolManager balance with the locker's own tokens, which is the class of F-041 without a gain. Step 3, launch pad tokens with lockPool, vesting, allocation or cap data: the DERC20 family on Base (33 tokens above 10,000 USD of one selector set, 4.2 million USD together), CloneDERC20VotesV2, Zora CreatorCoin and ContentCoin, DopplerERC20V1 on Robinhood Chain (10 tokens), StonkCoin (STONKFI, 1.18 million USD), SEND LaunchToken, GANG. Result: Vested amounts are held by the token contract and paid on release to the beneficiary, so they are outside balanceOf of holders. lockPool blocks transfers to one pool address and is onlyOwner; pool() was read for all 44 tokens above 10,000 USD with these functions and none names the PoolManager. DopplerERC20V1 adds a holding cap for receivers while isBalanceLimitActive, which reads 0 on the Robinhood Chain tokens read. StonkCoin.balanceOf adds claimableAllocation(account), which the first transfer turns into balance. The allocation comes from the account's own backing of the raise before launch (StonkFi.back uses msg.sender), claimableAllocation(PoolManager) is 0 and the raise is launched, so no account can create one for the PoolManager. SEND pays holder rewards in a second asset to msg.sender on claim. These tokens are made by the launch pads, and what their owners can do is pool-creator scope. PAXG has a rewards module since its last upgrade: an account joins a payout group through the registrar role, through its own EIP-712 or ERC-1271 signature, or by accepting a proposal itself. The PoolManager has no isValidSignature and cannot accept. Rewards are paid from the claim source to the group's destination and leave the account's balance unchanged. This group is issuer scope and is covered by the issuer findings (F-019, F-036 and the Ethereum issuer finding of cycle 5). ## Reading of the source (audit-walk-a)

- all 21 networks, cycle 7. OpenZeppelin audit, C-01: an ERC-20 representation of the native currency lets one payment be credited twice, once as msg.value under address(0) and once as a balance increase under the token, which drains native pools (worked case Celo, with Polygon as a network where deltas can be inflated). Result: Closed in the source. Hazard in one sentence: sync the token face, pay with settle and value, then settle the face for the same inflow. Closing statements: a settle with value reverts while any token is synced (src/PoolManager.sol:356); a native credit is taken from msg.value only when no currency is synced (353-354); every write of a nonzero synced currency also writes the reserves (285-286, src/libraries/CurrencyReserves.sol:27-32), so a face synced after a native payment starts from the higher balance; a token settle clears the slot (361); the contract has no receive or fallback function and only settle and settleFor are payable (300-307). The report says the fix makes the next settle after a sync settle that currency or revert. The source is looser in one way: sync(address(0)) clears the slot without a settle (283, documented at src/interfaces/IPoolManager.sol:165-171). I walked the orders that this allows and each inflow is still credited under one id only, because the stale reserves are overwritten by the next token sync. Reliance: A1 (the synced currency lives in transient storage for one transaction and is rolled back on revert), A2 and A3 (native value reaches the PoolManager through settle, and anything forced in is credited once under one id). Per network: an address that reports the PoolManager's native balance exists on Celo (CELO token, transfer works), Arc (0x3600000000000000000000000000000000000000, six decimals, transfer works), Polygon (0x1010, transfer of 1 without value returned false), Optimism and Zora (LegacyERC20ETH, transfer disabled). My query found no such answer from these candidates on the other 16 networks, and the ledger holds a face search for each of them. On all 21 deployed PoolManagers my walk with a stub token that returns the native balance of its argument gave: sync while locked succeeded, settle with 1000 wei reverted with NonzeroNativeValue, a zero value settle paid 0 and cleared the slot, settle with 1000 wei then credited 1000, a new sync and settle of the face paid 0, and a native take of 1000 closed the unlock. The real faces on Celo, Polygon, Arc, Optimism and Zora gave the same seven answers. The walk shows the contracts deployed today. The checkout was not compiled. Result: These are stated limits and nothing in src closes them. What src provides is separation: pool state is stored per pool id (src/PoolManager.sol:93), deltas per caller and currency (src/libraries/CurrencyDelta.sol:10-41), hook deltas are booked to the hook address in the two currencies of its pool (PoolManager.sol:181, 224, 381-384). OpenZeppelin audit, M-01: assembly blocks marked memory-safe wrote past the scratch space or over the free memory pointer (hook return data, the TickMisaligned error, two argument custom errors, the ERC-20 transfer call). Result: Closed. The hook return data is copied to memory at the free memory pointer, which is then advanced by the padded length (src/libraries/Hooks.sol:140-149). TickMisaligned and the two argument revert helpers build their data at the free memory pointer and revert at once (src/libraries/TickBitmap.sol:57-63, src/libraries/CustomRevert.sol:49-79, 83-118). The single argument helpers write 36 bytes into the 64 byte scratch space (CustomRevert.sol:14-46). The ERC-20 transfer writes its 68 bytes of calldata at the free memory pointer, reads the answer into the first scratch word and zeroes the three words it used (src/types/Currency.sol:55-80). Reliance: A10 only, that MSTORE, MLOAD, RETURNDATACOPY and CALL behave as on Ethereum, which cycle 1 tested on every network. - all 21 networks, cycle 7. Trail of Bits audit, take invariants UNI-TAKE-1 to UNI-TAKE-3: after a take the caller's delta falls by the amount, the recipient's balance rises by it and the singleton's balance falls by it. Result: UNI-TAKE-1 holds from the source alone: the debit is written before the transfer and the call reverts as a whole if the transfer fails (src/PoolManager.sol:291-297, src/types/Currency.sol:44-53, 81-86). UNI-TAKE-2 and UNI-TAKE-3 rest on A3 and A4 and the source cannot enforce them: the token branch accepts an empty answer or a 32 byte 1 and makes no code size check (Currency.sol:64-74), so a take of an address without code moves nothing, and a token may deliver less to the recipient or charge the sender more. In each case the caller is debited the full amount, so the shortfall falls on the caller, except where a token charges the PoolManager on top, which the ledger holds as F-092 for Ethereum, Arc and BNB Smart Chain. Unit theme-transfer-side-effects of this cycle searches for further tokens of that kind. - BNB Smart Chain, cycle 7. Method rule L-464: does any count of this unit for BNB Smart Chain rest on eth_getLogs through one endpoint. Result: No. Every BNB Smart Chain figure of this unit comes from eth_call with state overrides, rotated over bsc-dataseed1.bnbchain.org, bsc-rpc.publicnode.com, rpc-bsc.48.club and bsc-mainnet.public.blastapi.io, and no log query was made on this network. The ibBUSD result was repeated on three endpoints with the same balance before (56658476151267410600) and after (0). The two log counts of this unit are for Ethereum and Arc. The Arc count agrees on two endpoints. The Ethereum count of zero new WHITE charge transfers comes from one endpoint and is backed by the unchanged balanceOf(PoolManager), which does not depend on logs. Result: No. Five MULMODs have the constant modulus 2^256-1 (four limbs), and the inputs of their callers bound the product: liquidity << 96 times a price difference or a price (2^384), a fee growth difference times liquidity (2^384), an amount times Q96 (2^352), an amount times a fee below 10^6, liquidity times a price difference (2^288). Their quotient is at most 2^128. Of the other eight, six have a modulus of at most three limbs: the constants 2^128, 2^96 and 10^6, liquidity (uint128), a sqrt price (uint160) and 10^6 minus the fee. The remaining two take n1 + product and n1 - product of getNextSqrtPriceFromAmount0RoundingUp (SqrtPriceMath.sol:47 and 71), with a product n1 * sqrtPX96 below 2^384. A four limb modulus of at least 2^192 then leaves a quotient below 2^192. Both conditions of the fault never hold together in this code, whatever the input. This is stronger than the in-pool argument of OPCODES.md. Evidence: src/libraries/FullMath.sol:24

- all 21 networks, cycle 9. Part one. Which entries of the Solidity bug list apply to solc 0.8.26 with the settings of foundry.toml (via IR, optimizer on with 44,444,444 runs and the default Yul step sequence, Cancun), fetched again on 2026-11-24, and what SOL-2026-7 needs according to the primary source. Result: bugs_by_version.json lists eight entries for 0.8.26 (released 2024-05-21). By the conditions field of bugs.json six can apply to this build: SOL-2026-8 OverlappingRecursiveStorageStructCopyCorruptionViaIR (viaIR, introduced 0.8.13, fixed 0.8.39, needs a storage-to-storage copy of a recursive struct with a dynamic array into a target that contains the source), SOL-2026-7 YulOptimizerKnowledgeBaseStaleBookkeeping (yulOptimizer, 0.8.19 to 0.8.37, fixed 0.8.38, severity low), SOL-2026-6 MisorderedNamedParametersInRequireWithCustomErrors (viaIR, introduced 0.8.26, fixed 0.8.37, needs require(cond, Error({name: value})) ), SOL-2026-4 SpillSlotCollisionAcrossMutualRecursion (viaIR, fixed 0.8.37, needs a cycle of at least two mutually recursive functions), SOL-2026-2 UnsoundSpillInMutualRecursion (viaIR, fixed 0.8.36, needs intersecting recursive cycles) and SOL-2025-1 LostStorageArrayWriteOnSlotOverflow (no conditions, fixed 0.8.32, needs a storage array that crosses slot 2^256). Two cannot apply by their conditions: SOL-2026-8 for the evmasm pipeline (viaIR false) and SOL-2026-5 MemoryByteArrayElementDeleteClearsWholeWord (viaIR false). The post of 2026-10-22 confirms SOL-2026-7: affected steps LoadResolver (L) and EqualStoreEliminator (E), both in the default sequence; the trigger is a variable used to compute memory or storage addresses that is reassigned, one address derived from its value before and one after the reassignment with different constant offsets, and the two addresses equal at run time; then a load is replaced with an outdated value, a store of an equal value is removed, or a keccak256 is replaced. The fix is in 0.8.38 and is confined to KnowledgeBase and DataFlowAnalyzer. The default sequence in libsolidity/interface/OptimiserSettings.h at v0.8.26 contains three L and one E in the main part and none in the cleanup part fDnTOcmuO. Evidence: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ethereum/solidity/develop/docs/bugs.json; https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ethereum/solidity/develop/docs/bugs_by_version.json; https://blog.soliditylang.org/2026/10/22/yul-optimizer-knowledge-base-stale-bookkeeping-bug/; https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ethereum/solidity/v0.8.26/libsolidity/interface/OptimiserSettings.h ; copies in research/network-risk/cycles/009/core-code-optimizer-bug.work/dl/

## Reading of the source (theme-go-miscompile)

- Arbitrum One, Robinhood Chain, cycle 10. Nitro fork 0e44603 core/vm opcode handlers and core/state journal and transient storage for the Go issue 81863 shape. Result: Arithmetic handlers take pointers into the heap stack via pop1Peek1 (instructions.go 34-85), so no local address reaches uint256. journal.go 192-194, 262-264 and 313-315 select between a map entry and a new heap object. evm.go 164-195 picks the address of a global jump table. No store through a pointer chosen between two locals. Evidence: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/OffchainLabs/go-ethereum/0e44603/core/vm/instructions.go
- BNB Smart Chain, Polygon, cycle 10. bsc v1.8.2 and bor v2.11.1 core/vm and core/state for the shape. Result: Handlers pass &x of a popped copy to uint256 (bsc instructions.go 29-181, bor 30-202) but each address is a single fixed local. bor Run (interpreter.go 123-126) picks between evm.interrupt and new(atomic.Bool) with a zeroing store in the branch and then loads it atomically and passes it to runSwitch, so the address counts as used. Push handlers (bor 1044-1072) write through one pointer on both branches. Evidence: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/0xPolygon/bor/v2.11.1/core/vm/interpreter.go
- Avalanche, cycle 10. libevm d398bc4dbe41 core/vm and core/state and uint256 v1.2.4 for the shape. Result: Same handlers as upstream with a z.IsZero guard in opAddmod (instructions.go 174-181) that writes through the stack pointer on both branches; NewEVMInterpreter picks addresses of global tables (interpreter.go 60-82). uint256 v1.2.4 AddMod and SMod behave as v1.3.2. No function has the shape. Evidence: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ava-labs/libevm/d398bc4dbe41/core/vm/instructions.go
- Elysium, Celo, cycle 10. Is the Elysium nitro build (go1.25.12) or the Celo op-geth backend (go1.24.13) affected by Go issue 81863. Result: No. The bug needs branchelim to run before dead auto elim, which began with CL 685676 on master in July 2025 (Go 1.26). In go1.25.12 compile.go branchelim runs after dead auto elim. Both versions were read from web3_clientVersion on 2026-11-24. Evidence: https://go.googlesource.com/go/+/refs/tags/go1.25.12/src/cmd/compile/internal/ssa/compile.go?format=TEXT
- Ethereum, Optimism, Base, Unichain, Zora, Worldchain, Ink, Soneium, X Layer, Monad, MegaETH, Tempo, Arc, HyperEVM, cycle 10. Does any other network's endpoint report a Go toolchain. Result: No. web3_clientVersion on 2026-11-24 reports reth, op-reth, base-reth, world-chain, xlayer reth, Monad, mega-reth, tempo, arc/v1 and hyperliquid evm, none of which is a Go program. Polygon's networks.json endpoint polygon.drpc.org reports Geth/v10.0.0/drpc, a proxy name, so publicnode was used for bor. Evidence: research/network-risk/cycles/010/theme-go-miscompile.work/clientversions.json
- Arbitrum One, Robinhood Chain, Polygon, BNB Smart Chain, Avalanche, cycle 10. ADDMOD, SDIV and SMOD vectors aimed at the only branch selected pointers in uint256 (AddMod tmpX and tmpY, SMod and SDiv sign branches), on every build that answered. Result: 12,112 shape vectors plus 185,529 battery and targeted vectors per network, each request paired with web3_clientVersion: 0 mismatches on nitro linux-arm64 and linux-amd64 go1.27.3, five bor go1.26.10 builds, two BSC geth go1.26.10 builds and avalanchego go=1.26.10. Evidence: research/network-risk/cycles/010/theme-go-miscompile.work/paired.json

## Reading of the source (theme-megaeth-executor)

- MegaETH, cycle 10. Part two (a): full replay of every mined MegaETH swap that crossed an initialized tick (the pool's liquidity changed between consecutive swaps with no ModifyLiquidity between) or that did not fit one step of SwapMath. The window is blocks 2,912,161 to 32,724,160, with tick spacing read from the Initialize events of all 143 pools. Result: All 2,885 reproduce. The block producer's results match the source's Pool.swap, TickBitmap.nextInitializedTickWithinOneWord, crossTick, SwapMath and SqrtPriceMath to the unit in end price, end tick, end liquidity and both amounts. That covers 1,640 swaps that crossed liquidity, up to 116 steps, and 1,245 multi-step swaps at one liquidity, up to 175 steps, 49 of them in hooked pools. The first pass left three swaps unmatched, because they ran out of liquidity to the top of the price range and their specified amount is larger than what they used. With a larger exact input or exact output and the end price as limit, all three reproduce in 61 steps at their block. Evidence: research/network-risk/cycles/010/theme-megaeth-executor.work/crossed.py, research/network-risk/cycles/010/theme-megaeth-executor.work/raw/crossed.json, research/network-risk/cycles/010/theme-megaeth-executor.work/raw/edge3.json; rpc https://mainnet.megaeth.com/rpc eth_getLogs and extsload at the swap blocks, 2026-11-24
- MegaETH, cycle 10. Part two (b): mined swaps at negative ticks and near the ends of the tick range against getTickAtSqrtPrice and getSqrtPriceAtTick (src/libraries/TickMath.sol), which use signed multiplication, SAR, SIGNEXTEND and the bit scans. Result: 53,811 Swap events in blocks 2,912,161 to 32,724,160 all satisfy the tick relation. 24,345 of them are at negative ticks. The lowest tick is -887,272 (MIN_TICK) and the highest is 887,271 (MAX_TICK - 1, at price MAX_SQRT_PRICE - 1). Six events lie beyond |tick| 400,000. The seven replay jobs that start or end beyond |tick| 400,000 reproduce, including the three that walk from tick -28,981 to 887,271 and three that come back. Evidence: research/network-risk/cycles/010/theme-megaeth-executor.work/raw/crossed.json (ticks), rpc https://mainnet.megaeth.com/rpc eth_getLogs 2026-11-24
- MegaETH, cycle 10. Part two (c), lead L-607: did the block producer roll back the transient unlock flag, the transient deltas and the pool storage of a PoolManager frame that reverted, in mined transactions where a later frame of the same transaction completed an unlock? The test compares, for each transaction, the receipt that the sequencer wrote with the status and surviving logs of debug_traceTransaction (callTracer, withLog) on the replica, which re-executes on the same pre-state. Result: Yes. 7,627 transactions emitted PoolManager Swap or ModifyLiquidity logs between blocks 30,862,220 and 32,724,219. In 1,347 of them a frame that entered PoolManager.unlock reverted. In 1,333 of those the reverted frame contained a swap, the quoter pattern, and a later unlock in the same transaction completed. The receipt status and every surviving log equal the re-execution in all 7,627, with no trace errors. Had the producer kept the unlock flag (src/libraries/Lock.sol), the later unlock would revert with AlreadyUnlocked (src/PoolManager.sol:105). Had it kept the deltas (src/libraries/NonzeroDeltaCount.sol), the later unlock would fail with CurrencyNotSettled (src/PoolManager.sol:112). Had it kept the reverted swap's slot0, the later Swap event would carry other prices. The window has no settle, take or sync inside a reverted frame. Evidence: research/network-risk/cycles/010/theme-megaeth-executor.work/frames.py, research/network-risk/cycles/010/theme-megaeth-executor.work/raw/frames.json; rpc https://mainnet.megaeth.com/rpc debug_traceTransaction and eth_getTransactionReceipt 2026-11-24
- MegaETH, cycle 10. Part three: whether a MegaETH per-frame budget (compute gas, data size, KV updates, state growth at 98/100 of the parent's remainder) or the detention cap after a volatile read can be breached in a child of the PoolManager's frame and caught there, so that the PoolManager continues with a failed subcall and returns another result than on Ethereum. Result: No. The resource limits spec says a child that exceeds its budget reverts with MegaLimitExceeded and the parent may continue. Every call the PoolManager makes treats failure as fatal: hooks (src/libraries/Hooks.sol:134-137), native and ERC-20 transfers (src/types/Currency.sol:48-52, 73-86), balanceOf, a high-level call that reverts on failure (src/types/Currency.sol:94, src/PoolManager.sol:285, 359), and unlockCallback (src/PoolManager.sol:110). The PoolManager reads gas() only to forward it. A breach below the PoolManager therefore reverts the PoolManager frame as a whole. A breach in the PoolManager's own frame reverts it as a whole for its caller. A transaction-level breach halts the transaction. The outcome is either the Ethereum result or a full revert, never a partial result. A token or hook that catches its own failed subcall is a token or hook matter and is not swept here. Evidence: https://docs.megaeth.com/spec/megaevm/resource-limits.md (Per-Call-Frame Runtime Budgets); src/libraries/Hooks.sol:134-137; src/types/Currency.sol:44-95
- MegaETH, cycle 10. Lead L-610: which per-frame budget a swap that crosses many initialized ticks reaches first, and whether a liquidity removal can reach one. Result: State growth binds first. Each crossing writes feeGrowthOutside0 and feeGrowthOutside1 of one tick (src/libraries/Pool.sol:602-612). A write counts as state growth only when the slot was zero at transaction start (resource accounting, Storage Slot Growth Rules). Outside values are zero only for ticks initialized above the current tick (Pool.sol:533-538), so an upward swap through freshly planted ticks adds up to 2 per tick. The PoolManager frame at depth 1 gets 980 of the 1,000 per-transaction limit, so it reverts with MegaLimitExceeded after about 490 such ticks, at roughly 24 million compute gas from 2 cold loads, 2 fresh SSTOREs and a bitmap load per tick, inferred from standard gas costs and not measured. Ticks with nonzero outside values cost about 14,000 compute gas per crossing. 200 million compute gas then allows about 14,000 crossings, 28,000 KV updates and 1.1 MB of data size, far below the shares of 490,000 KV updates and 12.8 MB. The swapper can stop at a price limit and continue in a later transaction (Pool.sol:344), and each planted tick adds growth only on its first upward crossing. A removal touches two ticks and one position (Pool.sol:146-238). Cycle 1 recorded the same bound qualitatively. The result is a delay without loss, and an eth_call measurement through a router was not run. Evidence: https://docs.megaeth.com/spec/megaevm/resource-accounting.md; https://docs.megaeth.com/spec/megaevm/resource-limits.md; src/libraries/Pool.sol:520-545, 602-612
- MegaETH, cycle 10. Part four, lead L-601: is Rex6 active on MegaETH mainnet, and what does it change for the instruction set the PoolManager uses?. Result: Active. The network upgrades overview gives Rex6 mainnet activation at timestamp 1787626800 (25 Aug 2026 03:00 UTC). mega-evm v1.7.3 scheduled it (#371), and the latest block read, 32,724,090, has timestamp 1795521101. Rex6 changes no opcode result. It sets one order for storage-gas and compute-gas charging (only CREATE2 changes), returns forwarded gas to the parent when a CALL or CREATE halts on the compute limit, adds a 32 byte data-size base per log, extends beneficiary detection to SELFDESTRUCT and EIP-7702 delegates, and corrects CREATE, EIP-7702, KeylessDeploy, fee-reward and system-transaction accounting. The PoolManager uses none of CREATE2, SELFDESTRUCT or KeylessDeploy. Its logs add 32 bytes each against a 13.1 MB limit. The forwarded-gas change affects gas_used only. The earlier 550-script pmdiff runs on MegaETH were made on 2026-11-24, after activation. Evidence: https://docs.megaeth.com/spec/network-upgrades/overview.md; https://docs.megaeth.com/spec/network-upgrades/rex6.md; https://raw.githubusercontent.com/megaeth-labs/mega-evm/main/CHANGELOG.md; rpc https://mainnet.megaeth.com/rpc eth_getBlockByNumber latest 2026-11-24
- MegaETH, cycle 10. ruint advisory RUSTSEC-2026-0220, which affects every release before 1.20.0. mega-evm main pins ruint 1.19.0 and the stateless validator pins 1.17.2. In those releases wrapping_shl and wrapping_shr on 256 bit values truncate the shift amount modulo 2^32, and the overflowing and checked shift flags give false negatives. Result: Not reachable from the PoolManager's bytecode. revm v112 (interpreter 37.0.3) calls ruint's shift only when shift < 256 and returns zero or the sign fill otherwise, for SHL, SHR and SAR. BYTE calls byte() only for index < 32 (bitwise.rs lines 107-158). The advisory says the shifted values were correct and only the flag was wrong, apart from the truncation above 2^32, which the guard excludes. The battery of OPCODES.md had already passed shift amounts at and above 256 on MegaETH. Evidence: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/rustsec/advisory-db/main/crates/ruint/RUSTSEC-2026-0220.md; https://github.com/alloy-rs/ruint/pull/603; https://raw.githubusercontent.com/bluealloy/revm/v112/crates/interpreter/src/instructions/bitwise.rs; https://raw.githubusercontent.com/megaeth-labs/mega-evm/main/Cargo.lock

## Reading of the source (theme-monad-compiled-mul)

- Monad, cycle 10. Every MUL, MULMOD, ADDMOD and EXP of the 24,009 byte runtime, with the operands Monad v0.16.5's compiler sees as literals. The compiler tracks literals per basic block: a block that is a jump destination starts with no known values, and only a JUMPI whose fall-through block is not a jump destination keeps them. sites.py models that rule and the constant folding of pure opcodes. Result: There are 13 MULMOD and 85 MUL in the code. Two MULMOD have a literal power of two modulus in their block and so take the inline path mul_mod2: pc 22378 with 2^128 (src/libraries/FullMath.sol:48 in the copy of mulDiv called from src/libraries/Position.sol:94 and 96, PUSH17 at pc 22359) and pc 22639 with 2^96 (FullMath.sol:48 in the copy called from src/libraries/SqrtPriceMath.sol:250, PUSH13 at pc 22624). The other eleven MULMOD go to the runtime call, which uses the 256 bit library shared with the interpreter: eight have no literal modulus or the modulus not(0) or 1000000 (pcs 22316, 22445, 22513, 22585, 22892, 22921, 23094, 23678), and three have the literal factor 2^96 with a modulus that is not(0) or unknown (pcs 20958, 22721, 22763). Twenty-five MUL have a literal operand: the first-step select of TickMath.sol:80 (pc 16780, literal 0x1fffcb933bd6fad37aa2d162d1a594001), the 19 multipliers of TickMath.sol:81-99 (pcs 17055 to 17557), the multiply by 255738958999603826347141 of TickMath.sol:225 (pc 18495), 3 times the denominator of FullMath.sol:82 (pcs 22777 and 22935), the BitMath.sol:34-47 constant (pc 21359) and the folded inverse of 15625 for the 1000000 denominator copy of FullMath.sol:99 (pc 22529). The first 23 have a zero 64 bit limb and are inlined through mul_with_bit_size; the last two have no zero limb and go to monad_vm_runtime_mul. The other 60 MUL multiply two values and go to monad_vm_runtime_mul. The EXP and ADDMOD bytes at pcs 24005 and 24008 are the metadata trailer. The deployed Monad PoolManager has the same bytes as the build except the 20 byte immutable at 13618-13637, so the pcs hold on chain. Evidence: research/network-risk/cycles/010/theme-monad-compiled-mul.work/sites.json; research/network-risk/cycles/010/theme-monad-compiled-mul.work/chain.json (eth_getCode on https://rpc.monad.xyz); https://raw.githubusercontent.com/category-labs/monad/v0.16.5/category/vm/compiler/ir/x86/virtual_stack.cpp lines 281-311; https://raw.githubusercontent.com/category-labs/monad/v0.16.5/category/vm/compiler/ir/x86/emitter.cpp lines 1016-1028 and 3407-3427
- Monad, cycle 10. MULMOD by 2^128 at pc 22378 and by 2^96 at pc 22639 as Monad v0.16.5 compiles them: modop_optimized (emitter.cpp 7590-7684) rewrites a power of two modulus into mul_mod2 (7991-8084), which for exp 96 and 128 (last_ix 1, inline_threshold 1) calls mul_with_bit_size(exp, a, b) with b in a general register or a stack slot (6720-6981), which runs MulEmitter (6465-6716) and mul_with_bit_size_by_rax (6381-6463). Transcribed instruction by instruction into Python (64 bit limbs, carry flag, 32 bit writes that clear the upper half, imul with a sign extended 32 bit immediate, mulx that leaves flags alone, rdx saved through a spare register, through rbx or on the machine stack) and run against Python integers. Result: No mismatch in 1,000,000 cases for each modulus. The operands were random, all limbs set, 2^256-1, low one or two limbs zero, one below 2^128 and the other above, powers of two, negative values and limb patterns of 0, 1, 2^31, 2^32, 2^63 and 2^64-1. The left operand started in a general register, a stack slot or a vector register, the right in a register or a stack slot, 15 percent with both in the same slot, with random choices of which of the three register sets hold other live values. Every rdx branch of mul_with_bit_size ran (dst holds rdx, swapped with tmp, through a spare register or rbx; left holds rdx; rdx live on the stack, pushed or moved). For 96 bits no mask is applied (96 & 31 is 0), and the top limb is right because every operation on it is a 32 bit one; a mutation that keeps the upper half on 32 bit writes fails all 4,000 of 4,000 cases, and mutations that drop the high half of mulx fail more than half, so the harness sees such faults. The remainder these sites return equals mulmod(a, b, 2^exp) for every input tried, so the reconstructed quotient of the two mulDiv copies is the specified one. Evidence: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/category-labs/monad/v0.16.5/category/vm/compiler/ir/x86/emitter.cpp lines 6262-6981 and 7590-8084; research/network-risk/cycles/010/theme-monad-compiled-mul.work/muljit.py; research/network-risk/cycles/010/theme-monad-compiled-mul.work/run.py; research/network-risk/cycles/010/theme-monad-compiled-mul.work/run-summary.json; research/network-risk/cycles/010/theme-monad-compiled-mul.work/coverage.json; research/network-risk/cycles/010/theme-monad-compiled-mul.work/mutate.json
- Monad, cycle 10. MUL with one literal operand as mul_optimized (emitter.cpp 6983-7043) compiles it: power of two or negated power of two literals to a shift, literals with a zero limb to mul_with_bit_size(256), other literals to the runtime call. Run for the 24 literals the PoolManager multiplies by (the 19 TickMath multipliers, the first-step select whose third limb is 1 and so takes the copy shortcut of mul_sequence, 255738958999603826347141 times a signed log_2, 3, and the two full width constants), and for random literals. Result: No mismatch in 1,000,000 cases over the 24 site literals (916,672 inline, 83,328 runtime) and 1,000,000 cases with random literals (724,402 inline, 128,504 runtime, 116,601 shift). The multiplicands included negative two's complement values, which is what getTickAtSqrtPrice feeds the multiply by 255738958999603826347141 for prices below 1. - Monad, cycle 10. Which mined Monad results exercise each compiled path, from 1,580 Swap events of 31 pools in blocks 124,993,964 to 124,996,219 read with eth_getLogs. Result: The TickMath literal multiplies and the multiply by 255738958999603826347141 run on every swap, and bits 0x1 to 0x40000 of the absolute tick all appear in the emitted ticks (0x20000 in 844 swaps, 0x40000 in 463), while 0x80000 appears in none. The general mulDiv 512 bit branch, with the multiply by 3 at pc 22935 and the runtime inverse products, is reachable in these pools: 751 consecutive pairs have (liquidity << 96) times the price at or above 2^256. pc 22639 needs liquidity times the price step at or above 2^256; the largest liquidity seen has 74 bits and the largest product 159 bits, so no mined swap in the window ran it. pc 22378 runs only in Position.update when the fee growth difference times the liquidity reaches 2^256, and ModifyLiquidity events do not carry amounts, so no mined result shows it. The way to confirm either site from blocks without sending a transaction is to find a mined swap or liquidity change whose inputs cross that bound and compare the token amounts of its Swap event or of the token Transfer events with the formulas; none was found in the window. - Ethereum, Optimism, Base, Unichain, Zora, Worldchain, Ink, Soneium, Celo, X Layer, Arbitrum One, Robinhood Chain, Elysium, Polygon, BNB Smart Chain, Avalanche, Tempo, Arc, cycle 10. The same question for the other 20 networks: does any of them run a compiled or rewritten multiplication path in block production that simulated calls do not reach. Result: No client read in earlier cycles for these networks compiles EVM code to native code in block production; BNB Smart Chain's fused instruction feature was removed in v1.8.0. MUL and MULMOD there run the interpreter that the 185,529 vectors and the PoolManager scripts of OPCODES.md exercised. The block producers of MegaETH and HyperEVM are closed and remain in the open list of OPCODES.md; this unit adds nothing for them. Evidence: research/network-risk/OPCODES.md (table of client readings and the open list)

## Reading of the source (theme-closed-producers)

- MegaETH, cycle 11. Part one, lead L-626: every mined PoolManager transaction in blocks 2,900,000 to 30,862,219 and 32,724,220 to 32,731,000 (the windows cycle 10 did not trace), read with debug_traceTransaction (callTracer withLog) on the public replica, which re-executes with the stock interpreter, against the receipt that the sequencer's closed executor wrote. For liquidity removals, fee collections and payments inside a reverted frame, prestateTracer diffMode against eth_getStorageAt at the block (post values when the transaction is the last PoolManager transaction of its block, pre values at block-1 when it is the first). Result: 43,342 transactions traced, 0 errors, 0 status mismatches, 0 log mismatches. 8,580 had a PoolManager frame that was undone and in 8,481 a later unlock completed, so the producer rolled back the unlock flag (src/libraries/Lock.sol:10-27, src/PoolManager.sol:104-114). 87 transactions ran take inside a reverted frame, 2 ran settle, 1 ran sync and 2 ran modifyLiquidity, and each was followed by work that completed with the receipt equal to re-execution, so the producer also rolled back the outgoing transfer and the negative delta of take (src/PoolManager.sol:291-297) and the credit of settle (src/PoolManager.sol:349-365). 151 transactions removed liquidity and 454 collected fees (ModifyLiquidity with negative or zero delta). 681 transactions were compared on storage: 2,042 post slots and 1,819 pre slots, 0 mismatches. The output kept details of the first 600 interesting transactions only; the counts cover all 43,342. With cycle 10 the receipts of 50,969 PoolManager transactions now equal re-execution. Evidence: research/network-risk/cycles/011/theme-closed-producers.work/raw/mega.json (frames2.py mega.json); https://mainnet.megaeth.com/rpc
- MegaETH, cycle 11. Part one: is the public MegaETH stateless validator run by any party that publishes its results or mismatches?. Result: No public publisher was found. The documentation describes the validator, a fatal stop on any header commitment mismatch, and an optional --report-validation-endpoint that sends mega_setValidatedBlocks callbacks to an operator-chosen endpoint, but names no public operator or feed. L2BEAT lists state validation as fraud proofs with fewer than five external challengers. The validator was not run in this unit (no software built), so the producer's storage writes are covered by the replica's re-execution and eth_getStorageAt only, as above. Evidence: https://docs.megaeth.com/node-operation/stateless-validation.md (lines 146, 249); https://l2beat.com/layer2s/projects/megaeth
- HyperEVM, cycle 11. Part two, lead L-627: do nanoreth and hyper-evm-sync compare state root and receipts root with what hl-node produced, and do they stop on a mismatch?. Result: Receipts yes, state no. nanoreth (commit f0cad31, the build at rpc.purroofgroup.com) checks gas used, receipts root and logs bloom after execution and returns an InsertBlockError on a mismatch, which leaves the block invalid and the node unable to advance. Its reth fork replaces the computed state root with zero before comparing it with the header, whose stateRoot is zero. hyper-evm-sync asserts receipts (success, cumulative gas, logs) and panics on a mismatch; its blake3 state hash is not compared. Both inject the results of HyperCore read precompiles from the block files. Both clients also carry the same 18 hard-coded state patches for improper self destructs in blocks 1,467,569 to 1,531,366, which shows that the validator once wrote state that stock revm would not; all are before the PoolManager's first log after block 45,998,366, and the PoolManager bytecode has no SELFDESTRUCT. Recorded as an operator level information finding. Evidence: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/hl-archive-node/nanoreth/f0cad31/src/node/consensus/reth_copy.rs; https://raw.githubusercontent.com/hl-archive-node/reth/14509628ed37e9a9b7110ea855a67f427c4d61fc/crates/engine/tree/src/tree/payload_validator.rs; https://raw.githubusercontent.com/hyperliquid-dex/hyper-evm-sync/main/src/run.rs; https://raw.githubusercontent.com/hl-archive-node/nanoreth/f0cad31/src/node/evm/patch.rs

- Polygon, cycle 11. Part three: in bor v2.11.1, are transient storage and the access list per transaction under BlockSTM, and does a re-executed incarnation start clean?. Result: Yes. Each incarnation builds its state from a fresh copy of the clean state (core/parallel_state_processor.go:127-138, setupEVM, cleanStateDB.Copy()). ApplyMessage reaches StateTransition, which calls Prepare (core/state_transition.go:561); Prepare creates a new access list (core/state/statedb.go:3023-3026) and a new transient storage map (statedb.go:3050-3051). Transient writes are journaled (statedb.go:1370-1376) and reverted with the frame (core/state/journal.go:419-421). Transient storage is not part of the multi-version write set: MVWriteList omits reverted keys (statedb.go:295-305) and ApplyMVWriteSet copies the incarnation's current value of each persistent path (statedb.go:693-702), so a storage write undone by a reverted frame is settled at its restored value. - Ethereum, Optimism, Base, Unichain, Ink, Soneium, X Layer, Zora, cycle 11. Reread of the fixed-cache 0.1.10 get and insert paths that every cache user in this list runs: key equality, lock protocol, epochs, and what a reader sees while a writer is inserting. Result: No path returns a hash for another input. calc (lib.rs lines 527-540) takes bucket = hash & (capacity - 1) and tag = hash & !(capacity - 1). Key and value are Copy types, so NEEDS_DROP is false and ALIVE_BIT is never set, and EPOCHS is false in both alloy texts, so the epoch bits are not used. The tag never has bit 0 set because the low 17 bits are masked off. get_inner (lines 322-350) succeeds only if a Relaxed load of the bucket state equals the tag exactly and a compare-exchange from tag to tag | LOCKED_BIT with Acquire succeeds (try_lock_ret, lines 593-606). While a writer holds the bucket the state carries LOCKED_BIT, so a reader's expected value does not match and it returns None and hashes the input itself. Under the lock the reader returns the stored value only if key.equivalent holds, which for [u8] against Key compares the slice of length len, so length and every byte must match (alloy keccak_cache.rs line 88 in 1.6.0, line 128 in 1.6.1). insert_inner (lines 389-439) takes the lock with expected None, which fails if the bucket is locked, writes key and value together, and releases with a Release store of the new tag (unlock, line 613). An ABA case in which another key with the same 64 bit hash replaces the entry between the reader's load and its compare-exchange leaves a reader that fails the equality test and recomputes. The value stored is imp(input) computed for the same input as the key (get_or_try_insert_with_ref, lines 506-524). This build has no lock-free read path: the string LOCK_FREE does not occur in lib.rs. Evidence: https://static.crates.io/crates/fixed-cache/fixed-cache-0.1.10.crate (src/lib.rs); https://static.crates.io/crates/alloy-primitives/alloy-primitives-1.6.0.crate; https://static.crates.io/crates/alloy-primitives/alloy-primitives-1.6.1.crate
- Ethereum, Optimism, Base, Unichain, Ink, Soneium, X Layer, Zora, Worldchain, Celo, MegaETH, Tempo, Arc, cycle 11. Does the KECCAK256 opcode go through the cache in each interpreter these nodes run, and does the hashing of storage keys for the state trie go through it as well. Result: Both do where the feature is on, and only the opcode result reaches the PoolManager. revm-interpreter 37.0.3 (X Layer), 42.0.0 (Base) and 43.0.2 (op-reth v2.9.0-rc.1) implement KECCAK256 in instructions/system.rs lines 18-40 as KECCAK_EMPTY for length 0, else primitives::keccak256 over the memory slice, and revm-primitives 24.0.1, 42.0.0 and 43.0.0 re-export alloy_primitives::keccak256 (lib.rs lines 39-41). evm2 at rev 66687c18, which reth v2.11.0 runs, calls alloy_primitives::keccak256 in interpreter/instructions/crypto.rs lines 2 and 14. alloy-primitives utils/mod.rs lines 147-150 route keccak256 through keccak_cache::compute when keccak-cache-global is set. reth's trie hashes account and slot keys with the same function (crates/trie/common/src/key.rs line 16, hashed_state.rs line 55). Those hashed keys feed the state root. SLOAD and SSTORE look up the plain slot word, so a wrong trie key hash would give a wrong state root and a halted or forked node, while the slot the PoolManager reads and writes comes only from the KECCAK256 opcode result. Evidence: https://static.crates.io/crates/revm-interpreter/revm-interpreter-37.0.3.crate; https://static.crates.io/crates/revm-interpreter/revm-interpreter-43.0.2.crate; https://static.crates.io/crates/revm-primitives/revm-primitives-24.0.1.crate; https://raw.githubusercontent.com/alloy-rs/evm2/66687c18b34d3bdbb899f5eb7605070615c03475/crates/evm2/src/interpreter/instructions/crypto.rs; https://raw.githubusercontent.com/paradigmxyz/reth/v2.11.0/crates/trie/common/src/key.rs; https://raw.githubusercontent.com/paradigmxyz/reth/v2.11.0/crates/trie/common/src/hashed_state.rs
- Ethereum, Optimism, Base, Unichain, Zora, Worldchain, Ink, Soneium, Celo, X Layer, Polygon, MegaETH, Tempo, Arc, cycle 11. Bucket collision test: KECCAK256 of 1 to 88 byte inputs chosen to share a bucket of the cache, sent interleaved so each lookup evicts the previous entry, in parallel requests, against the Python keccak. Result: No wrong hash on any of the 14 endpoints. The bucket index is hash & (2^17 - 1) with hash = rapidhash_v3_micro_inline::<false, false>(input, RapidSecrets::seed(0)) (alloy keccak_cache.rs lines 48-60 in 1.6.0, 88-100 in 1.6.1; fixed-cache calc; rapidhash 4.4.1 and 4.5.1 v3/rapid_const.rs lines 236-310, which are identical in the two versions). The script transcribes that function in Python. A pool of 34,400 inputs (300 random inputs of each length 1 to 88, 3,000 delta-slot inputs of address word then currency word as CurrencyDelta.sol builds them, 2,000 mapping-slot inputs and 3,000 position-key inputs of 58 bytes as Position.sol builds them) fell into 3,723 buckets that hold two or more inputs. 3,528 of those buckets mix lengths and 1,556 hold a PoolManager-shaped input. Each bucket was sent as A B A B A B plus A without its last byte, A with an extra zero byte and A again. 300 extra groups put 87 byte inputs, which are cached, next to their 88 byte extensions, which skip the cache. That is 36,059 hashes per round, in chunks of 500 records, four requests at a time, three rounds per endpoint, 108,177 hashes per endpoint, all as specified. World Chain and Celo do not enable the cache by their manifests and served as controls. Polygon's eth_call does not reach Bor's block-import cache (next item). The transcription of rapidhash could not be compared with the compiled crate because building a Rust harness was not permitted in this session. If it is wrong, the inputs still exercise the cache at random buckets, and every result was checked. - Polygon, cycle 11. Bor v2.11.1, which the Polygon publicnode endpoint reports (bor/cb3d19c5f690/v2.11.1-private), adds its own cache of 64 byte KECCAK256 results. Can it return a hash for another input. Result: No. opKeccak256 (core/vm/instructions.go lines 259-290) uses the cache only when the input is exactly 64 bytes and evm.Config.Keccak256Cache is set. It copies all 64 bytes into a [64]byte key, and on a miss it hashes the data and stores (key, hash). Keccak256Cache is BoundedCache[[64]byte, common.Hash] (keccak_cache.go line 26), a sync.Map keyed by the whole array, written with LoadOrStore so an entry is never replaced, and capped at 65,536 entries, past which Store does nothing (bounded_cache.go lines 28-59). The cache is created per block in ProcessBlock (blockchain.go lines 1276-1288, 1328-1329 and 1348) and given to the prefetcher and the BlockSTM V2 workers. Speculative runs can only add pairs of an input and its true hash, which are right in any later run. eth_call does not set the field, so the bucket test on Polygon could not reach it. The 64 byte inputs it serves are the delta slots and mapping slots of src/libraries/CurrencyDelta.sol:12-14 and src/libraries/TickBitmap.sol:69-70. The same block adds an ecrecover result cache (core/vm/evm.go lines 57-87). The PoolManager source has no ecrecover or staticcall (grep of src/), so that cache is outside its path. Evidence: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/0xPolygon/bor/v2.11.1/core/vm/instructions.go; https://raw.githubusercontent.com/0xPolygon/bor/v2.11.1/core/vm/keccak_cache.go; https://raw.githubusercontent.com/0xPolygon/bor/v2.11.1/core/vm/bounded_cache.go; https://raw.githubusercontent.com/0xPolygon/bor/v2.11.1/core/blockchain.go; https://raw.githubusercontent.com/0xPolygon/bor/v2.11.1/core/vm/evm.go
- BNB Smart Chain, Arbitrum One, Robinhood Chain, Elysium, Avalanche, cycle 11. Do the other geth-family clients put a cache in front of KECCAK256. Result: Not in the sources read. BSC v1.8.2 (the version the BSC endpoint reports) computes crypto.Keccak256Hash(data) on every call (core/vm/instructions.go lines 232-243). The OffchainLabs go-ethereum master branch, which Nitro builds on, and the ava-labs libevm main branch, which avalanchego 1.15.3 builds on, reset a per-interpreter Keccak state and hash the data on every call (instructions.go lines 236-246 in both). For Nitro and libevm these are branch heads, not the commits the endpoints run. Evidence: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/bnb-chain/bsc/v1.8.2/core/vm/instructions.go; https://raw.githubusercontent.com/OffchainLabs/go-ethereum/master/core/vm/instructions.go; https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ava-labs/libevm/main/core/vm/instructions.go
- Base, X Layer, cycle 11. L-633: X Layer pins ruint 1.18.0 and Base ruint 1.19.0, inside RUSTSEC-2026-0220. Does every SHL, SHR, SAR and BYTE handler of the revm-interpreter they pin clamp the amount before calling ruint, and does any precompile or handler they run call a ruint shift with an unclamped amount. Result: The handlers clamp, and the other code read has no unclamped shift. The advisory says the shifted values of overflowing_shl and overflowing_shr were right and only the overflow flag was wrong, and that wrapping_shl and wrapping_shr took the amount modulo 2^32. revm-interpreter 37.0.3 (X Layer) and 42.0.0 (Base) convert the amount with as_usize_saturated (macros.rs lines 122-126) and call << and >> (which are wrapping_shl and wrapping_shr) and arithmetic_shr only when the amount is below 256, else return 0 or the sign fill. BYTE indexes only below 32 (bitwise.rs lines 107-158). SIGNEXTEND shifts by at most 247 (arithmetic.rs lines 126-136). A Python transcription of the ruint 1.19.0 u256 paths of wrapping_shl, wrapping_shr and arithmetic_shr (bits.rs lines 437-467, 573-603, 612-623) matched the EVM definition on 509,184 cases covering every amount 0 to 255. A grep of revm-precompile 36.0.3 and 42.0.1, op-revm 20.0.0, revm-handler 20.0.3 and 42.0.1, alloy-evm 0.36.0 and 0.38.0 and alloy-op-evm 0.32.0 finds no call to a wrapping, overflowing, checked or saturating shift, and every << or >> with a U256 operand uses a constant amount. Base's crates/common/evm sources (precompiles/mod.rs, handler.rs, evm.rs and the other 11 files) shift only by constants. base-common-evm2 is in the Base workspace, but no package in the Base lockfile depends on it. The xlayer-reth crates directory has no EVM or precompile crate (builder, chainspec, flashblocks, intercept, legacy-rpc, monitor, rcs-filter, rpc, tests, version), and those crates were not read line by line. Evidence: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/rustsec/advisory-db/main/crates/ruint/RUSTSEC-2026-0220.md; https://static.crates.io/crates/revm-interpreter/revm-interpreter-37.0.3.crate; https://static.crates.io/crates/revm-interpreter/revm-interpreter-42.0.0.crate; https://static.crates.io/crates/ruint/ruint-1.19.0.crate; https://static.crates.io/crates/revm-precompile/revm-precompile-42.0.1.crate; https://raw.githubusercontent.com/base/base/v1.5.6/crates/common/evm/src/handler.rs; https://github.com/okx/xlayer-reth/tree/v0.0.7/crates; research/network-risk/cycles/011/theme-keccak-cache.work/ruint119_shift.py

## Reading of the source (theme-monad-settlement-path)

- Monad, cycle 11. Which of the settlement opcodes Monad v0.16.5 compiles inline and which it hands to a runtime function that the interpreter also calls, and how the compiled code passes operands and takes the result of such a call. Result: Inline in compiled code: CALLER and ADDRESS (read_context_address), CALLVALUE (read_context_word), RETURNDATASIZE, CALLDATASIZE and MSIZE (read_context_uint32_to_word), CALLDATALOAD (Emitter::calldataload with the assembly helper monad_vm_runtime_load_bounded_le_raw) and SIGNEXTEND. Handed to a runtime function: KECCAK256 (runtime::sha3), CALLDATACOPY, RETURNDATACOPY, MCOPY, TLOAD, TSTORE, CALL, STATICCALL and SELFBALANCE (emitter.hpp 388-485, 525-552). The interpreter's instruction table calls the same runtime functions for these (instruction_table.hpp 821-833, 942-954, 1053-1065, 1306-1318, 1360-1390), so the eth_call tests of earlier cycles (the KECCAK256, MCOPY and copy vectors of the battery and the 50 call semantics tests of callsem.py) ran the code that block execution runs for them. The only compiled-specific part is the call glue. RuntimeImpl::pass stores every operand that is in a register into its stack slot, call_impl passes each operand as a pointer to that slot or to a rodata copy of a literal, in pop order, which is the order of the C++ parameters for every function above, and the result is written to a fresh stack slot at the new top (emitter.cpp 443-501). That slot can be the slot of the deepest input, which is the same aliasing the interpreter uses (call_runtime.hpp: the result pointer is the deepest stack argument). Each of these functions reads all its inputs before it writes the result: sha3 reads size and offset first (keccak.hpp 28-45), tload copies the key first (storage.hpp 35-45), and call and staticcall take the operands by reference into call_impl and write the result after it returns (call.cpp 198-221, 272-293). CALLVALUE uses the 32 byte big-endian env.value through movbe per limb or vpermq plus vpshufb, both a full byte reversal. Evidence: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/category-labs/monad/v0.16.5/category/vm/compiler/ir/x86/emitter.cpp lines 443-590, 2238-2281, 3043-3082, 3385-3394, 3816-3892; https://raw.githubusercontent.com/category-labs/monad/v0.16.5/category/vm/compiler/ir/x86/emitter.hpp lines 130-205, 388-565; https://raw.githubusercontent.com/category-labs/monad/v0.16.5/category/vm/interpreter/call_runtime.hpp; https://raw.githubusercontent.com/category-labs/monad/v0.16.5/category/vm/interpreter/instruction_table.hpp; https://raw.githubusercontent.com/category-labs/monad/v0.16.5/category/vm/runtime/keccak.hpp; https://raw.githubusercontent.com/category-labs/monad/v0.16.5/category/vm/runtime/storage.hpp; https://raw.githubusercontent.com/category-labs/monad/v0.16.5/category/vm/runtime/call.cpp; copies in research/network-risk/cycles/011/theme-monad-settlement-path.work/src
- Monad, cycle 11. Monad v0.16.5 inline CALLDATALOAD at every offset location the emitter distinguishes (literal up to 2^31-1, literal from 2^31 to 2^32-1 through rodata, literal of 2^32 or more, general register live and not live in each of the three register sets, AVX register, stack slot), with is_bounded_by_bits<32>, the 32 byte load or the bounded load helper for fewer than 32 remaining bytes, and the byte swap. Result: No mismatch with the specification in 411,200 cases: every calldata length from 0 to 300 with every offset from 0 to length plus 40 and nine large offsets at each location, and 50,000 random cases with lengths up to 5,000 and offsets whose upper limbs are set. Every branch of monad_vm_runtime_load_bounded_le_raw ran (sizes 1, 2, 3 to 4, 5 to 8, 9 to 16, 17 to 31 and zero or negative), and no case read a byte outside the calldata buffer. The 17 to 24 byte case depends on shrd and shrx masking a count of 64 to 120 to six bits; the transcription models that masking and the result is right. Seven of ten planted faults were caught (between 280 and 31,960 failing cases each); the three not caught are equivalent for calldata below 2^31 bytes (a 16 bit size read, a 31 bit offset mask and the rodata threshold). The PoolManager runs CALLDATALOAD at 44 sites, 40 with a literal offset; in the 584 scripts compared below the compiled transcription executed it 84,050 times in the PoolManager. Evidence: research/network-risk/cycles/011/theme-monad-settlement-path.work/settlejit.py, run_units.py, units.json, mutate.py, mutate.json; https://raw.githubusercontent.com/category-labs/monad/v0.16.5/category/vm/compiler/ir/x86/emitter.cpp lines 636-644, 3155-3258 and is_bounded_by_bits; https://raw.githubusercontent.com/category-labs/monad/v0.16.5/category/vm/runtime/transmute.S lines 22-118
