Lead L-694, toolchain part: does the Succinct toolchain behind Base's range program carry the 128 bit shift-parts fault of LLVM 235261 or a like one in RISC-V lowering?. Result: The range workspace at base/base 6efa7566 names toolchain succinct-1.96.0-64bit-v2 and target riscv64im-succinct-zkvm-elf (Cargo.toml comment, read in cycle 13). That tag of succinctlabs/rust is rustc 1.96.0, its target spec is generic-rv64 with +m and LP64, and it pins rust-lang/llvm-project 1cb4e38 on branch rustc/22.1-2026-01-27. In that LLVM, RISCVTargetLowering::lowerShiftLeftParts and lowerShiftRightParts build the select condition with getSetCC(ShamtMinusXLen, 0, SETLT), which is a true 0-or-1 boolean, so the MIPS fault shape cannot arise. With +m, MUL and MULHU on i64 are native and i128 MUL is custom-lowered. Cycle 13's RV64IM rebuild of the same crates matched all vectors. No RISC-V scalar i128 miscompile was found in a search of the 2026 LLVM bug lists; the one 2026 RISC-V wrong-code report read (issue 176001) concerns vector register spills, which an RV64IM target without V does not use. Evidence: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/succinctlabs/rust/succinct-1.96.0-64bit-v2/compiler/rustc_target/src/spec/targets/riscv64im_succinct_zkvm_elf.rs ; https://raw.githubusercontent.com/succinctlabs/rust/succinct-1.96.0-64bit-v2/.gitmodules ; https://github.com/succinctlabs/rust/tree/succinct-1.96.0-64bit-v2/src ; https://raw.githubusercontent.com/rust-lang/llvm-project/1cb4e3833c1919c2e6fb579a23ac0e2b22587b7e/llvm/lib/Target/RISCV/RISCVISelLowering.cpp ; https://github.com/llvm/llvm-project/issues/176001
- all 21 networks, cycle 14. Per network: after this unit, is there a proof or settlement build that an ordinary account can drive to a result that differs from the node on an opcode the PoolManager runs?. Result: No on every network as far as tested. OP Mainnet, Unichain, Ink: no, the respected kona prestate is scanned on every path and its own shift handlers run (this unit). Base: no known divergence. The toolchain lowering is sound, the rebuild matched, and the published ELF itself was not run. Celo, X Layer: unknown program, but the challengers are allowlisted, so an ordinary account cannot use it. Arbitrum One: no, the replay go-ethereum f1c5f02 computes the same words as 0e44603. Robinhood Chain, Elysium: no, same replay and whitelisted validators. World Chain, Zora, Soneium: operator or permissioned games (cycle 12). Ethereum, Polygon, BNB Smart Chain, Avalanche, Monad, MegaETH, Tempo, Arc, HyperEVM: no separate proof build, covered by OPCODES.md. Evidence: research/network-risk/cycles/014/theme-proof-images.work ; research/network-risk/OPCODES.md ; research/network-risk/cycles/013/theme-proof-builds-2.research.json

## Reading of the source (theme-reth-cache-drift)

- all 21 networks, cycle 14. Whether the PoolManager's own storage, its transient storage, or the balanceOf staticcall of sync can read a stale word from the reth execution cache branch for a destroyed account without code. Result: The branch is taken only for accounts whose info at the start of the block had the empty code hash and that the block destroyed. The PoolManager has had code since deployment and cannot be destroyed under EIP-6780, so its account is never on the branch and insert_storage replaces each of its written words after every block. Transient storage (src/libraries/CurrencyDelta.sol:21-39, src/libraries/CurrencyReserves.sol:17-36, src/libraries/NonzeroDeltaCount.sol:14) lives in the EVM journal and is not in the execution cache. The balanceOf read of sync and settle (src/PoolManager.sol:279-288, 349-364, src/types/Currency.sol:90-95) reads the token's storage, which can be stale only for a token created in the block that destroyed its address. The account cache entry of a branch account is removed, so its code hash and balance are read fresh, and code is looked up by code hash. Evidence: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/celo-org/reth/74cc8bbce7631c3586ab446460590fef6630d258/crates/engine/execution-cache/src/cached_state.rs lines 863-882; src/PoolManager.sol:279-288
- all 21 networks, cycle 14. Which accounts can reach the stale branch, including EIP-7702 delegated accounts, accounts emptied under EIP-161, and the contracts a victim pool depends on. Result: Reachable: an address created and self-destructed in one transaction, an account without code that a creation landed on and that self-destructed in the same transaction, and an empty account removed under EIP-161, each re-created later in the same block. All of them carry code deployed in that block. An EIP-7702 delegated account has a non-empty code hash, so a destroyed one would take the clear-everything branch, and it cannot be destroyed because it was not created in the transaction and its nonce is above zero; after its delegation is cleared it keeps storage and a nonce and still cannot be destroyed or created over. Tokens, hooks, routers, PositionManager and Permit2 already used by a pool had code before any such block and cannot be destroyed; a proxy runs its implementation with the proxy's own storage. A victim pool can therefore depend on a branch account only by choosing a token or hook made in that pattern, which is an attacker-made contract (actor pool-creator). Evidence: https://patch-diff.githubusercontent.com/raw/paradigmxyz/reth/pull/28148.patch
- Ethereum, Unichain, Ink, Soneium, Tempo, Arc, cycle 14. Is the old branch present at the reth revision the endpoint reports. Result: No. Ethereum reth v2.11.0, op-reth v2.10.0-rc.4 (65e80332, pins ethereum-optimism/reth op-v2.7.0-2 ce8cfb1; rc.1 pins op-v2.7.0-1 ed91041, also fixed), Tempo v1.19.1 (paradigmxyz/reth 167933d) and Arc v0.8.6-rc1 and v0.8.5 (circlefin/arc-reth 508cbdf) all remove the account only when its current info is None and otherwise write the re-created account's storage (cached_state.rs lines 1165-1185, Arc 864-884). Evidence: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ethereum-optimism/reth/ce8cfb1fd25c2da86004eda677dc55dfa0d5c0af/crates/engine/execution-cache/src/cached_state.rs; https://raw.githubusercontent.com/paradigmxyz/reth/v2.11.0/crates/engine/execution-cache/src/cached_state.rs; https://raw.githubusercontent.com/paradigmxyz/reth/167933d17ad47fe7354f5942ddd6f0d3e343bb41/crates/engine/execution-cache/src/cached_state.rs; https://raw.githubusercontent.com/circlefin/arc-reth/508cbdf7d6ba49b4ce735d678863897067fa381a/crates/engine/execution-cache/src/cached_state.rs; web3_clientVersion and arc_getVersion queried 2026-11-24
- Optimism, Zora, Worldchain, X Layer, BNB Smart Chain, cycle 14. Does the block producer of OP Mainnet, Zora, World Chain, X Layer or reth-bsc read through the execution cache. Result: No in the public code. The op-reth OP payload builder destructures BuildArguments with .. and reads state_by_block_hash directly (op-reth v2.8.1 rust/op-reth/crates/payload/src/builder.rs line 257, rc.4 line 193). conduit-op-reth v2.5.1 and world-chain v2.8.2 use an op-reth OP builder whose lock entry does not depend on reth-execution-cache, and World Chain's flashblocks builder discards the cache (crates/builder/src/payload_builder.rs line 125, execution_cache: _). xlayer-builder and the X Layer OP builder do not depend on reth-execution-cache. The reth-bsc miner sources (src/node/miner) do not reference it. On these networks the branch is on the validation path of followers only. Evidence: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/op-reth/v2.8.1/rust/op-reth/crates/payload/src/builder.rs; https://raw.githubusercontent.com/worldcoin/world-chain/v2.8.2/crates/builder/src/payload_builder.rs
- Unichain, Ink, Soneium, Optimism, cycle 14. Lead L-703: what changed between op-reth v2.10.0-rc.1 and rc.4 in the engine tree, execution cache, prewarming, state root task and op-revm handler. Result: The two Cargo.locks differ only in the reth fork tag (op-v2.7.0-1 ed91041 to op-v2.7.0-2 ce8cfb1, 106 crates), snap 1.1.1 to 1.1.2 and a removed example; revm 43.0.3, revm-interpreter 43.0.2 and alloy-evm 0.39.0 are unchanged. All files reachable from the module trees of reth's engine/tree (36 files, including prewarm, the block access list executor, txpool prewarm, precompile cache and state root strategy), engine/execution-cache, trie/sparse, revm, evm/evm, engine/primitives, payload/basic and storage/provider are byte-identical between the two fork commits. In the optimism repository, op-revm changes only test code in fast_lz.rs (the module after line 99 is cfg(test)); handler.rs is unchanged. op-reth's evm, consensus, payload and node changes remove type parameters (OpEvmConfig now fixed to OpChainSpec and OpReceipt), keep the same EVM factory OpEvmFactory with NullRefundPolicy, and add a test for the Isthmus withdrawals root. No change alters a storage, transient storage, balance or code read inside a transaction. Evidence: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/op-reth/v2.10.0-rc.1/rust/Cargo.lock; https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/op-reth/v2.10.0-rc.4/rust/Cargo.lock; https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/op-reth/v2.10.0-rc.4/rust/op-revm/src/fast_lz.rs
- Ethereum, Optimism, Base, Unichain, Zora, Worldchain, Ink, Soneium, Celo, X Layer, BNB Smart Chain, Tempo, Arc, cycle 14. Other caches in front of state on reth based clients, looking for an index that is not the full content or address. Result: The execution cache indexes code by code hash, accounts by full address and storage by (full address, full slot); clear() keeps the code cache because its mapping cannot change. The precompile cache is per precompile address, indexed by the full input bytes, returns an entry only when the stored spec matches and the call has at least the recorded gas, stores only successful outputs that consumed no state gas, and is applied only through map_cacheable_precompiles, which skips precompiles marked stateful; Celo's transfer precompile is built with .stateful() (alloy-celo-evm lib.rs line 125). The payload builder's CachedReads is indexed by address and slot, is pre-filled from a committed block and used only for a job whose parent is that block hash, and falls through to the database for slots it lacks. Base's txpool prewarm keeps its own CachedReads and starts a fresh one for each head. The sparse trie cache feeds only state root computation. The src/ code calls no precompile. Evidence: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ethereum-optimism/reth/ce8cfb1fd25c2da86004eda677dc55dfa0d5c0af/crates/engine/tree/src/tree/precompile_cache.rs; https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ethereum-optimism/reth/3c5f2f11c4e5a5647e6e911cd131ccf1bada4f25/crates/payload/basic/src/lib.rs lines 131-246; https://raw.githubusercontent.com/celo-org/celo-kona/refs/tags/celo/reth-v1.0.10/crates/alloy-celo-evm/src/lib.rs
- HyperEVM, cycle 14. HyperEVM nanoreth execution cache. Result: Blocks are produced by Hyperliquid's own node, which answers web3_clientVersion with hyperliquid evm Mainnet. The archive follower nanoreth pins hl-archive-node/reth 1450962, whose cache invalidates the whole storage of a destroyed account before continuing (crates/engine/tree/src/tree/cached_state.rs lines 381-387), so it has no stale words of that kind. Evidence: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/hl-archive-node/reth/14509628ed37e9a9b7110ea855a67f427c4d61fc/crates/engine/tree/src/tree/cached_state.rs
- Arbitrum One, Robinhood Chain, Elysium, Polygon, Avalanche, Monad, cycle 14. Exposure of non-reth networks to the reth execution cache fault. Result: Not applicable. Their endpoints report nitro v3.13.0-rc.9 and an unversioned nitro, bor v2.11.1, avalanchego 1.15.3 and Monad 0.16.7, none of which uses the reth engine tree. BNB Smart Chain's own endpoint runs geth v1.8.2; reth-bsc is covered in the follower finding. Evidence: web3_clientVersion on the endpoints in state/networks.json, queried 2026-11-24

## Reading of the source (theme-closed-producers-2)

- HyperEVM, cycle 15. L-738. Do mined v3 style swaps on HyperEVM, produced by the closed hl-node validator, match the exact FullMath, SqrtPriceMath and TickMath formulas of src/libraries on the 512 bit product branch, the amount above 2^160 branch, the overflow fallback of getNextSqrtPriceFromAmount0RoundingUp, and on swaps that end on a tick?. Result: Window: HyperEVM blocks 50,165,552 to 52,165,551 on the archive client https://rpc.purroofgroup.com, 3,268,303 v3 style Swap logs, 131,330 Mint and 221,319 Burn logs (research/network-risk/cycles/015/theme-closed-producers-2.work/raw/logs999.jsonl). Pools were identified from their own getters (factory, token0, token1, fee, tickSpacing) and kept only when factory.getPool(token0, token1, fee) or getPool(token0, token1, tickSpacing) returned the pool, which is what a PoolCreated log would establish; the PoolCreated log scan over 52 million blocks was started and abandoned as too slow. 431 pools of 14 factories pass, holding 2,258,337 swaps (69 percent). The largest factories are 0xff7b3e8c00e57ea31477c32a5b52a58eea47b072 (1,115,904 swaps), 0x07e60782535752be279929e2dffdd136db2e6b45 (495,284), 0xb1c0fa0b789320044a6f623cfe5ebda9562602e3 (278,022) and 0x32b9da73215255d50d84feb51540b75acc1324c2 (220,491). Stage A, without RPC: 1,686,939 swaps equal one v3 swap step to the unit from the price, tick and liquidity of the pool's previous log, 35,596 of them through the 512 bit branch of mulDiv or mulDivRoundingUp. No swap reached the overflow fallback of getNextSqrtPriceFromAmount0RoundingUp and no logged amount is at or above 2^160. 2,995 swaps end exactly on the price of a tick that is a multiple of the spacing. Stage B, with eth_call at the parent block for slot0, liquidity, the tick bitmap and liquidityNet, and the block's Mint and Burn logs applied in order: all 2,995 end-on-tick groups and random samples of 3,000 groups with a 512 bit step and 25,000 groups that may need one inside a multi-step swap (two random draws, which can overlap), 30,995 groups in all. 33,760 swaps reproduce price, tick, liquidity and both amounts to the unit, 19,015 of them through the 512 bit branch (65,309 mulDiv calls with a product of 512 bits), 7,359 with several steps. 22,032 needed the pool's real fee, which differs from fee() on dynamic fee pools and was found by search: one free parameter is fitted per swap and price, tick, liquidity and both amounts must then all match; most fees found are multiples of 100 pips between 0 and 4,000, and a few are other values such as 10,562. 4 did not reproduce: 0x47a2f2ff4d1e218bba017d19222073eaa07b5740289dcca39cd3c88a2ddae25c (block 50,624,670); 0x5a64629ddf197c4e3c2addd942cf25e0a55d7d0b4b659d56249adb3f9b471458 (block 51,255,107); 0xd144959f18fd332b6c3c8111486b41111e44e91ca82d1cc28ffd01b848df7eca (block 51,371,005); 0x3d3c51a3d7ee8bbd78940198e2850863299c7c9a20ff4d913a9d16251678cef0 (block 51,370,051). Each is explained by the collector: the pool also emitted a liquidity event with topic 0xd78218c0d304e8893cb3200abe394bbc8d5b7804d9c51f236df9fdcf481d02d3 (a Mint variant with ticks in topics 2 and 3) that the collector does not read, and with that event applied the liquidity before the swap equals the logged liquidity in every case (chkmis.py; for 0x47a2f2ff, 3,174,629,732,523,735,714,636 + 6,417,522,110,843,946,721,988 = 9,592,151,843,367,682,436,624, the logged value). Planted faults: MULMOD one too high on 512 bit products made 131 of 137 swaps fail, and getSqrtPriceAtTick one unit high on multiples of 10 made 117 of 121 fail, so the comparison sees both classes. A fallback fault cannot be shown because no mined swap reaches that branch. The transcription used is tools/opdiff/v4math.py of src/libraries/FullMath.sol:14-120, SqrtPriceMath.sol:31-52 and TickMath.sol:57-160. Validator output on the 512 bit branch is now checked on tens of thousands of swaps against 493 before. The fallback branch and amounts above 2^160 still have no mined instance on HyperEVM, in v3 style pools or in the PoolManager. Evidence: research/network-risk/cycles/015/theme-closed-producers-2.work/v3check.py and raw/stageA.json, raw/stageB-onTick.json, raw/stageB-m512.json, raw/stageB-m512q.json, raw/stageB-m512q2.json, raw/plant-mulmod.json, raw/plant-tick.json; eth_call and eth_getLogs on https://rpc.purroofgroup.com
- MegaETH, HyperEVM, cycle 15. L-728. Has any mined PoolManager transaction on MegaETH or HyperEVM called clear(), with an exact credit or otherwise?. Result: No. debug_traceTransaction with callTracer was run over every transaction that emitted a PoolManager log or an ERC-20 Transfer to the PoolManager: 51,233 on MegaETH (through block 32,770,383, https://mainnet.megaeth.com/rpc) and 2,783 on HyperEVM (through block 52,165,551, https://rpc.purroofgroup.com). Every trace returned; no call frame into the PoolManager carries selector 0x80f0b44c, clear(address,uint256), in a completed or reverted frame. The frames hold 64,663 and 2,910 unlock calls. So there is nothing to replay, and clear of an exact credit (src/PoolManager.sol:310-319, which compares amount.toInt128() with the caller's delta and books its negation) rests on the reference interpreter and the step traces of OPCODES.md on these two networks. A transaction that pays only native value and clears, with no log and no token transfer, would not be in the set. Evidence: research/network-risk/cycles/015/theme-closed-producers-2.work/clearscan.py, raw/clear-4326.jsonl, raw/clearx-4326.jsonl, raw/clear-999.jsonl, raw/clearx-999.jsonl
- MegaETH, cycle 15. L-732. Which reth revision do the public MegaETH locks name, and does its execution cache keep stale storage for an account that was destroyed and re-created without code in one block?. Result: mega-reth itself is not public (https://raw.githubusercontent.com/megaeth-labs/mega-reth/main/Cargo.toml returns 404) and the public RPC reports mega-reth/v2.2.3-72527bc; reth has no v2.2.3 tag (the execution cache file at that tag returns 404). mega-evm v1.7.4's Cargo.toml says it is built against reth v2.3.0 (revm 40.0.3, alloy-evm 0.36.0), and the stateless-validator lock at e1618ed7 pins reth tag v2.3.0 at commit 9384bc53d8c0c77e59cac83fdaaf3b372c6d2216. The execution cache at v2.2.0 and at v2.3.0 (identical to 9384bc53) still has the branch that reth pull request 28148 fixes: when an account was destroyed and its original info had no code, insert_state removes the account from the cache and continues, so a re-created account's new storage is never written to the cache and a value read earlier stays (cached_state.rs lines 904-923 at v2.3.0, 863-882 at v2.2.0). The pull request changes that to remove only when the account has no current info. Whether the MegaETH sequencer reads through this cache cannot be read. The branch only touches an address that held no code at the start of the block and was destroyed and re-created inside it, so it cannot reach the PoolManager's storage or a token or hook that an existing pool already uses; a contract the attacker re-creates is its own, which is at most pool-creator level, and a stale read on the sequencer would publish state that the stateless validator rejects, which is operator level. Evidence: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/paradigmxyz/reth/v2.3.0/crates/engine/execution-cache/src/cached_state.rs and https://patch-diff.githubusercontent.com/raw/paradigmxyz/reth/pull/28148.patch
- HyperEVM, cycle 15. L-748. Which HyperCore action produced the first unsigned system transfer in the name of 0xc20699185c15D0a2fD65779BB5d69f5b0B113c00, and can HyperCore do the same for a contract that no spot token links?. Result: The address is the USDC treasury address that Coinbase named as AQAv2 treasury deployer on 8 June 2026; it has no code (eth_getCode returns 0x) and nonce 1,057,535 at block 52,160,000. Binary search of eth_getTransactionCount on the archive client puts its first transaction in block 37,597,803 (2026-06-12 03:59:16 UTC): system transaction 0x2a36e3161a6271d7bcf0145928660f63fd5a5c0839fdcd2400b081107b991385 (0x01f391a92efbdff628ea8b24a09adaa08a215fca6f7b38cb3db7bbb8ed378b61 on the archive client), USDC transfer(0x6b9e773128f453f5c2c60935ee2de2cbc5390a24, 2,000,000,000) with gas price 0, next to a system transaction from 0x2000000000000000000000000000000000000000 to that linked contract. This is the AQAv2 rebalance: the Hyperliquid documentation says the treasury deployer designates the treasury address, AQAv2 is activated by validator vote after both deployers stake 500k HYPE and send authorization transactions from their staking accounts, and the linked HyperEVM contract then rebalances with the treasury address in a 9:1 ratio. The address was therefore designated by a staked deployer and activated by validator vote; it is not a contract that HyperCore picked without a record. For the PoolManager to be named the same way, a treasury deployer staking 500k HYPE and a validator vote would be needed, so F-020 stays at operator level. Evidence: https://hyperliquid.gitbook.io/hyperliquid-docs/hypercore/aligned-quote-assets; https://www.livebitcoinnews.com/coinbase-activates-aqav2-for-hyperliquid-usdc-treasury/; eth_getTransactionCount, eth_getBlockByNumber 0x23db20b on https://rpc.purroofgroup.com; eth_getSystemTxsByBlockNumber and eth_getCode on https://rpc.hyperliquid.xyz/evm

## Reading of the source (theme-evm2-jit-codegen)

- Ethereum, Tempo, cycle 15. Can the evm2 JIT crates be built here so that their own differential tests run on the PoolManager runtime?. Result: No. The LLVM backend needs LLVM 23 (crates/jit/README.md), and the machine has LLVM 18.1.3 (llvm-config --version). The workspace Cargo.toml patches the ark crates from a git repository on github.com, which this environment cannot clone, and codeload.github.com returned 403 for source archives of both revisions. The review therefore worked from source: 58 files of crates/jit (codegen, builtins, backend, llvm, runtime, context) were fetched from raw.githubusercontent.com at 66687c18 and at 35aa3280 by following module declarations (research/network-risk/cycles/015/theme-evm2-jit-codegen.work/crawl.py, copies in research/network-risk/cycles/015/theme-evm2-jit-codegen.work/r66 and r35), plus crates/evm2 at 66687c18. Between the two revisions 8 of the 58 files differ. In codegen the only change is block_analysis.rs lines 2249-2250, which gives opcodes flagged UNKNOWN no stack inputs, and a test. peephole.rs, const_fold.rs, translate/mod.rs, memory_sections.rs and sections.rs are byte-identical. Evidence: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/DaniPopes/evm2/66687c18b34d3bdbb899f5eb7605070615c03475/crates/jit/README.md
- Ethereum, Tempo, cycle 15. Which PoolManager opcodes the JIT sends to builtins that wrap the interpreter's own arithmetic, and whether those builtins match the interpreter. Result: The runtime (24,009 bytes, no metadata trailer) contains 112 distinct opcodes (research/network-risk/cycles/015/theme-evm2-jit-codegen.work/census.json). DIV, SDIV, MOD, SMOD, ADDMOD, MULMOD and EXP with an unknown exponent are calls to builtins (translate/mod.rs 776-803). The builtins call ruint wrapping_div, wrapping_rem, add_mod, mul_mod and pow, and evm2's i256_div and i256_mod (builtins/src/lib.rs 112-160). These are the same functions the interpreter uses, linked natively into the same binary at the same ruint version (builtins are resolved by address, builtins/src/ir.rs 1-40). The rev! macro reads the operands top first and writes the result into the lowest slot, which is the specified order. So MULMOD with modulus 2^256-1 at FullMath.sol:24 and with a pool denominator at FullMath.sol:48, SqrtPriceMath.sol:252 and FullMath.sol:112 runs the code that the 185,529 vectors already tested through the interpreter. KECCAK256, CALLDATALOAD, CALLDATACOPY, RETURNDATACOPY, MCOPY, SLOAD, SSTORE, TLOAD, TSTORE, LOG and the calls are builtins as well (lib.rs 162-575, 762-875) and were read: CALLDATALOAD past the end pads with zeros through evm2 read_word_padded, RETURNDATACOPY fails before charging gas when offset plus length exceeds the return data, MCOPY expands memory to max(dst, src) plus length, KECCAK256 of length 0 touches no memory, TSTORE fails in a static frame and TLOAD does not. Evidence: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/DaniPopes/evm2/66687c18b34d3bdbb899f5eb7605070615c03475/crates/jit/builtins/src/lib.rs
- Ethereum, Tempo, cycle 15. Inline lowering of SIGNEXTEND, BYTE, SHL, SHR, SAR, LT, GT, SLT, SGT, EQ, ISZERO and the JUMPI condition, transcribed with LLVM poison semantics. Result: No mismatch. SIGNEXTEND is select(ext < 31, (x << (248 - 8ext)) >>s (248 - 8ext), x), BYTE is select(i < 32, (v >> (248 - 8i)) & 0xff, 0), and the shifts select 0, or for SAR the sign fill, when the count exceeds 255; the poisoned shift result is only in the unselected arm (translate/mod.rs 685-691, 804-875). Comparisons are i256 icmp, ISZERO is icmp eq 0, and JUMPI branches on icmp ne of the whole word (line 1050). jitmodel.py runs these on 631,353 vectors (the battery and targeted sets, every pair of 196 edge values for every index and count, all 256 powers of two and their negations as divisors and moduli) and makes 1,068,620 checks against the specification without a mismatch or undefined operation. Planted faults are caught: BYTE guard < 33 (367 mismatches), shift guard > 256 (1,659), SAR default without the sign (2,746), SIGNEXTEND guard < 30 (31). A SIGNEXTEND guard of < 32 gives no mismatch because index 31 shifts by 0, so that mutation is equivalent. This covers the SIGNEXTEND, SAR, SDIV and SMOD of TickBitmap.compress and position (TickBitmap.sol:20-38, 54-67). Evidence: research/network-risk/cycles/015/theme-evm2-jit-codegen.work/jitmodel.py
- Ethereum, Tempo, cycle 15. Every peephole rule in peephole.rs, with most care for MULMOD with the constant moduli 2^96, 2^128 and 2^256-1, SDIV and SMOD by -1 and -2^255, EXP with a constant base or exponent, and the inline EXP gas. Result: No mismatch. A power of two modulus 2^k lowers MULMOD to (a*b mod 2^256) & (2^k - 1) and ADDMOD to (a+b mod 2^256) & (2^k - 1), which is exact because 2^k divides 2^256 (peephole.rs 161-213). This is the path for MULMOD by 2^128 at pc 22378 and by 2^96 at pc 22639, which a PUSH in the same block supplies (census.json). 2^256-1 and 1,000,000 are not powers of two and go to the ruint builtin. SDIV by -1 negates, by -2^255 returns x == -2^255, and by other signed powers of two uses LLVM sdiv, whose only undefined case is excluded; SMOD by 0, 1 or -1 is 0 and by other signed powers of two uses srem, which keeps the dividend's sign (53-160). EXP with a power of two base 2^k is select(e < ceil(256/k), 1 << ke, 0) and charges (263 - clz(e)) / 8 bytes of gas, which equals the specified byte length for every exponent tested (215-305). The PoolManager's own constant operands are a dividend of -887272 or 887272 for SDIV and SMOD (pc 7400-7443) and a dividend of 0xd76453e0 for DIV (BitMath.sol:45), which no rule matches, so they use the builtins. Planting a mask of 2^k instead of 2^k - 1 gives 14,252 mismatches. Evidence: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/DaniPopes/evm2/66687c18b34d3bdbb899f5eb7605070615c03475/crates/jit/codegen/src/compiler/translate/peephole.rs
- Ethereum, Tempo, cycle 15. Constant folding and range folding in the bytecode analysis (const_fold.rs), including folded constants that are stored in place of an executed instruction (translate/mod.rs 633-656). Result: No unsound rule. try_const_fold calls ruint and evm2 i256 for the arithmetic and writes its own rules only for DIV and MOD by zero, SIGNEXTEND, BYTE and the three shifts (const_fold.rs 113-168); these were transcribed and match on all vectors. try_range_fold (213-389) gives a range below 2^31 that must hold every result when at least one input is a range or an unknown value. 60,000 random abstract inputs (ranges, inline constants, large constants including the BitMath byte table words, and unknown values) were each tested on sampled concrete values: 657,425 cases, none outside the range. Planting a range one smaller for MOD gives 30 failures. EXP folds only when its exponent is constant, so its gas stays static (bytecode/mod.rs 751-767). Evidence: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/DaniPopes/evm2/66687c18b34d3bdbb899f5eb7605070615c03475/crates/jit/codegen/src/bytecode/passes/const_fold.rs
- Ethereum, Tempo, cycle 15. Edge refinement after a JUMPI in block_analysis.rs: the DUP, LT and GT patterns with ISZERO chains that bound a stack value on one edge, and at_most. Result: Sound. branch() (block_analysis.rs 1943-2017) recognises PUSH-target JUMPI after a DUP or a DUP and PUSH compared with LT or GT in either order, with any number of ISZEROs, and bounds the original value by c - 1 or c on the edge where the test says so. 38,465 random stacks, depths, constants and patterns were executed concretely and the bound held on every taken edge; a planted bound of c - 2 fails 20 times. at_most (160-168) keeps an infeasible edge's value unchanged and never widens a constant. Ranges only hold values below 2^31. Evidence: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/DaniPopes/evm2/66687c18b34d3bdbb899f5eb7605070615c03475/crates/jit/codegen/src/bytecode/passes/block_analysis.rs
- Ethereum, Tempo, cycle 15. Dynamic JUMP and JUMPI through the dispatch table, jump target conversion, and multi-target jumps that switch on the low 64 bits. Result: No mismatch. A dynamic target saturates to 2^64-1 when it does not fit in 64 bits (u256_to_u64_saturating, translate/mod.rs 2269-2277), and the table holds every valid JUMPDEST of the code (2102-2172). jumptable.py transcribes the rank table and finds that each of the 24,030 tested pcs (0 to max_pc + 64, 2^40 and 2^64-1) dispatches to its own JUMPDEST when it is one of the 610 valid ones and to the invalid jump block otherwise; shifting the bitmap by one plants 1,220 errors. A multi-target jump truncates to 64 bits only when the analysis committed every value: constant sets hold only valid targets, ranges are below 2^31, an enumerated invalid constant must fit in 64 bits (fits_switch_case, 1938-1941), and an unknown operand marks the state failed (1686-1742), so no value of 2^64 or more can alias a valid pc. Evidence: research/network-risk/cycles/015/theme-evm2-jit-codegen.work/jumptable.py
- Ethereum, Tempo, cycle 15. Memory expansion in compiled code: MLOAD and MSTORE inline checks, the per-section cache of checked ranges, the memory section analysis that skips checks, and mresize. Result: Correct as read. build_ensure_memory (translate/mod.rs 1858-1920) saturates offsets at 2^63-1, and mresize calls resize_evm with length 0, which still grows memory to the offset (evm2 memory.rs 101-114). A later access is exempt only if its base equals an earlier checked base and its constant addend is at least the earlier one, so its offset cannot exceed 2^64 and its end lies below memory already allocated. memory_sections.rs propagates a lower bound on memory size that is the minimum over predecessors (join_state 285-297) and only counts constant accesses that always expand memory; MCOPY counts max(dst, src) (bytecode/mod.rs 790-806). Checks are skipped only where that bound covers the exact required size. Evidence: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/DaniPopes/evm2/66687c18b34d3bdbb899f5eb7605070615c03475/crates/jit/codegen/src/bytecode/passes/memory_sections.rs
- Ethereum, Tempo, cycle 15. Gas charged per section against per-instruction charging, and stack checks at section entry: can compiled code return a different result from a call or decide a branch differently?. Result: No. Gas sections end at every branching instruction and at every instruction whose host effect depends on the remaining gas: calls, creates, SLOAD, SSTORE, BALANCE, EXTCODE*, SELFDESTRUCT and host-table opcodes (sections.rs 229-256, bytecode/mod.rs 1214-1240). The static gas of the section is charged at its head, so a frame that runs out of gas inside a section halts at its head instead of a few instructions later, with the same exceptional halt, all frame gas consumed and every effect reverted. GAS returns the remaining gas plus the gas owed by later instructions of its section (translate/mod.rs 1143-1153, sections.rs 109-141), which is the specified value. Sections without a check carry the deficit as negative remaining gas until a signed check before any builtin that charges or reads gas. Stack bounds are checked at the head of a stack section and never ahead of a host-effect instruction. At 35aa3280 the SSTORE builtin skips a cold load when the remaining gas is below the full cold cost, as the interpreter at that revision does; the SLOAD builtin is unchanged and uses the additional cold cost like the interpreter (evm2 host.rs 14-31 at both revisions). Evidence: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/DaniPopes/evm2/66687c18b34d3bdbb899f5eb7605070615c03475/crates/jit/codegen/src/bytecode/passes/sections.rs
- Ethereum, Tempo, cycle 15. How a node decides to compile a contract, whether compiled and interpreted frames mix in one transaction, and what happens to a block when they disagree. Result: evm2 compiles a code hash after 8 lookups (jit_hot_threshold) when the code is at most 24 KiB, 24,576 bytes (runtime/config.rs 17, 280-290, 368-377). The PoolManager's deployed code is 24,009 bytes on Ethereum and on Tempo (eth_getCode, queried 2026-11-25), so it is eligible even under evm2's default, and reth v2.11.0 removes the limit (max-bytecode-len default 0) and keeps the threshold of 8. The decision is per frame: run_supported looks up the code hash and spec, runs the compiled function if it is resident and otherwise returns None so that the interpreter runs the frame (runtime/src/evm2_evm.rs 59-104). Compilation runs in background workers, so one transaction can run the PoolManager frame compiled and a hook or token frame interpreted, or the reverse. On Ethereum, a reth node whose compiled code disagreed with the specification would compute a different state root and fork itself off, while geth and the other clients decide the canonical chain (F-129). Tempo has one client; its release binary is built without the JIT feature (cleared in cycle 14), so no Tempo validator runs this code. Evidence: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/DaniPopes/evm2/66687c18b34d3bdbb899f5eb7605070615c03475/crates/jit/runtime/src/runtime/config.rs
- Ethereum, Tempo, cycle 15. Whether an ordinary account can reach compiled code on the networks.json endpoints through eth_call or switch it on. Result: No. The Ethereum endpoint reports reth/v2.11.0-b9abbcc, rpc_modules lists rpc, net, web3, txpool, debug, eth and trace, and reth_jit returns Method not found (queried 2026-11-25). Tempo reports tempo/v1.19.1-a9d6748 and refuses rpc_modules. Only an operator can enable the JIT, so the actor for any JIT fault is operator. Evidence: https://ethereum-rpc.publicnode.com
- Optimism, Base, Unichain, Zora, Worldchain, Ink, Soneium, Celo, X Layer, Arbitrum One, Robinhood Chain, Elysium, Polygon, BNB Smart Chain, Avalanche, Monad, MegaETH, Arc, HyperEVM, cycle 15. Does any of the other 19 networks run the evm2 JIT?. Result: No. web3_clientVersion on 2026-11-25 (research/network-risk/cycles/015/theme-evm2-jit-codegen.work/clientversions.json): OP Mainnet op-reth v2.8.1, Unichain, Ink and Soneium op-reth v2.10.0-rc.4, Base reth v2.5.2 base v1.5.6, Zora conduit-op-reth v2.5.1, Worldchain world-chain v2.8.2, Celo reth v2.2.0, X Layer reth v2.3.0. op-reth v2.10.0-rc.4 and v2.8.1 build on revm 43 and op-revm with no evm2 dependency (rust/Cargo.toml of those tags), and reth v2.2.0, v2.3.0, v2.5.2 and v2.8.2 have no evm2 entry in their manifests. Arbitrum One and Elysium run Nitro, Polygon bor, BNB Smart Chain geth, Avalanche avalanchego, Arc its revm based node, and Monad, MegaETH and HyperEVM their own executors, which earlier cycles read separately. Robinhood Chain answered 429 to this query and runs Nitro by earlier cycles. Evidence: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/op-reth/v2.10.0-rc.4/rust/Cargo.toml

## Reading of the source (theme-monad-emitter-blocks)

- Monad, cycle 15. Task 2 (lead L-726): is the PoolManager compiled at all by Monad's x86 emitter. Method: the emitter was built from downloaded source (category-labs/monad v0.16.7 and v0.16.5 category/vm and category/core from cdn.jsdelivr.net, asmjit at commit 9eb6edbf711ceb25346ee40bae68b40a4505cdf5 from raw.githubusercontent.com, evmc master of category-labs/evmc with the fork's four struct fields added by hand), the runtime symbols it only references were stubbed, and native::compile was run with the production CompilerConfig on the build of this checkout and on the code read with eth_getCode from 0x188d586ddcf52439676ca21a244753fa19f9ea8e at https://rpc.monad.xyz (24,009 bytes, sha256 prefix 288b97729c9e4f34; it differs from build/PoolManager.json only in the 20 immutable bytes at offset 13606, which hold the PoolManager address). Result: It is compiled. The size check compares Emitter::estimate_size() (text size + 32 per pending CALLDATALOAD handler + read-only data + 4 x bytecode size, emitter.cpp 1020-1030) with max_code_size(10,240, 24,009) = 10,240 + 32 x 24,009 = 778,528 bytes (x86.hpp 53-65, types.hpp CompilerConfig max_code_size_offset = 10 x 1024, x86.cpp 308-315 and 468-479). The built emitter prints 285,084 bytes for the deployed code and 285,059 for the build with a zero immutable under v0.16.7, and 284,482 and 284,425 under v0.16.5, for MonadTraits MONAD_EIGHT, NINE and TEN alike, and returns an entry point (error_code NoError). This is a measurement from a build, not a bound. The asmjit commit is the vcpkg pin of 2025-05-08, not the submodule pin of the release, which could not be read without the GitHub API; a different asmjit could move the estimate by a few percent at most, and the margin is a factor of 2.7. Evidence: https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/gh/category-labs/monad@v0.16.7/category/vm/compiler/ir/x86.cpp ; https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/gh/category-labs/monad@v0.16.7/category/vm/compiler/ir/x86.hpp ; https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/gh/category-labs/monad@v0.16.7/category/vm/compiler/ir/x86/emitter.cpp ; https://raw.githubusercontent.com/microsoft/vcpkg/master/ports/asmjit/portfile.cmake ; eth_getCode 0x188d586ddcf52439676ca21a244753fa19f9ea8e at https://rpc.monad.xyz block 0x775837e ; cycles/015/theme-monad-emitter-blocks.work/driver.cpp, drv, drv165
- Monad, cycle 15. Task 3 (lead L-725): which execution mode Monad validators run by default and after how much interpreted gas the PoolManager is compiled. Result: The execution daemon builds vm::VM vm{trace_calls ? InterpreterOnly : Dual} (cmd/monad/main.cpp line 488 at v0.16.7, line 479 at v0.16.5), so a node runs Dual unless it is started with --trace_calls. The published full node instructions recommend --trace_calls only for archive and RPC nodes, and the validator installation page says nothing about execution flags. The docs list monad 0.16.5 for mainnet and 0.16.7 for testnet. In Dual mode VM::execute_raw (vm.cpp 140-191, identical in v0.16.5 and v0.16.7) runs a contract in the interpreter and starts asynchronous compilation once the gas the interpreter has spent on that code hash, summed over all executions, reaches max_code_size(10,240, code size), which is 778,528 gas for the 24,009 byte PoolManager; when the node's code cache is not yet warm it compiles at once. A validator that follows the published setup therefore runs the PoolManager as native code after its first few transactions, and RPC nodes with --trace_calls interpret it. Evidence: https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/gh/category-labs/monad@v0.16.5/cmd/monad/main.cpp ; cycles/014/theme-monad-native-path.work/src/monad-v0.16.7_cmd_monad_main.cpp lines 484-488 ; https://docs.monad.xyz/node-ops/full-node-installation.md ; https://docs.monad.xyz/node-ops/validator-installation.md ; https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/gh/category-labs/monad@v0.16.7/category/vm/vm.cpp ; https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/gh/category-labs/monad@v0.16.7/category/vm/code.hpp
- Monad, cycle 15. Task 1: the compiled code of the never-mined paths against Monad's interpreter. A harness (harness.cpp) links Monad's real interpreter (interpreter::execute), the real emitter (native::compile) and the real runtime library from v0.16.7, with one in-memory host that keeps storage, transient storage, warm sets, logs and balances and reverts them per frame. Every transaction runs twice from the same state, once interpreted and once as native code, with MonadTraits MONAD_TEN, and the harness compares every call result (status, gas left, return bytes), all storage and transient storage, balances and logs. Users and an ERC20 are host-level accounts; inside unlockCallback a user runs a script of PoolManager calls and can read its own delta through exttload and pay it, mint it, or clear it exactly. Paths: clear of an exact credit (src/PoolManager.sol:310-319), transferFrom and burn through an allowance or an operator (src/ERC6909.sol:35-48, src/ERC6909Claims.sol:13-22), approve and setOperator (src/ERC6909.sol:50-64), donate (src/libraries/Pool.sol:466-480), the overflow fallback of getNextSqrtPriceFromAmount0RoundingUp (src/libraries/SqrtPriceMath.sol:52), the amount above 2^160 branch of getNextSqrtPriceFromAmount1RoundingDown (src/libraries/SqrtPriceMath.sol:97), and take, mint, clear and swap amounts drawn from edge sets around 2^64, 2^96, 2^127, 2^128, 2^159 to 2^161, 2^255 and 2^256 - 1. Result: No difference. 20,000 mixed scenarios (629,823 transactions and 676,709 calls inside unlocks) and nine per-path batteries of 100,000 calls each (approve, transferFrom, burn, clear, donate, fallback, amount above 2^160, take, swap; 291,020 transactions) give identical results in the interpreter and in native code, gas left included. The v0.16.5 build gives the same on 5,450 scenarios. The only raw difference is the status class of an exceptional halt: native code reports EVMC_FAILURE where the interpreter reports EVMC_OUT_OF_GAS, both with zero gas left; a receipt and a calling frame see only failure, so the harness compares halts as one class. A trace build of the interpreter records coverage: every instruction of clear (17 of 17), transferFrom (60 of 60), approve, setOperator, _burnFrom (37 of 37), Pool.donate (42 of 42), UnsafeMath.simpleMulDiv (35 of 35) and the fallback at SqrtPriceMath.sol:52 (12 of 12) ran; 7,505 of 10,418 PoolManager instructions ran in total. Two planted emitter faults are caught: SUB without borrow propagation (emitter.cpp 2481) makes 200 of 200 mixed and 90 of 90 battery scenarios differ, and an off-by-one in LT with a literal left operand (emitter.cpp 4029) makes 111 of 200 mixed and 48 of 90 battery scenarios differ. The emitter's own assembly log (CompilerConfig asm_log_path, with a comment for every EVM instruction and block) was written for the deployed code (pm.asm, 48,691 lines) and cut into the blocks that hold an instruction of each path (blocks/*.asm, blocks/summary.json, blocks/routines.json). Result: The paths occupy 85 blocks with 940 EVM instructions and 3,264 x86 instructions: clear 5 blocks (0xde6 to 0xe31), transferFrom 11, approve 1 (0x2518), setOperator 1 (0x20c1), _burnFrom 7, Pool.donate 8, the fallback 3 (0x5d5d, 0x5d6c, 0x5d71), getNextSqrtPriceFromAmount0RoundingUp 15, getNextSqrtPriceFromAmount1RoundingDown 13, simpleMulDiv 6. Of the EVM instructions, 624 emit no code (PUSH, DUP, SWAP and POP live in the virtual stack), 163 call runtime routines (DIV and MOD of variable operands, SLOAD, SSTORE, TLOAD, TSTORE, KECCAK256, LOG, CALL, memory growth), 112 use AVX moves for block-exit spills and wide literals, 52 are four-limb GPR arithmetic or comparisons (cmp or sub followed by sbb, add followed by adc), and the rest are shifts, setcc after fused ISZERO pairs, and branches. A comparison feeding JUMPI stays in CPU flags, and a dynamic JUMP checks the target below 24,009 with the three upper limbs zero and then goes through a jump table over every byte offset (fallback block 0x5d71). The comparison of whole transactions above runs exactly these instruction sequences on all their entries, so a Python model of each routine was not needed; the comparison is with Monad's interpreter, which cycles 1 to 14 matched to the specification on 185,529 vectors and the mined replays, and not with pyevm.py. - Monad, cycle 15. Whether the overflow fallback at src/libraries/SqrtPriceMath.sol:52 and the amount above 2^160 branches at src/libraries/SqrtPriceMath.sol:97 and :105 can decide the outcome of a swap that succeeds, which would make a compiled-only fault there reach funds. Result: They cannot. The fallback runs only on an exact-input step that stops short of its target (src/libraries/SwapMath.sol:74-82) with amountRemainingLessFee times the current price sqrtC at or above 2^256 (src/libraries/SqrtPriceMath.sol:41-43), so the input is at least 2^256 / sqrtC. Inside one step the token1 output equals input times sqrtC times sqrtN / 2^192, where sqrtN is the price at which the step stops, so the output is at least 2^64 times sqrtN. A zeroForOne step searches for its target inside the current bitmap word (src/libraries/TickBitmap.sol:94-104, src/libraries/Pool.sol:348), and word 0 begins at compressed tick 0. A step that starts at a positive tick therefore never has a target below tick 0, where the price is 2^96, so sqrtN is at least 2^96 and the output is at least 2^160, which reverts in the toInt128 of src/libraries/Pool.sol:455 or :459. A step that starts at or below tick 0 has sqrtC of at most about 2^96, so the input is at least 2^160 and reverts the same way. The price limit can only move the target closer. The verifier of this cycle supplied this argument; the bound on liquidity alone does not exclude the fallback. The harness agrees: all 100,000 fallback calls and all 100,000 calls above 2^160 reverted with 0x93dafdf1 in both engines. Branch :105 (exact output above 2^160) needs more than 2^160 of output and was never reached, as cycle 12 found (jumpmap neverReached). A wrong result in these blocks could only change which error a reverting frame returns. Evidence: src/libraries/SqrtPriceMath.sol:31-52 ; src/libraries/SwapMath.sol:60-100 ; src/libraries/Pool.sol:453-460 ; cycles/015/theme-monad-emitter-blocks.work/mass/summary.txt

## Reading of the source (theme-untaken-branches-source)

- all 21 networks, cycle 15. Task 1, jump pairs 9042/9048 (unlockCallback CALL, PoolManager.sol:110) and 15088/15094 (balanceOf STATICCALL, Currency.sol:94). Sides: 9048 falls through to 9049 with the result left at its default 0 and skips the decoding of the returned bytes; 15094 falls through to 15095 and returns the default 0 balance without decoding. Condition for the untaken side: the success word is zero at 9048 (or 15094) while it was nonzero at 9042 (or 15088). Result: Unreachable on every network for any value a CALL or STATICCALL can push. The disassembly of the build reads CALL, SWAP1, DUP2, ISZERO, PUSH2 0x24c2, JUMPI at 9035-9042 and PUSH0, SWAP2, PUSH2 0x241a, JUMPI at 9043-9048, and STATICCALL, SWAP1, DUP2, ISZERO, PUSH2 0x24c2, JUMPI, PUSH0, SWAP2, PUSH2 0x3afa, JUMPI at 15081-15094. Both JUMPIs of a pair test the same stack word: the first leaves through 0x24c2 (9410: RETURNDATACOPY of all return data and REVERT) when the word is zero, the second runs only when it is nonzero and then jumps. No network can make one word both zero and nonzero, so a CALL that returns 2, or any other nonzero word, still takes the decode side. The decode side checks return data size (9263-9272 for unlockCallback, 15104-15108 for balanceOf, both require at least 32 bytes) and reverts otherwise. callsem.py, rerun this session on all 21 networks, returned 50 of 50 specified words, including the success flags of calls that revert, fail a static write or carry value. Evidence: research/network-risk/cycles/015/theme-untaken-branches-source.work/dis.py 9029-9060 and 15000-15110 on research/network-risk/build/PoolManager.json; research/network-risk/cycles/015/theme-untaken-branches-source.work/callsem-rerun.json
- all 21 networks, cycle 15. Task 1, pc 15021 (Currency.sol:91-92). Sides: taken goes to the balanceOf STATICCALL at 15026, fallthrough runs SELFBALANCE at 15023. Condition for the untaken side: the currency word masked to 160 bits is zero inside balanceOfSelf. Result: Unreachable on all 21 networks. balanceOfSelf has two callers, sync (PoolManager.sol:281-285) and _settle (PoolManager.sol:353-359), and each tests isAddressZero on the same currency value first and takes another branch for address(0). The condition is AND and JUMPI on a value from calldata or transient storage; it reads no environment opcode, so no chain property enters. SELFBALANCE stays dead code, and no network difference in SELFBALANCE (for example a native balance mirrored elsewhere, F-008 on Polygon or the USDC faces on Arc) can reach the settlement arithmetic through it. Evidence: src/types/Currency.sol:90-96
- all 21 networks, cycle 15. Task 1, pc 16370 (Hooks.sol:137). Sides: fallthrough computes bytes4(data) from a hook calldata shorter than 4 bytes; taken uses the first 4 bytes. Condition: mload(data) < 4. Result: Unreachable on all 21 networks. data is always an abi.encodeCall of an IHooks selector with at least one argument (Hooks.sol:180, 190, 202, 204, 225, 237, 256, 300, 323, 333), so its length is at least 36 bytes. The length is written by the compiler's encoder in memory and does not depend on any opcode result outside MLOAD and LT, which the opcode battery covers. Evidence: src/libraries/Hooks.sol:131-155
- all 21 networks, cycle 15. Task 1, ABI decoder bounds at pcs 1378, 2396, 3087, 5298, 10926 and 11947. Sides: revert to 816 when calldata is shorter than the head of a second static struct. Condition: CALLDATASIZE minus 4 is less than the head of the second struct while an earlier JUMPI of the same function (for example 1327 before 1378) passed with a larger bound. Result: Unreachable on all 21 networks. Both tests compare CALLDATASIZE, a single value per frame, against two constants, and the earlier test uses the larger one. A network cannot return two CALLDATASIZE values in one frame. pmdiff4 (malformed calldata on a third of 10,773 calls) matched the reference on all 21 networks in cycle 12. Evidence: research/network-risk/opcodes/jumpmap.json
- all 21 networks, cycle 15. Task 1, Panic 0x41 at pcs 5583, 11761, 11789, 11817 and 19089. Sides: Panic 0x41 when a memory struct allocation moves the free memory pointer above 2^64 - 1 or below its old value. Condition: the free memory pointer exceeds about 2^64 before the allocation. The one input from outside that moves the pointer before these allocations is hook return data, because callHook advances the pointer by returndatasize rounded up plus 32 (Hooks.sol:142-148). Result: Unreachable on all 21 networks. Reaching 2^64 needs return data of about 2^64 bytes, which no transaction gas cap allows: the largest simulated call gas any endpoint grants is about 150 million on Monad (OPCODES.md check 2), while 2^64 bytes of memory cost far more than 2^100 gas under the quadratic rule. Currency.transfer trusts mload(0) only when return data is longer than 31 bytes and fails on 1 to 31 bytes; Yul evaluates the call before the or() term, which the bytecode does. The extsload loops run once even for n = 0 and then return the 64 byte header. For n = 2^256 - 1 the shifted length wraps and the function returns 32 bytes, for n = 2^256 - 2 it returns 0 bytes, and 2^251 returns a header with length 2^251 and no elements; all are view calls that cannot move funds. The array forms with a length of 2^64 or 2^251 are refused by the ABI decoder. The wrapped error for a reverting hook grows by 32 bytes per word of data, 228 bytes for empty data. ## Reading of the source (theme-bracketed-credits)

- Base, BNB Smart Chain, cycle 16. Lead L-771: does the Base B20 stablecoin precompile or a BNB Smart Chain Jenner CAS20 token redirect a transfer by a pattern in the recipient address, or call another contract during a transfer, as Tempo T15 zone deposit addresses do?. Result: No on both. Base answers reth/v2.5.2 base/v1.5.6. In v1.5.6 the B20 V3 transfer resolves the recipient with B20CreditRecipientStrategy::ExcludingZeroAndSelf, which returns the address unchanged and only rejects zero and the token itself (credit_recipient.rs), checks the executor, sender and receiver policies through is_authorized, which reads registry membership from storage (guards.rs lines 80-94, policy logic v1.rs lines 366-389), and move_balance debits from and credits to the named address (v3.rs lines 55-118, 209-232). BNB Smart Chain answers Geth/v1.8.2. At tag v1.8.2 cas20 transfer calls move and returns a 32 byte true (cas20_token.go lines 175-189); move checks the two policies and writes exactly the source and recipient balance slots (lines 239-269); isAuthorized walks stored policy ids and members only (cas20_policy.go lines 169-199). Neither path calls a contract, so neither opens a bracketing window inside take. Evidence: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/base/base/v1.5.6/crates/common/precompiles/src/b20_stablecoin/logic/v3.rs; https://raw.githubusercontent.com/base/base/v1.5.6/crates/common/precompiles/src/common/ops/credit_recipient.rs; https://raw.githubusercontent.com/base/base/v1.5.6/crates/common/precompiles/src/policy/logic/v1.rs; https://raw.githubusercontent.com/bnb-chain/bsc/v1.8.2/core/vm/cas20_token.go; https://raw.githubusercontent.com/bnb-chain/bsc/v1.8.2/core/vm/cas20_policy.go; web3_clientVersion on https://mainnet.base.org/ and https://bsc-dataseed1.bnbchain.org

ERC-4337 handleOps as a carrier that runs several accounts' code in one transaction: can an ordinary account place operations before and after another user's payment to the PoolManager and book it. Result: EntryPoint v0.7 code (16,035 bytes) is at 0x0000000071727De22E5E9d8BAf0edAc6f37da032 on all 21 networks, and handleOps is public with only a reentrancy guard (EntryPoint.sol v0.7 lines 174-200), so any account can bundle a victim's signed operation between two of its own. A user operation runs as one call to the sender account, and a user who pays the PoolManager does sync, pay and settle inside one unlock in that call (src/PoolManager.sol:104-114, 279-288, 349-364); another operation cannot run inside it. An operation that sends tokens to the PoolManager outside an unlock gives them up as surplus whether or not anyone brackets it. Paymaster and beneficiary payments go to the paymaster and in native value, and native value is credited only as msg.value (src/PoolManager.sol:352-354). No new loss found. Hazard of a user design that splits sync and settle across two operations is noted in one line only. Result: A retryable executes as its own transaction from the aliased L1 sender, and the L2 gateway's finalizeInboundTransfer pays the recipient there. A manual ArbRetryableTx.redeem only schedules the retry as a separate transaction after the caller's transaction (cleared in an earlier cycle from tx_processor.go and block_processor.go), so its transient sync never covers the payment. ArbRetryableTx exists on all three chains (code at 0x6e). Elysium has no CCTP, LxLy or Teleporter code. Arbitrum One and Robinhood Chain carry CCTP v2 code, covered by the CCTP finding. - all 21 networks, cycle 16. Task 2: balance changes without a transfer call between two frames of one transaction (native credits, protocol mints, fee refunds, rebases) that an ordinary account could book with sync and settle. Result: Native value is credited only as msg.value of settle (src/PoolManager.sol:352-354) and the PoolManager has no receive or fallback (grep of src/ finds none), so coinbase rewards, forced ETH, deposit mints and system credits in native value give no one a credit. On networks where the native asset has an ERC-20 face (Celo CELO token, Arc 0x3600..., Polygon 0x1010, OP and Zora legacy ETH) the only inflows that can happen inside an attacker's transaction without a call are SELFDESTRUCT payments, which are the attacker's own money. Rebases of B20 Asset splits and CAS20 multipliers need issuer roles and run in the issuer's transaction (earlier cleared items); token specific oracle rebases are a token hazard and were not swept. ## Reading of the source (theme-megaeth-validator-build)

- MegaETH, cycle 16. L-768 and L-626, Task 1: can the public MegaETH stateless validator at e1618ed7 be built here without installing a toolchain?. Result: Task 1. The MegaETH stateless validator at e1618ed7 builds and runs with the installed stable toolchain (rustc 1.97.0, cargo 1.97.0) and no RUSTC_BOOTSTRAP. rust-toolchain.toml pins nightly-2026-04-23 with components only (rustfmt, clippy, rust-src, miri, rust-analyzer); no crate of the workspace, of mega-evm v1.7.3 or of salt carries a #![feature] attribute (grep over the fetched trees), and the workspace declares rust-version 1.94. The work copy drops rust-toolchain.toml so the installed compiler is used. Two steps failed and were resolved: (1) cargo build --offline against the cycle 15 cargohome stops at dependency resolution with 'no matching package named bincode' because that fetch was partial (483 crates); cargo fetch from crates.io inside the work directory completed it. (2) the build script of mega-system-contracts v1.7.3 (crates/system-contracts/build.rs:318-347) panics with 'forge command not found' when the crate's scripts/ directory exists, because in a repository build it re-derives the five system contract bytecodes with Foundry. The scripts/ directory of the work copy was renamed, which makes build.rs take its published crate path: it skips the forge re-derivation and still runs Phase 2, which checks the checked-in constants in src/generated against the versioned artifacts (build.rs:364-385). cargo build --release --offline -p stateless-validator then finished (build/build2.log, EXIT 0). The binary uses revm 40.0.3, revm-handler 20.0.3, revm-interpreter 37.0.3 and ruint 1.17.2 from the validator's own Cargo.lock. The forge attestation of system contract bytecode is the one check this build did not run. In --block-list mode the validator fetched each block's witness with mega_getBlockWitness and the block from https://mainnet.megaeth.com/rpc, verified the witness, re-executed every transaction with mega-evm v1.7.3 on the stock revm interpreter and compared state root, receipts root, logs bloom, withdrawals root and gas used with the header the sequencer published. Target set: every block holding a PoolManager ModifyLiquidity with negative liquidityDelta (210 events in 210 blocks), with zero liquidityDelta, i.e. fee collection (545 in 545), an ERC-6909 mint (40 in 40) or burn (81 in 81) from the full PoolManager log history of blocks 2,900,000 to 32,766,000 (cycles/013/theme-mined-branches.work/raw/logs-4326.json and cycles/015/theme-closed-producers-2.work/raw/pmtail-4326.jsonl), plus the 75 blocks of the take, settle and sync inside reverted frames listed in cycles/011/theme-closed-producers.work/raw/mega.json (75 of the 87 cycle 11 counted are in that file's sample). Result: 911 distinct blocks, 911 validated, 0 failed. Anchored check: 45 of these blocks (15 removal, 10 fee collection, 5 burn, 5 mint, 10 reverted-frame blocks, seed 16) were also run in chain-following mode with --start-block set to the parent block hash and --end-block to the block, which in addition checks the witness pre-state against the parent's state root (stateless-core executor.rs:837-841); 45 of 45 validated. Wider sweep: all other blocks that hold any PoolManager log or a cycle 11 sampled transaction, 42734 blocks; all 42734 were run, 42734 validated and 0 failed. Control: the same 911 blocks run with a build whose revm-interpreter MULMOD returns one more than the correct result whenever the 512 bit product exceeds 2^256 (patched copy under build/plant, [patch.crates-io] in build/sv-plant) give 611 validated and 300 failed, mostly with a receipts root mismatch; the failures cover 138 of 210 removal blocks, 67 of 545 fee collection blocks, 25 of 81 burn blocks and 75 of 75 reverted-frame blocks, so the comparison sees a wrong product in these blocks. So for every mined MegaETH liquidity removal, fee collection, ERC-6909 mint and burn and every sampled take inside a reverted frame, the closed sequencer's post-state equals an independent re-execution by the open interpreter, to the state root. Task 3 was not needed. Evidence: research/network-risk/cycles/016/theme-megaeth-validator-build.work/blocks.txt, cats.json, runall/results.jsonl, anch/summary.txt, runrest/results.jsonl, runplant/results.jsonl; mega_getBlockWitness and eth_getBlockByNumber on https://mainnet.megaeth.com/rpc
- MegaETH, cycle 16. Task 4: when a PoolManager call inside unlock meets a mega-evm compute gas, data size, key-value update or state growth limit, can an inner frame stop while outer frames continue with PoolManager state the source assumes rolled back?. Result: Task 4. mega-evm v1.7.3 meters four extra dimensions per transaction (Rex constants: compute gas 200,000,000, data 12.5 MiB, key-value updates 500,000, state growth 1,000; crates/mega-evm/src/constants.rs:192-211) and, from Rex4, gives each inner frame 98/100 of its parent's remaining budget (limit/frame_limit.rs:162-171). A transaction-level exceed is latched and reported as OutOfGas; once latched, every later metered opcode in every frame halts (record_compute_gas returns false on a latched exceed, limit/limit.rs:460-480, and the instruction wrapper sets a halt action, evm/instructions.rs:581-594), and every frame return is marked OutOfGas (limit.rs:846-856), so the top frame halts and revm reverts the whole transaction apart from nonce and fee. A frame-local exceed found during execution ends that frame with Revert and revert data MegaLimitExceeded(kind, limit); revm's process_next_action reverts the frame's journal checkpoint for any non-ok result (revm-handler 20.0.3 src/frame.rs:416-423), which undoes storage, transient storage and logs of that frame, and the parent continues. A frame-local exceed found only when the frame returns (before_frame_return_result, limit.rs:801-845) rewrites a successful result to Revert after revm has already committed the frame; the source says so at limit.rs:827-830. The late detection exists for CREATE frames (code size recorded in after_frame_run, limit/data_size.rs:324-335) and for a SELFDESTRUCT whose usage was recorded before its inner instruction halted (limit.rs:450-456); the PoolManager bytecode has neither opcode, so no PoolManager frame can be committed and reported failed. Every outward call of the PoolManager reverts the PoolManager frame when the callee reports failure: the native and ERC-20 transfer (src/types/Currency.sol:40-84), the hook call (src/libraries/Hooks.sol:131-139) and the balanceOf read of sync and settle (src/types/Currency.sol:90-96, src/PoolManager.sol:279-288 and 349-365). So a callee frame reported failed, whether rolled back or not, ends with the PoolManager frame reverted, and that revert undoes Lock (src/libraries/Lock.sol:13-19), NonzeroDeltaCount (src/libraries/NonzeroDeltaCount.sol:20-32) and CurrencyDelta (src/libraries/CurrencyDelta.sol:35-39) together with the payment. No rewrite goes from failure to success, so a payment frame can never be reported successful with its transfer undone. Read-only test on https://mainnet.megaeth.com/rpc with eth_call and code overrides (probe/limits.py, probe/loop.py; the test contracts touch no PoolManager state): a child that creates 990 new storage slots under a parent that gave it all its gas returns success 0 with MegaLimitExceeded(3, 980) and the parent completes; through DELEGATECALL the child's writes are read back as zero after the failed call and the parent's own later write is present, while 900 and 979 slots succeed and persist. A child in an endless loop returns MegaLimitExceeded(2, 58,776,709) and the parent completes. These match the reading: a frame-local exceed rolls back that frame and only that frame. Evidence: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/megaeth-labs/mega-evm/v1.7.3/crates/mega-evm/src/limit/limit.rs (fetched, identical to the work copy) and the v1.7.3 checkout in research/network-risk/cycles/016/theme-megaeth-validator-build.work/build/cargohome/git/checkouts/mega-evm-86ab85a902904159/59b8e39; src/types/Currency.sol:40-84; src/libraries/Hooks.sol:131-139; src/PoolManager.sol:104-114; eth_call on https://mainnet.megaeth.com/rpc via research/network-risk/cycles/016/theme-megaeth-validator-build.work/probe/limits.py
- MegaETH, cycle 16. The validator's lock pins ruint 1.17.2 and revm-interpreter 37.0.3, and earlier cycles read mega-evm v1.7.4 with ruint 1.19.0. Does the version split leave PoolManager arithmetic unchecked?. Result: The validator binary built here, with ruint 1.17.2, reproduces the sequencer's state root on every block run, including the 300 blocks in which a wrong 512 bit MULMOD is visible. A ruint difference between the two builds on any operation these blocks use would show as a mismatch, and none did. Operands that no mined block reaches are covered only by the battery of OPCODES.md. - Monad, cycle 16. Task 3. The emitter source between v0.16.5 and v0.16.7 (category/vm/compiler and category/vm/runtime, file by file), and which changes reach instructions of the deployed PoolManager. The PoolManager's blocks were located by an instrumented copy of the emitter that writes a marker for every emitter function entered and every branch arm taken while each EVM instruction is emitted (shapes/instrument.py; the markers are logger calls and the emitted asm text is identical to the uninstrumented build). Result: Only compiler/ir/x86.cpp, x86/emitter.cpp, emitter.hpp, types.hpp, virtual_stack.hpp and runtime/allocator.hpp and cached_allocator.hpp differ; no runtime .cpp or .S file changed, so the arithmetic routines (math.S, the DIV, MOD, SDIV, SMOD, ADDMOD, MULMOD and EXP calls) are the same. Changes that reach the PoolManager: (a) shift_literal_by_non_literal (emitter.cpp 5231-5235 and 5254-5328) handles SHL, SHR and SAR of a literal value by a variable count with two unaligned loads from a 96-byte read-only window and per-qword shifts; it is used at 6 PoolManager sites, SHL at pcs 16643 (inside the TickBitmap.flipTick code, src/libraries/TickBitmap.sol:47-75), 16691 (the mask shl(and(tick, 0xff), 1), src/libraries/TickBitmap.sol:72), 21183 (1 << bitPos, src/libraries/TickBitmap.sol:110) and 21364 (the De Bruijn table of BitMath.leastSignificantBit, src/libraries/BitMath.sol:40-42), SHR at 19356 (type(uint256).max >> (255 - bitPos), src/libraries/TickBitmap.sol:96) and 23648 (the table of BitMath.mostSignificantBit, src/libraries/BitMath.sol:21-22); under v0.16.5 the same sites move the literal into an AVX register and take shift_avx_reg_by_non_literal. The window arithmetic was checked by hand: for shift 8k+b with k up to 32 the loads stay inside bytes 31 to 95 of the window and the mask sits at bytes 0-15 (SHL) or 80-95 (SHR, SAR), and for every bit i the two loads contribute the same stream bit. (b) touch_memory skips the bound check and memory growth when the same non-literal offset element was already checked with at least the same size in the block (6301-6313); 15 PoolManager MLOAD and MSTORE sites use it, and 14 of them run in the cycle 15 scenarios (the one left, pc 16254, is next to the hook call revert path at src/libraries/Hooks.sol:152). Since the element is the same value and memory never shrinks inside a frame, the skipped check would have passed. (c) The block-exit stack write orders elements by stack index through a preallocated count array and loads GPR-held words into a YMM register word by word (mov_words_to_ymm, 2061); every block exit with register-held values uses it. (d) block_prologue jumps straight to the error label when max_delta - min_delta > 1024 (1342), where v0.16.5 tested min_delta < -1024 or max_delta > 1024; no stack size satisfies both runtime checks in exactly the cases the new test catches, so the outcome is the same. (e) Read-only data alignment 32 to 64 bytes (735) and add96. Changes that do not reach it: MSTORE8 of a value held at a stack offset (3399-3412; the PoolManager has no MSTORE8), the CLZ rewrite (2692-2733 and 8266-8293; no CLZ opcode), debug comments, the allocator refactor (stack memory allocation only). Both versions were run on every input of this unit with no difference between engines or between versions. - Monad, cycle 16. Task 4, shapes. For MULMOD, ADDMOD, SDIV, SMOD, SIGNEXTEND, SAR, BYTE, SHL, SHR, EXP, CALLDATALOAD, MSTORE8, MCOPY, TLOAD and TSTORE: every shape the v0.16.7 emitter can pick (read from the dispatch code), which shapes the deployed PoolManager's blocks use (from the instrumented asm log), and whether PoolManager scenarios execute each site (operand classes recorded at the same pc in the interpreter, which runs the same path as the native code because every result is equal). Result: Shapes the emitter can pick. SHL, SHR, SAR: fold of two literals; literal count of 256 or more (0, or the sign fill for SAR) or 0 (identity); literal count with the value in an AVX register (shift_avx_reg_by_literal) or in general registers or a stack slot (shift_general_reg_or_stack_offset_by_literal); variable count with a literal value of 0 (or all ones for SAR, identity), any other literal value (shift_literal_by_non_literal, new in v0.16.6/7), the value in an AVX register (shift_avx_reg_by_non_literal, count bounded to 256 in rax) or in general registers, or a stack slot moved to them (shift_general_reg_by_non_literal with test_high_bits192). BYTE: literal index of 32 or more gives 0; fold; literal or variable index with the source in general registers, an AVX register, or a stack slot (6 leaves). SIGNEXTEND: fold; literal index of 31 or more gives the value; literal index with the source in AVX or general registers or a stack slot; variable index bounded to 31 with the source in AVX, general registers, or a stack slot or literal (5 leaves). MULMOD and ADDMOD: literal modulus 0 or 1 gives 0; folds; a literal operand equal to the absorbing element; a power-of-two literal modulus becomes an AND mask (operand equal to 1 or 0) or mul_mod2 / add_mod2, which inline the product or sum truncated to n bits for n up to 128 and call runtime mul_192 or mul above; anything else calls the runtime. SDIV and SMOD: literal folds, divisor 0, power-of-two divisor (sdiv_by_sar with negation, smod_by_mask), otherwise the runtime call. EXP: literal folds and gas by exponent width, otherwise the runtime. CALLDATALOAD: literal offset bounded or out of range, variable offset bounded by bits with a runtime check. MSTORE8: value literal, in general registers, AVX, or a stack slot (general register or AVX temporary). MCOPY, TLOAD, TSTORE: runtime calls only. The PoolManager scenarios do run the 2^96 site (pc 22639) 113,230 times, always with a product above 2^256, yet f5 changes none of their results: on a correct node that branch returns an amount of at least 2^160, which either loses the comparison at src/libraries/SwapMath.sol:68 or :90 or reverts later in a cast, and a garbage remainder almost always gives a garbage amount that does the same. - all 21 networks, cycle 16. Task 2, halts other than REVERT, constructed with eth_call and state overrides against the deployed PoolManager of each of the 21 networks (HaltProbe.sol, halt.py, halt_fix.py in the work directory). A probe frame writes its own transient slot and then either (variant 1) enters unlock and, in the callback, mints 5 claims, syncs a currency and writes a second slot, or (variant 2) syncs a currency outside unlock, and then halts. Kinds: REVERT as control, INVALID (0xfe), stack overflow by unbounded internal recursion, out of gas by an endless loop, and, under STATICCALL, a TSTORE by the probe, PoolManager.sync and PoolManager.unlock. A later frame then reads the unlock flag, the nonzero delta count, the probe's delta, the synced currency and reserves with exttload (src/Exttload.sol:10-15), the probe's claim balance and the probe's own two slots. In a second test the call into the probe was given every gas value from 1 up to the first value at which it succeeds (step 1 over the last 8,000 gas below that value and step 9 or coarser below), so that out of gas falls at every reachable point inside the PoolManager, the callback and the balanceOf staticcall: 362,827 attempts, 362,743 of them failing. The first successful gas is 39,572 on most networks, 39,324 on Monad, 81,193 on MegaETH and 281,586 on Tempo, where creating a storage slot costs more. Result: No leak on any network: 0 failed attempts read back a write. The successful controls show every written slot (synced currency 0x00000000000000000000000000000000c0ffee16 and reserves 1000 plus the attempt id, the probe slots 7 and 9), so the reads can see a write that survives. A static call into PoolManager.sync or unlock fails at its first TSTORE (src/libraries/Lock.sol:13, src/libraries/CurrencyReserves.sol:29-30) and writes nothing, so a static violation cannot leave a write by construction. PoolManager never catches a failed callee: the hook call bubbles the failure (src/libraries/Hooks.sol:134-137), token and native payouts revert (src/types/Currency.sol:48-52 and 73-83), and the callback is a plain high level call (src/PoolManager.sol:110), so a halt in any of them reverts the whole unlock. On MegaETH the simulated call runs on the RPC node, not the closed sequencer (OPCODES.md, MegaETH row). Evidence: eth_call with state overrides on the rpc URL of each network in state/networks.json, 2026-11-25, results in cycles/016/theme-revert-rollback-mined.work/raw/halt_all.json and raw/halt_fix.json; https://eips.ethereum.org/EIPS/eip-1153 (a reverted frame undoes its transient writes and those of inner calls); src/libraries/Lock.sol:10-27; src/PoolManager.sol:104-114, 279-288
- all 21 networks, cycle 16. Task 2, call depth 1024: how deep a chain of self calls with all gas gets under a 30,000,000 gas eth_call, and what the PoolManager does when a call it makes fails for depth. Result: The chain stops at depth 358 on 18 networks, 357 on Tempo and 291 on MegaETH (98/100 forwarding), well short of 1,024, because each level keeps 1/64 of the gas: (63/64)^1024 is 9.9e-8, so reaching depth 1,024 needs about 10^10 gas at the top, and (98/100)^1024 is 1.0e-9 on MegaETH. Where depth were reached, the failed outgoing call returns 0 without halting the PoolManager frame, and every outgoing call of the PoolManager turns a failure into a revert (src/libraries/Hooks.sol:137, src/types/Currency.sol:52 and 83, src/PoolManager.sol:110), so the unlock reverts and its transient writes go with it. Evidence: eth_call depthRun() with state override on every rpc URL in state/networks.json, 2026-11-25 (raw/halt_all.json); src/libraries/Hooks.sol:131-137; src/types/Currency.sol:40-83
- Base, Tempo, Celo, Arc, cycle 16. Tokens the node implements natively, inside frames that revert or halt: the probe TokenRollbackProbe.sol was placed by state override at the PoolManager address of Base, Tempo, Celo and Arc so that it holds what the PoolManager holds, and it transferred 1 unit of Base B20 OUSD (0xB2000000000000000000002fEb517dFeC7415344) and AMDc (0xb2000000000000000000000d8ce462e99ee7a47b), Tempo TIP-20 pathUSD (0x20c0000000000000000000000000000000000000), the CELO ERC-20 face (0x471EcE3750Da237f93B8E339c536989b8978a438) and the Arc USDC face (0x3600000000000000000000000000000000000000) inside a frame that then reverted, hit INVALID, overflowed the stack or ran out of gas, and under STATICCALL; on Celo and Arc also a native value transfer read back through the face. A take or settle inside an undone frame is only safe if these precompile balances roll back with the transient delta. Result: All eight cases roll back: in every halted or static case the sender and recipient balances of both faces read afterwards equal those before, and the successful control moves one unit (raw/token_rollback.json). Ethereum USDC was run as a bytecode control with the same result. On Arc a native transfer of 1 wei lowers the sender's face balance by one face unit (10^12 wei) and the recipient's face shows 0, because the face reports floor(balance / 10^12); this is the rounding of the existing two-face hazard (F-100, F-108), and one face unit is worth 10^-6 USDC, far below the gas of a round. Evidence: eth_call with state overrides on https://base-rpc.publicnode.com, https://rpc.mainnet.tempo.xyz, https://forno.celo.org and https://rpc.mainnet.arc.io, 2026-11-25; src/PoolManager.sol:291-297, 349-364; src/types/Currency.sol:60-94

The call trees of all scan hits on OP Mainnet, Robinhood Chain, Base, BNB Smart Chain and Tempo were walked for failed frames below a PoolManager frame (ooghunt.py). Result: No out of gas below a PoolManager frame occurs in these transactions; every failure is a REVERT. 20 failures are under an unlock that itself reverted, as the source requires (src/PoolManager.sol:110). Two on Base sit below a successful swap: hook 0xd6155ce86ff3a33f52493e08cf77d7bbdf21fffc caught a reverting call of its own (selector 0xda1e42b9) and answered the PoolManager normally, so the PoolManager caught nothing; both transactions replay equal in the reference. The out of gas case was therefore tested by construction in the gas sweep above.
