- all 21 networks, cycle 16. Task 3, ERC-4337 bundles on every network, which join several users' operations into one transaction. Whether transient storage is cleared between operations, and a mined bundle in which two unrelated senders' operations both called the PoolManager. Bundles among PoolManager transactions (UserOperationEvent of EntryPoint 0.6, 0.7 and 0.8, aa.py): Base 5,610 PoolManager transactions in blocks 61,965,599 to 61,973,598, 170 bundles, 1 with two or more senders, 0 where two senders reached the PoolManager; Ethereum 6,000 PoolManager transactions in blocks 26,489,705 to 26,490,154, 65 bundles, 1 with two or more senders, 0 where two senders reached the PoolManager; Polygon 6,000 PoolManager transactions in blocks 97,904,651 to 97,919,750, 223 bundles, 2 with two or more senders, 0 where two senders reached the PoolManager; Arbitrum One 6,000 PoolManager transactions in blocks 527,245,513 to 527,333,512, 59 bundles, 0 with two or more senders, 0 where two senders reached the PoolManager; Optimism 6,000 PoolManager transactions in blocks 159,986,660 to 159,993,159, 0 bundles, 0 with two or more senders, 0 where two senders reached the PoolManager; Robinhood Chain 3,000 PoolManager transactions in blocks 122,805,462 to 122,811,461, 64 bundles, 0 with two or more senders, 0 where two senders reached the PoolManager; Unichain 3,000 PoolManager transactions in blocks 64,830,284 to 64,836,583, 0 bundles, 0 with two or more senders, 0 where two senders reached the PoolManager. Result: Transient storage is not cleared between operations: EIP-1153 discards it only at the end of the transaction, and the EntryPoint runs every operation as a nested call of the one handleOps transaction. The unlock flag and the deltas cannot pass from one operation to the next, because unlock clears the flag and requires every delta to be zero before it returns (src/PoolManager.sol:104-114). Only the synced currency and reserves can. No mined bundle with two senders' PoolManager calls was found: the only multi-sender bundles have one operation that reaches the PoolManager, for example Base 0x61046bec99fa8dc23efda3e63f0bedc7e18b233fb191c09ff26edfbaced2b66c (EntryPoint 0.6, senders 0x0de04d745d88dc18e7c519f1935a3e27917e795f and 0xcbeebaf9d1f94a6678dad25e14afd2fb042bc579, only the second calls unlock, sync, settle, swap, mint and take). sync needs no unlock and leaves the synced currency and reserves in transient storage until a settle by anyone resets it (src/PoolManager.sol:279-288, 349-364). A first party that leaves a sync gains nothing: settle credits msg.sender or the named recipient (src/PoolManager.sol:300-307, 364), so a credit from a stale sync goes to the second party. The second party can lose only through its own integration. If it pays native value without its own sync, settle reverts with NonzeroNativeValue (src/PoolManager.sol:356, recorded as F-071). If it pays an ERC-20 without syncing first, it is credited the balance change since the first party's sync: a take of its own after that sync makes the subtraction at src/PoolManager.sol:360 revert or under-credits it, and unlock then reverts with CurrencyNotSettled (src/PoolManager.sol:112). No path moves another user's pool balance or claims. Evidence: https://eips.ethereum.org/EIPS/eip-1153; eth_getLogs, eth_getTransactionReceipt and debug_traceTransaction on the endpoints in aa.py, 2026-11-25 (raw/aa2_*.json, raw/aa_*.json); src/PoolManager.sol:104-114, 279-288, 300-307, 349-364
- Tempo, cycle 16. Task 3, Tempo type 0x76 batched and sponsored transactions: does transient storage survive between the calls of a batch, and can two unrelated users share it?. Result: The calls of a batch share one transient map: execute_batch takes one checkpoint before the first call, runs every call with the transaction's caller as sender, rolls the checkpoint back when any call fails and keeps all writes otherwise (handler.rs execute_batch, lines 1284-1366 on main). Every call has the same msg.sender, so only the signer's own calls share the state, and a fee sponsor pays fees without becoming a caller. Two unrelated users cannot share a batch, so no mined transaction of that kind can exist; zone portal batches are the one Tempo context that joins parties and are recorded as F-135. sync needs no unlock and leaves the synced currency and reserves in transient storage until a settle by anyone resets it (src/PoolManager.sol:279-288, 349-364). A first party that leaves a sync gains nothing: settle credits msg.sender or the named recipient (src/PoolManager.sol:300-307, 364), so a credit from a stale sync goes to the second party. The second party can lose only through its own integration. If it pays native value without its own sync, settle reverts with NonzeroNativeValue (src/PoolManager.sol:356, recorded as F-071). If it pays an ERC-20 without syncing first, it is credited the balance change since the first party's sync: a take of its own after that sync makes the subtraction at src/PoolManager.sol:360 revert or under-credits it, and unlock then reverts with CurrencyNotSettled (src/PoolManager.sol:112). No path moves another user's pool balance or claims. Evidence: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/tempoxyz/tempo/main/crates/evm/src/handler.rs (execute_batch, lines 1267-1366), fetched 2026-11-25; src/PoolManager.sol:279-288, 349-364
- HyperEVM, cycle 16. Task 3, HyperEVM system transactions: are they joined with user transactions so that transient storage is shared?. Result: No. The public replay client builds the environment for each system transaction and each signed transaction separately, calls transact once per transaction and commits state after each (run.rs lines 99-168 and the loop over system_txs at line 217). Each system transaction is its own transaction and starts with empty transient storage, so nothing joins it with a user's PoolManager call. The validator itself is closed (F-120). Evidence: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/hyperliquid-dex/hyper-evm-sync/main/src/run.rs, fetched 2026-11-25; src/libraries/Lock.sol:10-27
- Optimism, Base, Unichain, Zora, Worldchain, Ink, Soneium, Celo, X Layer, cycle 16. Task 3, OP Stack deposit transactions: are deposits joined with other transactions?. Result: No. The deposit specification processes each deposit as a transaction of its own with its own receipt, sender and gas accounting, and the revm journal used by op-reth clears transient storage in commit_tx, discard_tx and finalize at the end of every transaction (inner.rs lines 141, 174 and 207) and restores it on checkpoint_revert (line 622). A deposit therefore shares no transient state with a user's PoolManager call. Evidence: https://specs.optimism.io/protocol/deposits.html; https://raw.githubusercontent.com/bluealloy/revm/main/crates/context/src/journal/inner.rs, both fetched 2026-11-25
- Arbitrum One, Robinhood Chain, Elysium, cycle 16. Task 3, Arbitrum retryable redeems, automatic and manual: does a redeem run inside the transaction that scheduled it?. Result: No. A redeem is returned by TxProcessor.ScheduledTxes as a new transaction (tx_processor.go lines 924-957) and the block processor applies it after the originating transaction as a transaction of its own, keeping the group's redeems and checkpoint (block_processor.go lines 91 and 126-159), and every transaction passes through StateDB.Prepare, which resets transient storage before code runs (state_transition.go lines 735-736). A redeem shares no transient state with the transaction that created or redeemed it. Evidence: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/OffchainLabs/nitro/master/arbos/block_processor.go; https://raw.githubusercontent.com/OffchainLabs/nitro/master/arbos/tx_processor.go; https://raw.githubusercontent.com/OffchainLabs/go-ethereum/master/core/state_transition.go, all fetched 2026-11-25
- all 21 networks, cycle 16. The reference interpreter tools/opdiff/pyevm.py, used by earlier cycles to judge PoolManager behaviour, was extended here for whole mined transactions and gave one wrong result first. Result: pyevm.py gives a DELEGATECALL frame CALLVALUE 0 instead of the value of the calling frame (tools/opdiff/pyevm.py:205 passes 0 as value). This unit's copy (pyevm_tx.py) carries the value through and also adds block context, logs, ecrecover, modexp, EIP-7702 designators and an approximate GAS. The PoolManager build contains no DELEGATECALL (OPCODES.md, bytecode census), and the delegate calls of pmdiff6.py run inside the unlock callback, which the PoolManager calls without value, so no earlier PoolManager comparison is affected. Evidence: tools/opdiff/pyevm.py:195-205; tools/opdiff/pmdiff6.py:5-6 and 62; research/network-risk/OPCODES.md:146

## Reading of the source (theme-library-paths)

- HyperEVM, cycle 17. L-808, RUSTSEC-2025-0137: which functions of ruint 1.15.0 (hyper-evm-sync, revm 19.2.0, revm-interpreter 15.2.0) and 1.16.0 (nanoreth f0cad31, hl-archive-node/revm fdf9b16, revm-interpreter 25.0.3) call reciprocal_mg10, and is the divisor normalised on the DIV, MOD, SDIV, SMOD, ADDMOD and MULMOD paths?. Result: Yes on every path. reciprocal_mg10 is exported as reciprocal and called by reciprocal_2_mg10 (reciprocal.rs line 111), div_nx1_normalized and div_nx1 (small.rs 1.16.0 lines 39 and 75, 1.15.0 lines 27 and 62); reciprocal_2 is called by div_nx2_normalized, div_nx2, div_nxm_normalized and div_nxm (small.rs 1.16.0 lines 112 and 144, knuth.rs lines 35 and 120). The only non-test callers of those are algorithms::div (1.15.0 mod.rs lines 49-99) and div_inlined (1.16.0 mod.rs lines 56-107), which trim zero limbs, send one limb divisors with a one limb numerator to native division and route the rest to div_nx1, div_nx2 or div_nxm. Each of these shifts the divisor by its leading zeros before the reciprocal (small.rs lines 69-75 and 138-144, knuth.rs lines 105-120) and calls the normalized variant only when the shift is zero. Uint::div_rem, wrapping_div, wrapping_rem, reduce_mod, add_mod and mul_mod reach only those two entry points (div.rs and modular.rs of both tags). revm-interpreter 15.2.0 and 25.0.3 call wrapping_div and wrapping_rem after a zero check, add_mod and mul_mod directly, and / and % on absolute values in i256_div and i256_mod (arithmetic.rs lines 26-63 and 31-83, i256.rs lines 80-130 and 92-143); the hl-archive-node fork's arithmetic.rs, i256.rs and bitwise.rs equal the crates.io 25.0.3 files. The precondition d >= 2^63 therefore always holds, and FullMath (src/libraries/FullMath.sol:24, 35, 48, 62-73, 112), SqrtPriceMath (src/libraries/SqrtPriceMath.sol:62, 252), UnsafeMath (src/libraries/UnsafeMath.sol:14, 26) and TickBitmap (src/libraries/TickBitmap.sol:24-26, 57-64) cannot hand it an unnormalised divisor. Evidence: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/rustsec/advisory-db/main/crates/ruint/RUSTSEC-2025-0137.md; https://static.crates.io/crates/ruint/ruint-1.15.0.crate and ruint-1.16.0.crate (sha256 11256b5f and 9ecb38f8, the second equal to the checksum in nanoreth f0cad31 Cargo.lock); https://static.crates.io/crates/revm-interpreter/revm-interpreter-25.0.3.crate; https://raw.githubusercontent.com/hl-archive-node/revm/fdf9b16bdd4388a680c97440c6e7f085647ece01/crates/interpreter/src/instructions/arithmetic.rs; https://raw.githubusercontent.com/hl-archive-node/nanoreth/f0cad31/Cargo.lock; https://raw.githubusercontent.com/hyperliquid-dex/hyper-evm-sync/main/Cargo.lock
- HyperEVM, cycle 17. Release-mode run of ruint 1.15.0 and 1.16.0 on the division and modular vectors, called the way revm-interpreter 15.2.0 and 25.0.3 call them, against Python integers. Result: No wrong word. A Rust harness (research/network-risk/cycles/017/theme-library-paths.work/harness/src/main.rs) links each ruint version by path from the crates.io archives and runs DIV and MOD through wrapping_div and wrapping_rem with the handlers' zero check, SDIV and SMOD through a transcription of i256_div and i256_mod, ADDMOD and MULMOD through add_mod and mul_mod, and two sequences from the source: the 512 bit product and remainder of FullMath.mulDiv (two mul_mod calls, one by 2^256-1) and UnsafeMath.divRoundingUp. 3,585,969 vectors: 106,769 from battery.py and targeted.py (every DIV, MOD, SDIV, SMOD, ADDMOD, MULMOD, MULDIV512 and DIVUP vector, including the 16,858 MULMOD and mulDiv vectors of the 1.21.0 equal-top-limb shape) and 3,479,200 new ones with divisors of every bit length 1 to 256 (every normalisation shift for one, two, three and four limb divisors), numerators of every limb count, 257 bit ADDMOD sums, 512 bit MULMOD products and FullMath shaped denominators. Both versions in release mode with debug assertions off, as the clients ship, gave 0 mismatches; the same builds with debug assertions on gave 0 mismatches and never tripped the d >= 2^63 assertion, which a direct call with d = 1 does trip (reciprocal.rs line 78 in 1.15.0, 79 in 1.16.0). A flipped output word is caught by the comparison. Evidence: research/network-risk/cycles/017/theme-library-paths.work/out/compare-target-1.15.0.json, compare-target-1.16.0.json, compare-targetd-1.15.0.json, compare-targetd-1.16.0.json, vectors-meta.json; research/network-risk/cycles/017/theme-library-paths.work/vectors.py, compare.py

## Reading of the source (theme-monad-exact-sites)

- Monad, cycle 17. Task 1, method and proof of execution. The harness of cycle 16 (category-labs/monad v0.16.7 with asmjit e8c8e2e4 and evmc f6b7c57e, v0.16.5 with evmc 34795f4e, the release keccak) was relinked with two recompiled objects only: a copy of category/vm/compiler/ir/x86.cpp that, at chosen EVM pcs, emits an execution counter before the instruction (rax saved to and restored from a fixed address, mov and lea only, so flags and the virtual stack are untouched) and optionally, after the instruction, a call that records the word the instruction left on top of the stack (the code of Emitter::runtime_print_top1); and interpreter/execute.cpp built with a copy of instruction_table.hpp whose MONAD_VM_NEXT and MONAD_VM_NEXT_PUSH record the stack top at the same pcs. emitter.cpp is not changed. Two ways of reaching the sites were used: PoolManager calls (pc 12232, 15519, 22378, 22639) and, for operands no call can supply and for pc 16642, an entry into the deployed runtime's own basic block: bytes 0..46 of the 24,009-byte runtime are replaced by a 45-byte prologue (copy calldata[0x120:] to memory 0, push eight calldata words, jump to calldata word 0; a JUMPDEST at pc 38 stores the top word and returns it), the other 23,962 bytes unchanged. Entries used: 0x5703 (the 2^128 copy of mulDiv, called from Position.update at pcs 5969 and 5981), 0x5810 (the 2^96 copy, called from getAmount1Delta at pcs 23088 and 23161), 0x3c94 (Hooks.beforeSwap after the hook call) and 0x40d7 (the bytes4 mask block). Result: Arm identity. In the v0.16.7 asm log (which prints a comment per EVM instruction) the text emitted for each of the five site instructions is identical between the plain build, the counter build (once the five counter lines are removed; the rest of the 48,691-line log is identical) and the single-site capture builds (the plain text is a prefix of the capture build's text). The texts are: pc 22378 MULMOD loads a from [rbp-128..-104] into r13,r14,r15,r12 and b0,b1 from [rbp-96],[rbp-88], computes r10 = lo(a0*b0) by mulx, r11 = hi(a0*b0) + a1*b0 + a0*b1 (64-bit imul) and zeroes r8, r9; pc 22639 is the same with 32-bit imul and add on limb 1 (mod 2^96); pc 15519 SAR(128) of the word in r12..r15 is mov rax,r15; sar rax,63; mov r10,r14; mov r11,r15; mov r8,rax; mov r9,rax; pc 16642 SHL(3) of the word in r12..r15 is three shld and one shl by 3; pc 12232 CALLDATALOAD is the bswap_to_ymm arm with the bound test on the offset limbs and the 32-byte vmovups read. In v0.16.5 the same instructions open each site's text (v0.16.5 prints no per-instruction comment, so the text was located by the counter lines). Compiled from the prologue runtime, the enclosing blocks B5703, B5810, B3c94 and B40d7 equal the deployed runtime's blocks once label numbers, block numbers and read-only data offsets are replaced by the bytes they point to (both compiled in one process so that host pointers agree); the one exception, B3c94 under v0.16.5, differs only in the order of three independent stores at the block exit (see the v0.16.5 heap-address item). Marker counts, native = interpreter in every file and on both releases: pc 22378 274 (prologue) + 18 (ordinary calls); pc 22639 200 (prologue) + 57 (ordinary swaps) + 188 (hook swaps); pc 15519 116 (prologue) + 648 (ordinary swaps through a returns-delta hook); pc 16642 47 (prologue only); pc 12232 1,220 (ordinary extsload and exttload calls). Every file gives 0 mismatches between interpreter and native in status, gas, return data, storage, transient storage, balances, logs and the captured site words. Evidence: research/network-risk/cycles/017/theme-monad-exact-sites.work/asm/sitecheck.json ; research/network-risk/cycles/017/theme-monad-exact-sites.work/asm/blockcheck.json ; research/network-risk/cycles/017/theme-monad-exact-sites.work/out/summary.json ; research/network-risk/cycles/017/theme-monad-exact-sites.work/src/patch.py
- Monad, cycle 17. Task 2, the 2^128 site (pc 22378, src/libraries/FullMath.sol:47-49 inside the copy at 0x5703). Operands driven through the PoolManager's own block: prod1 = 1 with prod0 = 0, 1, 2^96, 2^96 + 1, 2^128 - 1, 2^128, 2^128 + 1 and random (each product split as a times a divisor b, in both operand orders; 2^256 + 1 is split by its known factor 1238926361552897), 60 products of the shape a pool produces (b between 2^96 and 2^127, a = ceil(2^256 / b) plus 0 to 2^30), the largest prod1 the require allows (2^128 - 1 and 2^128 - 2) and one above, and 256 combinations of edge low words (0, 1, 2^63, 2^64 - 1, 2^64, 2^64 + 1, 2^96 - 1, 2^96, 2^96 + 1, 2^127, 2^128 - 1 and random) for both operands with high words set. 356 calls; 274 reach the MULMOD (the others have prod1 = 0 and leave at the prod1 == 0 branch, or fail the require). SqrtPriceMath.sol:97 and :105 pass Q96 as the multiplier with liquidity as the denominator (copy at 0x588a and mulDivRoundingUp, MULMOD by a runtime call), and SwapMath.sol:65, :74 and :104 use the denominator 1e6 (copy with MULMOD at pc 22513, runtime call); these are not mul_mod2 sites. Arithmetic. For a power-of-two denominator N = 2^k the correct remainder is prod0 mod N, which is never above prod0, so gt(remainder, prod0) at FullMath.sol:52 is 0 on a correct node and prod1 stays 1. The emitted arm can only produce a value below N (limbs 2 and 3 are zeroed, limb 1 is 32-bit for 2^96). With any remainder r below N, FullMath.sol:52-75 return at least 2^(256-k) - 1: 200,000 random cases per site of a Python transcription give a least value of exactly 2^160 - 1 for k = 96 and 2^128 - 1 for k = 128 (the borrow case r > prod0 with prod0 < N). Such a result cannot be accepted: Position.update returns it as feesOwed and Pool.modifyLiquidity casts it with toInt128 (src/libraries/Pool.sol:192, src/libraries/SafeCast.sol:56-58), which reverts at 2^127 and above; getAmount1Delta returns at least 2^160 - 1, and every use reverts in a cast (Pool.sol:222-223 and :232-234 through SqrtPriceMath.sol:278-287 in modifyLiquidity; in a swap, SwapMath.sol:68-69 and :89-91 either cap the step at the target, after which the amount of at least 2^160 - 1 reaches the toInt128 casts at Pool.sol:455 or :459, or the comparison fails and the faulty value is replaced by amountRemaining). A quotient below 2^127 needs a remainder above 2^256 - 2^223 + prod0 at the 2^96 site and above 2^255 + prod0 at the 2^128 site, more than 2^222 above anything the arm can write. So the borrow of L-800 cannot be produced by this arm, and a remainder that stays below N changes an accepted amount on no path. - Monad, cycle 17. Task 4. A fault planted in the native code after each site's instruction, one at a time (HX_FAULT_PC): bit 127 of the remainder cleared at pc 22378, bit 95 at pc 22639, no sign fill in the top word at pc 15519, carries between words lost at pc 16642, the last byte of the word lost at pc 12232. Every input file was run against every fault on both releases, comparing whole runs (counter build) and the site word (capture build). Result: Site-level tests catch every fault: pc 22378 q128 112 and ordinary 5 scenarios differ; pc 22639 q96 80 and ordinary 21; pc 15519 prologue 44 and hook 324; pc 16642 35; pc 12232 756. Whole-run comparisons catch only the pc 12232 fault (588 of 1,348). The other four change no PoolManager result, for reasons the source fixes: a remainder smaller than the true one leaves (prod0 - r) >> k unchanged, so the quotient at FullMath.sol:66-75 is the same; the SAR result at pc 15519 is consumed only by SIGNEXTEND 15 at pc 15522, which ignores bits 128 to 255; pc 16642 is unreachable. This is why cycle 16 saw no effect of its fault at pc 22639, and it means that whole-output differential testing cannot see faults of these kinds at these sites. They are also faults that move no funds. Evidence: research/network-risk/cycles/017/theme-monad-exact-sites.work/fault/summary.txt ; src/libraries/FullMath.sol:52-75
- Monad, cycle 17. Whether Monad's native code for the PoolManager is a function of the bytecode alone, on both releases. Result: Not under v0.16.5. Its block-exit writer collects stack elements in std::unordered_map<StackElem *, int32_t> dep_counts and emits the writes in that map's iteration order (category/vm/compiler/ir/x86/emitter.cpp:1433 and :1466 at v0.16.5), which follows heap addresses. One extra early allocation in the compiling process changes 322 to 414 lines of the 48,757-line asm log of the deployed PoolManager. v0.16.7 replaced the map with a vector in stack index order, with the comment that this keeps the emitted code independent of heap addresses (emitter.cpp:1456-1469 and :1502), and its log is identical across the same perturbations. The orders seen are reorderings of independent stores. Four heap layouts of v0.16.5 give 2,000 of 2,000 cycle 15 scenarios equal between engines with identical native digests, and all v0.16.5 runs of this unit used a third and fourth layout. Different v0.16.5 validators can therefore run different machine code for the same contract, but no case where the order changes a result was found. Evidence: https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/gh/category-labs/monad@v0.16.5/category/vm/compiler/ir/x86/emitter.cpp ; https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/gh/category-labs/monad@v0.16.7/category/vm/compiler/ir/x86/emitter.cpp ; research/network-risk/cycles/017/theme-monad-exact-sites.work/layout/

## Reading of the source (theme-real-address-runs)

- all 21 networks, cycle 17. Task 1 method. A driver (scripts/realrun.py in the work directory) regenerates script sets 1, 2 and 6 of tools/opdiff (pmdiff.py seed 7_2026_11_24, 250 scripts; pmdiff2.py seed 11_2026_11_24, 300 scripts; pmdiff6.py, 706 scripts) with every reference to the PoolManager pointed at the network's real PoolManager address from state/networks.json, and runs each as one eth_call at 25 million gas against 'latest'. The state override contains only the driver (unlock callback, which also pays native value from its own overridden balance in set 6), the token doubles at 0xc0ffee01, 0xc0ffee02 and 0xc0ffee05 and the hook doubles at 0x486b.... and 0x486c....; the PoolManager's code, storage and balance are left as on chain. Pools are created by the scripts with those currencies and hooks, so no existing pool is touched. For each network the code at the real address was fetched in the same run (24,009 bytes, 24,050 on Unichain). Records were compared call by call with Ethereum's record at Ethereum's real address after replacing the 20 bytes of each PoolManager address with a marker (scripts/compare.py, scripts/alldiffs.py), and with the fresh-address results stored in opcodes/pmdiff.json, pmdiff2.json and pmdiff6.json. Every script whose answer differed from the stored fresh answer was run again at the real address with 2,000,000,000, 150,000,000, 50,000,000 or 30,000,000 gas, the first the endpoint accepts (scripts/gasretry.py). Ethereum's fresh-address answers for sets 2 and 6 were rerun the same day for a call-by-call comparison. Result: At Ethereum's real address 0x000000000004444c5dc75cB358380D2e3dE08A90 the 250 set 1 records and the 300 set 2 records are byte-identical to the stored fresh-address reference hashes, and the 706 set 6 records equal this cycle's Ethereum fresh-address rerun except where a script reads the PoolManager's own storage (owner, controller, accrued fees, extsload ranges) and in script 260, where the revert data of a native take to the PoolManager itself names the PoolManager's address; scripts 275 to 277 are byte-identical between the two addresses. So placing the scripts at the real address, with real code and storage, changes no amount, delta, slot or revert reason that does not come from the stored state itself. Every client named in OPCODES.md as keeping a code or jump cache keys it by content, and the real address runs are consistent with that. - Base, cycle 17. Base, ERC-6909 claims held by address(0). balanceOf(address(0), 0) on the real PoolManager returns 45,056,898,864 (about 4.5e-8 ETH of native claims). Result: This is existing state, not an interpreter effect: the value is the same at blocks 61,054,597 to 62,054,600 on two endpoints. mint accepts any recipient (PoolManager.sol:322-329, ERC6909.sol:79-83), so somebody minted claims to address(0) and paid for them; those claims can never be burned or moved, because burn and transferFrom need msg.sender to be address(0) or approved by it (ERC6909Claims.sol:13-22, ERC6909.sol:35-48). The native backing stays in the PoolManager as surplus. No other user loses anything. Evidence: eth_call balanceOf(address,uint256)(0,0) on https://mainnet.base.org/ and https://base-rpc.publicnode.com at seven block heights; src/ERC6909Claims.sol:13-22
- Monad, cycle 17. Monad reports a RETURNDATACOPY past the end of return data as 'out of gas' (JSON-RPC code -32603), where the specification and the other clients name it an out-of-bounds halt. Result: Both are exceptional halts that consume the frame's gas and return failure to the caller, and the vector's outcome equals the specification. The PoolManager never copies return data beyond RETURNDATASIZE (Hooks.callHook and CustomRevert.bubbleUpAndRevertWith use returndatasize as the length), so the label cannot change a result of the bytecode. Only an off-chain tool that parses the error text would see it. Evidence: research/network-risk/cycles/017/theme-real-address-runs.work/raw/offsets-143.json (failMessages)

## Reading of the source (theme-reference-interpreter-audit)

- all 21 networks, cycle 17. Reference interpreter fault 1, stack limit: tools/opdiff/pyevm.py:102-110 handles PUSH1 to PUSH32, DUP1 to DUP16 and PUSH0 with `continue`, which skips the only overflow check at pyevm.py:218, so a frame can hold 1025 or more items and still succeed. The same lines are in cycles/013/theme-mined-branches.work/pyevm2.py:143-151 (check at :281) and cycles/016/theme-revert-rollback-mined.work/pyevm_tx.py:131-139 (check at :266). The specification halts when a push meets a full stack of 1024 (cancun/vm/stack.py:55). Result: Confirmed as a reference fault: of seven frames that reach 1025 items, the chain halts all seven and all three copies let four of them succeed (1025 PUSH0, 1024 PUSH0 then DUP1, 1025 PUSH1 then POP, 1024 PUSH0 then DUP1 then ADD). All 21 networks halt them, so no network differs. No PoolManager comparison can rest on the fault: the built PoolManager reaches at most 49 stack items over 60 buildcheck cases (111 liquidity changes, 242 swaps), far from 1024, and a reference that wrongly succeeds can only add a mismatch, never hide one. Fixed in this unit's copy pyevm_tx17.py. ## Reading of the source (theme-monad-exit-writer)

- Monad, cycle 18. L-840 question 1. Does the spill step before the dependency loop of Emitter::write_to_final_stack_offsets in monad v0.16.5 remove every dependency cycle?. Result: No, and it does not need to. The spill step (emitter.cpp:1401-1418) only frees one AVX register as scratch (init_yx1): when no register is free it moves the value of the first unreserved AVX holder (virtual_stack.cpp:530-541) to memory, or drops the register when the element already has a stack offset, general register or literal (virtual_stack.cpp:553-565). It runs before the dependency count is built at 1433-1461, so a spilled element is counted as a memory element. Cycles are left for the second loop (1564-1621). The dependency relation is a function: an element has at most one stack offset, so it blocks at most one other element (the owner of that offset). Every element that is not on a cycle is reached from a leaf and is written in the first loop (1478-1542), so after it exactly the cycle members have a count, and that count is 1. The second loop rotates each cycle through two AVX registers. yx1 is init_yx1 and yx2 is a free register or, when none is free, the register of the last AVX element written in the first loop (1550-1561). When no register is free, 15 of the 16 registers belong to elements other than init1; at most one of them (the popped jump target) is off the stack, so at least 14 AVX stack elements are written in the first loop and yx1 != yx2 holds in every order. Each cycle member's slot is read before it is overwritten, because the slots of a cycle are final indices of its own members only and stack indices of distinct elements are disjoint. The iteration order of the map decides which cycle is rotated first and which register serves as yx2; neither changes a stored word. Evidence: research/network-risk/cycles/016/theme-monad-harness-exact.work/dl/monad-0.16.5/category/vm/compiler/ir/x86/emitter.cpp:1401-1418 ; research/network-risk/cycles/016/theme-monad-harness-exact.work/dl/monad-0.16.5/category/vm/compiler/ir/x86/emitter.cpp:1433-1461 ; research/network-risk/cycles/016/theme-monad-harness-exact.work/dl/monad-0.16.5/category/vm/compiler/ir/x86/emitter.cpp:1550-1621 ; research/network-risk/cycles/016/theme-monad-harness-exact.work/dl/monad-0.16.5/category/vm/compiler/ir/x86/virtual_stack.cpp:530-565 ; https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/gh/category-labs/monad@v0.16.5/category/vm/compiler/ir/x86/emitter.cpp
- Monad, cycle 18. L-840 question 2. Is a dependency skipped at the AVX register check (emitter.cpp:1457-1459) ever read later from a register that an earlier write in the loop reassigned?. Result: No. Every register write the writer emits goes to yx1 or yx2: the loads at 1496, 1499 and 1511 in the first loop and 1588-1598 in the cycle loop. In the first loop yx1 is init_yx1 until the first AVX element is popped, and from then on it is the register of the AVX element popped most recently (1484-1487). An AVX element x whose memory slot is a final index of another element e is not counted as a blocker of e, so e may be written over x's slot first. x is then read from its own register when it is popped. That register can be overwritten only after it became yx1, which happens when x itself is popped, and x is fully written by then. init_yx1 is a register no stack element holds. AVX elements are never on a cycle, because they have no outgoing edge, so all of them are written in the first loop, before any cycle-loop write to yx1 or yx2. The writer writes no general register: mov_general_reg_to_mem (1833-1840) only reads them, and mov_literal_to_ymm (1961-1988) writes only the target ymm and does not change flags. The pc of a popped jump target is taken into its operand before the writer runs (3544-3576). Evidence: research/network-risk/cycles/016/theme-monad-harness-exact.work/dl/monad-0.16.5/category/vm/compiler/ir/x86/emitter.cpp:1457-1459 ; research/network-risk/cycles/016/theme-monad-harness-exact.work/dl/monad-0.16.5/category/vm/compiler/ir/x86/emitter.cpp:1478-1542 ; research/network-risk/cycles/016/theme-monad-harness-exact.work/dl/monad-0.16.5/category/vm/compiler/ir/x86/emitter.cpp:1833-1840 ; research/network-risk/cycles/016/theme-monad-harness-exact.work/dl/monad-0.16.5/category/vm/compiler/ir/x86/emitter.cpp:1961-1988 ; research/network-risk/cycles/016/theme-monad-harness-exact.work/dl/monad-0.16.5/category/vm/compiler/ir/x86/emitter.cpp:3544-3576
- Monad, cycle 18. L-840 question 3. Can an element whose stack offset lies below min_delta be left with a nonzero dependency count?. Result: No element has such an offset. Stack offsets come from three places only: the entry elements of each index from -1 down to the new min_delta (virtual_stack.cpp:298-302 and 326-330), the positive offsets 0..max_delta-1 (305-308, 334-337) and offsets that a destroyed or moved element returned (free_stack_offset, 202-208), all of which were handed out from the first two. min_delta never rises inside a block (continue_block takes the minimum, 321). Stack::get also asserts its index is at most top_index and at() asserts it is inside negative_elems_ (365-383). An offset above top_index is skipped at 1450 and creates no count. - Monad, cycle 18. Whether the read-only data that the writer's literal loads use depends on the order. Result: The order changes where a literal lands in the read-only table, not its value. RoData keys each entry by its bytes and returns the offset of the existing entry on a repeat (emitter.cpp:339-436). - Monad, cycle 18. L-812 and L-849. Which Monad release mainnet validators run, from headers, RPC client strings and release records. Result: The release page lists v0.16.5 as released to mainnet on 2026-10-22 and v0.16.7 as released to testnet on 2026-11-19 with mainnet N/A; the monad-bft v0.16.7 release tells operators not to upgrade without an announcement, and the v0.16.7 upgrade page says it applies to testnet only. The latest mainnet header has extraData of 32 zero bytes and no version field, and admin_nodeInfo is disabled on rpc3.monad.xyz. web3_clientVersion on 2026-11-25 (out/rpc/clientversion.txt): Monad/0.16.7 on rpc.monad.xyz, rpc1.monad.xyz, rpc-mainnet.monadinfra.com and the Tatum gateway; Monad/unknown on rpc3.monad.xyz, rpc4.monad.xyz and Ankr; proxy strings on rpc2.monad.xyz (eRPC), Originstake (eRPC), dRPC and thirdweb. So validators are on v0.16.5 by the published schedule while some mainnet full nodes run v0.16.7. No vote, proposal or validator-set field naming a version was found. This unit shows that the two releases store the same words at every block exit, so the mix gives no split. Evidence: https://docs.monad.xyz/developer-essentials/changelog/releases ; https://github.com/category-labs/monad-bft/releases/tag/v0.16.7 ; https://docs.monad.xyz/node-ops/upgrade-instructions/v0.16.7 ; eth_getBlockByNumber latest and web3_clientVersion on the endpoints named, 2026-11-25

## Reading of the source (theme-sync-leak-census)

- MegaETH, cycle 18. L-842, task 1: every MegaETH PoolManager transaction that ends successfully with an ERC-20 still synced, and every later transaction of the same block that calls settle, settleFor or take. Result: None found. debug_traceTransaction with callTracer (https://mainnet.megaeth.com/rpc, mega-reth/v2.3.1-4499c42 at start and end) was run on 72,184 transactions: the 51,233 of the cycle 15 list (PoolManager logs or an ERC-20 Transfer to the PoolManager, blocks 7,009,653 to 32,770,383), 93 found by eth_getLogs for PoolManager logs and Transfers from or to the PoolManager from 32,770,384 to 32,814,962, and 20,858 more that appear only in Blockscout's internal transaction list (frames without a log, mostly failed). Every trace returned. The PoolManager frames were put in execution order with the reverted flag of the frame or an ancestor, and the source's transient model was replayed: sync(X) sets the synced currency and the reserves from the PoolManager's own balanceOf child call (src/libraries/CurrencyReserves.sol:27-32, src/PoolManager.sol:279-288), sync(0) and settle reset it (src/PoolManager.sol:283, 362), the state is empty at the start of each transaction. 36,875 completed ERC-20 syncs and 12,598 native ones; 54,803 completed settle calls each returned exactly what the model predicts (msg.value with nothing synced, balance rise since the sync otherwise, src/PoolManager.sol:349-364): zero mismatches. No successful transaction ends with an ERC-20 synced, so there is no later same-block settle to examine; 8,312 of 46,201 blocks hold several of these transactions. A settle credited from another transaction's sync would also show as a mismatch here, independently of finding the first transaction. Planted check (seed 18018, 200 sampled traces): dropping the first ERC-20 sync was detected 200 of 200 times, dropping the last settle left an ERC-20 synced or a mismatch 197 of 200 times (the other 3 end with a native settle). Not covered: a transaction that calls only sync and emits no log, makes no token transfer and is outside the Blockscout ranges read; it changes nothing unless a later settle is credited, and every later settle in the set was checked. Evidence: research/network-risk/cycles/018/theme-sync-leak-census.work/census.py, analyse.py, plant.py, raw/census-4326*.jsonl, raw/analysis.json, raw/plant-4326.json
- Monad, cycle 18. L-842, task 1 on Monad: PoolManager transactions that end with an ERC-20 synced, and settles of later transactions of the same block. Result: None found in a contiguous sample. Monad has about 650 PoolManager transactions per 1,000 blocks and eth_getLogs is limited to 100 blocks, so a full census was not possible from public endpoints. All 30,092 transactions with a PoolManager log or an ERC-20 Transfer from or to the PoolManager in blocks 125,250,001 to 125,295,000 (eth_getLogs in 450 windows of 100 blocks, https://rpc.monad.xyz and https://rpc-mainnet.monadinfra.com, Monad/0.16.7 at start and end) were traced with callTracer. 33,893 completed ERC-20 syncs, 24,580 syncs inside reverted frames, 42,244 completed settles, all equal to the model's value; no transaction ends with an ERC-20 synced; 6,771 of 16,675 blocks hold several. The client source explains why: every transaction, and every re-execution after a failed optimistic merge, runs on a fresh State built over the block state (execute_transaction.cpp lines 458 to 497), transient storage lives in AccountState::transient_storage_ (account_state.hpp line 70), and BlockState::merge copies only the account and storage_ of each address (block_state.cpp lines 194 to 250), so transient storage never reaches the next transaction. Evidence: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/category-labs/monad/v0.16.7/category/execution/ethereum/execute_transaction.cpp ; https://raw.githubusercontent.com/category-labs/monad/v0.16.7/category/execution/ethereum/state2/block_state.cpp ; https://raw.githubusercontent.com/category-labs/monad/v0.16.7/category/execution/ethereum/state3/account_state.hpp ; research/network-risk/cycles/018/theme-sync-leak-census.work/raw/census-143.jsonl, raw/logs-143.json
- MegaETH, cycle 18. MegaETH client source: where transient storage is cleared between transactions. Result: mega-evm (main, version 1.7.4; crates.io 1.7.2) pins revm 40.0.3, which uses revm-context 18.0.3. TLOAD and TSTORE are the stock host handlers wrapped for compute gas (mega-evm src/evm/instructions.rs lines 611-612 and 2205-2206) and the host delegates tstore and tload to the stock journal (src/evm/host.rs lines 90-91). That journal clears transient_storage in commit_tx, discard_tx and finalize (revm-context 18.0.3 src/journal/inner.rs lines 154, 188, 246). The sandbox that mega-evm uses for keyless deploys merges accounts and storage only, and its own path calls commit_tx (src/evm/execution.rs line 1023). EIP-1153 requires all transient values to be discarded at the end of the transaction. The producer itself is closed; the mined census above is the evidence that it behaves this way. Evidence: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/megaeth-labs/mega-evm/main/Cargo.toml ; https://static.crates.io/crates/mega-evm/mega-evm-1.7.2.crate ; https://static.crates.io/crates/revm-context/revm-context-18.0.3.crate ; https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ethereum/EIPs/master/EIPS/eip-1153.md

- HyperEVM, cycle 19. Silent log gap check (L-881) on the endpoints behind earlier censuses of chain 999: windows of 2,000 blocks from deployment block 45998366 to head plus windows on blocks earlier reads used, eth_getLogs of PoolManager Swap and ModifyLiquidity logs compared with the PoolManager logs in every endpoint's own receipts on 20 sampled blocks per window (seed '<chainId>-<window>'), receipts checked against the block's transaction count. Result: No endpoint returned fewer logs than the receipts hold. https://rpc.purroofgroup.com: 13 of 13 windows answered, 4 logs, 134 sampled blocks (4 with logs), getLogs 4 against receipts 4, 0 blocks short, 0 blocks whose receipts did not cover every transaction; https://rpc.hyperliquid.xyz/evm: 5 of 13 windows answered, 0 logs, 50 sampled blocks (0 with logs), getLogs 0 against receipts 0, 0 blocks short, 0 blocks whose receipts did not cover every transaction. The official endpoint never answered with an empty list where the archive node had logs: it refused 8 of 13 windows loudly ('rate limited' or 'execution aborted (timeout = 5s)'). Its blocks list fewer transactions than the reth archive nodes because it leaves HyperCore system transactions out of eth_getBlockByNumber, and its own receipts cover every transaction it lists. Because PoolManager logs are sparse on HyperEVM, the windows hold only 4 logs, so the decisive test is the known-block check: 40 of 40 blocks of transactions sampled from the 2,782 transaction census list (seed '999-known') give the same PoolManager log count by getLogs and by receipts on purroofgroup, hyperlend and the official endpoint. Each swap was run twice from parent-block state on https://rpc.purroofgroup.com (web3_clientVersion reth/v0.1.0-f0cad31 at 16:35:50 UTC, every 5,000 groups and at the end of each shard, last at 17:45:01 UTC on 2026-11-25). The lenient run repeats the cycle 18 rule and finds the 36,665 swaps with 104,643 calls on the 512 bit branch of mulDiv again, the same counts as cycle 18. The strict run reads the fee and never searches it: fee() at block-1, moved by FeeAdjustment(uint24,uint24) logs (topic 0x0cba8718, 117 groups) earlier in the block. It uses only the open price limit (MIN+1 or MAX-1), exact input with the logged paid amount or exact output with the logged received amount. The logged price may serve as the limit only when its bytes, without leading zeros, stand at a byte boundary in the transaction input. A pass 2 over the groups that failed pass 1 adds two values read from debug_traceTransaction (callTracer) of the swap's own transaction: the one word answer of the first STATICCALL that the pool's swap call makes to an address other than its two tokens (the fee the pool's code asked for), and the zeroForOne, amountSpecified and sqrtPriceLimitX96 arguments of the pool's own swap call. For every strict match that touched the branch, the same rerun was repeated with every 512 bit result of mulDiv and mulDivRoundingUp replaced by result + 1. The swap counts as needing the branch when that rerun fails. Result: All 36,665 swaps that cycle 18 counted on the 512 bit branch match price, tick, liquidity, amount0 and amount1 to the unit under the strict rule (out/strict-final-summary.json). All 36,665 take the branch in their strict rerun (104,643 calls), and 31,044 fail when the branch result is made one unit wrong, so 31,044 swaps need src/libraries/FullMath.sol:14-116 on 512 bit products to come out right. The plan names the second factory 0x5f95e92c338e6453111fc55ee66d4aa1df4e8e59, but eth_getCode returns no code at that address. The address with code, 10,699 bytes, is the one cycle 15 recorded. The Routescan API answers 'chain not supported' and hyperscan.com redirects to another site, so the pools were identified from their bytecode instead. Their dispatcher selectors and PUSH32 event topics were compared with the interfaces of cryptoalgebra/Algebra at tags integral-v1.0, integral-v1.1 and integral-v1.2.2. Pools of 0xf77bd082 carry communityFeeLastTimestamp() and Fee(uint16) and lack the pluginFee getters, which is the Integral 1.0/1.1 interface. Pools of 0x5f95e92c carry lastFeeTransferTimestamp(), getPluginFeePending(), skim(), sync(), SwapFee(address,uint24,uint24) and BurnFee(address,uint24), which is the Integral 1.2.2 interface. Both emit the Uniswap v3 topics for Swap, Mint and Burn. Result: The swap step was taken from the tagged source and agrees with the reruns below. The tick table is a doubly linked list of initialized ticks: ticks(int24) returns liquidityTotal, liquidityDelta, prevTick and nextTick. prevTickGlobal and nextTickGlobal bracket the current tick, and a three layer bitmap tree is used only to find a neighbour on insertion (TickStructure._addOrRemoveTick, TickTree.getNextTick). The fee in pips is globalState.lastFee. On 1.0/1.1 it is changed by Fee(uint16) when the plugin calls setFee. On 1.2.2 the plugin's beforeSwap returns overrideFee and pluginFee, the fee is overrideFee + pluginFee when overrideFee is not 0 and lastFee + pluginFee otherwise, and SwapFee is logged just before Swap. The community fee and the plugin fee only split feeAmount after the step and change neither price nor amounts. PriceMovementMath.movePriceTowardsTarget is the v3 step with the input recomputed from the new price, and TokenDeltaMath.getToken0Delta/getToken1Delta and PriceMovementMath.getNewPrice equal SqrtPriceMath getAmount0Delta, getAmount1Delta, getNextSqrtPriceFromInput and getNextSqrtPriceFromOutput operation by operation. So the rerun uses tools/opdiff/v4math.py, the transcription of src/libraries. ## Reading of the source (theme-inbox-deployed)

- Arbitrum One, Robinhood Chain, Elysium, cycle 19. Lead L-873, tasks 1 and 2: the Inbox implementation each Arbitrum-family rollup uses today and how every externally callable function computes the sender passed to the Bridge. Result: No caller-chosen sender. Rollup contracts 0x4DCeB440 (Arbitrum One), 0x23a19d23 (Robinhood) and 0x508C173d (Elysium) return Inbox proxies 0x4dbd4fc5, 0x1a07cc4b and 0xce59f8b6 with EIP-1967 implementations 0x7c058ad1, 0x8d3b93df and 0x748c47ee. All three are verified on Sourcify (exact_match or match) with byte-identical Inbox.sol and AbsInbox.sol. The bytecode dispatchers hold 28 selectors each, all present in the verified ABI, none extra. Every message goes through _deliverToBridge, which passes applyL1ToL2Alias(sender) to enqueueDelayedMessage (Inbox.sol:317-326). sendL2Message, sendL2MessageFromOrigin, sendUnsignedTransaction, sendContractTransaction, sendL1FundedUnsignedTransaction, sendL1FundedContractTransaction, createRetryableTicket, unsafeCreateRetryableTicket, createRetryableTicketNoRefundAliasRewrite and both depositEth functions use msg.sender, which the alias then shifts. The three ToFork functions use undoL1ToL2Alias(msg.sender), so the Bridge sees msg.sender unaliased, only when msg.sender equals tx.origin and the chain id differs from the deploy-time chain id; eth_call of sendUnsignedTransactionToFork reverts with NotForked (0xa301bb06) on all three parent chains, and an unsigned EOA transaction keeps the Nitro EOA check that the PoolManager's code fails. debug_traceCall from each PoolManager's alias preimage shows enqueueDelayedMessage kind 3 with sender equal to the PoolManager for sendContractTransaction, sendUnsignedTransaction and sendL2Message, so only an account at the preimage reaches it. allowListEnabled and paused are false on all three. The Inbox source does not differ between the three chains or from the nitro-contracts main copy that cycle 18 read. Result: Arbitrum One PoolManager 0x360e68fa...fb32 has preimage 0x24fd68faccca8ca495c1b759fd9eee466db9ea21, Robinhood 0x8366a39c...0951 has 0x7255a39cc670b4001a1121b8f6a443a643e3f840, both on Ethereum, and Elysium 0xE2e105d3...23F1 has 0xd1d005d3f7209a9da11f83ccf3e7398a753812e0 on HyperEVM. Each has no code, nonce 0 and balance 0. Acting from one needs its private key or a CREATE or CREATE2 deployment that lands on that fixed 160-bit address, a second-preimage search of about 2^160 work. HyperEVM system transactions come only from 0x2222222222222222222222222222222222222222 and the 0x20-prefixed token system addresses, so HyperCore cannot produce a transaction from the Elysium preimage. The Robinhood PoolManager address also holds 24,009 bytes of code on Ethereum with nonce 1; a contract cannot be tx.origin, so it would be aliased like any contract. Evidence: eth_getCode, eth_getTransactionCount, eth_getBalance on https://ethereum-rpc.publicnode.com and https://rpc.hyperliquid.xyz/evm; https://hyperliquid.gitbook.io/hyperliquid-docs/for-developers/hyperevm/hypercore-less-than-greater-than-hyperevm-transfers; research/network-risk/cycles/019/theme-inbox-deployed.work/raw/alias.txt

Lead L-878 and task 5: how the deployed OptimismPortal on each of the nine chains computes the from field of a deposit, and whether an ordinary account can make it equal the PoolManager. Result: No for ordinary accounts. Five implementations are in use: 0xb20b23af (version 6.1.0; OP Mainnet, Unichain, Ink, Soneium), 0x03863ab7 (6.0.1; Base), 0xe89f13c5 (5.6.1; Zora, World Chain), 0x2c431080 (5.1.1; Celo) and 0xa0fefc3a (5.2.0; X Layer), each matching SystemConfig.optimismPortal(). 0x03863ab7, 0xe89f13c5 and 0xa0fefc3a are verified on Sourcify: depositTransaction (and depositERC20Transaction on X Layer) sets from to msg.sender and replaces it with applyL1ToL2Alias(msg.sender) unless EOA.isSenderEOA(), which is msg.sender == tx.origin or 23 bytes of code starting 0xEF0100. 0xb20b23af and 0x2c431080 are not on Sourcify; their bytecode carries the same markers (PUSH20 0x1111...1111 before the TransactionDeposited topic, ORIGIN, PUSH3 0xEF0100), and their extra selectors are deleteProvenWithdrawal (0xba93107d) and setGasPayingToken. debug_traceCall shows from equal to an EOA caller on all nine, and from equal to the aliased L1CrossDomainMessenger when called through L1StandardBridge.bridgeETH on OP Mainnet, Base, Unichain, Zora, World Chain, Ink and Soneium. Celo's second TransactionDeposited site uses the fixed sender 0xdeaddeaddeaddeaddeaddeaddeaddeaddead0001 and the L1Block target behind a CALLER check against the stored SystemConfig. The PoolManager address of each chain has no code and nonce 0 on Ethereum, and so does its alias preimage; reaching either needs a key for a fixed address. EIP-3541 stops a deployed contract from having code that starts with 0xEF, so the delegation test cannot be met by a contract. Evidence: https://sourcify.dev/server/v2/contract/1/0x03863ab7f64b733cff85c8ff44a86601c568ca70; https://sourcify.dev/server/v2/contract/1/0xe89f13c5ee4033b2d3cd76c9d6958efbfe26d3c2; https://sourcify.dev/server/v2/contract/1/0xa0fefc3a457f6a1ae2d81fc172d6de090a9f4033; https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ethereum-optimism/superchain-registry/main/superchain/configs/mainnet/op.toml (and unichain, zora, worldchain, ink, soneium, celo); https://docs.base.org/base-chain/network-information/base-contracts; debug_traceCall on https://eth.drpc.org; research/network-risk/cycles/019/theme-inbox-deployed.work/raw/portals.json, bytescan.json, op_deposit_traces.json, op_deposit_traces_retry.txt, op_celo_bridge_trace.txt
