## Reading of the source (theme-megaeth-producer)

- MegaETH, cycle 19. Task 1. Tie the build mega-reth/v2.3.1-4499c42 that https://mainnet.megaeth.com/rpc answered on 2026-11-25 (web3_clientVersion at 16:17 and 16:18 UTC, before and after every batch; the answer came from the gateway cache, header x-cache-status HIT) to source, and say what changed in mega-evm since v1.7.3. Result: No public source carries 4499c42. raw.githubusercontent.com returns 404 for megaeth-labs/mega-reth (the node stays closed), and the MegaETH docs cite a different private revision, mega-reth ab60376631228edab3a6df180f295280bad26e93 (40 citations in llms-full.txt, captures of 2026-07-24). The public megaeth-labs/reth fork is archived and empty. Provider changelogs found reach v2.2.2 only. So the build is not tied to a revision, and its mega-evm pin is unknown. What is public: stateless-validator main is now version 2.2.0 and pins mega-evm tag v1.7.4 with revm 40.0.3 (Cargo.toml lines 15, 44, 64); mega-evm v1.7.4 pins revm =40.0.3 and alloy-evm =0.36.0 and has no [patch] redirect (Cargo.toml lines 141, 147). Of the 58 source files of crates/mega-evm/src that exist in both tags, 55 are byte-identical between v1.7.3 and v1.7.4 and the other 3 (evm/instructions.rs, evm/precompiles.rs, limit/limit.rs) differ in comments only (tagdiff/*.diff). The v1.7.4 release notes list tooling, docs, tests and CI changes only. A new public repository, megaeth-labs/revm, forks revm v112 (revm 40.0.3) with gas-accounting and code-deposit hooks whose defaults keep upstream behaviour; it says the node and validator move their pins to it together, and neither mega-evm v1.7.4 nor the validator uses it yet. None of this changes an arithmetic, jump, memory or storage handler that the PoolManager reaches. Evidence: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/megaeth-labs/stateless-validator/main/Cargo.toml; https://raw.githubusercontent.com/megaeth-labs/mega-evm/main/Cargo.toml; https://github.com/megaeth-labs/mega-evm/releases; https://raw.githubusercontent.com/megaeth-labs/revm/main/MEGAETH-FORK.md; https://docs.megaeth.com/llms-full.txt; research/network-risk/cycles/019/theme-megaeth-producer.work/dl/tagdiff
- MegaETH, cycle 19. Task 2. Which executor answers each public method: eth_call, eth_estimateGas, eth_callMany, eth_createAccessList, eth_simulateV1, the realtime methods and the mega_ namespace. Result: No documented read-only method is run by the sequencer. The gateway sends eth_call to its compute pool and rewrites it to the node method mega_callWithBlock. It sends eth_estimateGas there too, rewritten to eth_estimateGasWithCpuLimit, and sends eth_callMany and eth_createAccessList to the same pool. Each page says the node simulates the call. The architecture page says RPC nodes are replicas that apply the sequencer's results without running them again, and that replicas are the default. Called directly, mega_callWithBlock and eth_simulateV1 return -32601 'is not supported', and debug_traceCall and trace_call are listed as unavailable. The mega_ methods that remain (getBlockWitness, getWithdrawalProof, outputAtBlock) read data and execute nothing. eth_sendRawTransactionSync and realtime_sendRawTransaction return the sequencer's own receipt for a submitted transaction. That is the producer's result, but only for a real transaction, which this review may not send. No response field names the executor. The battery and the targeted vectors therefore cannot reach the producer through a read-only call. This rests on the published docs. The gateway source (mega-rpc) is private, so it is unconfirmed that the compute pool holds replicas only. Evidence: https://docs.megaeth.com/developer-docs/rpc/reference.md; https://docs.megaeth.com/developer-docs/rpc/reference/eth_call.md; https://docs.megaeth.com/developer-docs/rpc/reference/eth_estimategas.md; https://docs.megaeth.com/developer-docs/rpc/reference/eth_callmany.md; https://docs.megaeth.com/developer-docs/rpc/reference/eth_sendrawtransactionsync.md; https://docs.megaeth.com/architecture.md; eth_call/mega_callWithBlock/eth_simulateV1 on https://mainnet.megaeth.com/rpc 2026-11-25 (raw-headers.txt)
- MegaETH, cycle 19. Task 3. What the docs and public source say about the producer's compiler, and what the only public MegaETH compiler computes for MULMOD, SAR, SHL, SIGNEXTEND, SDIV, SMOD and CALLDATALOAD, with constant operands at pcs 22378, 22639, 15519, 16642 and 12232. Result: The docs never mention a compiler or JIT. llms-full.txt (752,661 bytes) has no match for jit, AOT, ahead-of-time, evmone or revmc. Only the stateless-validator README (line 26) calls the sequencer's executor parallel and JIT-compiled. The one public compiler is megaeth-labs/evmone-compiler, which is archived (default branch aot-compiler). It specialises nothing on constant operands. compiler.cpp passes immediates only to PUSH and fuses only PUSH followed by JUMP or JUMPI (lines 136-139, 175-180), so MULMOD by 2^128 or 2^96, SAR 128, SHL 3 and CALLDATALOAD run the generic handler. Several of its handlers break the specification. A transcription compiled with clang 18 (build/proto_handlers.cpp and .out) confirms four of them: (1) sar computes is_neg as x < 0 on an unsigned _BitInt(256) (aot_instructions.hpp:297-305 with aot_execution_state.hpp:18), so SAR(128, -5) gives 2^128-1 where the specification gives all ones; (2) signextend builds its mask as 1u << (b-1) in 32 bits (aot_instructions.hpp:207-218), so SIGNEXTEND(15, 2^127+7) gives no sign fill; (3) byte shifts by a byte count where a bit count is needed (lines 275-285); (4) mulmod writes stack[2] and never pops (lines 184-190). sdiv and smod divide _BitInt values, which is undefined at INT_MIN / -1. Dynamic JUMP lands on the next JUMPDEST at or above the target, because get_jumpdest never checks the key it found (aot_execution_state.hpp:53-58). The README says the prototype supports opcodes up to Shanghai. The PoolManager build hits those handlers at 19 SAR, 114 SIGNEXTEND (40 of them SIGNEXTEND 15) and 13 MULMOD sites, and every swap unpacks a BalanceDelta with sar(128) and signextend(15) (src/types/BalanceDelta.sol:63, :69). Under those handlers mined swap amounts would be wrong in nearly every block. The validator reproduces every block's state root, and mined swaps replay to the unit (OPCODES.md cycles 10 to 18). So the production executor does not use these handlers, and the prototype says nothing about the code that writes blocks. Its source is not public, and the five sites can be read only through mined results. Evidence: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/megaeth-labs/evmone-compiler/aot-compiler/lib/compiler/aot_instructions.hpp; https://raw.githubusercontent.com/megaeth-labs/evmone-compiler/aot-compiler/lib/compiler/compiler.cpp; https://raw.githubusercontent.com/megaeth-labs/evmone-compiler/aot-compiler/lib/compiler/aot_execution_state.hpp; https://raw.githubusercontent.com/megaeth-labs/evmone-compiler/aot-compiler/lib/compiler/README.md; https://raw.githubusercontent.com/megaeth-labs/stateless-validator/main/README.md; research/network-risk/cycles/019/theme-megaeth-producer.work/build/proto_handlers.out
- MegaETH, cycle 19. Task 4. Mined executions at the five sites and re-execution of their blocks with the pre-state anchored to the parent root. 212 PoolManager transactions were traced with debug_traceTransaction (struct logger): all 116 transactions with a PoolManager log in blocks 32,814,963 to 32,826,734 (123 logs in 100 blocks), all 82 transactions with a Swap in the 51 pools whose hook has BEFORE_SWAP_RETURNS_DELTA (from the 143 Initialize events of the full history), and the 14 census transactions that call extsload(bytes32[]). The selection is complete, not sampled, so there is no seed. The first pass hit HTTP 429 on 107 transactions; those were rerun on one thread with 1.5 s pauses on the same endpoint. No other endpoint was used. Each block was then run with the stateless validator build of cycle 16 (e1618ed7, mega-evm v1.7.3), anchored at the parent block's hash. Result: Executions inside PoolManager code frames: pc 15519 (SAR of a hook's BeforeSwapDelta, src/types/BeforeSwapDelta.sol:27 via src/libraries/Hooks.sol:266-270) ran 87 times in 82 transactions and 79 blocks; pc 12232 (CALLDATALOAD of the array length, src/Extsload.sol:42) ran 14 times in 14 transactions; pcs 22378, 22639 and 16642 never ran. Every replica result equals Python. All 87 SAR inputs have the top bit clear and 17 are zero words, so no mined hook returned a negative specified delta. None of the 116 new transactions reaches any site. All 193 blocks (93 site blocks and 100 new blocks) were reproduced, state root and receipts root included, with the witness pre-state checked against the parent's state root. The cycle 16 build with a planted MULMOD fault fails 32 of 45 of these blocks: 29 of 30 new blocks and 3 of 15 returns-delta blocks. So the comparison can see a wrong product in ordinary swaps. Cycle 17 showed that a whole-output comparison cannot see a faulty word at pcs 15519, 22378 or 22639, because SIGNEXTEND 15 at pc 15522 and the quotient at FullMath.sol:66-75 drop the bits concerned. The same property means a fault at those sites changes no amount. pc 22378 runs only in calls that revert at Pool.sol:192, and pc 16642 has no caller. This raises the mined coverage of pc 15519 and pc 12232 from zero to the counts above. It cannot raise coverage of the other three sites, because no mined transaction reaches them. Evidence: research/network-risk/cycles/019/theme-megaeth-producer.work/raw/sites-pass1.jsonl, sites-pass2.jsonl, sites-pass3.jsonl, validate.txt, validate-plant.txt, anch/, anch-plant/, summary.json; debug_traceTransaction and mega_getBlockWitness on https://mainnet.megaeth.com/rpc (mega-reth/v2.3.1-4499c42@mnet-ash-rpc-2 at start and end); src/types/BeforeSwapDelta.sol:27; src/libraries/Hooks.sol:266-279; src/Extsload.sol:42
- MegaETH, cycle 19. Task 5 (lead L-883). Find a mined block whose state growth reached the 1,000 entry block limit. Headers of blocks 32,806,000 to 32,826,000 were read in batches of 50 (20,001 headers). The 21 blocks above 20 million gas were traced with prestateTracer in diffMode, and each transaction's new nonzero slots and new accounts were counted. Result: No block in the window comes near the limit. The largest estimate is 58 entries (block 32,823,122, 86 transactions), and the blocks of 107 million to 260 million gas grow state by 1 or 2 entries because their gas is compute. The count is an estimate from the trace and leaves out mega-evm's own fee-recipient and clearing rules, but the margin to 1,000 is large. The docs confirm both limits at 1,000 and say the transaction that crosses the block limit is still included and later candidates are skipped. Without a capped block the question of where skipped transactions are placed afterwards stays open. F-062 is unchanged (plausible, low, no funds move). Evidence: https://docs.megaeth.com/spec/megaevm/resource-limits.md; https://docs.megaeth.com/spec/megaevm/resource-accounting.md; research/network-risk/cycles/019/theme-megaeth-producer.work/raw/gasscan.json, growth-top.json
- MegaETH, cycle 19. mega-evm v1.7.3 added discard_tx and discard_transaction for a transaction whose execution panicked. Without them, an embedder that catches the panic and reuses the EVM keeps the panicked transaction's state writes, logs, transient storage, memory and frames. Result: No evidence of a leak on chain. If transient storage survived into the next transaction, the PoolManager's lock flag and deltas (src/libraries/Lock.sol:10-27, src/PoolManager.sol:104-114) could carry over. Cycle 18's census found no transaction that ended with a currency still synced, and no settle credited from another transaction's sync, in 72,184 MegaETH transactions. All 193 blocks here are reproduced by a validator that starts each transaction fresh. Whether the closed producer catches panics and whether its pin includes v1.7.3 is unknown (see leads). Evidence: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/megaeth-labs/mega-evm/v1.7.4/crates/mega-evm/src/evm/mod.rs (lines 395-440); https://raw.githubusercontent.com/megaeth-labs/mega-evm/v1.7.4/crates/mega-evm/src/block/executor.rs (lines 762-782); https://github.com/megaeth-labs/mega-evm/releases

## Reading of the source (theme-tempo-nested-exec)

- Tempo, cycle 19. Every non-test caller of enter_execution in evm2 35aa3280 (the was_running flag) and what it does with the transient storage map. Result: enter_execution (crates/evm2/src/evm/mod.rs:454-458) only sets running and the guard puts the old value back on drop (mod.rs:1230-1239). It has five callers: execute_precompile (mod.rs:407), inspect_log (mod.rs:969), execute_tx (mod.rs:1315), execute_message_inspected (mod.rs:1456) and run_interpreter (mod.rs:1854). Four of them run a precompile, an inspector hook, a message or an interpreter frame inside the transaction that is already running, on the same State and therefore on the same transient map, which is what a CALL does on Ethereum. The fifth, execute_tx, is the entry of a top-level transaction and is reached only from transact and transact_with_inspector. The flag exists so that setters can refuse changes while code runs (mod.rs:421-443). It does not start a second transaction. Evidence: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/DaniPopes/evm2/35aa32800b147b00e616d4e1869a3835aa86701f/crates/evm2/src/evm/mod.rs (lines 407, 454-458, 969, 1230-1239, 1315, 1456, 1854)
- Tempo, cycle 19. Where evm2 creates, clears and copies the transient map: clear_transaction_state, ExecutedTx resolution, committed_copy, take_transient_storage, rollback. Result: The map is a field of State (crates/evm2/src/evm/state/mod.rs:58-59). clear_transaction_state empties it with the journal, logs and warm sets (state/mod.rs:555-569). It runs when an executed transaction is committed, discarded or detached (tx.rs:222-245), when a transaction or system call fails (mod.rs:1318-1320, system.rs:133-136), after validate_tx (mod.rs:1346) and when the backing database is replaced (state/mod.rs:269-272 through Evm::set_database at mod.rs:700-702). committed_copy builds a new State with an empty map (state/mod.rs:135-150) and has no caller outside tests in evm2 or in the 578 Rust files of the Tempo workspace. take_transient_storage removes the slots of one named address (state/mod.rs:873-878). Each TSTORE is journaled (state/mod.rs:837-866) and rollback restores it (state/mod.rs:911-918), so a reverted frame or batch puts the PoolManager's slots back. Nothing clears the map between frames: execute_initial_frame in crates/evm2/src/ethereum/mod.rs contains no clearing step. Evidence: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/DaniPopes/evm2/35aa32800b147b00e616d4e1869a3835aa86701f/crates/evm2/src/evm/state/mod.rs (lines 58-59, 135-150, 555-569, 837-918), crates/evm2/src/evm/tx.rs:222-245
- Tempo, cycle 19. Every non-test caller of transact, call_tx, validate_tx, system_call, execute_system_call, committed_copy, set_database and take_transient_storage in the Tempo workspace at a9d6748 (all 52 members including consensus, payload builder, transaction pool, precompiles, precompile macros, zones) and in evm2 (including evm2-jit and evm2-inspectors). Result: None runs while a user transaction is on the call stack. Block level: the EIP-2935 history system call before the first transaction (crates/evm/src/block.rs:858-870) and the committee system call after the last one (block.rs:554-603, called from finish_with_block_access_list at block.rs:1043-1048); evm2's own block executor runs transact once per block transaction and its system calls before or after them (crates/evm2/src/block/ethereum/execution.rs:188, 213, 285-458). Separate EVM instances: the pool validator (crates/transaction-pool/src/validator.rs:572), the payload prewarm workers (crates/payload/builder/src/prewarming.rs:181-194), the zone sequencer, payload and RPC crates (crates/zones/evm/src/executor.rs:306, crates/zones/payload/src/builder.rs:865, crates/zones/payload/src/prewarming.rs:176, crates/zones/node/src/rpc/mod.rs:1507), genesis (crates/evm/src/genesis.rs:76, 104) and the fuzz harness. The system transaction handler calls execute_system_call as the body of the system transaction itself, at its start (crates/evm/src/handler/config.rs:512-536), and only for the fixed system signature (crates/primitives/src/transaction/envelope.rs:234-236). No precompile, the fee manager, the account keychain, the payment channel reserve, the T14 configurable account shim or the batch handler calls any of these functions. Evm::transact has no running check (mod.rs:1285-1288), so the guarantee rests on there being no such caller, which the search confirms for this revision. Evidence: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/tempoxyz/tempo/a9d6748/crates/evm/src/block.rs (lines 554-603, 858-870, 1043-1048); crates/evm/src/handler/config.rs:512-536; search list in cycles/019/theme-tempo-nested-exec.work/callers_all.txt
- Tempo, cycle 19. Storage credit settlement drains transient slots at the end of a transaction (take_transient_storage). Result: settle_storage_credit_refunds takes only the slots of 0x1060000000000000000000000000000000000000 (crates/evm/src/handler/config.rs:444-490) and is called from settle_transaction (config.rs:251-256), which the AA handler calls after execute_batch has returned (crates/evm/src/handler.rs:1704-1720). By then every user frame, and so every PoolManager.unlock, has finished. The PoolManager's slots are keyed by its own address (state/mod.rs:832-838) and are never selected. Evidence: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/tempoxyz/tempo/a9d6748/crates/evm/src/handler/config.rs:444-490 and crates/evm/src/handler.rs:1704-1720
- Tempo, cycle 19. Nested calls made by precompiles (TIP-20 zone deposit forwarding) and T14 batch calls: map shared, emptied or cleared?. Result: The only precompile in production that calls user code is TIP-20 deposit_virtual (crates/precompiles/src/tip20/mod.rs:1073-1115), which goes through the storage provider's call (crates/precompiles/src/storage/evm.rs:677-740). That runs a message with Host::execute_call on the same Evm, so it shares the map like a CALL and is journaled; the provider refuses it inside a checkpoint or past the nested call limit (evm.rs:689-695), and deposit_virtual refuses it from inside another precompile (tip20/mod.rs:1081-1088). The callee sees msg.sender equal to the token, so a reentry into the PoolManager from the portal has the token as its own locker with its own deltas, which is ordinary CALL semantics; the payout side of that path is F-135. A batch of calls in one Tempo transaction runs each call as a top-level frame on the same State under one checkpoint (crates/evm/src/handler.rs:1284-1371) with the same sender, which matches a smart account multicall on Ethereum: an unlock has relocked before its call returns (src/PoolManager.sol:104-114), and a sync left open by one call of the batch belongs to the same sender. Evidence: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/tempoxyz/tempo/a9d6748/crates/precompiles/src/storage/evm.rs:677-740; crates/precompiles/src/tip20/mod.rs:1073-1115; crates/evm/src/handler.rs:1284-1371
- Tempo, cycle 19. Read-only probe: driver unlocks the PoolManager, syncs pathUSD and mints 1 to open a delta, then calls 28 precompile and control paths and reads the lock, delta count, synced currency, reserves and its delta with exttload before and after, on eth_call at latest and on eth_simulateV1 at block time 1796745600 (T14 rules). Result: In all 56 runs the five slots after the probe call equal the slots before it: lock 1, count 1, currency pathUSD, reserves as synced, delta -1. 16 of 28 probe calls succeeded at latest and 15 at T14 time, the rest reverted inside the precompile and were rolled back without touching the PoolManager's slots. The paths include TIP-20 approve, transfer and a transfer to a zone-style address, fee manager setUserToken, storage credit setBudget, keychain revokeKey, DEX withdraw, the channel reserve, the T14 configurable account address, and a contract that writes SSTORE and TSTORE. Endpoint tempo/v1.19.1-a9d6748 before and after. A second simulation left pathUSD synced at the end of one transaction and read all four slots as zero in the next transaction of the same block, at latest and at T14 time. Evidence: rpc https://rpc.mainnet.tempo.xyz eth_call and eth_simulateV1, cycles/019/theme-tempo-nested-exec.work/probe_latest.json, probe_t14.json, carry.json

## Reading of the source (theme-avalanche-multicoin)

- Avalanche, cycle 20. Task 1, the code the C-Chain runs and every writer of the asset partition. The public endpoint answered web3_clientVersion avalanchego/1.15.3 commit 983815fd, go 1.26.10, before and after every batch. At v1.15.3 the node registers the SAE C-Chain VM for the EVM chain id (node/node.go:1240, saevm.Factory from vms/saevm/cchain), and graft/coreth holds only params, nativeasset, customtypes and precompile packages. A search of the whole avalanchego v1.15.3 tree and of the libevm revision it pins (d398bc4dbe41, go.mod:30) lists every caller of AddAssetBalance, SubAssetBalance, GetAssetBalance, SetState with SkipStateKeyTransformation and MarkHeldXChainAsset. Result: There are four writers and none is open to an ordinary account today. (1) Import.transferNonAVAX calls AddAssetBalance for each non-AVAX output (vms/saevm/cchain/tx/import.go:237-246), run from FinishExecutingBlock (vms/saevm/cchain/hooks.go:257-269). Import.sanityCheck rejects any non-AVAX input or output with no fork gate (tx/import.go:117-128). The txpool runs it on every gossiped transaction (txpool/txpool.go:163) and PotentialEndOfBlockOps runs it on every atomic transaction, also when VerifyBlock rebuilds a peer's block and compares hashes (hooks.go:464, sae/blocks.go:77-90, sae/block_builder.go:77-127). A block carrying a non-AVAX import is therefore rebuilt without it and rejected. (2) Export.transferNonAVAX calls SubAssetBalance (tx/export.go:267-281); export inputs are rejected the same way (export.go:136-138) and each input needs a secp256k1 signature that recovers to the debited address (export.go:174-196), which the PoolManager, a contract, cannot give. (3) NativeAssetCall (graft/coreth/nativeasset/contract.go:142-157) is mapped to DeprecatedContract, which reverts, from Banff on (graft/coreth/params/hooks_libevm.go:113-124, 133-147). (4) AddAssetBalance with a zero amount only touches the account (extstate/statedb.go:139-143). The validators that still run the older full coreth tree check the same thing behind rules.IsBanff (coreth plugin/evm/atomic/import_tx.go:106-117 on ava-labs/coreth master and at avalanchego v1.14.2). The SAE end of block ops only move native AVAX and nonces (vms/saevm/hook/hook.go:186-212, saexec/execution.go:416-436). Evidence: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ava-labs/avalanchego/v1.15.3/vms/saevm/cchain/tx/import.go
- Avalanche, cycle 20. Task 2, whether a write into the asset partition of the PoolManager account could land on a key the EVM later reads as a PoolManager slot. Result: No, by construction and independent of who writes. libevm applies TransformStateKey in GetState, GetCommittedState and SetState unless the caller passes SkipStateKeyTransformation (libevm core/state/statedb.go:346-363, 419-425, statedb.libevm.go:115-121). The C-Chain hook clears bit 0 of byte 0 of every EVM key (extstate/statedb.go:48-56), so SLOAD and SSTORE (core/vm/instructions.go:517, 528) only reach keys with that bit clear. Asset keys always have it set (assetBalanceKey, extstate/statedb.go:59-62). The two key sets are disjoint, so no asset balance can equal any PoolManager slot, including the half of the keccak derived pool, tick, position and bitmap slots whose own bit 248 is set: those are stored at the key with the bit cleared. The fold of F-040 is the price of this separation and is already covered there. The only raw EVM read is GetCommittedState before Apricot Phase 1 (extstate/statedb.go:102-113), which sets SSTORE refunds of blocks from 2020 and does not run today. Evidence: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ava-labs/avalanchego/v1.15.3/vms/saevm/cchain/libevm/extstate/statedb.go
- Avalanche, cycle 20. Task 3, the precompiles and the PoolManager storage read by RPC (scripts/probe.py, probe2.py, oldops.py, outputs raw/probe.json, raw/probe2.json, raw/oldops.json, block 101,376,238 and later). Result: eth_call to 0x0100000000000000000000000000000000000001 (NativeAssetBalance) and ...0002 (NativeAssetCall) and to the genesis contract ...0000 reverts with empty data, both from the PoolManager address and from 0x...0a11ce. The old multicoin opcodes 0xcd and 0xcf are undefined ('invalid opcode: opcode 0xcd not defined'). For 52 pool state words of 13 pools seen in recent Swap logs (32 of them with bit 248 set in the slot), eth_getStorageAt of the slot, eth_getStorageAt of the slot with bit 248 flipped, extsload of both all return the same non-zero word. The raw asset partition could not be read: eth_getProof answers 'the method eth_getProof is not available' on api.avax.network (the SAE RPC does not register it), debug_storageRangeAt, debug_dumpBlock and debug_accountRange do not exist, and the other public endpoints tried (publicnode, ankr, 1rpc, drpc, meowrpc, omniatech) returned a challenge page, an API key demand, a quota error or no answer. So the absence of asset keys in the PoolManager's trie rests on the source reading above, not on a proof. Evidence: eth_getStorageAt, eth_call and eth_getProof on https://api.avax.network/ext/bc/C/rpc, recorded in research/network-risk/cycles/020/theme-avalanche-multicoin.work/raw/probe2.json
- Avalanche, cycle 20. Task 4, whether the held X-chain asset flag (the former IsMultiCoin) on an account changes SLOAD, SSTORE, BALANCE, SELFBALANCE or EXTCODEHASH. Result: The flag is a bool account extra (customtypes/state_account_ext.go:11-25), set only by AddAssetBalance and read only there. TransformStateKey ignores the address (extstate/statedb.go:48), so SLOAD and SSTORE are the same with or without it. BALANCE and SELFBALANCE read the native balance, which the flag does not touch. The flag enters stateObject.empty() (libevm core/state/state_object.go:95-97), so it only matters for an account with nonce 0, zero balance and no code: EXTCODEHASH of such an account returns keccak256 of empty code instead of zero (instructions.go:417-426), it escapes EIP-161 deletion, and a value call to it skips the new account surcharge. The PoolManager has code and nonce 1, so none of this applies to it, and src/ does not use EXTCODEHASH or code size checks (no match for extcodehash, extcodesize or .code.length in src/). The CREATE collision check reads nonce and code hash only (core/vm/evm.go:456-459), so a pre-Banff asset balance at a future address cannot block a deployment. Evidence: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ava-labs/libevm/d398bc4dbe41/core/state/state_object.go
- Avalanche, cycle 20. Native AVAX that an ordinary account can push into the PoolManager outside the EVM: an atomic import whose output address is the PoolManager mints AVAX to it at the end of a block (hook.go:209-211, tx/import.go:206-224), and export cannot debit it without its key. Result: Harmless. Native settle credits msg.value and never reads the native balance (src/PoolManager.sol:349-355), and sync of the native currency only resets the synced currency (src/PoolManager.sol:279-283). Minted AVAX is a surplus nobody can claim through the PoolManager, the same as a forced send by SELFDESTRUCT on Ethereum, and it arrives between transactions, never inside an unlock. Evidence: src/PoolManager.sol:349-355
- Avalanche, cycle 20. State overrides used as evidence on Avalanche. libevm applies `state` overrides through SetStorage, which writes raw keys, and `stateDiff` overrides through SetState, which transforms them (libevm internal/ethapi/api.go:985-997, core/state/statedb.go:427-445). Result: Measured on the endpoint: a `state` override of key 2^248+0x1234 is invisible to extsload of either 2^248+0x1234 or 0x1234 and also wipes the real storage (owner slot reads zero), while the same key under `stateDiff` is read under both indexes. The shared scripts in research/network-risk/tools/opdiff use only `code`, `balance` and `stateDiff` overrides (pmdiff3.py:104, pmdiff6.py:145), so their Avalanche results are not affected. A script that seeds keccak derived slots with a `state` override on the C-Chain would put half of them into the asset partition. Evidence: eth_call with state overrides on https://api.avax.network/ext/bc/C/rpc, recorded in research/network-risk/cycles/020/theme-avalanche-multicoin.work/raw/probe2.json
- Ethereum, Optimism, Base, Unichain, Zora, Worldchain, Ink, Soneium, Celo, X Layer, Arbitrum One, Robinhood Chain, Elysium, Polygon, BNB Smart Chain, Monad, MegaETH, Tempo, Arc, HyperEVM, cycle 20. The theme across networks: does any other of the 21 networks keep a non-EVM namespace inside a contract's own storage trie that public transactions can write?. Result: No such namespace is known on the other 20. The multicoin partition is a C-Chain feature of coreth and of the SAE C-Chain VM. The cycle 19 storage key test (statekeys.py and extsload over the deployed PoolManagers) found that no other network folds a bit of a storage or transient index, which a partition with a key hook would show. A partition without a key hook would collide with EVM slots and be visible to SLOAD; none was seen. This covers only what an EVM read can see. The closed clients (HyperEVM's validator, MegaETH's producer) were not read. Evidence: research/network-risk/state/cleared.json (cycle 19 established-l1 statekeys rerun and the 21 network fold test)

Result: Miscompilations on amd64 or arm64, by shape: #76967 constant facts propagated through an out-of-range jump table index (go1.25.6); #77253 static array initialisation that stores a stack pointer in a global (go1.25.8, go1.26.1); #77618 64-bit AND/OR constant folded into a sign-extended 32-bit immediate, seen in strings.HasSuffix (go1.26.1, amd64); #77623 regalloc clobbers one register twice when both inputs share it, shown by *y = *x with y the same pointer (go1.26.1); CVE-2026-27143 loop bounds check elimination with a negative or non-unit step (go1.25.9, go1.26.2); CVE-2026-27144 overlap detection misses a no-op interface conversion on the right side of an assignment (go1.25.9, go1.26.2); #78404 devirtualisation, now comparing types by pointer identity (go1.26.3); #79182 (x + x) << 63 or << 31 rewritten to x << 0 on amd64 (go1.25.11, go1.26.4); #80517 prove learns a fact before it holds and drops a bounds check, #79874 32-bit slice mask for a 64-bit slice (go1.25.13, go1.26.6); stack slot merging with a copied address (go1.25.13, go1.26.6); #81689 and #81668 stack-allocated slice backing store kept after a range or an &s[i].f escape (go1.26.9); #81863 dead store through a CondSelect (go1.26.11, F-117); #81868 the canonical Const64 amount of a narrow shift got the narrow type (go1.26.11, 'confirmed crashes, maybe misscompilations'). The other compiler fixes are crashes, hangs or build errors (regalloc loop, zero-sized values, write barrier, race instrumentation, PCALIGN loop, rotate amounts on 32-bit targets, DWARF heapaddr), other architectures (riscv64 sign extension, mips HI/LO and offsets, PPC64 atomics, arm32 and s390x merge locals), or cgo and linker hardening. bor v2.11.1, BNB Chain geth v1.8.2 and avalanchego 1.15.3 report go1.26.10, which holds every fix up to go1.26.10; what it lacks is #81863 and #81868 (and the open #82839). Evidence: https://go.dev/doc/devel/release; https://go.googlesource.com/go/+log/go1.25.5..go1.25.6?format=JSON and the 19 later ranges up to https://go.googlesource.com/go/+log/go1.26.10..go1.26.11?format=JSON (saved in research/network-risk/cycles/020/theme-evidence-audit.work/dl/go, summary compiler_commits.txt); https://go.googlesource.com/go/+/4659d630da3f96d3f463444057848f70d420bd0c?format=JSON; https://go.googlesource.com/go/+/babc19e1ad8cf2243b25553917af08fc4ad92948/test/fixedbugs/issue79182.go
- Polygon, BNB Smart Chain, Avalanche, Ethereum, cycle 20. Task 3: the shapes of #81868 (C1: an 8, 16 or 32 bit value shifted by a constant), #79182 (C2: shift left by 63 or 31, flagged when the operand is x + x, x * 2 or x << 1) and #81689/#81668 (C3: make of a slice with a non-constant length) added to the cycle 18 shapescan and run over holiman/uint256 v1.3.2 and v1.2.4 and the core/vm, core/state, core/types, trie, rlp and common/math trees of bor v2.11.1, bsc v1.8.2, coreth and graft/evm of avalanchego 1.15.3, libevm d398bc4dbe41, nitro geth 0e44603 and Celo op-geth c7ed55b8. A positive control file with the issue 79182 reproducer gives C1, C2 (dbl=true) and C3. Result: uint256 has no C1 site; its only C2 sites are Sqrt (v1.3.2 uint256.go:1335-1337, v1.2.4 1322-1326), z2[i] << 63 of a word that is not doubled, and no opcode calls Sqrt. The only C1 site in core/vm of every tree is BitVec.setN (bor core/vm/analysis_legacy.go:41, bsc :40, libevm analysis.go:40): byte(a >> 8) of a uint16, which marks the push data bits of PUSH2 to PUSH16 for jump destination analysis. Its shift amount is an untyped constant, which the SSA builder gives a 64-bit operand, while the faulty rule rewrote 8, 16 and 32 bit amounts; this was not checked in compiler output. It was tested on chain: for PUSH2 to PUSH16 at all eight alignments, a program jumps to each 0x5b byte inside and around the push data (1,620 cases, 1,080 of them must fail). Polygon (five bor v2.11.1 go1.26.10 builds), BNB Chain (Geth v1.8.2 go1.26.10, two builds), Avalanche (avalanchego 1.15.3 go1.26.10) and Ethereum (reth v2.11.0, control) give the specified outcome on all 1,620. The other C1 sites are bloom9, trie nibble encoding and the OP Stack FastLZ cost estimate, none on the path of a PoolManager opcode. C3 sites in core/vm (Memory.Resize and GetCopy, makeLog, codeBitmap, precompile inputs) build slices that are stored or returned whole; the three go1.26.10 builds already carry the #81689 and #81668 fixes. ## Reading of the source (theme-mined-gas-cap)

- all 21 networks, cycle 20. Lead L-913, measured. For each network, the gas cap of a mined ordinary transaction, and the gas of a full liquidity exit of a real position by its real owner at the real PoolManager, compared with that cap and not with the eth_call limit. Result: Every sampled exit fits under the mined cap with a margin of at least 15 times on every network, including HyperEVM small blocks. Method: for each network, positions of the deployed PositionManager were sampled below nextTokenId (the newest 40 ids and random older ones), kept when liquidity > 0 and hooks = 0, and eth_estimateGas was called from ownerOf(tokenId) for modifyLiquidities with BURN_POSITION (all liquidity removed and fees collected) then TAKE_PAIR to the owner, on 2026-11-25. Largest estimate per network (positions estimated): Ethereum 232,219 (20), OP Mainnet 281,366 (9), Base 235,285 (20), Unichain 234,404 (7), Zora 222,099 (20), World Chain 285,481 (20), Ink 167,714 (4), Soneium 240,197 (20), Celo 243,990 (20), X Layer 215,639 (20), Arbitrum One 258,999 (20), Robinhood Chain 269,856 (20), Elysium 223,274 (20), Polygon 403,097 (20), BNB Chain 320,073 (19), Avalanche 264,918 (20), Monad 382,525 (18), MegaETH 534,813 (20), Tempo 976,067 (20), Arc 205,841 (20), HyperEVM 197,982 (20). Mined caps: 16,777,216 on Ethereum, the seven OP Stack chains, BNB Chain and Arc; 30,000,000 on Celo (block limit), Monad and Tempo; 32,000,000 on the Arbitrum family; 33,554,432 on Polygon; 3,000,000 in HyperEVM small blocks and 30,000,000 in big blocks; at least 50,000,000 on Avalanche and 210,000,000 on X Layer (block limit); at least 984,000,000 on MegaETH (mined user transactions). The worst ratio is Tempo, 976,067 against 30,000,000. The two failures (one burned between calls on OP Mainnet, one BNB Chain token whose transfer reverts, 0x9c3aba46) are not gas. The gas of the exit does not grow with anything another account does: Pool.modifyLiquidity has no loop (src/libraries/Pool.sol:146-238), it writes two tick words, at most two bitmap words, the position (src/libraries/Position.sol:76-101) and the pool liquidity (Pool.sol:226), and clears ticks with delete (Pool.sol:592-594). The only zero to nonzero writes it can make are the two fee growth inside words of the position (Position.sol:100-101), which depend on the position, not on others. Outputs: out/exits.json, out/exits_137.json. Evidence: research/network-risk/cycles/020/theme-mined-gas-cap.work/out/exits.json; src/libraries/Pool.sol:146-238; src/libraries/Position.sol:76-101; https://eips.ethereum.org/EIPS/eip-7825
- all 21 networks, cycle 20. Claim redemption under the mined cap: burn(holder, id, balance) and take(currency, holder, balance) by real ERC-6909 holders at the real PoolManager, run with a gas limit of 16,777,216 (3,000,000 on HyperEVM). Result: Fits by a wide margin where measured. A measuring driver placed by state override at each holder address called unlock and, in the callback, burn and take, recording GAS around each call, then reverted. 14 networks returned holders from recent Transfer logs: Ethereum 8 of 8 succeeded, largest burn plus take 56,374 gas; OP Mainnet 38,236; Unichain 55,336; World Chain 38,236; Ink 58,548; Celo 7 of 7, 38,839; X Layer 55,342; Arbitrum One 6 of 8, 58,815 (two token transfers reverted inside take, a token property); Robinhood Chain 134,721; Elysium 54,733; Polygon 78,557; Avalanche 4 of 4, 44,689; Monad 105,405; Arc 44,461. Base, Zora, Soneium, BNB Chain, MegaETH, Tempo and HyperEVM returned no holder (rate limits or no Transfer logs in the window). The code path has no loop on any network: burn is one tstore delta and one balance write, plus one allowance write when the caller is not the owner (src/PoolManager.sol:332-336, src/ERC6909Claims.sol:13-22, src/ERC6909.sol:85), and take is one delta and one transfer (src/PoolManager.sol:291-297). Output: out/claims.json. Evidence: research/network-risk/cycles/020/theme-mined-gas-cap.work/out/claims.json; src/PoolManager.sol:291-297; src/PoolManager.sol:332-336; src/ERC6909Claims.sol:13-22
- all 21 networks, cycle 20. Do public endpoints apply the mined cap to simulation? eth_call with gas 16,777,216, 16,777,217, 30,000,000, 30,000,001, 33,554,433 and 60,000,000 to an address without code, and a binary search of the largest gas need for which eth_estimateGas still succeeds (probe contract by state override that reverts unless GAS is at least X). Result: eth_call accepted 60,000,000 gas on all 21 endpoints, so no eth_call result says anything about the mined cap. eth_estimateGas does apply a ceiling: it returned at most 16,777,216 on Ethereum (reth v2.11.0), the seven OP Stack chains, BNB Chain and Arc; 30,000,000 on Celo, Tempo and HyperEVM; about 32,000,000 of execution gas on Arbitrum One, Robinhood Chain and Elysium; 33,554,432 on Polygon; 50,000,000 on Avalanche; 150,000,000 on Monad; 210,000,000 on X Layer; and no ceiling below 2^32 on MegaETH. On Monad the estimator ceiling is the block limit, above the 30,000,000 per transaction limit that consensus enforces, so an estimate on Monad can exceed what can be mined. No exit needs more than 1,000,000 gas, so the mismatch does not reach the PoolManager. Evidence: research/network-risk/cycles/020/theme-mined-gas-cap.work/out/probe_caps.json; research/network-risk/cycles/020/theme-mined-gas-cap.work/out/estcap.json; https://docs.monad.xyz/developer-essentials/gas-pricing
- Optimism, Base, Unichain, Zora, Worldchain, Ink, Soneium, Ethereum, BNB Smart Chain, Arc, cycle 20. Source of the 16,777,216 cap on Ethereum, the OP Stack chains, BNB Chain and Arc. Result: EIP-7825 rejects any transaction with a gas limit above 2^24 at txpool and block validation. Karst (Upgrade 19) activates it on OP Mainnet, Soneium, Ink, Unichain and Zora, with deposits exempt. BEP-652 makes it mandatory on BNB Chain; the largest user transaction in 300 recent BNB Chain blocks (135,712,831 to 135,713,130) had exactly 16,777,216 gas, and the larger ones are zero-price system transactions to 0x1000. On Base, World Chain and Arc the estimator ceiling of exactly 16,777,216 is the evidence; this closes lead L-110 for Arc and the cap part of L-095 for World Chain. Evidence: https://eips.ethereum.org/EIPS/eip-7825; https://docs.optimism.io/notices/upgrade-19; https://raw.githubusercontent.com/bnb-chain/BEPs/master/BEPs/BEP-652.md; research/network-risk/cycles/020/theme-mined-gas-cap.work/out/scan_user_4326_56.json
- Arbitrum One, Robinhood Chain, Elysium, cycle 20. Mined cap on the Arbitrum family, read from ArbGasInfo. Result: getGasAccountingParams() at 0x6c returns speedLimit 7,000,000, gasPoolMax 32,000,000 and maxTxGasLimit 32,000,000 on all three chains. A mined Arbitrum One transaction (0x4d2011c4...e988) carried 32,003,281 gas including the parent chain data component. Exits use at most 270,000. Evidence: eth_call 0x612af178 to 0x000000000000000000000000000000000000006C on arb1.arbitrum.io, rpc.mainnet.chain.robinhood.com and rpc.elysium.kinetiq.xyz, output research/network-risk/cycles/020/theme-mined-gas-cap.work/out/arbgasinfo.txt
- Monad, Tempo, cycle 20. Mined caps on Monad and Tempo. Result: Monad documents a 30M transaction gas limit and a 150M block limit; consensus (TfmValidator, TFM_MAX_GAS_LIMIT) rejects larger transactions. Tempo TIP-1010 caps a transaction at 30,000,000 and general (non-payment) gas at 30,000,000 per block. Tempo exits, the costliest measured because a new storage slot costs 250,000 gas, use at most 976,067. A removal can add at most two fresh writes beyond what was sampled (Position.sol:100-101), about 500,000 more on Tempo. Evidence: https://docs.monad.xyz/developer-essentials/gas-pricing; https://d3qv7503rlaw88.cloudfront.net/uploads/Monad_Execution_Report_e1563cbb25.pdf; https://github.com/tempoxyz/tempo/blob/main/tips/tip-1010.md
- HyperEVM, cycle 20. HyperEVM: does an exit fit a small block, which every account uses unless it sets the big block flag on HyperCore?. Result: Yes. Small blocks hold 3,000,000 gas and big blocks 30,000,000. The largest sampled exit used 197,982 gas, so 15 such exits fit one small block. The estimator ceiling of 30,000,000 is the big block size, so an estimate between 3,000,000 and 30,000,000 is only minable after the flag is set. Evidence: https://hyperliquid.gitbook.io/hyperliquid-docs/for-developers/hyperevm/dual-block-architecture; research/network-risk/cycles/020/theme-mined-gas-cap.work/out/exits.json
- MegaETH, cycle 20. MegaETH, normal sequencer path: can an ordinary account grow the SALT bucket of a victim position's fee growth words until the two fresh writes of a removal (Position.sol:100-101) exceed what one user transaction can carry?. Result: Not at a practical cost. User transactions with 984,000,000 gas were mined in blocks 32,838,613 to 32,838,912, so the per transaction cap set by the sequencer is at least that. Under the rule recorded in F-105 (storage gas 20,000 times (multiplier minus 1), a bucket doubles at 80 percent use), two writes exceed 984,000,000 only at multiplier 32,768. My model puts that at about 3.36 million entries in one bucket and 7.3e14 gas, about 733 ETH at the 1,000,000 wei base fee floor, spread over about 74,000 blocks, because each entry costs more as the bucket grows and a 10,000,000,000 gas block holds fewer of them. The base fee would rise long before that. The L1 deposit path with its 1,000,000 gas limit stays F-105. Evidence: https://docs.megaeth.com/spec/megaevm/resource-limits.md; research/network-risk/cycles/020/theme-mined-gas-cap.work/out/scan_user_4326_56.json
- Celo, X Layer, Avalanche, cycle 20. Celo, X Layer and Avalanche, where no 2^24 cap is active. Result: The estimator accepted gas up to the block limit on Celo (30,000,000) and X Layer (210,000,000), and up to 50,000,000 on Avalanche (block limit 80,000,000). The largest user transactions in 120 recent blocks were 9,000,000 (Celo), 10,000,000 (X Layer) and 5,943,301 (Avalanche). Exits use at most 265,000. Evidence: research/network-risk/cycles/020/theme-mined-gas-cap.work/out/estcap.json; research/network-risk/cycles/020/theme-mined-gas-cap.work/out/scan_user_more.json
- Polygon, Monad, Tempo, Optimism, Base, Unichain, Zora, Worldchain, Ink, Soneium, cycle 20. Scripts in OPCODES.md that ran out of gas or ran above the mined cap under eth_call (full-range swaps on Polygon, Monad and Tempo, scripts above 16,777,216 on the OP Stack chains). Result: These are swaps. Pool.swap stops at the caller's sqrtPriceLimitX96 (src/libraries/Pool.sol:344), so a swap too long for one transaction is split by price limits, and no victim needs a swap to exit. The dust-tick cost hazard is already F-064, F-111, F-115, F-039 and F-063. Evidence: src/libraries/Pool.sol:344

## Reading of the source (theme-outside-signature-senders)

- Ethereum, cycle 20. Ethereum: every path that starts a call whose sender is not set by a signature or by the calling frame, and whether an ordinary account can make that sender the PoolManager. Result: None can. The only such calls are the EIP-4788, EIP-2935 and request queue system calls (including the builder deposit and exit queues in go-ethereum master), each with From params.SystemAddress 0xfffffffffffffffffffffffffffffffffffffffe and a fixed target (core/state_processor.go lines 379-395, 411-425, 465-480; params/protocol_params.go line 246). Signed transactions must come from an account without code other than a delegation (core/state_transition.go preCheck, line 602). An EIP-7702 authority is recovered from its signature (core/types/tx_setcode.go lines 145-165) and is rejected if it holds code that is not a delegation (core/state_transition.go lines 1144-1146), so the PoolManager, with 24,009 bytes of code and nonce 1, can never be an authority. Evidence: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ethereum/go-ethereum/master/core/state_processor.go; https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ethereum/go-ethereum/master/core/state_transition.go; https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ethereum/go-ethereum/master/core/types/tx_setcode.go; research/network-risk/cycles/020/theme-outside-signature-senders.work/raw/pm_nonces.json
- Polygon, cycle 20. Polygon: bor state sync (commitState), span commits and any other system message, and whether their sender can be the PoolManager. Result: No. Every system message is built by GetSystemMessage with From params.BorSystemAddress 0xffffFFFfFFffffffffffffffFfFFFfffFFFfFFfE and Value 0 (consensus/bor/statefull/processor.go lines 71-80, params/config.go line 271), and CommitState sends it to the StateReceiver (consensus/bor/contract/client.go line 73). The StateReceiver accepts only that system address (System.sol lines 4-7) and forwards each record to its receiver as onStateReceive(uint256,bytes) with itself as msg.sender (StateReceiver.sol lines 42-57). No path names a sender chosen by Ethereum or Heimdall. The PoolManager has no fallback and no onStateReceive, so a record naming it as receiver reverts. Its nonce on Polygon is 1. Evidence: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/0xPolygon/bor/v2.11.1/consensus/bor/statefull/processor.go; https://raw.githubusercontent.com/0xPolygon/bor/v2.11.1/params/config.go; https://raw.githubusercontent.com/0xPolygon/bor/v2.11.1/consensus/bor/contract/client.go; https://raw.githubusercontent.com/0xPolygon/genesis-contracts/master/contracts/StateReceiver.sol; https://raw.githubusercontent.com/0xPolygon/genesis-contracts/master/contracts/System.sol
- BNB Smart Chain, cycle 20. BNB Smart Chain: Parlia system transactions, who signs them and where they may go. Result: Every system message is built with From header.Coinbase (parlia.go lines 1389, 2069, 2096, 2110, 2131, 2137-2146), the coinbase must equal the address recovered from the header seal (lines 996-998), and a transaction counts as a system transaction only if its target is one of the fourteen system contracts, its gas price is zero and its recovered sender is the coinbase (lines 323-335, 106-121). The sender is therefore a validator key and the target a fixed system contract. Even a validator cannot make it the PoolManager, because that would need the PoolManager's private key. The PoolManager's nonce is 1. Evidence: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/bnb-chain/bsc/v1.8.2/consensus/parlia/parlia.go
- Avalanche, cycle 20. Avalanche C-Chain: atomic import and export, the native asset precompiles, and any other path whose sender is not a signer or calling frame. Result: None reaches the EVM with a chosen sender. An import is an operation that mints to the named addresses and runs no EVM code (vms/saevm/cchain/tx/import.go lines 206-225, hooks.go lines 228-243). An export debits a C-Chain address only when a secp256k1 signature recovers to that address (export.go lines 175-197). nativeAssetCall used the precompile's caller as sender when it was active and is now DeprecatedContract, which reverts (graft/coreth/nativeasset/contract.go lines 176-180); an eth_call to 0x0100000000000000000000000000000000000002 and 0x0100000000000000000000000000000000000001 on avalanchego/1.15.3 reverted with empty data. Evidence: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ava-labs/avalanchego/v1.15.3/vms/saevm/cchain/tx/export.go; https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ava-labs/avalanchego/v1.15.3/vms/saevm/cchain/tx/import.go; https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ava-labs/avalanchego/v1.15.3/graft/coreth/nativeasset/contract.go; research/network-risk/cycles/020/theme-outside-signature-senders.work/raw/onchain_tests.json
- Monad, cycle 20. Monad: system transactions and staking syscalls. Result: A system transaction is accepted only when its recovered sender is SYSTEM_SENDER 0x6f49a8F621353f12378d0046E7d7e4b9B249DC9e, it is a legacy transaction, and its target is the staking precompile (validate_system_transaction.cpp lines 47, 51, 59); it then runs the native staking syscall, not EVM code at a chosen address (execute_system_transaction.cpp lines 178-182, 205-232). SYSTEM_SENDER cannot be an EIP-7702 authority (validate_monad_transaction.cpp line 53). The header comment calls it a key known to consensus (system_sender.hpp lines 22-25); I did not establish whether the key is public. In neither case can the sender be the PoolManager, whose nonce is 1. Evidence: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/category-labs/monad/v0.16.7/category/execution/monad/validate_system_transaction.cpp; https://raw.githubusercontent.com/category-labs/monad/v0.16.7/category/execution/monad/execute_system_transaction.cpp; https://raw.githubusercontent.com/category-labs/monad/v0.16.7/category/execution/monad/system_sender.hpp; https://raw.githubusercontent.com/category-labs/monad/v0.16.7/category/execution/monad/validate_monad_transaction.cpp
- MegaETH, cycle 20. MegaETH: deposits, mega system transactions, keyless deploys and pre-block system calls, for an ordinary account. Result: An ordinary account cannot make any of them carry the PoolManager as sender. Deposits take from from the portal, which aliases contract callers (see the MegaETH finding of this unit for the governance path). Mega system transactions must be legacy transactions recovered to 0xA887dCB9D5f39Ef79272801d05Abdf707CFBbD1d and calling the Oracle contract (system/tx.rs lines 22-25, 40-70; execution.rs lines 104-110). Pre-block system calls use 0xff..fe (system/tx.rs lines 129-133). The keyless deploy signer is recovered from its signature (cleared in earlier cycles). Evidence: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/megaeth-labs/mega-evm/v1.7.4/crates/mega-evm/src/system/tx.rs; https://raw.githubusercontent.com/megaeth-labs/mega-evm/v1.7.4/crates/mega-evm/src/evm/execution.rs
- Tempo, cycle 20. Tempo: system transactions, sub-blocks, fee payers, type 0x76 batches with keychain signatures, and TIP-1107 configurable accounts (T14, scheduled for 8 December 2026). Result: None lets an ordinary account act as the PoolManager. A system transaction is a legacy transaction with signature (0,0) and sender Address::ZERO (envelope.rs lines 26-29, 234-236, 379-384), and the block executor accepts one only with target address zero carrying sub-block metadata, refusing every other target (block.rs lines 617-660); the committee system call uses caller zero and a fixed target (lines 589-591). Sub-block transactions are refused (lines 671-676; handler.rs line 1400). A fee payer signs separately and does not change the sender. A keychain signature names user_address, which must equal the recovered signer (handler.rs lines 667-676); a key authorization must be signed by that account or, from T6, by an admin key of it (handler.rs lines 566-573, 775-792); and the keychain precompile accepts authorizeKey only when msg.sender is tx.origin and the transaction is signed by the root key or an admin key (account_keychain/mod.rs lines 1193-1209). The PoolManager is never tx.origin, so no key can be registered for it. A configurable account address is the last 20 bytes of a keccak256 of its configuration (tip-1107.md lines 84-99) and must have empty code or the 0xef marker (line 171); the PoolManager has code, and matching its address would need a 160 bit preimage. Address zero, the protocol fee controller on Tempo, reaches only the sub-block metadata target and the committee contract. Evidence: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/tempoxyz/tempo/a9d6748/crates/primitives/src/transaction/envelope.rs; https://raw.githubusercontent.com/tempoxyz/tempo/a9d6748/crates/evm/src/block.rs; https://raw.githubusercontent.com/tempoxyz/tempo/a9d6748/crates/evm/src/handler.rs; https://raw.githubusercontent.com/tempoxyz/tempo/a9d6748/crates/precompiles/src/account_keychain/mod.rs; https://raw.githubusercontent.com/tempoxyz/tempo/a9d6748/tips/tip-1107.md
- Arc, cycle 20. Arc: who may name the sender of a CallFrom subcall, checked in source and on chain. Result: Only Memo 0x5294E9927c3306DcBaDb03fe70b92e01cCede505 and Multicall3From 0x522fAf9A91c41c443c66765030741e4AaCe147D0 may call CallFrom (evm.rs lines 661-669, 1665-1680; execution-config call_from.rs), both pass their own msg.sender (Memo.sol line 43, Multicall3From.sol lines 43, 58, 81), and the EVM rejects a child caller that is neither the calling helper nor tx.origin (evm.rs lines 946-955). On arc/v1: an EOA calling CallFrom directly with the PoolManager as sender reverted with 'unauthorized caller'; an EOA calling Memo with a USDC transfer ran it as the EOA (reverted 'transfer amount exceeds balance'); a contract placed by state override calling Memo reverted with 'sender spoofing requires tx.origin as sender'. The PoolManager is never tx.origin. Evidence: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/circlefin/arc-node/main/crates/evm/src/evm.rs; https://raw.githubusercontent.com/circlefin/arc-node/main/contracts/src/memo/Memo.sol; research/network-risk/cycles/020/theme-outside-signature-senders.work/raw/onchain_tests.json; research/network-risk/cycles/020/theme-outside-signature-senders.work/raw/arc_stub_memo.json
- HyperEVM, cycle 20. HyperEVM: senders of system transactions in a fresh census, and whether an ordinary account can make HyperCore name the PoolManager. Result: In blocks 52231708 to 52233207 (1500 blocks, eth_getSystemTxsByBlockNumber on 'hyperliquid evm Mainnet') there were 1031 system transactions from 28 senders: the HYPE bridge 0x2222222222222222222222222222222222222222, 25 token system addresses 0x20..., the CoreDepositWallet 0x6b9e773128f453f5c2c60935ee2de2cbc5390a24 (2,175 bytes of code) and the treasury 0xc20699185c15d0a2fd65779bb5d69f5b0b113c00. None names the PoolManager or its owner as sender, target or argument, HyperCore spotMeta links none of 195 linked tokens to either, and the PoolManager's nonce is 1. The archive client takes the sender from the upstream from field, falling back to 0x2222... for empty input and the token system address otherwise (nanoreth src/node/types/reth_compat.rs lines 236-249), and treats any zero gas price transaction as a system transaction (executor.rs lines 44-49), so the sender is whatever HyperCore states. That choice stays with HyperCore at operator level, recorded as F-020; an ordinary account cannot link a token to the PoolManager (cleared in cycle 4). Evidence: research/network-risk/cycles/020/theme-outside-signature-senders.work/raw/hl_systx_census.json; research/network-risk/cycles/020/theme-outside-signature-senders.work/raw/hl_spotMeta.json; https://raw.githubusercontent.com/hl-archive-node/nanoreth/master/src/node/types/reth_compat.rs; https://raw.githubusercontent.com/hl-archive-node/nanoreth/master/src/node/evm/executor.rs
- MegaETH, Polygon, BNB Smart Chain, Avalanche, Monad, Tempo, Arc, HyperEVM, Ethereum, cycle 20. Has any path that writes a sender outside a signature ever acted as the PoolManager on the nine networks?. Result: No evidence of it. eth_getTransactionCount of the PoolManager is 1 on all nine endpoints (Ethereum, Polygon, BNB Smart Chain, Avalanche, Monad, MegaETH, Tempo, Arc, HyperEVM), the value set at creation. Deposits, Parlia system transactions, Monad system transactions and HyperEVM system transactions bump the sender's nonce, so none of them has been sent in its name. Bor system messages and Tempo system transactions do not bump a nonce, but their senders are fixed constants. Evidence: research/network-risk/cycles/020/theme-outside-signature-senders.work/raw/pm_nonces.json
- all 21 networks, cycle 20. Signature checks that tokens or Permit2 could run on behalf of the PoolManager (EIP-2612 permit, ERC-1271). Result: None can succeed. src/ has no isValidSignature function (no match for isValidSignature or 1271 in src/), so an ERC-1271 check against the PoolManager reverts or returns no magic value, and an ecrecover check would need its private key. The PoolManager also never approves a spender: its only outgoing calls are transfer, balanceOf, the hook selectors, unlockCallback and empty value calls (src/types/Currency.sol:40-80, src/PoolManager.sol:104-114). Evidence: src/types/Currency.sol:40-80
- all 21 networks, cycle 20. What the code does when a call reaches it with msg.sender equal to the PoolManager itself. Result: Nothing useful to an attacker. unlock calls IUnlockCallback(msg.sender).unlockCallback, and the PoolManager has no such function, so the call reverts (src/PoolManager.sol:104-114). take, settle, mint, burn, clear, swap, modifyLiquidity and donate require the lock (src/PoolManager.sol:96-99). The owner functions check msg.sender against the stored owner (lib/solmate/src/auth/Owned.sol:19-23) and fee collection against protocolFeeController (src/ProtocolFees.sol:44-57). The danger of a forged PoolManager sender lies in calls to tokens, which bypass all of this code. Evidence: src/PoolManager.sol:104-114

## Reading of the source (theme-reserved-address-routing)

- BNB Smart Chain, cycle 20. L-907: which reading of CAS20 routing is right, the cycle 19 probe (byte 10 = 0x02 or 0xff reverts under Jenner) or the tagged source (only ordinals 0x00 and 0x01 are routed). Result: The tagged source is right and the probe was misread. The three cycle 19 addresses 0xca52...0001, 0xca52...0000 and 0xca52...00ff all have byte 10 equal to 0x00. A new probe with byte 10 in {0x00, 0x01, 0x02, 0xff} on dataseed1 (Geth v1.8.2 4e1c8247), dataseed (same build), 48 Club (two builds in one batch, 9b93ce23 and 132104cd) and reth-bsc v0.1.4-hotfix-23b510f, with web3_clientVersion before and after, shows ordinals 0x00 and 0x01 reverting and 0x02 and 0xff answering empty success with gas estimate 21000 under the Jenner time override, and all of them answering empty success without it. No build routes differently from the tag, so the lead's concern that validators on different builds disagree has no support in these answers. Evidence: research/network-risk/cycles/020/theme-reserved-address-routing.work/raw/cas20_probe.json; https://raw.githubusercontent.com/bnb-chain/bsc/v1.8.2/core/vm/cas20.go lines 107-135
- BNB Smart Chain, cycle 20. L-908: every CAS20 function at v1.8.2 that changes a holder's balanceOf without a transfer signed or sent by that holder, who may call it, and whether an account with no role can move the PoolManager's balance between its own sync and settle. Result: No such path for an account with no role. balanceOf reads the raw balance slot for both variants (cas20_token.go lines 88-93); the Stablecoin variant adds only currency() (cas20_stablecoin.go lines 35-48); the Asset multiplier changes only scaledBalanceOf, balanceOfUI and totalSupplyUI (cas20_asset.go). The balance changing entries are mint and batchMint (MINT role, cas20_admin.go and cas20_asset.go lines 501-506), burn of the caller's own balance (BURN role), seizeWithMemo (SEIZE role, subject to the seize exempt policy), updateMultiplier (OPERATOR role, no balanceOf change), transferFrom (needs an allowance the PoolManager never grants; the PoolManager has no approve call) and permit (ecrecover only, cas20_permit.go lines 198-244, so a contract holder cannot be the signer). There is no interest, rebase, forced conversion or mint to all holders. A mint to the PoolManager between sync and settle credits the settler (src/PoolManager.sol:279-288, 349-364), but only a MINT role holder can do it, so it is an issuer action already recorded under F-007 and F-076. Evidence: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/bnb-chain/bsc/v1.8.2/core/vm/cas20_token.go, https://raw.githubusercontent.com/bnb-chain/bsc/v1.8.2/core/vm/cas20_admin.go, https://raw.githubusercontent.com/bnb-chain/bsc/v1.8.2/core/vm/cas20_asset.go, https://raw.githubusercontent.com/bnb-chain/bsc/v1.8.2/core/vm/cas20_stablecoin.go, https://raw.githubusercontent.com/bnb-chain/bsc/v1.8.2/core/vm/cas20_permit.go

The PoolManager reads balanceOf with a high level view call, which compiles to STATICCALL (src/types/Currency.sol:90-96), and pays with CALL (src/types/Currency.sol:73), so neither the caller being a contract nor the frame changes what it sees. L-917: on the five networks with protocol tokens or system code at reserved addresses, does an eth_call code override at such an address take effect, or does the node keep routing to native code. Result: It depends on the client and the range, and the answer is now measured. BNB Chain: the override takes effect at every CAS20 address, the singletons, 0x70, 0x1000 and 0x2000 on Geth v1.8.2 (override.go lines 75-82 put DisabledPrecompile in the map, and EVM.precompile then treats the address as an ordinary account, evm.go lines 46-51), and at CAS20 addresses on reth-bsc; reth-bsc keeps the native 0x70 precompile under Jenner and ignores the override there. Tempo: the same holds for the 12 byte TIP-20 prefix (pathUSD and two live tokens answer natively, unused addresses revert with Uninitialized without code and answer 0 with code); the fee manager, TIP-403 registry, factory and DEX ignore the override. Arc: the override takes effect at 0x3600..0000, 0x3600..0001, 0x3600..0004 and 0x1800..0005 and 0x1800..0009. HyperEVM: the read precompiles 0x800 to 0x813 ignore the override; 0x2222..22, 0x3333..33, 0x5555..55 and the token system addresses 0x2000..00 and 0x2000..77 take it. On every reth or revm based endpoint (Ethereum, the OP Stack chains, Celo, X Layer, Monad, MegaETH, Tempo, Arc, HyperEVM) and on avalanchego 1.15.3 an override at an active precompile (0x01, 0x02, 0x04, and 0x100 where active) is ignored, while Geth based bor, BSC and Nitro replace the precompile. - Base, Tempo, BNB Smart Chain, cycle 20. Whether an ordinary account can make an unused address in a native token range look like a token (B20 and TIP-20 treat any code as an initialized token; CAS20 needs the marker 0xEF), and so open or close a currency that pools could use. Result: No. Base routes 0xb2 followed by 9 zero bytes (flipping byte 9 or any earlier byte gives an ordinary account, flipping byte 10 or later stays routed), Tempo routes the documented 12 byte prefix 0x20c0 + 10 zero bytes, and CAS20 fixes 10 bytes. Getting code at such an address needs a CREATE or CREATE2 address or a private key with 80 to 96 fixed bits, and the CAS20 marker 0xEF cannot be deployed at all (EIP-3541). Tokens are created only through each network's factory. A pool whose currency is such a token is a pool with an issuer, already covered by F-027, F-031 and F-076. Evidence: research/network-risk/cycles/020/theme-reserved-address-routing.work/raw/prefix_probe.json; https://tempo.com/developers/docs/protocol/tip20/spec.md (TIP20Factory section, TIP20_PREFIX 20C00000000000000000000000)

Transactions that differed and were not first in their block were rerun with all earlier transactions of the block on one state. Result: No difference in any PoolManager result. The set holds 2395 settles with value (1,068 native Transfer logs into the PoolManager in 1,061 transactions, 175,530 USDC) and native payouts (1,327 logs out of the PoolManager in 960 transactions, 181,495 USDC), inside 15626 PoolManager frames (2,918 take, 2,074 settle, 2,084 sync, 2,078 swap, 47 modifyLiquidity, 41 mint, 4 burn, 8 initialize, 2,114 unlock, plus reads). 1,998 were rerun, 2 were set aside (one calls the Arc precompile 0x1800000000000000000000000000000000000003 with selector 1595ec0b, one reaches CREATE2, which the interpreter lacks). 1769 match the chain in every log, status and checked slot on the first pass and 126 more on the block-prefix pass. 8470 PoolManager slots were checked against block-end storage in 1824 transactions with no later PoolManager transaction in the block, all equal. In the 1671 blocks where only this transaction moved the PoolManager's native balance, the balance change equals the reference and equals the net of the system emitter logs for the PoolManager to the wei. 552 recipient balance changes were checked, all equal; 726 recipients were the sender or coinbase or shared the block and were not checked. The 102 transactions that still differ after both passes differ only in logs of contracts that report gas: UserOperationEvent actualGasUsed and actualGasCost of the EntryPoints 0x4337084d9e255ff0702461cf8895ce9e3b5ff108 (80) and 0x0000000071727de22e5e9d8baf0edac6f37da032 (20, one with the gas refund Transfer to the bundler), and word 5 of event 0x2fc0d44e of 0x69460570c93f9de5e2edbc3052bf10125f0ca22d (2). In all of them the PoolManager logs, the PoolManager native Transfer logs, the status and the checked slots are equal. One more, 0xa96f0c92...2abd, a Multicall3 aggregate3 that ran 15 iterations of a loop on chain and 23 in the reference; eth_simulateV1 of the block prefix on arc.drpc.org at the mined gas limit gives the mined 95 logs and at twice the limit gives 127 logs with 4 PoolManager logs, the reference's result, so the loop is bounded by remaining gas, which the reference does not meter. Limits: no Arc endpoint serves debug_ or trace_ methods (-32601), so the output of each PoolManager frame was not compared directly, only through the logs, storage and balances it leaves; 23 inner unlock frames fail in the reference inside successful transactions, and their effects are consistent with the chain's logs. - Arc, cycle 21. Task 3 of L-944: native take from the real PoolManager at 0x8366a39c...0951 by eth_call with state overrides (a driver at a fresh address calls unlock, runs the items, records success, return data and balances, and reverts), sent in JSON-RPC batches bracketed by web3_clientVersion and arc_getVersion to both Arc endpoints at the same block 33,142,279, and the same scripts to the Ethereum PoolManager 0x000000000004444c...8A90 at block 26,495,018. Recipients: a codeless address, a contract that reverts, a contract that loops until out of gas, an address made blocklisted by a state override of its slot at 0x1800...01 (no public blocklisted address could be listed: getLogs over the precompile's Blocklisted event needs more than the 1,000 block range the official endpoint allows, dRPC allows 100, and the explorer API returned a challenge), address(0), the precompiles 0x01, 0x02, 0x04 and 0x100, the Arc addresses 0x1800...00 to ...03 and the USDC face 0x3600...00, the PoolManager itself, and a contract that self-destructs when called. Amounts 0, 1 and the rest of the balance (2,410,964.98 USDC on Arc). Also settle with value 1, sync(address(0)) with value, settle with value 0 and take with value. Result: The two Arc endpoints return byte-identical records on all 17 scripts (54 items), so the builds 37812c61 and 8e8edb7a agree on every probed value path. Against Ethereum, success flags, return data and balance changes are equal except where F-125 and F-049 already say: a payout of 1 or of the full balance to address(0) or to the blocklisted address fails on Arc with NativeTransferFailed wrapping Error('Zero address not allowed') or Error('Blocked address') and moves nothing, and every take to 0x1800...00 to ...03 or to 0x3600...00 fails on Arc even with amount 0, because those addresses reject empty calldata, while they are plain accounts on Ethereum. Each failure reverts only the take, so the caller's delta is never debited without a transfer or the reverse (src/PoolManager.sol:291-297, src/types/Currency.sol:44-52). The reverting and gas burning recipients give identical wrapped errors on both chains. The precompiles 0x01, 0x02, 0x04 and 0x100 accept value on both, and the full PoolManager balance can be paid to them, which the caller owes and must settle. A take to the PoolManager fails on both, since no contract in src/ outside src/test declares receive or fallback. The self-destructing contract was created before the transaction, so it is not marked destroyed and the take succeeds on both; the destroyed-in-transaction branch of the hook was not reached by these probes. The settle items behave alike on all three: settle credits msg.value, sync and take are not payable. Result: Yes in the mined sample. The replay models transfer(from, to, amount) as: caller must be 0x3600, zero addresses and blocklisted accounts refused, a zero amount moves nothing and logs nothing, otherwise balances move by exactly amount and a Transfer log from 0xff...fe is emitted when from differs from to (native_coin_authority.rs v0.8.6 lines 286-345), and isBlocklisted as a read of slot keccak(account, 2) of 0x1800...01. With that model every one of the 1,998 rerun transactions gives the mined emitter logs, and the PoolManager balance changes equal those logs to the wei in all 1,671 isolated blocks. The 18 versus 6 decimal split and its rounding are cleared in earlier cycles and were not reopened. ## Reading of the source (theme-blind-read)

- Ethereum, Optimism, BNB Smart Chain, Unichain, Polygon, X Layer, Worldchain, Soneium, Tempo, Robinhood Chain, Base, Arbitrum One, Celo, Ink, Elysium, Zora, cycle 21. Assumption T3, ranked first in the blind list: transient slots of the real PoolManager written in one transaction must be empty in the next transaction of the same block. eth_simulateV1 at the real PoolManager address ran, in one simulated block, a driver (state override) that calls unlock and syncs a stub token inside the callback, ending (1) in success with the currency still synced, (2) INVALID inside and at the top, (3) REVERT, (4) a completed unlock followed by INVALID at the top. After each transaction a separate transaction read IS_UNLOCKED, NONZERO_DELTA_COUNT, RESERVES_OF and CURRENCY through exttload(bytes32[]), and the driver read its own transient slot; a second block read them again. Worldchain, Celo and X Layer were run on thirdweb, ankr and drpc endpoints because the networks.json endpoints refused eth_simulateV1 with HTTP 401 and 403. Result: On all 16 networks the in-transaction read returned the synced stub token, so the write happened, and every later transaction and the next block read 0 in all four PoolManager slots and in the driver slot. An IS_UNLOCKED value of 1 would have let any later caller run take() outside unlock (src/PoolManager.sol:96-99,291-297,112). No leak exists on the simulation path of these endpoints. Raw answers with web3_clientVersion before and after are in research/network-risk/cycles/021/theme-blind-read.work/xtx-all.json and xtx-alt.json, script research/network-risk/cycles/021/theme-blind-read.work/scripts/xtx.py. Evidence: research/network-risk/cycles/021/theme-blind-read.work/xtx-all.json
- all 21 networks, cycle 21. Assumption C5, ranked third: CALLVALUE must equal a real debit, because native settle credits msg.value with no balance check (src/PoolManager.sol:353-354). eth_call of a top-level transfer of 1 wei and of 1e18 wei from an address with zero balance on all 21 networks. Result: All 21 endpoints refused both calls with an insufficient funds or OutOfFunds error, and the sender balance is 0. Together with the earlier internal-call value tests (tools/opdiff/callsem.py) no endpoint lets a call carry value that was not debited. Results in research/network-risk/cycles/021/theme-blind-read.work/xtx-all.json. Evidence: research/network-risk/cycles/021/theme-blind-read.work/xtx-all.json
- all 21 networks, cycle 21. Assumption T5, never isolated before: TSTORE must fail in a static context. The earlier static write test wrote TSTORE and SSTORE together, so the SSTORE alone would fail the frame. Probe C staticcalls the real PoolManager's sync(X), which writes only transient storage (src/PoolManager.sol:279-288, src/libraries/CurrencyReserves.sol:27-31), then reads CURRENCY and RESERVES_OF. In the same eth_call it checks that sync(X) by plain call sets the slot and sync(address(0)) clears it, that a sub-frame that unlocks, syncs in the callback and then reverts or halts with INVALID leaves CURRENCY, IS_UNLOCKED and NONZERO_DELTA_COUNT at 0, and that a completed unlock leaves IS_UNLOCKED at 0 with the currency still synced. Result: 18 of 18 words as specified on all 21 networks, including Avalanche, Monad, MegaETH, Arc and HyperEVM whose endpoints have no eth_simulateV1. The review's reference interpreter (tools/opdiff/pyevm.py) running the build of this checkout gives the same 18 words. Results in research/network-risk/cycles/021/theme-blind-read.work/static-all.json, scripts research/network-risk/cycles/021/theme-blind-read.work/scripts/static_rollback.py and scripts/local_ref.py. The first run gave out of gas on every network because a failed static frame burns all forwarded gas; the rerun gives each call a fixed allowance. Evidence: research/network-risk/cycles/021/theme-blind-read.work/static-all.json
- all 21 networks, cycle 21. Blind reading of every file in src/ outside src/test: every assembly block listed in research/network-risk/cycles/021/theme-blind-read.work/assumptions.md with the opcode result it needs. Constants recomputed in python3: the 19 TickMath multipliers equal floor(2^128 / sqrt(1.0001)^(2^i)) plus 0 or 1, the log constant 255738958999603826347141 equals floor(2^64/log2(sqrt(1.0001))) plus 1, the four transient slot constants equal keccak256(name) minus 1, and getSqrtPriceAtTick(+-887272) returns MAX_SQRT_PRICE and MIN_SQRT_PRICE. Result: No line computes or decides differently from what its comments and the specification say. take, mint, burn, settle and clear are gated only by IS_UNLOCKED (src/PoolManager.sol:96-99) and the only settlement check is NonzeroDeltaCount at the end of unlock (src/PoolManager.sol:112), so the code's safety rests on transient storage rules T2 to T4, which probes A and C and the earlier work test. The checked addition in CurrencyDelta.applyDelta (src/libraries/CurrencyDelta.sol:37) and the checked subtraction in _settle (src/PoolManager.sol:360) revert rather than wrap. PoolManager has no receive or fallback, so native value enters only through settle and settleFor (src/PoolManager.sol:300-307) or through value that bypasses code. Evidence: src/libraries/TickMath.sol:80-111
- all 21 networks, cycle 21. Step 3 comparison of the fifteen highest ranked blind assumptions with OPCODES.md, findings.json and cleared.json. Result: Twelve of the fifteen were already tested with evidence that exercises the scenario itself (arithmetic, signed opcodes, division by zero, call output buffers, keccak lengths, jump analysis, gas, sender spoofing, empty-code calls, shared transient frames, frame rollback, dual faces). Three were exercised only near the scenario: transient storage across transactions (one generic simulation on Arbitrum), top-level value without a debit (internal calls only) and TSTORE alone in a static frame. Probes A, B and C close those on the networks whose endpoints serve the method. The table is in research/network-risk/cycles/021/theme-blind-read.work/assumptions.md. Evidence: research/network-risk/cycles/021/theme-blind-read.work/assumptions.md

The two clients compute different hashes for the same system transaction (0 of 222 equal), so a census must match by content and not by hash. Because nb-20261125-2 fails a block whose re-executed system receipts differ from the source commitment, every block hyperlend served had matching system receipts. That commitment comes from the operator's own block source, so it shows the archive client and hl-node agree, not that the header authenticates them. The ordering that the sync and settle clearances need (src/PoolManager.sol:279-288, 349-364) holds in every sampled block, and nothing found lets an ordinary account place a system transaction between a user's sync and settle.
