Only 81667 is a generic miscompile, and go1.27.3 holds it. go1.27.2 to go1.27.3 (2 commits): crypto/x509 distrust list only. go1.27.3 to go1.27.4 (26 commits, released 2026-11-10): 81866 deadstore through CondSelect (the 1.27 backport of 81863, a generic miscompile on targets with CondSelect, amd64 and arm64 among them), 81927 x86 assembler PCALIGN loop (a build hang), 82106 method indices in export data, 82657 runtime nextFrame for frameless wrappers (a fatal error during panic unwinding on arm64 and similar targets), cgo and linker hardening (four CVEs). go1.27.3 lacks all of these. After go1.27.4 on the branch (11 commits to 2026-11-24): runtime race callback g0 check on amd64 (82784, race builds only), Windows exception check, time, net, encoding/json. No compiler change. Master fixes after the last merge of master into the go1.27 branch (a5f29a67, 2026-07-14) that are not on release-branch.go1.27 and concern amd64 or arm64 code: 82825 (7684884c6d0e, 2026-11-04): SBBQcarrymask and SBBLcarrymask lack clobberFlags, so an unbounded shift by y and a materialised y ==, !=, <= or > width comparison read the SBB's flags, amd64 and 386, wrong booleans only; 82777 (45071c879089): arm64 CSINV with constant false flags folds to boolean Not (XOR 1) instead of MVN; 607cfcea17a4 (2026-07-15): arm64 noov comparisons of a - x*y with 0 absorbed into InvertFlags are wrong when a - x*y is the minimum integer; a15f882163a2 (2026-11-24): arm64 (REVW (REVW p)) folded to p loses the zero extension; 83036 (d2cdd7563032): phiopt replaces a loop-carried boolean phi of constants with the entry condition (generic). The same rule text is present in go1.27.3, go1.26.10 and go1.25.12. Other master fixes in the window are compile failures (b253a4ab5d9b amd64 ADC/SBB constant flags, b3f5034b15a7 arm64 pair offsets), performance (2bc055441f04 #34950, db11f9069e1f on ports whose Ctz lowering uses its argument twice, which amd64 and arm64 do not), latent (12a1a3503252 convertIntWithBitsize: in go1.27.3 its only caller, limit.add, masks the sum to b bits so the sign extension cannot change a result; 461534e2add9 MNEGW), other targets (s390x 82774, MIPS 82772 and 82776, loong64 and riscv64 82773, write barrier 83238 on 386, arm, mips64 and ppc64), front end side effect order (81696 make, 83209 append of make, 81697 range with blank second variable, 82708 make+copy, the last only after a master-only change), or x86 assembler checks for hand-written assembly (b0d3d283f1a4 high byte registers with REX; no amd64 assembly file in the go1.27.3 standard library names AH, BH, CH or DH). ## Reading of the source (theme-ruint-releases)

- all 21 networks, cycle 21. Task 1, fix #681 (mul_mod quotient skip). The quotient-skip test was read in the crate sources of ruint 1.18.0, 1.19.0, 1.20.0, 1.20.1 and 1.21.1 from static.crates.io (sha256 of the .crate files are listed in the work directory). Result: Releases 1.18.0 to 1.20.1 do not have the fault. Their mul_mod (src/modular.rs:94-102) forms the full double-width product and runs the general division, and they do not contain rem_nxm_spare_limb. 1.21.1 contains the fix: src/algorithms/div/knuth.rs:133-136 skips the top quotient limb only when the top two normalized numerator limbs are strictly less than the divisor's. That condition is sufficient, so the skipped digit is always zero. The main-branch CHANGELOG still lists #681 under Unreleased and has no 1.21.1 section. The statement that 1.21.1 holds the fix therefore rests on the crate code, not on the changelog. When the harness copy was changed to <=, as in 1.21.0, it gave 109,148 wrong mul_mod results in 1,000,000 cases (seed 21024). The five releases gave none. Evidence: https://static.crates.io/crates/ruint/ruint-1.21.1.crate (src/algorithms/div/knuth.rs:133-136, src/modular.rs:114-150); https://raw.githubusercontent.com/recmo/uint/main/CHANGELOG.md
- all 21 networks, cycle 21. Task 1, change #634 (Shl and Shr by primitive integer types). The impl_shift macro and the overflowing_shl_big and wrapping_shl paths were read in all five releases. Result: In 1.18.0, 1.19.0 and 1.20.0 the operators exist only for usize, u8, u16, u32, isize, i8, i16 and i32, plus u64 and i64 on 64-bit targets (src/bits.rs:924-928 in 1.20.0). They convert with `rhs as usize`. 1.20.1 and 1.21.1 add u128 and i128 and convert with usize::try_from(rhs).unwrap_or(usize::MAX) (1.20.1 src/bits.rs:858-924). On 64-bit hosts, the change itself changes no value for any type the older releases implement. The value faults in this area come from the release-specific code listed in the next entries. Evidence: https://static.crates.io/crates/ruint/ruint-1.20.1.crate (src/bits.rs:852-924); https://static.crates.io/crates/ruint/ruint-1.20.0.crate (src/bits.rs:852-928)

- all 21 networks, cycle 21. Tasks 1 to 3, faults #701 and #704 (wrapping_from of negative integers). The macro impl_from_signed_int and support/num_bigint.rs were read in all five releases. They are byte-identical (md5 e9783126 and 02ce5067). Result: All five releases have both faults and none has a fix. Uint::wrapping_from(-v) for a primitive narrower than the Uint returns the narrow two's complement zero-extended. For example, -10i16 becomes 65526 in a U256 (src/from.rs:494-521). Every one of the 625,497 negative inputs out of 1,000,000 (seed 21029) gave that result in each release. For BigInt the result is the magnitude (src/support/num_bigint.rs:53-62). Most clients compile the num-bigint feature, according to their lockfiles. No instruction handler on the PoolManager's path calls wrapping_from, saturating_from, a signed-primitive conversion or a BigInt conversion. A search of revm-interpreter 35.0.1 to 43.0.2, evm2 35aa3280 and mega-evm v1.7.4 instructions.rs finds only U256::from of bool, u8, usize, u64 and the non-negative literal 1 or 31 (From<i32> on a positive value). Signed opcodes are built from wrapping_neg, limb XOR and wrapping_sub (revm i256.rs; evm2 i256.rs:52-62).
